comments.body:
Selectable terminology/phraseology decision confirmed by Jonathan:

Separate four independent layers:
1. Locale/language: en-GB canonical fallback, en-US and future languages; spelling, grammar, date/number/time formats.
2. Domain vocabulary: events, security, gaming/MDT, emergency operations and tenant-specific terminology overlays.
3. Operational/communication profile: UK JESIP/plain-language, agency-specific UK profiles, US public-safety/incident-command profiles where lawfully sourced, ICAO phraseology where lawfully sourced, and event-adapted derivatives.
4. Organisation overrides: versioned tenant terms/codes mapped to canonical Eventiva concepts.

User choice and shared safety:
- Users may select their preferred display locale and terminology profile. Stable canonical concept/action/status IDs remain stored and transmitted so analytics, permissions, agents and integrations do not depend on wording.
- UI can show preferred label plus canonical code/plain-language explanation on demand. Search accepts synonyms across installed profiles.
- Shared operational channels, voice/radio procedure, training exercises and safety-critical workflows also declare a channel/incident profile. Participants see a clear warning/dual label when their personal profile differs; spoken/read-back phraseology follows the shared channel profile to prevent dangerous mismatches.
- Persist the source and target profile/version with messages/forms/training/completion evidence so historical meaning remains reconstructable after updates.
- Agents receive canonical concepts plus active user and operational profiles and must reply in the selected terms without changing underlying action semantics.

Profile governance:
- Every profile records authority/source, jurisdiction, version/effective date, licence/reuse basis, intended context and mapping confidence.
- Do not copy or claim conformance to proprietary/restricted ICAO, emergency-service or industry material without the required permission. Prefer authoritative public definitions and separately licensed packs where necessary.
- “Event-adapted” profiles are labelled adaptations, not official emergency/aviation standards or endorsements.
- Profile tests verify round-trip mapping, ambiguity, plural/grammar/accessibility, agent interpretation and cross-profile handover.
- Training content can render for each profile while assessment evidence records the exact terminology/standard version taught.

Apply this to EVE-13 canonical taxonomy, EVE-28 localisation, EVE-71 MDT/live operations, EVE-245 training and EVE-244 foundational manifest/profile contracts.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
Correction from Jonathan: operational/domain terminology and phraseology are selected by the tenant administrator and apply consistently across the tenant, not chosen independently by each end user.

- Tenant policy selects the active domain vocabulary and operational/communication profile, with optional event/channel-specific profile only where explicitly governed for interoperability.
- End users cannot independently switch MDT/status/radio/operational terminology, because inconsistent wording within one tenant could create confusion and unsafe handovers.
- Personal preference remains available only for language/locale and accessibility presentation where it does not alter canonical operational meaning; tenant policy may also fix locale for regulated/shared forms.
- Admin changes require preview, mapping/ambiguity checks, training/content impact analysis, versioned activation and audit. Historical records retain the profile/version under which they were created.
- Cross-tenant or multi-agency collaboration displays canonical/plain-language equivalents and source profile labels without changing either tenant’s configured vocabulary.
- Agents use the tenant/event/channel profile consistently for every participant.

This supersedes the user-selectable terminology wording in the immediately preceding comment on each issue.

comments.body:
Training, competency and permission decision confirmed by Jonathan:

Evidence levels remain distinct:
1. Viewed/participated.
2. Knowledge demonstrated by assessment.
3. Practical competency signed by an authorised assessor.
4. Operational authorisation for a defined role/resource/action/scope/time.

Credential model:
- Completion, assessment, practical competency, qualification, licence, induction and certification are versioned signed credential/claim records on the worker profile with issuer, subject, scope, evidence, source content/version/profile, issue/valid-from/expiry, renewal, status and revocation.
- A credential is not itself an unrestricted role. Tenant policy explicitly maps an accepted credential type/issuer/level to one or more permission groups, role memberships, feature flags/surfaces or eligibility conditions.
- Roles/permission groups remain live relationship subjects. Prefer conditional/dynamic membership based on valid credentials rather than copying permanent grants.
- When the credential expires, is suspended/revoked, its issuer loses trust, required training changes or evidence is invalidated, derived access is automatically suspended/removed and affected assignments are surfaced.

Grant policy:
- Tenant administrators define whether an outcome auto-activates access, requires assessor approval, requires manager/security approval or only contributes to an eligibility decision.
- Low-risk product training may automatically unlock UI/features after passing.
- Sensitive, regulated, financial, permissions, live-control and safety capabilities require the configured practical assessment/independent approval and cannot be granted merely by viewing or passing a quiz.
- Policy declares scope: tenant, module, event, site, resource class, individual resource, shift/time window and permitted actions.
- Every derived grant shows an explain-access path such as: Jane → signed Event Controller competency → Live Operations role → dispatch action on Event A.
- Permission simulator supports hypothetical credential completion/expiry/revocation and previews gained/lost access before policy publication.

Operational checks:
- Eligibility also considers qualification validity, site/event induction, role/resource permission, required supervision, suspension/restrictions, assurance level and refresher/recency requirements where lawful.
- Assignments re-evaluate at planning time, shift start and sensitive action time according to policy. Offline clients use bounded signed eligibility evidence and reconcile changes visibly.
- Agents may recommend training or initiate an authorised grant workflow but cannot self-issue competency, approve their own evidence or bypass separation of duties.

This is a core EVE-13 authorisation requirement; direct EVE-245 training and EVE-154 qualification/eligibility requirement; related EVE-80 HR and EVE-244 credential/policy contract requirement.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
External qualification verification decision confirmed by Jonathan:

- Accept Eventiva-issued signed credentials, standards-based verifiable credentials, trusted issuer API/registry evidence, QR/digital signatures and uploaded certificate/licence evidence.
- Uploaded/unverified evidence may be stored provisionally but cannot activate Sensitive/Restricted operational permissions or eligibility until the tenant’s configured verification policy succeeds.
- Low-risk policy may permit bounded provisional access with explicit expiry/supervision, but this must be visible, auditable and never the default for regulated/safety capability.

Verification states:
- Unverified
- Evidence submitted/pending
- Automatically verified
- Manually verified
- Verification failed/rejected
- Expired
- Suspended
- Revoked
- Superseded

Evidence and trust:
- OCR/AI extracts issuer, subject, qualification, scope, dates, restrictions and identifiers as proposed data only; it never establishes authenticity by itself.
- Verify cryptographic signatures/QRs, issuer endpoints, trusted registries and revocation/status lists where available. Manual verification records named verifier, method, source, timestamp, confidence, notes and evidence.
- Tenant-managed issuer trust registry defines accepted issuers, credential types, assurance/verification methods, jurisdictions, refresh frequency and which permission scopes they may unlock.
- Show credential validity separately from evidence verification and issuer trust. A genuine credential from an untrusted issuer does not automatically satisfy policy.
- Prefer hashes, issuer references and minimised extracted fields over retaining unnecessary document copies. Original evidence uses the declared security/retention/residency profile and subject-erasure/legal-hold rules.
- Periodically revalidate revocation/expiry where supported. Changes immediately re-evaluate live conditional permissions, assignments and eligibility, with offline bounded evidence/degraded behaviour.
- User can inspect and challenge a verification outcome; corrections preserve immutable provenance.
- Import/export uses portable credential/evidence/status representations and does not falsely claim another system’s assurance.

This is a direct EVE-154 qualification/eligibility and EVE-245 training requirement; related EVE-80 HR, EVE-13 authorisation and EVE-244 credential contracts.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
Assessment-integrity decision confirmed by Jonathan:

- Do not build or enforce invasive anti-cheating/proctoring as a core Eventiva capability. Webcam monitoring, biometric attention/identity analysis, screen surveillance, lockdown browsers and AI “cheating detection” are out of core scope.
- Eventiva does not need to guarantee that an unsupervised learner completed an assessment without external help.

Core assessment levels remain:
1. Practice: unlimited/low-stakes, immediate feedback.
2. Knowledge check: authenticated learner, configurable attempts, question pools/randomisation and pass mark.
3. Verified knowledge assessment: optional passkey reauthentication, timing, signed result and controlled window.
4. Supervised/practical competency: named authorised assessor, structured rubric, evidence and sign-off.

- High-risk/regulated operational permission must rely on the configured practical/authorised verification rather than algorithmic cheating detection.
- Tenants may integrate a third-party proctoring extension under the normal module sandbox, permissions, privacy, lawful-basis, residency, cost and feature-flag controls, but it remains optional/disabled by default and is not presented as Eventiva’s guarantee.
- Learners receive clear assessment rules, evidence/decision visibility and an appeal/correction route. Accessibility accommodations must not be treated as suspicious behaviour.
- Keep ordinary integrity controls: versioned question banks, randomisation, attempt policy, result provenance, issuer/assessor identity, tamper-evident records and audit.

This narrows EVE-245 scope and informs EVE-154 competency evidence and EVE-13 privacy/policy contracts.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
Training content versioning/retraining decision confirmed by Jonathan:

All published training:
- Immutable published versions; edits create a new draft/version.
- Completion/evidence records retain exact course/module/content/question/profile versions.
- Learner/admin views show version, publication date, supersession and available change notes.

Change-impact classes:
- Editorial: wording/presentation only; existing completion remains valid.
- Minor: useful content change without changed competency; optional notification/review.
- Material: procedure, answer or expected behaviour changed; focused delta training/assessment may be assigned.
- Critical: safety, security or regulatory change; affected competency/access may be suspended until required retraining completes.

Eventiva/default course packs:
- Impact classification, structured changelog, source/standard changes, affected lessons/questions/competencies/roles, learner-facing explanation and migration/retraining policy are mandatory before publication.
- Show a clear version-to-version diff and explain how internal Eventiva changes alter training, assessment, qualification and live conditional permissions.
- Generate focused delta paths containing changed mandatory material rather than requiring the entire course where safe.
- Eventiva-owned critical/regulated defaults can impose minimum retraining consequences that tenants cannot silently weaken; they remain transparent and versioned.

Tenant/user-authored courses:
- Exact versioning remains mandatory, but change-impact classification, retraining assignment and access consequence are optional authoring fields by default.
- Authoring UI prompts for impact, suggests a classification/diff using deterministic analysis/AI assistance, and explains consequences. It does not silently enforce retraining when the tenant leaves the optional fields unset.
- Tenants may configure policy requiring impact classification for selected authors, modules, regulated content or integrity profiles.

Governance:
- Named authorised publisher approves classification; AI may propose but not approve critical/regulated impact.
- Changing impact after publication is audited and notifies affected administrators/learners.
- Offline clients receive signed version/impact manifests and cannot present obsolete critical training as current.
- Agents explain why retraining/access changed using the course diff and canonical policy evidence.

This is a direct EVE-245 requirement and refines EVE-154 live competency, EVE-80 HR and EVE-13 authorisation/audit contracts.

comments.body:
## BINDING production provider direction — Neon (2026-11-15)

Jonathan confirmed Neon as Eventiva's intended production PostgreSQL provider. Production tenancy uses a dedicated Neon Postgres project per tenant in AWS London (`eu-west-2`) under the existing EVE-13 policy. The approved PostgreSQL 17 Docker image remains CI/local conformance tooling, not the hosted production database.

EVE-42 must validate the approved `@effect/sql-pg@0.53.1` / `pg@8.23.1` path against Neon pooled and direct connections, SSL and connection lifecycle/autosuspend, direct migration connections where required, DDL and extension availability, transactional semantics, branching/test isolation, controlled tenant routing, regional placement, RLS as control-plane defense, and exact integer/time/UUIDv7 fidelity. Portable contracts remain provider-neutral and no implementation may rely on unavailable Neon features.

A Neon branch is not equivalent to a dedicated tenant production project. Branches may be used for isolated development/conformance only after quota, cost and data isolation are verified. No production mutation, credential exposure, paid resource, destructive test or provider configuration change is authorized by this direction.

comments.body:
## Core distributed execution policy — 2026-11-15 (Jonathan approved)

**Effect Cluster sharding is part of the Eventiva core execution architecture NOW**, not an optional feature added only for agent runs or advanced deployments. Preserve **one cluster-capable authorized execution path** across all editions: domain and action contracts remain transport-/driver-neutral, and server-side cluster routing, runner orchestration and storage are composed in backend infrastructure/adapters. There must not be an independent local-only business-execution engine that behaves differently from distributed mode.

**Deployment defaults**
- **Community / single-host default:** run **one Effect Cluster runner** locally (with any required co-located services) in a supported single-host profile, with no requirement for Eventiva Cloud, SaaS identity or a multi-machine cluster. It must run the same action, authorization, transaction, persistence and dispatch semantics as multi-runner mode; a single runner is a deployment size, not a separate implementation.
- **Cloud / Production default:** **multiple independent runner processes/instances**, distributing work/shard ownership and recovering from runner loss. Define a production-ready minimum topology and expose actual achieved runner count, shard ownership, health, degraded state and capacity. Do not silently claim distributed redundancy when only one runner is healthy.
- **Scalability:** Community/self-hosted may explicitly opt into multi-runner; a single physical host may run one or several runner processes. Cloud may scale runner count based on actual capacity/load controls. Work remains stable across runner placement; no process-local state dependency.
- **Runtime config and topology:** typed, validated deployment-profile config selects topology, runner count, shard count, timeouts/leases/health, endpoints and storage. Separate logical compute sharding from the already-approved one operational database per tenant. Support a fully local deployment via supported storage adapters, without requiring the managed Neon project; verify backend/cluster storage compatibility before claiming SQLite-only cluster support.
- **Safety/reliability:** persist business-critical actions by default with stable idempotency and A1 atomic audit/outbox/transition evidence. At-least-once delivery is not exactly-once execution; retain genuine business deduplication. Enforce same delegated permissions and approval gates on every runner and after a shard moves. Protect local and distributed paths equally.
- **Validation:** same conformance suite for single-runner Community and 2+ independent runners; real distribution, deliberate runner drain/SIGKILL, retry/deduplication, ordering, live configuration, restart/recovery, tenant isolation, and no double-applied business mutation. Include CI integration tests plus documented local launch commands; no fake in-memory-only unit tests substituted for cluster evidence. Test availability/reliability before declaring cloud readiness.

**Priority and execution:** Elevate EVE-252 to critical core-foundation implementation. EVE-40 has now landed and is Done. Begin EVE-252 compatibility/harness/contract work immediately on GPT/Codex in an isolated worktree, avoiding EVE-42 SQL implementation files; finish SQL-backed integration once EVE-42's required storage adapters are verified. Preserve the user's approved dependency/version, direct-to-main, signed commits, security approvals and spending guardrails. Ask explicit approval for any genuinely NEW dependency or paid infrastructure, not for ordinary coordination or task dispatch.

This decision supersedes any reading that Effect Cluster is optional, cloud-exclusive, agent-only, or that the archived pre-rebuild sharding prototype is already the active runtime.

## Agent-Native parity verification — 2026-11-15 (source-and-main audit)

The owner's highest-priority architectural rule is ALREADY BINDING in EVE-13: Eventiva must be **fully agent-native, not a chat sidebar added to a UI**. BuilderIO/agent-native is an approved capability/design reference, with shared actions, shared SQL-backed data and shared application/screen state. All first-party UI, autonomous agents and supported external protocols must invoke the **same authorized Effect action** and obey tenant, privilege, approval and audit controls.

**Authoritative baseline:** EVE-15's approved 126-row upstream capability matrix is pinned to `@agent-native/core@0.222.2` / `6b5cf68eda4b008357934ba0aca201f32cf6b187` (2026-10-29). Current upstream `BuilderIO/agent-native` main was observed at `5d8c5a62e5a18f48bb20b61d12f59223f15fcc8e` (2026-11-15); update/review version drift separately rather than silently altering the locked reference. Main upstream source now also documents shared actions over UI, agent, HTTP, MCP, A2A and CLI, shared application state, skills/memory, automations, teams and visual UI workflows. See https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native/blob/main/README.md and https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native/blob/main/PRODUCT.md . Avoid unverified claims that all protocol variants are implemented by upstream; EVE-15 requires source-backed comparison.

**Verified Eventiva implementation facts:** On `Resnovas/Eventiva` current `main`, portable `@eventiva/contracts` action specs/inventory, Effect runtime authorized invocation, provider-safe tool-schema projections, SQL storage, and Cluster execution exist. `validateParity` in `packages/contracts/src/inventory.ts` is a sound generic API, but current `tests/runtime/src/parity.spec.ts` and `apps/server/src/main.ts` only require **server** as the declared surface; they do not prove parity across mobile UI, real agent, MCP, ACP, A2A, CLI or HTTP. The production tree currently contains NO implemented agent turn loop, screen registry/context/navigation actions, inbound MCP/ACP adapters or end-to-end cross-surface tests. These are specified but largely Backlog: EVE-50 screen awareness (requires EVE-16 remote Expo module spike), EVE-52 agent loop (EVE-43 / EVE-40), EVE-46 HTTP, EVE-48 MCP, EVE-49 ACP inbound, EVE-55 thread projections, EVE-29 agent evaluation. **Do not claim 100% deployed parity yet.**

**Guardrails and next steps:**
1. Treat agent-native capability parity as a **mandatory release/acceptance criterion**, not optional future enhancement. Every new domain/feature registers a canonical Effect action, description and schemas, availability to permitted agent and human surfaces, tenant-aware data and auditable approvals.
2. Ensure screen-context projection for current record, selected entity, view/filters and controls; agent must know UI state without DOM scraping, consistently on React Native, web and MDT. Add unbound-interactive-control negative test and per-surface parity fixtures; do not add a separate agent-only business implementation.
3. Preserve the approved EVE-15 priority that **screen awareness comes ahead of MCP/ACP inbound** after their prerequisites (EVE-16), instead of postponing UI/agent shared state until after all protocol work. Existing EVE-52 agent loop and model/provider engine work remain critical for truly usable agents.
4. Maintain versioned capability conformance matrix explicitly separating **approved requirements**, **implemented on main**, **verified by tests**, **upstream-only** and **future/unapproved**. Compare both baseline pin and latest upstream source commit; document changes/new capabilities and necessary issues/dependencies.
5. Eventiva's portable contract uses Effect Schema and server-side Effect action handlers behind provider-neutral integration. Do not quietly replace Effect runtime with Agent-Native's Zod/Promise/Nitro storage, or add upstream npm packages without exact dependency approval. Incorporate beneficial upstream behavior through properly licensed adapters/ports per project rules. EVE-13 earlier said 'build on and use framework'; EVE-14 says 'read for behavior, do not depend'; record this distinction explicitly. User's current wording asks to **replicate the agent-native design and take heavy inspiration**, so audit behavior/feature parity first and do not assume a direct package dependency.

This note is a **verification finding, not a claim of completed functionality or authorization for new dependencies**. Identity EVE-43's existing orb owns its files and should not be interrupted.

issues.title: S1: Prove one Effect action serves UI, MCP and AI SDK from one inventory entry
issues.description:
## Goal

Prove that a single action defined in Effect Schema with one Effect handler and one authorization check can be invoked identically from a UI call, an MCP client and an AI SDK tool call, with the action listed once in a machine-readable inventory.

## Context

* Spec: <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> sections "Highest-priority core architecture rule", ownership and framework direction (Eventiva owns actions, server, auth, database; own Effect-native framework; AI SDK alongside Effect AI).
* Repository: Resnovas/Eventiva at main (322ab45 or later). Read `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills/coding-preferences/references/effect.md` and `ai.md` first.
* Upstream reference only: BuilderIO/agent-native at a0356c6, `packages/core/src/action.ts`, `action-*.ts`, `mcp/`, `authorization/`. MIT; read for behaviour, do not depend on it.
* Existing Effect stack in the repo: `effect` 3.19, `@effect/rpc`, `@effect/platform`, `@effect/cluster`.

## Work

1. In a throwaway spike branch (`spike/eve-s1-action-projection`), never merged, define `events.create` (input: title, startsAt; output: id) with Effect Schema, typed errors (`Data.TaggedError`) and a handler that writes to an in-memory store service provided by a `Layer`.
2. Add one authorization service: a caller identity with a tenant id and scopes; deny when scope `events:write` is missing.
3. Build an inventory entry (name, description, input and output JSON Schema derived from the Effect Schema via `JSONSchema.make`, required scopes).
4. Project it three ways: an `@effect/platform` HTTP route (the UI call), an MCP tool served with the official MCP TypeScript SDK wrapped in one `Effect.tryPromise` boundary, and an AI SDK `tool()` whose `execute` runs the same Effect.
5. Tests with `@effect/vitest`: same input gives the same result on all three paths; missing scope is denied on all three with the same typed error; a cross-tenant read is denied.

## Dependencies

The spike may add `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `ai` on the spike branch only. List exact versions in the finding; adding them to main needs approval on <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" />.

## Acceptance

* All three paths call the same handler (show the call graph or a trace with one handler span per call).
* JSON Schema for MCP and AI SDK comes from the one Effect Schema, with no hand-written duplicate.
* Tests above pass; paste the command and output.

## Out of scope

Persistence, real auth provider, UI components, A2A, ACP, webhooks.

## Done signal

A comment on this issue with: result (works / works with caveats / blocked), the shape of the action-definition API proposed for the framework, code links on the spike branch, test output, and any Effect versus vendor-SDK friction. Then give Jonathan one action decision (accept this API shape, or one named alternative).

## Escalation

comments.body:
## S1 result: works, with caveats

One `Action.make` definition serves an `@effect/platform` HTTP route (the UI call), an MCP tool and an AI SDK tool. All three run the same decode, the same authorization check and the same handler, and every JSON Schema comes from the one Effect Schema. No second schema definition was needed, so the escalation did not trigger.

Spike branch (throwaway, never merged): https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/tree/spike/eve-s1-action-projection/spikes/eve-s1-action-projection (commit ad68c3c)

* Action API: [src/action.ts](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/spike/eve-s1-action-projection/spikes/eve-s1-action-projection/src/action.ts)
* Inventory: [src/inventory.ts](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/spike/eve-s1-action-projection/spikes/eve-s1-action-projection/src/inventory.ts)
* Actions and store: [src/events.ts](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/spike/eve-s1-action-projection/spikes/eve-s1-action-projection/src/events.ts)
* Projections: [http.ts](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/spike/eve-s1-action-projection/spikes/eve-s1-action-projection/src/projections/http.ts), [mcp.ts](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/spike/eve-s1-action-projection/spikes/eve-s1-action-projection/src/projections/mcp.ts), [ai-sdk.ts](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/spike/eve-s1-action-projection/spikes/eve-s1-action-projection/src/projections/ai-sdk.ts)
* Tests: [test/projection.spec.ts](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/spike/eve-s1-action-projection/spikes/eve-s1-action-projection/test/projection.spec.ts)

## The API shape I propose for the framework

```ts
export const create = Action.make("events.create", {
  description: "Create an event in the caller's tenant and return its id.",
  input: Schema.Struct({ title: Schema.NonEmptyTrimmedString, startsAt: Schema.DateTimeUtc }),
  output: Schema.Struct({ id: EventId }),
  error: Schema.Never,              // action errors; Forbidden and InvalidInput are always added
  scopes: ["events:write"],
  handler: (input) => Effect.gen(function* () {
    const caller = yield* Caller    // subject, tenantId, scopes
    const store = yield* EventStore
    // ...
  })
})
```

`Action.make` returns an erased `Action<R>` with `invoke(raw: unknown): Effect<unknown, ActionFailure, R | Caller>`. `invoke` checks scopes, then decodes input, runs the handler inside an `action.<name>` span and encodes the output. Projections only ever call `invoke` and `encodeError`. `inventory(actions)` gives name, description, scopes, and input, output and error JSON Schema from `JSONSchema.make`. Each projection gets the caller as a `Caller` service (HTTP from the request, MCP and AI SDK per authenticated session), so no path can skip authorization.

## Evidence

```
$ cd spikes/eve-s1-action-projection && npm ci --ignore-scripts && npx tsc --noEmit -p . && npx vitest run
tsc: 0 errors
 ✓ test/projection.spec.ts (6 tests) 392ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

The six tests cover these cases, and each one runs all three paths through the real vendor entry point (a web `Request` into the router, an MCP `Client` over `InMemoryTransport`, and `generateText` with `MockLanguageModelV4` emitting a tool call):

1. The same input gives an identical result on all three paths: `{ ok: true, output: { id: "evt_1" } }`, and the read-back is identical too.
2. With `events:write` missing, all three return the same error: `{ _tag: "Forbidden", action: "events.create", missingScopes: ["events:write"] }`.
3. A cross-tenant read is denied as `EventNotFound` on all three paths, so it looks the same as a missing id and does not reveal that the event exists.
4. Invalid input gets the same `InvalidInput` error on all three paths.
5. Call graph (OpenTelemetry in-memory exporter): one handler span under each projection span.
6. MCP `tools/list` and the AI SDK tool advertise exactly the inventory's JSON Schema.

```
action.events.create trace=1a63e1c9 parent=projection.http
projection.http      trace=1a63e1c9 parent=http.server POST
action.events.create trace=07c1bb04 parent=projection.mcp
action.events.create trace=34b388ff parent=projection.ai-sdk
```

Mutation check: I removed the scope check, and test 2 failed on all paths. I then restored it.

## Effect versus vendor SDK friction

1. **MCP high-level API is Zod-only.** `McpServer.registerTool` accepts only Zod schemas, which would force a second schema definition. The SDK's low-level `Server` (`tools/list` and `tools/call` handlers) takes plain JSON Schema and works unchanged. The SDK marks `Server` as for "advanced use cases", but it is not removed. We should own this adapter in the framework.
2. **AI SDK validation should be left off.** `jsonSchema(schema, { validate })` would make the AI SDK reject bad model input before the action runs, with its own error type. Leaving out `validate` makes the Effect decode the only validator, so a bad model call gets the same typed `InvalidInput`.
3. **The AI SDK reports a tool error only when `execute` throws.** The adapter throws one `ActionToolError` that carries the encoded typed error, behind an `effect-boundary` comment. MCP returns `isError` with the encoded error in `structuredContent`.
4. **Zod is a required peer of both SDKs.** Spike code never imports it, but it ends up in the install.
5. **JSON Schema shape.** `JSONSchema.make` puts `$ref` and `$defs` in schemas built from refinements such as `NonEmptyTrimmedString`, with sibling keywords next to `$ref`, and it declares draft-07. Both SDKs accepted it. Some model providers' strict tool modes reject `$ref`, so the framework should inline definitions per provider (follow-up, not a blocker).
6. **Trace continuity.** Each vendor callback starts a new trace, because the SDK sits between the projection and the action. The framework adapter should propagate the incoming trace context (MCP `_meta` traceparent, AI SDK telemetry) so one request is one trace.
7. **Erased generics.** Building the heterogeneous inventory needed one widening cast in `Action.make`, around the union of action errors and common errors. No `any` was used.
8. **Version mismatch in the repo.** `@effect/vitest` 0.27 needs vitest 3.2, but the root pins vitest ^2.1.9. The spike uses 3.2.4.

## Dependencies (spike branch only; need approval on EVE-13 before main)

`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.2, `ai` 7.0.159, `zod` 4.1.12 (required peer), `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base` 2.0.1 (test exporter), `vitest` 3.2.4. Already in the repo: `effect` 3.19.19, `@effect/platform` 0.94.5, `@effect/opentelemetry` 0.61.0, `@effect/vitest` 0.27.0.

## Caveats on how the spike was done

* The spike lives in its own folder with an npm lockfile, outside the pnpm workspace and Nx, so main's lockfile is untouched. The repo's `check` gate was not run against it.
* The spike commit is authored by the session's configured AI identity and has no sign-off. I made it before I saw the Eventiva delivery exception (058251e), which sets the standing author and sign-off. Re-authoring it would need a force-push, and that was blocked in this session. Because the branch never merges, I left the commit as it is.
* HTTP identity comes from `x-eventiva-*` headers, which stand in for a real auth provider (out of scope).
* I read the vendor SDK APIs from their installed type definitions, not from Context7.

## Decision for Jonathan

**Recommend: approve this action API shape** (`Action.make` with schemas, scopes and handler, `invoke` as the only entry point, `Caller` as a required service, inventory from `JSONSchema.make`) and approve adding `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `ai` to main, with the MCP adapter built on the SDK's low-level `Server`.

The named alternative is to build actions on `@effect/rpc` `Rpc.make` and `RpcGroup`. That would reuse the RPC stack the repo already has, but scopes, descriptions and the inventory would have to live in annotations, and every projection would still need the same adapters.

*Posted by Claude (AI agent) for Jonathan.*
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
## Follow-up: running the projections without Zod

Jonathan asked for no Zod.

**Both vendor SDKs load Zod at runtime, so neither can be made Zod-free.** The MCP TypeScript SDK imports `zod/v4` in `dist/esm/types.js`, which defines its protocol messages. The AI SDK imports `zod/v4` in `ai`, `@ai-sdk/provider-utils` and `@ai-sdk/gateway`. Making Zod a peer we never import does not stop it being installed.

**Zod-free route, proven on the spike branch (commit 4d01d75):** use Effect AI (`@effect/ai` 0.33.2, the last line for effect 3.19) for both agent paths.

* MCP: [src/projections/mcp-effect.ts](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/spike/eve-s1-action-projection/spikes/eve-s1-action-projection/src/projections/mcp-effect.ts). `McpServer.addTool` takes the inventory's JSON Schema unchanged and an Effect handler, so there is no Promise boundary at all. It is tested over real HTTP JSON-RPC, and also against the official MCP client for interop (initialize, list, call all work).
* Model tool calling: [src/projections/effect-ai.ts](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/spike/eve-s1-action-projection/spikes/eve-s1-action-projection/src/projections/effect-ai.ts). An Effect AI `Toolkit` is built from each action's input fields, and the model sees the same JSON Schema as the inventory. Errors go back to the model as values (`failureMode: "return"`).
* An install of `effect`, `@effect/ai`, `@effect/platform`, `@effect/rpc` and `@effect/experimental` contains no Zod (`npm ls zod` is empty).

```
$ npx tsc --noEmit -p . && npx vitest run
 ✓ test/effect-ai.spec.ts (2 tests)
 ✓ test/mcp-effect.spec.ts (2 tests)
 ✓ test/projection.spec.ts (6 tests)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

**What this costs.**

1. It drops the AI SDK, which the house standard (`references/ai.md`, "AI SDK alongside Effect AI") requires. For Eventiva this needs Jonathan's explicit override of that rule.
2. Without the AI SDK we lose its UI hooks (`useChat`), so the chat UI is built on Effect or Rambo-UI.
3. We get fewer model providers. Effect AI on v3 ships OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock and OpenRouter; the AI SDK ships many more.
4. The newest `@effect/ai` (0.37) and its providers need effect 3.22, and the repo pins 3.19.19, so an effect bump is a follow-up.

**Smaller findings.**

* Effect's JSON-RPC serializer answers a single request with a one-element batch. The official client accepted it.
* The `McpSchema.Tool` in `@effect/ai` 0.33 has no `outputSchema` field.
* Toolkit typing widens when tools are built from a runtime list, which needs two casts in the adapter and none in action code.

*Posted by Claude (AI agent) for Jonathan.*

issues.description:
## Goal

Produce the parity list for Eventiva's Effect-native agent framework: every upstream Agent-Native module and every connection method, with a verdict and evidence.

## Context

* Spec: <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> framework direction, Connections and execution methods, Screen awareness.
* First pass already exists in the planning doc section 7 ([https://claude.ai/artifact/QYamSdBsxTZSUKeDAUqMRb](<https://claude.ai/artifact/QYamSdBsxTZSUKeDAUqMRb>)); it was built from names and line counts only.
* Upstream: [https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native](<https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native>), pin to the newest release tag on the day you start and record it (first pass used commit a0356c6, `@agent-native/core` 0.222.2). MIT.

## Work

1. Clone upstream at the pinned tag. For each directory in `packages/core/src` and each package in `packages/`, read its entry points and exports, and record: purpose (one line), non-test lines, upstream dependencies, and a verdict: Build in Effect, Wrap, Later, or Not needed, with a one-line reason tied to an <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> decision.
2. Mark every module that takes part in screen awareness or UI-to-agent registration (application state, browser context, action UI, navigation, WebMCP). These are Build by default.
3. Conformance matrix for ACP, HTTP API, MCP, A2A, webhooks, CLI, WebMCP, schedules and events, streaming, cancellation and resumption. For each: inbound supported (yes/no + file), outbound supported (yes/no + file), the upstream test that proves it, and what Eventiva must add. ACP inbound and outbound are both required.
4. Order phase-1 rows into a dependency sequence.

## Acceptance

* Every upstream module and package appears exactly once (script the listing and include the count).
* Every Build row names the <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> requirement it satisfies.
* Every conformance cell cites a file path or says "not found" with the search used.

## Out of scope

Writing framework code. Upstream app templates.

## Done signal

Publish the map as a Linear document attached to this issue, replace section 7 of the planning doc with a link to it, and comment a short summary plus one action decision for Jonathan: approve the phase-1 list as-is, or the specific rows you would change.

## Escalation

If a required interface has no upstream implementation and no viable standard SDK, record it as a gap on <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> rather than inventing scope.

issues.title: S3: Prove runtime loading and switching of a remote module on Expo web and Android
issues.description:
## Goal

Find out whether Expo, Re.Pack Module Federation v2 (native) and Module Federation v2 (web) can load, switch and dispose a remote UI module at runtime, and what that costs (dev builds, Expo SDK version, rebuild triggers).

## Context

* Spec: <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> sections React Native and Expo, Client-side dynamic module loading, Hot reloading.
* House UI reference: `.agents/skills/coding-preferences/references/ui.md` (self-hosted MF 2.0 on web, Re.Pack MF v2 on native, no Zephyr).
* Repo at 322ab45 declares `expo ~54.0.0` with `react-native 0.84.1`, and `@module-federation/enhanced ^0.21.2`. Expo 54 is documented for React Native 0.81, so check that pair first.
* Upstream Agent-Native's mobile app targets Expo SDK 57 (reference only).

## Work

1. Throwaway spike branch `spike/eve-s3-federation`, never merged. Pick the newest Expo SDK that Re.Pack's current release supports; record both versions and the source for that claim.
2. Host app plus one remote `Greeting` component, published as v1 and v2, on web (MF 2.0) and Android (Re.Pack).
3. In the running app, switch v1 to v2 without rebuilding the host; show state either handed over or deliberately remounted; dispose v1 (no listeners left); reject an incompatible v3 (wrong contract version) and fall back to the bundled copy; work offline from the cached or bundled copy.
4. Record which changes need a host rebuild (native module, shared dependency major) and whether a development build is required instead of Expo Go.
5. iOS: run it if a Mac is available; otherwise list the iOS check as outstanding.

## Acceptance

Commands and output for each target, a short screen recording or screenshots for the switch, and a support matrix (target by: state-preserving refresh, remote switch without rebuild, needs restart, needs native rebuild, unsupported).

## Out of scope

Real Eventiva screens, Rambo-UI components, agent registration of modules.

## Done signal

Comment on this issue with the matrix, versions and one action decision for Jonathan: adopt this stack and versions, or the named fallback (for example web-only federation first).

## Escalation

If Re.Pack cannot run inside Expo at all, stop and report the exact error and the nearest workable alternative.

## Initial module class and production gate (2026-11-15)

Canonical spec [https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c>). Owner's initial third-party UI lane is DECLARATIVE DATA ONLY over installed approved Rambo-UI/Expo components (<issue id="71b3a3b5-09a5-45f1-9c59-512c9368036e" label="EVE-259" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-259/implement-the-initial-declarative-ui-module-registry-over-approved" />). It does not require arbitrary executable RN download/federation. Preserve this spike's distinct trusted executable loading/OTA/shared-runtime/native/rebuild support matrix; web evidence is not native execution proof, native bundling is not device runtime proof. Existing approved production dependency matrix remains unchanged. Manifest trust/isolation assertions are not sandboxing; unsupported executable isolation fails closed. No new framework version/package/digest, provisioning or main push is authorized by this clarification. Record native/OTA/desktop gaps explicitly; do not hold portable declarative schema/registry design hostage to executable support. AI-authored planning addition.

comments.body:
## S3 spike result (agent run, 2026-10-31)

**Short answer:** runtime switching works on web today. On Android the Re.Pack bundles build on Expo SDK 56, but nothing has run on a device yet. Expo Go is out; a development build is required.

### Versions and sources

| Piece | Version tested | Source for the claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Re.Pack | 5.4.2 (latest, published 2026-10-22) | npm registry |
| Expo SDK | 56.0.24, which bundles RN 0.85.3 and React 19.2.3 | `expo/bundledNativeModules.json` |
| Module Federation | web: @module-federation/enhanced 2.9.2 on Rspack 2.3.0, and 0.22.0 on Rspack 1.7.12. Android: both pairs bundle | spike runs |

* **Why SDK 56:** it is the newest SDK that anyone upstream has run with Re.Pack. callstack/repack PR #1425 ("feat(expo): add first-class Re.Pack integration") targets SDK 56 with prebuild/CNG. That PR is still under review. The Re.Pack docs (re-pack.dev/docs/guides/expo-modules) cover only Expo Modules in a prebuild app and name no SDK version. Issue #1396 says Expo Go is not supported. SDK 57 (RN 0.86.3) and SDK 58 (RN 0.88.1) have no upstream evidence.
* **Repo mismatch:** `expo ~54.0.0` paired with `react-native 0.84.1` is invalid, because SDK 54 bundles RN 0.81.5. Fix this whichever way we decide.

### Support matrix

| Target | State-preserving refresh | Remote switch without host rebuild | Needs restart | Needs native rebuild | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Web, MF 2.0 | Yes. Host-held state handed to v2 (count 2 carried over), or deliberately remounted (count 0) | Yes. v2 and v3 were built while the host was running | No | No | **Proven** in headless Chromium |
| Android, Re.Pack MF v2 | Same React pattern; not run | Bundles built for host, v1, v2 and v3 (0 errors) | Not measured | Yes, for any native module or for a major bump of a shared react/react-native | **Bundles only**, not run on a device |
| iOS | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | **Outstanding** (no Mac) |
| Expo Go | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | **Unsupported**; use a dev build |

### What was proven on web

From `web/demo-output.txt`:

* **Switch:** v1 to v2 to v1 using `registerRemotes([{name, entry}], {force: true})` and `loadRemote`, with no host rebuild.
* **Dispose:** the listener count stayed at 1 across switches, so v1's listener was removed when v2 mounted. There were no page errors.
* **Contract check:** v3 declares contract 2.0.0 and was rejected. The host fell back to its bundled copy. A missing v9 also fell back.
* **Offline:** after going offline and reloading, the host and v2 loaded from the service-worker cache. A version that was never fetched falls back to the bundled copy.

### What needs a host rebuild

* A remote that adds a native module. Remotes cannot ship native code, which PR #1425 also confirms.
* A major-version change to a shared singleton (react, react-native).
* A change to the host's contract major.

A JS-only change to a remote needs no host rebuild.

### Android bundling workarounds

Each of these is needed on Re.Pack 5.4.2 with RN 0.85:

* Pin @babel/core 7. Babel 8 breaks `@react-native/babel-plugin-codegen`.
* Add @swc/helpers.
* Run react-native sources through `@react-native/babel-preset`. RN 0.85 uses Flow `component` syntax that Re.Pack's SWC/flow-remove-types path cannot parse.
* Turn off Re.Pack's codegen rule so codegen does not run twice.
* Set `getResolveOptions({ enablePackageExports: true })` so `@module-federation/enhanced/runtime` resolves.

### Not done, and why

* **Android device run:** the sandbox has no KVM and cannot reach dl.google.com, so there was no emulator, SDK or Gradle.
* **iOS:** no Mac was available.
* **Throwaway branch:** not pushed. The configured git identity is an AI, and the house rules need the accountable human as author. The spike sources, logs, screenshots and recording are kept in the project files under `eve-16-spike/`.

### New dependencies to approve (AI-12)

**Bumps:**

* expo ~54.0.0 to 56.0.24
* react-native 0.84.1 to 0.85.3
* react and react-dom pinned to 19.2.3
* @module-federation/enhanced ^0.21.2 to 2.9.2
* @rspack/core and @rspack/cli 1.6.8 to 2.3.0

**New:**

* @callstack/repack 5.4.2
* @callstack/repack-plugin-expo-modules 5.4.2
* @react-native-community/cli 20.2.0
* @react-native/babel-preset 0.85.3
* @babel/core 7.29.x
* babel-loader 9 (already a Re.Pack dependency)
* react-native-web 0.21.2

### Action decision for Jonathan

**Adopt Re.Pack 5.4.2 + Expo SDK 56 (RN 0.85.3) + Rspack 2.3 + MF 2.9.2 on a dev build, and ship web federation first.** Native federation stays behind a flag until one Android device run passes. The fallback is web-only federation, with native modules compiled into the app binary until Re.Pack's Expo integration (#1425) lands.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

issues.title: S4: Choose the offline sync engine for record edits and live text and canvas editing
issues.description:
## Goal

Pick the sync machinery that gives offline-first record and field editing plus live text and canvas co-editing together, on SQLite on the device and Postgres/Neon on the server, for human and agent edits alike.

## Context

* Spec: <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> Offline-first collaborative foundation (both editing models, designed and validated together from the start).
* Database pair: Postgres/Neon via Drizzle, SQLite local. House data reference: `.agents/skills/coding-preferences/references/data.md`.
* Upstream Agent-Native uses Yjs for collaboration (`packages/core/src/collab/`) and has no SQLite adapter.
* Convex was considered by Jonathan but not evaluated; include it.

## Work

1. Paper evaluation from current docs and source. Candidates at minimum: PowerSync, ElectricSQL, Zero (Rocicorp), Triplit, Replicache, Convex, LiveStore, Jazz, and Yjs or Automerge for documents. Score each against: SQLite on iOS, Android and web; Postgres/Neon as source of truth; authorization at sync time and revocation on reconnect; durable offline queue surviving restart; conflict rules for records; document CRDT support or clean pairing with Yjs; schema evolution for old clients; self-hostable and licence; Effect integration effort; Expo support.
2. Shortlist two. Build a throwaway prototype (`spike/eve-s4-sync`, never merged) with the top choice: two clients edit the same record field and the same text document, one offline, then reconnect; a third client loses permission while offline and its writes are rejected at sync.
3. Write the proposed conflict policy per data kind (record fields, lists, documents, canvas objects).

## Acceptance

A scored table with sources, the prototype's command output, and convergence shown for both models.

## Out of scope

Production schema, real Eventiva entities.

## Done signal

Comment with the table, prototype results and one action decision: adopt engine X (plus Yjs if paired), or the runner-up with the reason.

## Escalation

Any candidate that requires a paid hosted service with no self-host path is flagged, not silently chosen. New dependencies go to <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> for approval.

comments.body:
## S4 findings: offline sync engine

**Proposed decision:** adopt **PowerSync** (self-hosted Open Edition, Postgres bucket storage) for records and fields, paired with **Yjs** for text and canvas documents. Yjs updates travel as rows through the same PowerSync pipe. Every write goes through an Eventiva Effect action on the server, which handles permission checks, per-field merges and audit. Runner-up: **Electric with TanStack DB**, if the FSL licence turns out to be unacceptable. New dependencies needing approval under EVE-13: `@powersync/node`, `@powersync/web`, `@powersync/react-native` (all Apache-2.0), the `journeyapps/powersync-service` image (FSL-1.1-ALv2) and `yjs` (MIT).

Tags: Observed = run in the spike; Docs = from current vendor docs; Inferred = my reading, not verified.

### Scored table

Scores are 0 to 2 per criterion. **Gate** marks a hard requirement from EVE-13 that a candidate fails outright.

| Criterion | PowerSync + Yjs | Electric + TanStack DB + Yjs | Zero | Convex | LiveStore | Jazz | Triplit | Replicache |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SQLite on iOS, Android, web | 2 (Docs: RN/Expo, wa-sqlite web, Node) | 1 (client store is TanStack DB collections; SQLite persistence is not Electric's) | 1 (KV store over expo-sqlite / IndexedDB, not queryable SQL) | 0 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Postgres/Neon is source of truth | 2 (Observed) | 2 | 2 | **Gate** (own store; Postgres only as its storage) | **Gate** (event log is the truth) | **Gate** (own SQLite sync server) | **Gate** | 1 (bring your own backend) |
| Auth at sync, revocation on reconnect | 2 (Observed) | 1 (auth proxy plus shape `where`; revocation needs a re-shape) | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Durable offline queue survives restart | 2 (Observed: `ps_crud` survived process exit) | 1 (TanStack DB offline transactions, separate) | **Gate** (Docs: "Zero does not support offline writes") | **Gate** | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Record conflict rules under our control | 2 (Observed: our action decides, PATCH carries only changed columns) | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| Document CRDT or clean Yjs pairing | 2 (Observed text and canvas; vendor demo exists) | 2 (y-electric provider) | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 (native CRDT) | 1 | 1 |
| Schema evolution for old clients | 1 (Inferred: client schema is views over JSON rows, so additive changes are safe; renames need dual-write) | 1 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Self-host and licence | 1 (service FSL-1.1-ALv2, which becomes Apache after 2 years and bars a competing hosted sync product; SDKs Apache-2.0) | 2 (Apache-2.0) | 2 (Apache-2.0) | 1 (FSL) | 2 | 2 (MIT) | 0 (acquired by Supabase 2025-10-08, future unclear) | 0 (maintenance mode, superseded by Zero) |
| Effect integration effort | 2 (connector is 2 methods; wrap with `Effect.tryPromise`) | 1 | 1 | 0 (its own server runtime) | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Expo support | 2 (dev build; not Expo Go) | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| **Total / gates** | **18, no gate failed** | **14, no gate failed** | 17, **fails offline writes** | fails 2 gates | fails PG gate | fails PG gate | fails PG gate | deprecated |

Yjs is preferred over Automerge (both MIT) because upstream Agent-Native already uses Yjs (`packages/core/src/collab/`), so the ported collab module stays close to upstream.

No candidate requires a paid hosted service: Convex, PowerSync and Jazz all have self-host paths.

### Prototype

Code and logs: project files `eve-s4-sync/`. The spike used PowerSync service 1.27.2 in Docker, Postgres 16 with logical replication, three `@powersync/node` 1.2.0 clients (alice, bob, carol), each on its own SQLite file, and Yjs 13.6.33. The "server action" checks project membership per operation and applies field-level updates.

`node spike.mjs` (exit 0):

```
--- Scenario 1: bob goes offline; alice and bob edit the same field and the same text
[server] alice PATCH records/r1 -> applied
server while bob offline: {"title":"Title by alice (online)","status":"open"}
bob local while offline: {"title":"Title by bob (offline)","status":"confirmed"} | text: "[Bob offline] Run sheet: doors 19:00."
--- Scenario 2: carol goes offline, loses membership, keeps editing
[admin] removed carol from project p1 while she is offline
--- Reconnect bob and carol
[server] bob PATCH records/r1 -> applied
[server] carol PATCH records/r1 -> REJECTED (forbidden)
[server] carol PUT doc_updates/... -> REJECTED (forbidden)
RESULT server record: {"title":"Title by bob (offline)","status":"confirmed","updated_by":"bob"}
RESULT alice record : {"title":"Title by bob (offline)","status":"confirmed","updated_by":"bob"}
RESULT bob record   : {"title":"Title by bob (offline)","status":"confirmed","updated_by":"bob"}
RESULT carol record : null (rows remaining for carol: 0 )
RESULT alice text   : "[Bob offline] Run sheet: doors 19:00. Alice: add pyro check."
RESULT bob text     : "[Bob offline] Run sheet: doors 19:00. Alice: add pyro check."
RESULT alice canvas : {"truss-1":{"x":120,"y":0,"colour":"red"}}
RESULT bob canvas   : {"truss-1":{"x":120,"y":0,"colour":"red"}}
CHECKS {"fieldsConverged":true,"textConverged":true,"bothTextEditsKept":true,"canvasConverged":true,"revokedWritesRejected":true,"revokedDataRemovedFromDevice":true}
```

`node restart.mjs edit` then `node restart.mjs resume` (exit 0). Bob edits `status` offline and the process exits; alice changes `title`; a fresh bob process reconnects:

```
bob queued offline, ps_crud rows: 1 [{"op":"PATCH","id":"r1","type":"records","data":{"status":"on-hold"}}]
bob pending after restart: true ps_crud rows: 1
RESULT server: {"title":"Title by alice while bob was closed","status":"on-hold","updated_by":"bob"}
CHECKS {"queueSurvivedRestart":true,"bothFieldEditsKept":true}
```

Both models converged. The same field resolves to the last write to arrive; different fields both survive; text and canvas merge with no loss. Writes by a revoked user are rejected at sync and the data disappears from their device. A server-side write (standing in for an agent action) reached every client through replication.

### Gotchas observed

1. Two PowerSync databases in one process with the same `dbFilename` deadlock on `connect()`. Each needs a unique filename.
2. The connector must `complete()` a transaction even when the server rejects it, otherwise it retries forever. Rejected operations must be logged and shown to the user, never dropped silently.
3. Yjs emits one update per transaction (the seed alone produced 5 rows). Production needs client-side debouncing and server-side compaction into snapshot rows.
4. When revocation removes rows, the app must also drop its in-memory `Y.Doc`. Carol's local SQLite was cleaned, but her in-memory doc still held text.
5. The message "Could not apply checkpoint due to local data" is normal while uploads are pending.

### Proposed conflict policy per data kind

| Data kind | Policy |
|---|---|
| Record fields (default) | Per-field merge decided by the server action: PATCH carries only changed fields, and the last write to arrive wins. |
| Guarded fields (status transitions, money, assignments, dispatch state) | The action checks a precondition (expected version or state-machine transition). A conflict is rejected and shown to the user to resolve; never silent last-write-wins. |
| Quantities (stock, capacity, tickets) | Append-only movement rows (deltas), never overwrites. Totals are derived on the server. |
| Lists and ordering | Membership as rows with client-generated ids; order by fractional index per item; delete wins over a concurrent edit. |
| Documents (rich text) | Yjs `Y.Text` / `Y.XmlFragment`; updates are append-only rows, compacted on the server. Always merges. |
| Canvas objects | Yjs `Y.Map` per object, merged per property; z-order by fractional index; delete wins. |
| Live ops (dispatch, show control, hardware) | Online-only actions. An offline client may queue a *request* with a TTL, re-validated on reconnect, never auto-applied after the window closes. |

### Not done in this spike

- No React Native, Expo or web client was run (Node client only). Mobile and web support is from docs.
- Neon itself was not used (local Postgres 16). Neon logical replication is documented by both vendors but untested here.
- The spike is plain JS. Production wraps the connector and actions in Effect.
- The spike was not pushed to `spike/eve-s4-sync`, because this session's git identity is an AI tool and AI-03 forbids committing as Jonathan without his setup. The code is in project files instead.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body: Correction to the last bullet: Eventiva's AGENTS.md exception (058251e) now covers agent sign-off. This session's tooling still blocked committing as Jonathan, so the spike was not pushed to any branch. The code and logs remain in project files under `eve-s4-sync/`.

comments.body:
## S4 round two: web and Expo clients

Jonathan asked for web and Expo clients to be tested before adopting PowerSync.

**Result:** the web SDK and the Expo app's web target both pass every check in a real browser. The native Android build could not be compiled in this environment, because its network policy blocks Google's Android Maven host (`dl.google.com`). Nothing native was run.

### What ran

The setup is the same as in the first round: PowerSync service 1.27.2 (self-hosted), Postgres 16, and a backend acting as the Eventiva action server, which checks membership on every write. There were three Chromium 153 browser profiles (alice, bob and carol), each a full browser with its own storage.

Offline means the browser's network was cut; the SDK's disconnect was never called. Restart means bob's browser was closed completely and then cold-started with no network at all. The app shell, workers and wasm loaded from a service worker cache.

| Client | Stack | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Web | Vite app, `@powersync/web` 2.5.0 (wa-sqlite), Yjs 13.6 | 7 of 7 checks pass |
| Expo web | Expo SDK 58, React Native 0.88, react-native-web, `@powersync/web` 2.5.0 on web | 7 of 7 checks pass |
| Expo native (Android) | Same Expo app, `@powersync/react-native` 2.3.3 with op-sqlite 18.2.5 | **Not built**: Gradle cannot fetch the Android Gradle Plugin (`com.android.tools.build:gradle:9.2.1`) because `dl.google.com` returns 403 from the sandbox proxy |

The Expo app uses one code path on every platform. Only `src/db.native.js` (op-sqlite) and `src/db.web.js` (wa-sqlite with workers from `public/@powersync`) differ.

Output of `BASE=http://127.0.0.1:3001 node browser-test.mjs` against the Expo web export, with network-error console lines removed:

```
browser 153.0.8010.12 | UA Chrome/153.0.8010.12
initial record in all 3 browsers: {"title":"Initial title","status":"open","updated_by":"seed"}
--- bob and carol lose network (browser offline, no SDK disconnect call)
bob offline: pending ops 3 | local {"title":"Title by bob (offline)","status":"confirmed","updated_by":"seed"}
--- admin removes carol from the project while she is offline
--- bob closes the browser entirely while still offline, then relaunches with no network
bob after browser restart: pending ops 3 -> 3 | local {"title":"Title by bob (offline)","status":"confirmed","updated_by":"seed"} | text "[Bob offline] Run sheet: doors 19:00."
--- network restored for bob and carol
RESULT server record : {"title":"Title by bob (offline)","status":"confirmed","updated_by":"bob"}
RESULT alice record  : {"title":"Title by bob (offline)","status":"confirmed","updated_by":"bob"}
RESULT bob record    : {"title":"Title by bob (offline)","status":"confirmed","updated_by":"bob"}
RESULT carol record  : null | carol rejected: ["forbidden","forbidden"]
RESULT alice text    : "[Bob offline] Run sheet: doors 19:00. Alice: add pyro check."
RESULT bob text      : "[Bob offline] Run sheet: doors 19:00. Alice: add pyro check."
RESULT alice canvas  : {"truss-1":{"x":120,"colour":"red"}}
RESULT bob canvas    : {"truss-1":{"x":120,"colour":"red"}}
CHECKS {"fieldsConverged":true,"textConverged":true,"canvasConverged":true,"queueSurvivedBrowserRestart":true,"coldStartedFullyOffline":true,"revokedWritesRejected":true,"revokedDataRemovedFromBrowser":true}
```

The plain web client (`web-run-chromium.log`) produced the same CHECKS line.

### New findings

1. A fully offline cold start on web needs an app-shell service worker. Without one, `init()` hangs because the SQLite worker and wasm cannot be fetched. This is the app's job, not PowerSync's; the spike's service worker is in `web/server.mjs`.
2. On Expo web, Metro cannot bundle the PowerSync workers. Run `npx @powersync/web copy-assets` and point `database.worker` and `sync.worker` at `/@powersync/worker.js`. Vendor docs call React Native web support beta.
3. `@powersync/react-native` 2.x bundles the op-sqlite adapter directly and needs `@op-engineering/op-sqlite` 17 or 18. The old `@powersync/op-sqlite` package (peer op-sqlite 13 to 15) conflicts with it, so do not install both.
4. Expo prebuild for SDK 58 expects NDK 27.1. The build image had 28.2, which works once `android.ndkVersion` is set.

### Still unproven

- Native iOS and Android at runtime. This sandbox has no KVM (no emulator) and no access to Google's Android Maven, so the APK could not even be compiled.
- Safari and WebKit: only Chromium is installed here, and Safari's storage rules are the main web risk.
- Neon.

The spike code is in project files: `eve-s4-sync/web`, `eve-s4-sync/expo`, and `eve-s4-sync/local-stack`, a `docker compose` stack for testing the native app on an emulator.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body: Correction to finding 4: setting `android.ndkVersion=28.2.13676358` was not verified, because the build stopped earlier, at dependency resolution. Treat it as untested.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
## S4 round 3: Expo Android release APK builds

Result: `./gradlew assembleRelease` succeeded for the Expo spike app (PowerSync React Native + op-sqlite + Yjs). This proves the native build only. There is no KVM in the cloud environment, so the APK has not been run on an emulator or a device.

**APK:** `eve-s4-sync/expo/eve-s4-spike-release.apk`, 42,422,442 bytes (40.5 MiB), sha256 `cc94414a2bf9c452417f642ac311f32e207a62317a9a305dc1cdebbac54d7779`. It is signed with the debug key (the Expo template default). ABIs are arm64-v8a and x86_64. The JS bundle is 1.99 MB, with 759 modules.

`aapt2 dump badging`:
```
package: name='dev.eventiva.s4spike' versionCode='1' versionName='1.0.0' compileSdkVersion='37'
minSdkVersion:'24'
targetSdkVersion:'36'
uses-permission: name='android.permission.INTERNET'
```
The native libraries include `libpowersync.so` (417 KB arm64), `libop-sqlite.so` (1.6 MB arm64) and `libhermesvm.so`.

**Toolchain:** Expo SDK 58.0.22, React Native 0.88.1, Gradle 9.4.1, NDK 28.2.13676358, build-tools 37.0.0 and JDK 17. The build ran in the `mirror.gcr.io/reactnativecommunity/react-native-android:latest` image.

**Commands** (the full script is in `eve-s4-sync/expo/android-build/build.sh`):
```
npm install                                   # needed react-dom pinned to 19.3.0 to match react 19.3.0
npx @powersync/web copy-assets
EXPO_OFFLINE=1 CI=1 npx expo prebuild --platform android --no-install
# gradle.properties: reactNativeArchitectures=arm64-v8a,x86_64 and android.ndkVersion=28.2.13676358
# AndroidManifest: android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"
docker run --rm --network host ... -w /app/android mirror.gcr.io/reactnativecommunity/react-native-android:latest \
  ./gradlew --no-daemon --init-script /init-mirror.gradle assembleRelease
```

**Tail of the build log:**
```
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 9m 13s
387 actionable tasks: 302 executed, 85 up-to-date
real	9m14.176s
```

**Problems found, and what fixed them:**
1. Attempt 1 failed because Maven Central returned 429. The Gradle Plugin Portal redirects to Maven Central, so rewriting the `mavenCentral()` URL was not enough. The init script `android-build/init-mirror.gradle` puts `maven-central.storage-download.googleapis.com` first in pluginManagement and in every project's repositories, and it also rewrites `repo.maven.apache.org`. Google Maven (dl.google.com) now works.
2. Attempt 2 failed in `:app:createBundleReleaseJsAndAssets`. Metro could not resolve `isomorphic-webcrypto/src/react-native`, which **lib0 (a Yjs dependency) imports on React Native** but does not declare. This is a real gotcha for production: Yjs on React Native needs a webcrypto provider. For the spike, `metro.config.js` maps that import to `src/webcrypto-shim.js`. The shim uses `globalThis.crypto` when it exists and otherwise falls back to Math.random, which is acceptable for the spike only. **Proposed for production:** map the import to a module backed by `expo-crypto` (an Expo first-party package) so Yjs client ids come from a secure random source. That is a new dependency and needs approval when the real client is built.

**Not tested:** the Android runtime (no emulator), and sync against the local stack from a device. The next step is to install the APK on a real device on the same network as `local-stack`. The `usesCleartextTraffic` setting is there so the app can reach the plain-HTTP dev backend.

Logs for all three attempts are in `eve-s4-sync/expo/android-build/`. This is a throwaway spike and is not committed to the repository.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
## Native device test: PowerSync + Yjs on a real Android phone (2026-11-09)
Run on Jonathan's home network. The local stack (Postgres 16, PowerSync service 1.27.2 and the Node spike backend, via docker compose) ran on a MacBook. The release APK (sha256 cc94414a…d7779, matching the build) ran on an Android phone (powersync-react-native, RN 0.88, Android 37) as bob, and the Expo web build ran in Chrome 157 on the laptop as alice.
Result: 6 of 6 runbook checks pass on native, which closes the gap left by the web-only cloud run.
- Live sync: pass. Title edits went both ways within seconds, and the server applied 2 edits from each device.
- Offline edits queue: pass. In airplane mode the phone showed its own title, text and shape edits immediately, with pending 4.
- Concurrent edits: pass. The laptop made its own edits while the phone was offline.
- Queue survives restart: pass. After force-closing and reopening the app, still offline, the edits and pending count were still there (reported by Jonathan).
- Convergence: pass. On reconnect pending dropped to 0. Both devices showed the same title (bob's, the last to reach the server, matching Postgres), both text additions "[bob 21:41:34] [alice 21:41:58]", and the same shape x of 163.
- Revocation: pass. Bob was removed while offline with a queued title edit. On reconnect the server logged 3 REJECTED (forbidden), the phone showed rejected 3 and record null, and the server title was unchanged. Text and canvas stayed on screen until the app restarted; after restarting online they were empty, so the local copy was wiped.
Notes for the decision:
- Concurrent canvas moves converged to alice's x even though bob's update reached the server later. That is CRDT merge order, not last-writer-wins, and should be stated in the canvas conflict rules.
- After revocation, in-memory Yjs docs stay visible until they are reloaded. The production client should tear down open docs when a bucket is removed.
- The 42 MB APK had to be split into 8 MiB parts to pass the project-file tool's 16 MB response limit.
- iOS is still untested; that needs a Mac with Xcode.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
## Decision (2026-11-09): adopt PowerSync with Yjs

Jonathan approved the proposal on 2026-11-09. Eventiva's offline sync engine is:

* **PowerSync**, self-hosted Open Edition with Postgres bucket storage, for records and fields. The service is FSL-1.1-ALv2; the client SDKs are Apache-2.0.
* **Yjs** for text and canvas documents. Yjs updates travel as rows through the same PowerSync pipe.
* Every write goes through an Eventiva Effect action on the server, which does the permission check, the per-field merge and the audit record.

Runner-up, kept only as a fallback if the FSL licence becomes unacceptable: Electric with TanStack DB.

**Evidence:** Node clients (first findings comment), web and Expo web 7 of 7 (round two), and a real Android phone 6 of 6 against the local stack (2026-11-09 comment).

**Rules added to the spec** (EVE-13 offline section and EVE-51):

1. Concurrent canvas edits resolve by Yjs CRDT merge order, not last-writer-wins. The Android test showed two concurrent moves of the same shape converge to the same value on every device, but not necessarily to the edit that reached the server last. Any screen or doc that describes canvas conflicts must say this.
2. When the client loses a sync bucket (access removed), it tears down every open Yjs document from that bucket at once: destroy the in-memory `Y.Doc`, close its editors and drop presence. Waiting for a reload is not enough, because the Android test showed revoked text and canvas staying on screen until restart.

**Still open:** native iOS has not run (needs a Mac with Xcode). Tracked as its own follow-up issue, which does not block the decision. Safari/WebKit and Neon logical replication are also untested and are part of that follow-up's scope note. The `expo-crypto` webcrypto provider for Yjs on React Native still needs dependency approval when EVE-51 is built.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
## Approved foundation policy reference

Jonathan approved A2–A4 and S2–S4 on 2026-11-15. Approval cannot be self-issued or weakened; guarded offline/scheduled work uses explicit state/version/idempotency/deadline and online revalidation; protected audit fails closed; scarce resources use ledgers/reservations/CAS; device records use typed raw tables/migrations; migrations are forward-only expand/contract; canonical IDs/time/decimals follow S4. See [EVE-40](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema), [EVE-42](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state) and the [decision sheet](https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-architecture-decisions-3169b540-652d-4795-ae9c-7ad78a534f17). No dependencies or implementation are approved by this cross-reference.

comments.body:
## BINDING Neon CDC / PowerSync cost and compatibility gate — 2026-11-15

Fresh official Neon guidance confirms logical replication is enabled per project, permanently changes `wal_level` to `logical`, cannot be reverted, and restarts every compute. A connected subscriber prevents scale-to-zero and can create continuous compute cost. Inactive slots are removed after about 40 hours without acknowledged `flush_lsn`; branch restore removes slots. Neon supports at most 10 WAL senders and 10 replication slots by default.

For Eventiva/PowerSync, CDC must use a direct Neon endpoint without the `-pooler` suffix and a correctly privileged dedicated replication role; persistent replication is incompatible with PgBouncer pooling. Runtime Effect SQL queries must test pooled and direct paths separately. Do not enable replication or run tests on the existing historical PG16 Frankfurt project.

Plan the first London PG17 synthetic test project with replication disabled. Any later PowerSync/CDC integration trial requires separate owner approval, synthetic-only data, direct endpoint, measured active time, slot lag/retention and cost evidence before broad enablement. This is especially material for the project-per-tenant production model. A Neon branch remains a test-isolation mechanism, not equivalent production tenant isolation.

Official sources refreshed 2026-11-15:
- https://neon.com/docs/guides/logical-replication-guide (updated 2026-10-21)
- https://neon.com/docs/guides/logical-replication-neon (updated 2026-10-09)

Do not silently discard the approved PowerSync design if economics or scaling fail. Return an evidence-backed architecture proposal for owner decision.

issues.title: S5: Verify sharding across two independent runners with drain and runner-loss recovery
issues.description:
## Goal

Establish what the existing Effect Cluster setup already proves about sharding, and close the gap to the <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> bar: two independent runner processes, shard ownership, graceful drain and recovery after runner loss, with stated delivery guarantees.

## Context

* Spec: <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> Server-side sharding and load distribution; D3 says sharding takes priority over agent convenience.
* Repo: `packages/core/src/platform/` (cluster platform, colocated stack, supervised launch), `packages/cluster-tooling`, `packages/cluster-compose/docker-compose.postgresql.yaml`, root scripts `cluster:compose:*`, `platform:run:local-fiber`, `local-ci:cluster`. `@effect/cluster` 0.56.
* AGENT-SETUP.md: no shared databases or clusters during default setup; provision Postgres locally for this task only.

## Work

1. Read the platform and tooling code and list what exists: runner count, shard manager, storage, message persistence, entity definitions.
2. Run the existing compose demo (`pnpm cluster:compose:up`, then the verify script). Record output.
3. If it is single-runner, start two runner processes against one local Postgres and a demo entity. Show: entities spread across both runners; stop one gracefully and watch shards move; kill one with SIGKILL and watch recovery; send messages during each and record what was delivered, duplicated or lost.
4. State the guarantees observed (at-least-once, ordering per entity, idempotency needs). Do not claim exactly-once.
5. Note any spot where an agent run (long-lived, streaming) would be hurt by shard moves, and file each as its own Linear issue under <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" />.

## Acceptance

Commands and logs for each scenario, a guarantees table, and the list of gaps against <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" />.

## Out of scope

Kubernetes, production deployment, physical database partitioning.

## Done signal

Comment with results and one action decision: the existing platform is the base (with the listed gaps as tasks), or a named restructure.

## Escalation

If the cluster cannot run two runners without a code change, record the change needed and stop before making it on main.
