comments.body:
## S5 results (2026-10-31, run by Claude for Jonathan)

**Answer:** the existing platform is the base. Two independent runners work with no code change; the gaps below are filed as tasks.

### What exists (Observed)

* @effect/cluster 0.56.4 via `NodeClusterSocket.layer({ storage: "sql" })` (`packages/core/src/cluster/sql-socket-layers.ts`). There is no shard manager in this version: runners register in `cluster_runners` and own shards through Postgres advisory locks on a dedicated connection (`SqlRunnerStorage`). Messages and replies persist in `cluster_messages` / `cluster_replies` (`SqlMessageStorage`).
* Entities: `DemoEntity` (`Shoot` is not persisted; `ShootWithDelay`, `ShootAt` persisted) and singleton `CronShip`, hosted by `RunnerExtension` when `CLUSTER_APP_MODE` is `primary` or `runner`.
* Shard count is 2 (`SHARDS_PER_GROUP=2`) in compose, local stack and FPK.
* The compose `shard-manager` service is really an extra runner with no entities (see EVE-37).

### Commands

Environment: local Postgres 16 (initdb, port 5433), Node 22.23.4. Docker was available but the compose demo needs `cluster-tooling:build-local-images` plus Redpanda, so step 2 was done by running the same entrypoint directly:

```
CLUSTER_APP_MODE=primary PORT=34431 pnpm exec tsx --tsconfig packages/platforms/postgresql/tsconfig.run.json packages/platforms/postgresql/src/platform.ts
CLUSTER_APP_MODE=primary PORT=34432 (same)
CLUSTER_APP_MODE=slow-shooter PORT=34439 (same)
```

Both runners registered (`cluster_runners`: 127.0.0.1:34431 and :34432, healthy) and each logged 30 `DemoEntity` handler lines. Needed `PGPORT`/`PGHOST` as well as `DB_*`, otherwise schema bootstrap dials Postgres on the cluster `PORT` (EVE-38).

Then a probe (one Effect file, same `makeClusterSqlRunnerLayer` / `makeClusterSqlClientLayer` wiring): runners A and B, a client sending to 40 entities every 200ms for 250 rounds (10,000 persisted + 10,000 volatile messages), 4 persisted 25s jobs standing in for agent runs, 30 shards. Every send and every handler run is a row in Postgres, so the numbers are counted, not read from logs. B is signalled at +15s.

### Results

| Scenario | Placement | Persisted lost | Persisted duplicated | Order per entity | Volatile lost | Shard move time | 25s job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Steady state | A 19 entities / 11 shards, B 21 / 13 | 0 | 0 | kept | 0 | - | ran once |
| SIGTERM B, restart after 20s | A took all 40, B took 21 back ~3s after restart | 0 | 0 | kept | 332 | when in-flight handlers end, max 15s (`entityTerminationTimeout`) | finished on B if under 15s left; otherwise interrupted and re-run from the start on A |
| SIGKILL B, restart after 20s | A never took B's shards; B reclaimed them | 0 | 12 | kept | 1,751 | ~22s outage for B's entities | re-run from the start |
| SIGKILL B, no restart | A took all 40 | 0 | 0 | kept | 4,238 | 36.2s (= 35s `shardLockExpiration`) | re-run from the start on A |
| Runner with no entities (compose `shard-manager`) | 21 of 40 entities on it | 21 entities fail every message: `Entity type 'Probe' not registered` | - | - | - | - | - |

### Guarantees observed

* **Persisted RPC with a primary key:** at-least-once execution, one reply per request, per-entity order kept, no loss across drain or kill. Duplicates happen on SIGKILL (12 in 10,000), so handlers must be idempotent. Not exactly-once.
* **Volatile RPC:** at-most-once. Dropped whenever the shard is moving.
* **Entity mailbox:** serial. A long handler blocks every other message to that entity (worst entity: 73s with no deliveries).
* **Graceful drain:** works. Shards hand over once in-flight work finishes or 15s passes.
* **Runner loss:** detection is lock expiry, 35s by default; a restart at the same address inside that window takes its shards straight back.

### Gaps against EVE-13, filed as tasks

Agent-run issues (D3: fix how agent runs are modelled, not sharding):
* EVE-34 Agent runs restart from scratch when their shard moves (use `@effect/workflow` with activities)
* EVE-35 Keep a long agent run from blocking its entity's other messages
* EVE-36 Stream agent output from a durable log, not volatile RPCs

Platform:
* EVE-37 Remove the shard-manager process that owns shards with no entities
* EVE-38 Cut runner-loss failover from 36s and expose the cluster settings in config (also fixes `SHARDS_PER_GROUP=2`, the `PORT` fallback in `pgClientConfigFromEnv`, and `makeClusterSqlRunnerLayer` claiming to provide `SqlClient` when it does not)
* EVE-39 Make every entity action idempotent and persisted by default

### Evidence and code

Probe, harness, SQL and per-scenario logs are in the project files under `eve-18/` (README explains how to reproduce). Not pushed to GitHub: the clone's git identity is an AI tool, and the house rules forbid committing as an AI (AI-03), so the spike stays as files. Nothing touched main.

Tools not available: Graphify setup was not run (the per-clone `graphify setup` step); Context7 was not used, and @effect/cluster behaviour was read from the vendored source in `node_modules` instead.

Decided by Jonathan: keep the existing Effect Cluster platform as the sharding base, then fix the platform gaps first (EVE-37, EVE-38, EVE-39) and the agent-run tasks after (EVE-34, EVE-35, EVE-36).

Pushed to main (Eventiva ship-to-main exception):

issues.title: S6: Map PostHog and OpenTelemetry support across web, native and backend
issues.description:
## Goal

A verified capability matrix of which PostHog tools and which OpenTelemetry signals work on each Eventiva runtime, and the vendor-neutral telemetry contract that lets vendors be swapped.

## Context

* Spec: <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> OpenTelemetry and PostHog; D4 (remove Sentry, vendor-neutral, PostHog default).
* House: `.agents/skills/coding-preferences/references/telemetry.md` and the `feature-flags` skill (full required inventory, dedicated project per product, `telemetry: false`).
* Repo: `packages/core/src/observability/` uses `@effect/opentelemetry` and Sentry.
* No PostHog project creation or production change is authorized.

## Work

1. From current PostHog docs and SDK source (posthog-js, posthog-react-native, posthog-node), fill a matrix: rows = every house-required tool (analytics, identity and groups, tracing, logs linked to replay and person, error tracking with source maps, flags with Early Access, metrics, experiments, session replay with Replay Vision, heatmaps, toolbar, AI Observability, prompts with A/B, Skills, Datasets, Semantics); columns = web, iOS, Android, Node backend. Cells: supported, partial, not supported, with doc link and SDK version.
2. For OTel traces, metrics and logs: can PostHog ingest OTLP directly for each signal? If not, state the smallest collector or exporter path, without picking another vendor.
3. Draft the neutral contract: Effect services for events, flags, errors and LLM traces, with PostHog as one Layer and a no-op Layer for `telemetry: false`. Show how a second vendor would plug in.

## Acceptance

Every cell cites a source; gaps have a proposed follow-up.

## Out of scope

Provisioning, code on main.

## Done signal

Comment with the matrix and contract sketch, and one action decision: accept the contract and any collector path proposed.

## Escalation

If a required signal has no PostHog path, bring the export choice back to <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> as a decision.

comments.author: GitHub

comments.body:
## S6 findings: PostHog and OpenTelemetry capability matrix

Checked 2026-10-31 against the published SDK packages (unpacked and read: `posthog-js@1.444.0`, `posthog-react-native@4.85.1`, `posthog-react-native-session-replay@1.6.0`, `posthog-node@5.61.1`, `@posthog/core` latest, `@posthog/ai@8.17.2`, `@effect/opentelemetry@0.61.0` as pinned in `packages/core`) and the PostHog docs and monorepo READMEs via Context7. Nothing was provisioned. iOS and Android mean the Expo / React Native app (one app, per EVE-13); desktop uses the web SDK, so it inherits the web column.

Legend: Yes = supported in the SDK, Partial = works with a stated workaround, No = not supported, n/a = not meaningful on that runtime.

### 1. PostHog tools by runtime

| House-required tool | Web (posthog-js 1.444.0) | iOS + Android (posthog-react-native 4.85.1) | Node backend (posthog-node 5.61.1) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Analytics (capture) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Identity and groups | Yes: `identify`, `group` | Yes: `identify`, `group` | Yes: `identify`, `groupIdentify` |
| Tracing | Partial: `tracingHeaders` extension only adds session and distinct id headers to fetch/XHR; spans go through OTLP (section 2) | Partial: no SDK tracing; spans via OTLP from Effect, unverified on Hermes (F1) | Yes: SDK traces pipeline (`withSpan`, `traces` option, built on `@posthog/core` PostHogTraces) plus OTLP |
| Logs linked to replay and person | Yes: `logs` extension, `captureLog`, posts to `/i/v1/logs` with session id | Yes: `captureLog`, `posthog.logger.*`, `flushLogs` (min 4.44.0, docs: posthog.com/docs/libraries/react-native) | Partial: no SDK log API; Effect logs go out as OTLP, person and session link needs `posthog.distinct_id` and `$session_id` attributes carried from the request (F4) |
| Error tracking with source maps | Yes: exception autocapture, source maps via PostHog CLI | Yes: JS `captureException`, `PostHogErrorBoundary`; native crashes with `@posthog/react-native-plugin` (`nativeCrashes`, `androidNdkCrashes` from 4.78.0), symbols uploaded at build | Yes: `captureException` (docs: posthog.com/docs/libraries/node), source maps via CLI |
| Feature flags | Yes | Yes (`bootstrap` for cold start) | Yes, including local evaluation |
| Early Access | Yes: `getEarlyAccessFeatures`, `updateEarlyAccessFeatureEnrollment` | Partial: no SDK API; enrol by sending the enrollment event and person property through capture (F3) | Partial: same as native |
| Metrics | Yes: `posthog.metrics.count/gauge/histogram` to `/i/v1/metrics` | Partial: no SDK metrics; OTLP from Effect, unverified on Hermes (F1) | Yes (alpha): `client.metrics` plus OTLP |
| Experiments | Yes, including no-code web experiments | Yes, through flags plus capture | Yes, through flags plus capture |
| Session replay | Yes | Yes: `posthog-react-native-session-replay` 1.6.0 on iOS and Android; not on web or macOS targets of RN | n/a |
| Replay Vision | Yes: server-side scanners over recordings (PostHog `products/replay_vision`) | Yes: same, runs on whatever replay records | n/a |
| Heatmaps | Yes: `heatmaps` extension | No: no heatmap module in the RN SDK (F5) | n/a |
| Toolbar | Yes | No: web-only by design (F5) | n/a |
| AI Observability | n/a: Eventiva runs model calls on the server (EVE-13) | n/a: same | Yes: `@posthog/ai` with `vercel` (AI SDK) and `otel` subpaths; OTLP AI spans to `/i/v0/ai/otel` |
| Prompts with A/B | n/a | n/a | Yes: `@posthog/ai` `Prompts` (`get`, `getAll`, `compile`), A/B by pairing with a flag |
| Skills | n/a | n/a | Partial: PostHog LLM skills store is a project API (`/api/projects/:team/llm_skills`), currently behind PostHog's own `skills-store-in-sandbox` flag (F6) |
| Datasets | n/a | n/a | Yes: `@posthog/ai` `Datasets` |
| Semantics | n/a | n/a | Partial: PostHog semantic layer is a warehouse feature (canonical metrics in `system.information_schema.metrics`), not an SDK; no runtime code needed, adopt when the warehouse is wired (F6) |

Linking AI traces to replay and errors: the web SDK's `tracingHeaders` forwards the session id to our API, the server puts `$session_id` and the distinct id on the AI span and on any captured exception. That is the same propagation F4 needs for logs, so it is one piece of work.

### 2. OpenTelemetry signals: direct OTLP ingestion

PostHog ingests all three signals directly, so no collector is required:

| Signal | PostHog endpoint | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Logs | `POST /i/v1/logs` (also `/v1/logs`), protobuf, JSON or JSONL, project token as `Authorization: Bearer` or `?token=` | posthog `rust/capture-logs/README.md` |
| Traces | `POST /i/v1/traces`, HTTP, project token; stored in `posthog.trace_spans` | posthog `docs/internal/wizard-runs.md`, posthog.com/docs/distributed-tracing |
| Metrics | `POST /i/v1/metrics` (also Prometheus remote-write `/i/v1/prometheus/write`); stored in `posthog.metrics` with exemplar `trace_id` | posthog `rust/capture-apm-metrics/README.md` |
| AI spans | `POST /i/v0/ai/otel`; keeps only spans with `gen_ai.*`, `ai.*` and similar conventions, drops the rest | posthog `products/ingestion/.../fixing-ai-endpoint-rejections.md` |

The smallest exporter path is the one we already depend on: `@effect/opentelemetry` `Otlp.layer({ baseUrl, headers, resource })` appends `/v1/logs`, `/v1/metrics` and `/v1/traces` to `baseUrl` (`dist/esm/Otlp.js`), so `baseUrl = https://<region>.i.posthog.com/i` hits all three. It is built on Effect `HttpClient`, not the Node OTel SDK, which is why it is the candidate for the native app too (F1). AI SDK spans carry `ai.*` attributes, so a second OTLP trace exporter pointed at `/i/v0/ai/otel` gives AI Observability with no PostHog-specific code. Auth for `/i/v1/traces` and `/i/v1/metrics` is documented as the project token; the exact header form is confirmed only for logs and is checked in F2.

A collector becomes useful only for fan-out to two vendors at once, central redaction or tail sampling. Proposed: none now; `baseUrl` can point at a collector later without code changes.

### 3. Vendor-neutral contract (sketch, Effect v3)

Two layers of neutrality:

1. **Traces, logs, metrics: neutral by protocol.** Code uses only Effect's own `Effect.withSpan`, `Effect.log*` and `Metric`. Export is one `OtlpExport` layer built from config. Switching vendor = changing `telemetry.otlp.baseUrl` and headers. No vendor import in any module.
2. **Product telemetry: neutral by service.** Four `Context.Tag` services in core, vendors as Layers in `packages/integrations/*`:

```ts
// packages/core/src/telemetry/ (plain sketch, not committed)
export class ProductEvents extends Context.Tag("eventiva/ProductEvents")<ProductEvents, {
  readonly capture: (e: ProductEvent) => Effect.Effect<void>            // never fails the caller
  readonly identify: (id: ActorId, traits?: Traits) => Effect.Effect<void>
  readonly group: (kind: GroupKind, id: string, traits?: Traits) => Effect.Effect<void>  // tenant = group
}>() {}

export class Flags extends Context.Tag("eventiva/Flags")<Flags, {
  readonly evaluate: <A>(flag: FlagDef<A>) => Effect.Effect<A>          // FlagDef carries the safe default
  readonly enrolEarlyAccess: (flag: FlagKey, on: boolean) => Effect.Effect<void>
}>() {}

export class ErrorReports extends Context.Tag("eventiva/ErrorReports")<ErrorReports, {
  readonly report: (cause: Cause.Cause<unknown>, ctx: ErrorContext) => Effect.Effect<void>  // redacted ctx
}>() {}

export class LlmTelemetry extends Context.Tag("eventiva/LlmTelemetry")<LlmTelemetry, {
  readonly prompt: (key: PromptKey) => Effect.Effect<CompiledPrompt, PromptUnavailable>  // falls back to in-repo prompt
  readonly dataset: (key: DatasetKey) => Effect.Effect<Dataset, DatasetUnavailable>
}>() {}
// LLM generations themselves are OTel gen_ai spans, so they need no service.

// Config schema, not env switches (house feature-flags rule)
telemetry: { enabled: boolean /* telemetry: false */, otlp: { baseUrl, headers, aiTracesUrl? }, product: "posthog" | "none" }

// Composition
const TelemetryLive = Config.telemetry.pipe(Layer.unwrapEffect(cfg =>
  !cfg.enabled ? TelemetryNoop                                  // all four services no-op, no OTLP export
  : Layer.mergeAll(OtlpExport(cfg.otlp), productLayer(cfg.product))))
// productLayer("posthog") = PostHogWeb | PostHogNative | PostHogNode, picked per runtime entrypoint
```

**How a second vendor plugs in:** for traces, logs and metrics, point `otlp.baseUrl` at the new backend or at a collector. For events, flags, errors and prompts, add `packages/integrations/<vendor>` with Layers for the same four Tags and add its name to the `product` enum. Nothing above the integration package changes. Contract tests in `@effect/vitest` run against `TelemetryNoop`, the PostHog Layers and an in-memory test Layer, so a new vendor passes the same suite.

Redaction sits in core, before any Layer: `ErrorContext` and log annotations go through one Schema-based redactor, so every vendor receives the same redacted data.

### 4. Gaps and proposed follow-ups

- **F1** Spike: `@effect/opentelemetry` Otlp exporters on Expo / Hermes (fetch transport, JSON vs protobuf, background flush, offline queue) sending traces and metrics. Fallback if it fails: metrics as PostHog events on native only, behind the same `Metric` API.
- **F2** Smoke test the three OTLP endpoints and auth header against a dev PostHog project. Blocked until a dedicated Eventiva PostHog project is authorised (house: one project per product).
- **F3** Early Access on native and server: implement `Flags.enrolEarlyAccess` with the enrollment event and person property; listing features through the PostHog API from the server.
- **F4** Context propagation: session id and distinct id from clients (web `tracingHeaders`, native equivalent) into server spans, logs, errors and AI spans.
- **F5** Heatmaps and Toolbar are web-only upstream. Accept as a recorded gap for native; no workaround proposed.
- **F6** Skills and Semantics: track upstream; adopt Skills when PostHog's store leaves its flag, Semantics when the warehouse work starts. No runtime code.
- **F7** Version note: `packages/core` pins `@effect/opentelemetry@0.61.0` (Effect 3); npm latest is 4.1.1 (Effect 4). The contract is written for Effect 3; the Effect 4 move is its own decision, not part of this spike.
- Sentry removal stays in EVE-21; this contract is what replaces `SentrySpanProcessor` in `packages/core/src/observability/tracing.ts`.

No required signal lacks a PostHog path, so there is no export-choice escalation to EVE-13.

### Decision requested

Accept the contract above with direct OTLP to PostHog and no collector, and file F1 to F4 as child issues of EVE-13.

## Recheck 2026-10-31 (asked by Jonathan): native gaps

Rechecked the full `posthog-react-native@4.85.1` build (all JS, not only type files), `@posthog/core` and the PostHog docs pages.

**Correction:** React Native does have `addTracingHeaders` (`dist/posthog-rn.js` calls `patchFetchForTracingHeaders` from `@posthog/core`; docs: posthog.com/docs/libraries/react-native). It adds `X-POSTHOG-DISTINCT-ID` and `X-POSTHOG-SESSION-ID` to matching `fetch` requests, the same as web. So the Tracing cell for iOS + Android is "Partial: tracing headers yes, no SDK spans" and F4 (EVE-60) needs no native header work.

**Confirmed, still gaps in the RN SDK:**
* Spans and metrics: `@posthog/core` now ships `PostHogTraces` and `PostHogMetrics` (used by posthog-node), but the RN SDK does not wire either; no reference to `/i/v1/traces` or `/i/v1/metrics` anywhere in its build. The distributed tracing docs list only Node.js and Python installs plus "any OpenTelemetry-compatible client". The PostHog server accepts OTLP from any client, so the Effect OTLP path (EVE-57) remains the route.
* Early Access: no `getEarlyAccessFeatures` or enrollment code in the RN build; the RN docs page does not mention it. Route stays EVE-59.
* Heatmaps and Toolbar: no code in the RN build; the RN docs page describes neither. Both are posthog-js browser extensions.

Summary: the PostHog server side supports every signal; the gaps are in what the React Native SDK sends, and each has a route through OTLP or capture.

Recorded by Claude (agent) for Jonathan.

issues.title: S7: Find which AI providers allow users to bring their own subscription to Eventiva
issues.description:
## Goal

A per-provider table of sanctioned ways an Eventiva user can connect their own AI account (subscription or API key) or external agent, so Eventiva never relies on unofficial tokens or silent Eventiva-funded fallback.

## Context

* Spec: <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> End-user subscriptions and external agents.
* House AI stack: AI SDK alongside Effect AI, Vercel Connect for acting on behalf of users (`.agents/skills/coding-preferences/references/ai.md`).
* Upstream Agent-Native supports AI SDK providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Groq, Mistral, Ollama, OpenRouter) and ACP agents; read `packages/core/src/provider-api/` and `agent/harness/` for how it handles credentials.

## Work

1. For at least Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft/GitHub Copilot, Mistral, OpenRouter and local models (Ollama): what official delegation exists (OAuth "sign in with", API keys, organisation keys, ACP or MCP clients the user runs), whether a consumer chat subscription may be used by a third-party app under current terms, scopes, revocation and expiry, and who is billed. Cite the terms or docs page and its date.
2. External agents: which can connect inbound (MCP client, ACP client, A2A) and with what identity.
3. Propose the credential model: storage, scopes, per-run identity, quotas, revocation mid-run, audit, and the no-fallback rule.

## Acceptance

Every "allowed" cell cites a primary source; anything unclear is marked "not permitted until confirmed".

## Out of scope

Building connections; negotiating with providers.

## Done signal

Comment with the table and the credential model, and one action decision: the providers to support at launch.

## Escalation

Never test with scraped cookies or unofficial tokens. If a provider's terms forbid third-party use of a subscription, list it as API-key only.

comments.body:
## S7 findings: bring-your-own AI accounts (checked 2026-10-31)

Research only. No connection was built or tested, and no scraped cookies or unofficial tokens were used. Anything not backed by a primary source below is marked **not permitted until confirmed**.

### 1. Provider table

| Provider | Consumer subscription in a third-party app? | Sanctioned delegation for Eventiva | Billed to | Scopes, expiry, revocation | Primary source (read 2026-10-31) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Anthropic (Claude)** | **No.** "Anthropic does not permit third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications, or to route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users." Developers may not collect, store or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens. | (a) User's own Claude Console API key. (b) User's own Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform or Microsoft Foundry credential. (c) The **unmodified Claude Code binary**, which the user signs into themselves (allowed locally, and hosted only under the Commercial Terms, with every end user authenticating as themselves and no resale or intermediation). | The key or plan owner. Programmatic use from a subscription draws a separate monthly credit at API rates since 2026-06-15. | API keys: no expiry, revoked in Console. Claude Code login: Anthropic's own flow only. | [code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance) ("Authentication and credential use", "Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?"); programmatic credit: [the-decoder, 2026-05-14](https://the-decoder.com/claude-subscriptions-get-separate-budgets-for-programmatic-use-billed-at-full-api-prices/) citing ClaudeDevs |
| **OpenAI (ChatGPT)** | **Yes, but gated.** Sign in with ChatGPT plan usage (DevDay 2026-09-29): Plus and Pro only, not Business or Enterprise. "Available to all open-source partners and selected private clients"; an app must be "approved for ChatGPT plan usage". Eventiva is FCL-1.0 (fair-source, not OSI open source) and hosted, so it falls in the "selected private clients" path. **Not permitted until OpenAI approves our client.** | OIDC with PKCE, scope `chatgpt.tokens.use.direct` (with `openid profile email offline_access resource.invoke`), inference through the Responses API with restrictions (`store:false`, no hosted tools, no Files API). Until approval: user's own OpenAI API key, or Azure OpenAI through Foundry. | User's ChatGPT plan allowance. When it runs out, usage stops; no switch to partner billing. Users set per-app weekly caps. | Access token 1 h, refresh 30 days rolling; revoked when the user disconnects the app in ChatGPT settings, or by the app. Ineligible users get 403 `subscription_sharing_user_not_eligible`. | [developers.openai.com/siwc/quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/quickstart); [siwc preview limitations](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/preview-limitations); scope and lifetimes: [WorkOS, 2026-10-01](https://workos.com/blog/sign-in-with-chatgpt-plan-usage-scope); launch: [The New Stack, 2026-09-29](https://thenewstack.io/sign-in-with-chatgpt/) |
| **Google (Gemini)** | **No.** Using third-party software with Gemini CLI or Antigravity OAuth "is a violation of applicable terms and policies" and may lead to suspension (accounts were banned after OpenClaw and OpenCode OAuth use). | User's own Gemini API key (AI Studio, paid or unpaid terms) or Vertex AI credential in the user's own Google Cloud project. Running the user's own unmodified Gemini or Antigravity CLI on their own device over ACP is the CLI's own use, not Eventiva holding the token. | Key or project owner. | Keys revoked in AI Studio or Cloud console. | [Gemini CLI ToS and privacy, updated 2026-04-10](https://www.geminicli.com/docs/resources/tos-privacy) |
| **GitHub Copilot** | **Yes.** The Copilot SDK (GA 2026-06-02) lets an app act for a user who signs in with GitHub; it "requires a Copilot subscription" and the user's plan is billed. Multi-user servers are documented: "pass a per-session `gitHubToken`". | GitHub OAuth App (`gho_`) or GitHub App user token (`ghu_`), or fine-grained PAT; not classic PATs. Server-to-server for org-billed automation. BYOK for other providers without Copilot. | User's Copilot plan (usage-based AI credits since 2026-06-01), or org billing for server-to-server. | GitHub OAuth expiry and revocation rules; docs recommend a per-session token provider over long-lived tokens. | [Authenticate the Copilot SDK](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-sdk/authenticate-copilot-sdk/authenticate-copilot-sdk); [GA changelog 2026-06-02](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-06-02-copilot-sdk-is-now-generally-available/); [usage billing 2026-05-01](https://github.blog/2026-05-01-github-copilot-is-moving-to-usage-based-billing/) |
| **Microsoft (Foundry / Azure OpenAI)** | Not applicable (no consumer plan delegation found). Microsoft 365 Copilot subscription delegation: **not permitted until confirmed**. | Customer's own Foundry endpoint with API key or Microsoft Entra ID (keyless). | The customer's Azure subscription. | Key rotation in Azure; Entra tokens and RBAC. | [Foundry authentication and authorization](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry); [Configure Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/foundry-models/how-to/configure-entra-id) |
| **Mistral** | **Not permitted until confirmed.** No documented Le Chat subscription delegation or third-party OAuth. | User's own API key from Mistral Studio, per workspace. | Key owner's organisation. | Keys managed in Studio and Admin. | [Mistral platform overview](https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/le-chat-studio-admin) |
| **OpenRouter** | Not a subscription; an account the user tops up. **Allowed** and purpose-built for this. | OAuth PKCE: user authorises Eventiva and Eventiva receives a **user-controlled API key**; headless code flow for devices without a callback. | User's OpenRouter credits. | Auth code expires in 10 min; the key is the user's and they manage it on their key settings page. No spend-limit parameter in the flow, so Eventiva enforces its own cap. | [OpenRouter OAuth PKCE](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/auth/oauth) |
| **Ollama (local and cloud)** | Not applicable. | Local `http://localhost:11434`, no auth (desktop and self-hosted only; never reachable from our cloud). Ollama Cloud with the user's `OLLAMA_API_KEY` bearer key. | Local: nobody. Cloud: key owner. | Cloud keys do not expire; revoked on ollama.com. | [Ollama API authentication](https://docs.ollama.com/api/authentication) |

### 2. External agents connecting to Eventiva

| Direction | Protocol | Who | Identity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Inbound | **MCP server** (Eventiva exposes its actions) | Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor, Codex and any MCP client | OAuth 2.1 against Eventiva's own auth; the token is an Eventiva user grant with scoped actions, never a provider credential. |
| Inbound | **A2A** | Other agent platforms | Eventiva-issued agent principal tied to a user or service account; upstream Agent-Native already has `a2a-claims`. |
| Outbound | **ACP client** (Eventiva drives the user's own agent) | Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode (all in the ACP registry, [Zed, 2026-01-28](https://zed.dev/blog/acp-registry)) | The agent signs in through its own vendor flow on the user's device. Eventiva never sees or stores that credential. This is the only sanctioned way to use a Claude Pro or Max subscription from Eventiva. |
| Outbound | Webhooks and API | Automations | Eventiva service principal with per-action scopes. |

Upstream note: Agent-Native's `agent/harness/acp-builtin.ts` ships presets for Gemini CLI and Claude Code (`@zed-industries/claude-code-acp`), and `server/credential-provider.ts` stores personal and org provider keys with an org policy that can restrict personal keys. It also has a **deployment env fallback** (`source: "env"`), which Eventiva must disable for model credentials.

### 3. Proposed credential model

1. **Storage.** One `ModelCredential` record per (tenant, owner, provider): owner is a user or the tenant. Secrets are envelope-encrypted with a per-tenant key in the secret store; the database holds only the ciphertext reference, a fingerprint and metadata. Plaintext is never returned to the UI or an agent.
2. **Kinds.** `api-key`, `oauth-delegated` (OpenRouter key, Copilot GitHub token, ChatGPT plan token once approved), `cloud-identity` (Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry with Entra), `local-endpoint` (Ollama, desktop only), `acp-agent` (we hold nothing).
3. **Scopes.** Each credential lists allowed models, allowed Eventiva action classes, and allowed surfaces (interactive, background, automation). Tenant admins can forbid personal credentials or require tenant ones.
4. **Per-run identity.** Every agent run carries `{tenant, actingUser, credentialId, agentPrincipal}`; the credential is resolved per call through an Effect `ModelCredentials` service, never cached across users, and Copilot uses a per-session token provider.
5. **Quotas.** Eventiva-side caps per credential and per run (tokens and spend), on top of the provider's own caps (ChatGPT weekly caps, Copilot credits, OpenRouter balance).
6. **Revocation mid-run.** A provider 401 or 403, a refresh failure or a user revoke ends the current step with a typed `CredentialRevoked` error, pauses the run as `needs-credential`, and never retries with another credential.
7. **Audit.** Every model call logs run id, credential id and fingerprint (never the secret), provider, model, tokens, cost estimate and outcome, traced in OpenTelemetry and PostHog LLM analytics.
8. **No-fallback rule.** If the chosen credential is missing, expired, over quota or revoked, the run stops and asks the user. Eventiva never silently switches to another user's, the tenant's or an Eventiva-funded credential, and there is no environment-variable fallback. Eventiva-funded built-in AI is a separate, explicit, metered product choice.

### 4. Action decision: providers at launch

**Recommended launch set:**
- API keys: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini (and Vertex), Mistral, Microsoft Foundry.
- Sign-in flows that bill the user: **OpenRouter** (OAuth PKCE) and **GitHub Copilot** (Copilot SDK over GitHub OAuth).
- Local: **Ollama** on desktop and self-hosted, plus Ollama Cloud keys.
- **ACP** on desktop for the user's own Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI.
- **Apply now** for OpenAI Sign in with ChatGPT plan usage as a private client, and add it when approved.
- Not supported: Claude, Gemini or Mistral consumer subscriptions inside Eventiva itself.

issues.title: Split core into portable contracts and backend runtime, with a shared schema package
issues.description:
## Binding architecture approval — 2026-11-14

Jonathan approved this architecture on 2026-11-14 after the <issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" />, <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />, <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> and <issue id="57425d1f-fae5-49c9-af1e-51cd26f64d20" label="EVE-244" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-244/scaffold-the-fresh-nx-expo-effect-and-testing-foundation" /> research review. This is architecture approval only: it does not start implementation, approve unlisted dependencies, provision services, change spending limits, or re-enable paid AI gates.

This issue now implements a clean three-package boundary rather than extracting or preserving the archived core:

1. `@eventiva/contracts` (`type:core`, `layer:shared`; Effect peer only) owns portable action specifications and cross-runtime contracts.
2. `@eventiva/schema` (`type:shared`, `layer:shared`) owns database-neutral resources/fields and pure schema composition, replacing global registries and `defineExtensionTable` coupling.
3. `@eventiva/runtime` (`type:runtime`, `layer:backend`) owns Effect v3 execution/composition, ActionHost, authorization, audit, lifecycle and local dispatch; no driver/vendor SDK and no domain-specific handlers.

Features split into portable, `.server` and `.client` packages as required. Integrations/apps alone import drivers, vendor SDKs, Node platform layers or Cluster. Use explicit subpath exports, no root barrel, `sideEffects: false`, shared Effect singleton, acyclic Nx directions and portability gates for TypeScript, lint/import bans, browser bundling and Expo/Hermes.

Action specification and Effect handler are separate. A handler registers against exactly one specification. Dynamic modules register/unregister compatible manifests transactionally and dispose routes, actions, projections, listeners and scoped resources safely.

Any older extraction/legacy-API direction below is historical and superseded by this approval; rewrite it before implementation so implementers receive one unambiguous specification.

## Scope correction from Jonathan - stop current extraction

Decision recorded 2026-11-10: the current implementations under packages/cluster-compose, packages/cluster-tooling, packages/core, packages/databases (including pg), packages/extensions and packages/platforms were manually created legacy implementations. They are functional reference material but are not the implementation baseline for the Amp-led rebuild. They must be archived under Examples in a clearly named legacy location, preserving history and allowing agents to inspect behavior, and the production package foundations must then be designed cleanly from the approved specifications and current house standards.

Do not land the behavior-preserving package extraction attempted before this clarification. No commit-hook exception is approved or needed for relocating its legacy internals into new production packages. Stop before commit or push, preserve the uncommitted work only long enough to report/recover any useful inventory, then revert it safely. Before moving the current package tree, resolve the archive destination because Examples/packages-old already exists; do not overwrite or merge two legacy snapshots silently.

<issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" /> must be re-scoped after the archive/reset to create new portable contracts, runtime and schema package boundaries from scratch. Legacy code is evidence and may inform tests/contracts, but is not copied by default. Behavior that remains required must be justified by the approved product specification rather than preserved solely because the old code implemented it.

## Goal

Web and native code can import Eventiva's core contracts without pulling in drivers, cluster runtime or Node APIs, and extensions get schema helpers without importing database drivers.

## Context

* Decisions D5 and D6 on <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> (2026-10-31).
* At 322ab45 `packages/core` is tagged `type:core`, `layer:backend` and depends on `@effect/cluster`, `@effect/sql-pg`, `@effect/sql-mysql2`, `@effect/platform-node`, `drizzle-orm` beta and more. Its `src/` mixes contracts (config schemas, hook types, typeid) with runtime (cluster platform, SQL layers, observability).
* Extensions import `type:database` for helpers like `defineExtensionTable`.
* Packaging rule from <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" />: one entry point per module, `sideEffects: false`, no barrels that pull drivers or vendors.

## Work

1. Inventory every export of `packages/core/src/index.ts` and classify it: portable contract (no IO, no Node, no driver) or backend runtime.
2. Create `packages/core-contracts` (`type:core`, `layer:shared`, zero workspace dependencies, `effect` only) and move portable items there; keep runtime in `packages/core` (or rename to `core-runtime`) depending on contracts.
3. Create a `type:shared` schema package for Drizzle-neutral schema helpers; move `defineExtensionTable` and column facades; update extensions; then remove `type:database` from the extension constraint in `eslint.config.mjs` and update `module-boundaries.md` to match.
4. Add a lint fixture proving a `layer:frontend` package can import contracts and cannot import runtime.
5. Keep behaviour identical: all existing tests pass unchanged; never weaken a test.

## Acceptance

`pnpm exec nx run-many -t lint,typecheck,build,test` passes (paste output); a bundle of core-contracts contains no driver or Node import (show the check); graph refreshed.

## Done signal

Landed per the delivery rule (<issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> item 12); comment with evidence.

comments.body:
Amp update (autonomous agent): EVE-23 implementation landed on main by direct push under the Eventiva delivery exception. No PR, no new dependency, no change to Smartcloud safeguards or AI-overage controls. docs/architecture/eventiva-platform-and-marketplace.md was not touched.

**Commits** (rebased onto origin/main d0f582c just before the push; pushed `d0f582c..7df4217`):
- [3e1ab01](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/commit/3e1ab01) feat(platform): complete the EVE-23 contracts, schema and runtime boundaries
- [7df4217](https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/commit/7df4217) chore(graphify): refresh the code graph (EVE-23)

**Audit of EVE-244.** It already had: the spec/handler split (`define` / `implement`), subpath exports with `sideEffects: false`, the effect peer singleton, the type/layer/capability tags, scoped all-or-nothing action registration, and fixtures F1-F6, F8, F9 and F10 (formatjs).

It lacked: caller and authorisation contracts, ids, security profiles, a permission on each spec, database-neutral fields, resources and composition, authorisation in the action path, module-scoped resources and disposal, schema registration, a runtime import ban, a cycle check, and the bundle and Hermes checks.

**Added**
- `@eventiva/contracts`:
  - `./caller`: `Caller`, `CallerIdentity`, and `Authorizer` with `canInvoke` and `check`.
  - `./ids`: branded UUID `TenantId`, `SubjectId` and `SessionId`.
  - `./security`: `SecurityProfile` and `isWeaker`.
  - A required `permission` on every action spec, and the `Forbidden` platform error.
- `@eventiva/schema`:
  - `./field` and `./resource`: no driver, no column types and no tenant id.
  - `./compose`: pure, order-independent, no global registry, with typed errors `DuplicateResource`, `DuplicateField`, `UnknownTarget`, `WeakerClassification` and `InvalidName`.
  - Manifests gain an optional `resources` list.
- `@eventiva/runtime`:
  - `invoke` runs in this order: flag gates, then `canInvoke` before decode, then decode, then `check` on the decoded input, then the handler. The Caller is read on every call.
  - `register` now also checks resources and composition. It builds an optional module `layer` in a child scope and fails with `ActivationFailed` if the layer fails, releasing what it acquired. On scope close it removes the module first and releases the layer second, exactly once.
  - `ActionHost.schema` returns the composed schema of registered modules.
- Boundaries:
  - The runtime (`capability:actions`) may import only effect and no Node built-ins.
  - New tests: F7 cycle check against the real packages; F11 runtime ban; F12 browser bundle of every contracts and schema subpath contains only those packages and the effect dependency closure, with no Node import; F13 a one-subpath bundle drops the rest; F14 React Native's own `hermes-compiler` compiles the bundle.
  - The bundle checks use the Vite already installed; esbuild, publint and attw were not added. A mutation that imported `node:fs` into contracts failed F12, then was reverted.
- `apps/server`: a deny-by-default Authorizer granting its own service identity `platform.status` only.
- Docs: `docs/foundation.md`, `ai-docs/src/11_foundation`, `packages/README.md`, and a regenerated `LLMS.md`.

issues.title: Port notifications, messaging channels and transactional email
issues.description:
## Goal

Users and agents can reach people through in-app notifications, email and chat platforms (Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp), and people can talk to the Eventiva agent from those channels, all through the same actions and permissions as the app.

## Upstream reference (pinned tag from <issue id="cc5eba91-a4f7-4542-b332-10d3e1d70ed8" label="EVE-15" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-15/s2-build-the-upstream-agent-native-capability-map-and-protocol" />)

* `packages/core/src/notifications/` (7 files): notification store, registry of channels, routes; built-in in-app and email channels; `registerNotificationChannel()` for more.
* `packages/core/src/integrations/` (52 files, 28k lines): chat-platform adapters `adapters/{slack,microsoft-teams,discord,telegram,whatsapp,email,google-docs}.ts`, channel settings, awaiting-input store (agent pauses for a reply), proactive delivery, A2A continuations.
* `packages/core/src/email-catalog/` (9 files): registry of system email templates, authorization for sending, body redaction in logs, provider metrics.

## Eventiva form

* `notifications` extension: actions `notifications.send`, `notifications.list`, `notifications.markRead`, `notifications.preferences.update`; channel is an Effect service with one Layer per channel.
* `integrations.messaging-<platform>` packages, one per platform, each behind a neutral `MessagingChannel` service (send, receive webhook, verify signature). Inbound messages become agent runs under the linked user's identity and scopes; unlinked senders get nothing.
* `email` service with templates in Effect Schema, provider Layer swappable (no vendor in domain), bodies redacted in telemetry.
* Prefer the house Chat SDK where it covers a platform (house `ai.md`), wrapped at one Effect boundary.

## Work

1. Read the three upstream modules; list every action and setting they expose.
2. Build notifications plus the in-app and email channels first; then Slack and Microsoft Teams; then the rest in one issue each if large.
3. Webhook signature checks and replay protection for every inbound channel.
4. Screen: notification centre and channel settings built from Rambo-UI, with projections.

## Acceptance

An agent and a user each send the same notification through the same action; a Slack message to the bot starts an agent run as the linked user and is refused for an unlinked user; an email send is logged with the body redacted; flag off disables the feature.

## Depends on

<issue id="07c58289-6f1c-488e-a130-5f718b473fce" label="EVE-14" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-14/s1-prove-one-effect-action-serves-ui-mcp-and-ai-sdk-from-one-inventory" /> (action contract), credentials and identity from phase 1.

## Out of scope

SMS and voice calls; marketing email.

issues.title: Port files, private attachments, artifacts and document import
issues.description:
## Goal

Users and agents upload, store, attach and import files (images, PDFs, Office, Notion, Figma), with private files encrypted and every access checked, and agent-produced outputs kept as first-class artifacts.

## Upstream reference (pinned tag from <issue id="cc5eba91-a4f7-4542-b332-10d3e1d70ed8" label="EVE-15" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-15/s2-build-the-upstream-agent-native-capability-map-and-protocol" />)

* `file-upload/` (18 files): upload registry, S3 client, attachment bytes and text extraction, inline image downscaling, size limits, owned attachments.
* `private-blob/` (8 files): encrypted private blobs (`blob-crypto.ts`), attachment references, S3 private storage.
* `artifacts/detect.ts`: detects agent outputs that should become artifacts.
* `ingestion/` (13 files): import from docx, pptx, spreadsheets, Office, Notion, Figma (nodes to HTML), media; orchestration and selection.

## Eventiva form

* `files` extension: actions `files.upload.begin`, `files.upload.complete`, `files.get`, `files.delete`, `files.attach`, `files.detach`; every read is an authorized action, never a public URL by default (short-lived signed URLs only).
* `BlobStore` neutral service; S3-compatible Layer (works with R2, S3, MinIO) in an integration package; envelope encryption for private blobs with keys from the secret store.
* Offline: files queued locally (SQLite metadata plus local file cache) and uploaded on reconnect; same queue as S4 sync.
* `ingestion` as separate integration packages per source (office, notion, figma), each turning a source into text plus structure the agent can read.
* Artifacts: agent outputs saved as versioned files linked to the run and the record they belong to.

## Acceptance

Upload offline on mobile, reconnect, file appears for another user with permission and is refused for one without; a private blob is unreadable in storage without the key; a docx imports to readable text the agent can quote; deleting the record removes or orphans attachments per a written rule.

## Depends on

<issue id="07c58289-6f1c-488e-a130-5f718b473fce" label="EVE-14" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-14/s1-prove-one-effect-action-serves-ui-mcp-and-ai-sdk-from-one-inventory" />, <issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" /> (sync queue).

issues.description:
## Goal

Users and agents search everything they are allowed to see (events, people, stock, files, comments) by keyword and by meaning, with results filtered by permission.

## Upstream reference (pinned tag from <issue id="cc5eba91-a4f7-4542-b332-10d3e1d70ed8" label="EVE-15" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-15/s2-build-the-upstream-agent-native-capability-map-and-protocol" />)

## Eventiva form

* `search` extension: modules register searchable resources with a Schema-described projection; actions `search.query` (keyword plus semantic, filters, pagination) and `search.reindex` (admin).

A user and an agent get identical results for the same query; a record the user cannot read never appears, including in counts; offline keyword search works on mobile; reindex after a schema change completes without downtime.

People and agents comment on any record or document, mention others, and propose changes that a person accepts or rejects, so agent work can be reviewed before it lands.

issues.title: Port localization for people and for the agent
issues.description:
## Goal

Every string a person sees, and every message the agent uses about the platform, is translatable, with per-user locale, time zone and formats.

## Upstream reference (pinned tag from <issue id="cc5eba91-a4f7-4542-b332-10d3e1d70ed8" label="EVE-15" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-15/s2-build-the-upstream-agent-native-capability-map-and-protocol" />)

* `localization/` (19 files): message catalogs per area (core, agent resources, automation outcomes, consent banner, billing notices and more), default messages, actions to change locale. Upstream uses i18next and react-i18next.

## Eventiva form

* `i18n` contracts in core-contracts (message keys as Schema, ICU message format); runtime wraps one i18n library behind a neutral service (choose and record; i18next is upstream's choice and works on React Native).
* Actions `locale.set`, `locale.get`; locale and time zone live in user settings and in the screen-context projection so the agent answers in the user's language and formats.
* Rambo-UI components take message keys, never raw strings; a lint rule flags hard-coded user-facing strings.
* Bundles load per module and work offline.

## Terminology and module-pack requirements

Localization and domain terminology are separate layers. A tenant profile maps stable canonical concepts to event, community-role-play or other vocabulary without changing action, entity, permission, telemetry or API identifiers. Agents receive canonical meaning plus rendered terminology. Every module includes namespaced default messages, locale bundles and the terminology concepts it introduces in its validated manifest; catalogues are dynamically loadable, cacheable offline and removed cleanly on module deactivation. The same validation applies to first-party, tenant-private and community modules.

## Acceptance

Switch a user to a second locale and every screen and agent reply follows; dates and currency follow locale; a missing key fails CI; offline locale switch works.

## Depends on

<issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" /> (core contracts), Rambo-UI base components.

## Out of scope

Translating content users type (event descriptions).

comments.author: GitHub

comments.body:
Selectable terminology/phraseology decision confirmed by Jonathan:

Separate four independent layers:
1. Locale/language: en-GB canonical fallback, en-US and future languages; spelling, grammar, date/number/time formats.
2. Domain vocabulary: events, security, gaming/MDT, emergency operations and tenant-specific terminology overlays.
3. Operational/communication profile: UK JESIP/plain-language, agency-specific UK profiles, US public-safety/incident-command profiles where lawfully sourced, ICAO phraseology where lawfully sourced, and event-adapted derivatives.
4. Organisation overrides: versioned tenant terms/codes mapped to canonical Eventiva concepts.

User choice and shared safety:
- Users may select their preferred display locale and terminology profile. Stable canonical concept/action/status IDs remain stored and transmitted so analytics, permissions, agents and integrations do not depend on wording.
- UI can show preferred label plus canonical code/plain-language explanation on demand. Search accepts synonyms across installed profiles.
- Shared operational channels, voice/radio procedure, training exercises and safety-critical workflows also declare a channel/incident profile. Participants see a clear warning/dual label when their personal profile differs; spoken/read-back phraseology follows the shared channel profile to prevent dangerous mismatches.
- Persist the source and target profile/version with messages/forms/training/completion evidence so historical meaning remains reconstructable after updates.
- Agents receive canonical concepts plus active user and operational profiles and must reply in the selected terms without changing underlying action semantics.

Profile governance:
- Every profile records authority/source, jurisdiction, version/effective date, licence/reuse basis, intended context and mapping confidence.
- Do not copy or claim conformance to proprietary/restricted ICAO, emergency-service or industry material without the required permission. Prefer authoritative public definitions and separately licensed packs where necessary.
- “Event-adapted” profiles are labelled adaptations, not official emergency/aviation standards or endorsements.
- Profile tests verify round-trip mapping, ambiguity, plural/grammar/accessibility, agent interpretation and cross-profile handover.
- Training content can render for each profile while assessment evidence records the exact terminology/standard version taught.

Apply this to EVE-13 canonical taxonomy, EVE-28 localisation, EVE-71 MDT/live operations, EVE-245 training and EVE-244 foundational manifest/profile contracts.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
Correction from Jonathan: operational/domain terminology and phraseology are selected by the tenant administrator and apply consistently across the tenant, not chosen independently by each end user.

- Tenant policy selects the active domain vocabulary and operational/communication profile, with optional event/channel-specific profile only where explicitly governed for interoperability.
- End users cannot independently switch MDT/status/radio/operational terminology, because inconsistent wording within one tenant could create confusion and unsafe handovers.
- Personal preference remains available only for language/locale and accessibility presentation where it does not alter canonical operational meaning; tenant policy may also fix locale for regulated/shared forms.
- Admin changes require preview, mapping/ambiguity checks, training/content impact analysis, versioned activation and audit. Historical records retain the profile/version under which they were created.
- Cross-tenant or multi-agency collaboration displays canonical/plain-language equivalents and source profile labels without changing either tenant’s configured vocabulary.
- Agents use the tenant/event/channel profile consistently for every participant.

This supersedes the user-selectable terminology wording in the immediately preceding comment on each issue.

issues.title: Agent runs restart from scratch when their shard moves
issues.description:
## Goal

An agent run (long-lived, multi-step, streaming) survives a shard move or runner loss by resuming from its last completed step, never by re-running finished steps.

## Context

* Found in <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" />. Evidence: `/mnt/project-files/eve-18/` (scenario folders `drain` and `killnorestart`, `analysis.txt`, "long jobs" section).
* A persisted 25s entity RPC (`Long`) stood in for an agent run. With @effect/cluster 0.56.4:
  * SIGTERM of the owning runner: the runner waits up to `entityTerminationTimeout` (15s default) for the handler. When the run had more than 15s left it was interrupted (`long-interrupted`) and the new owner started it again from the beginning (first drain run: interrupted at +15s, restarted on the other runner, finished 25s later).
  * SIGKILL: the run restarted from the beginning on the surviving runner 36s later (killnorestart: start 22:21:51, restart 22:22:39, done 22:23:04).
* The caller still got one reply, so the reply is at-least-once-executed, exactly-once-replied. Any side effects inside the run (LLM spend, tool calls, emails, DMX output) would happen twice.
* <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> D3: sharding takes priority over agent convenience, so the fix belongs in how agent runs are modelled, not in pinning entities.

## Work

1. Model an agent run as an `@effect/workflow` workflow driven by `ClusterWorkflowEngine` (already in `@effect/cluster` 0.56.4; `@effect/workflow` is already a dependency of `packages/platforms/postgresql`). Each model call and each tool call is an `Activity` with an idempotency key of `runId:stepIndex`.
2. The run entity only starts, signals and queries the workflow; it never awaits the whole run inside a handler.
3. Add an Effect test with `@effect/vitest` and `TestRunner` (or two SQL runners against a test Postgres) that kills the owning runner between step 2 and step 3 and asserts steps 1 and 2 ran once and step 3 ran once after recovery.

## Acceptance

* The kill test passes; activity execution counts are asserted, not logged.
* A short doc in `ai-docs/src` explains "agent run = workflow; activity = one model or tool call; idempotency key = runId:step".

## Out of scope

Choosing the model provider, the streaming transport (see the streaming issue), Kubernetes.

## Done signal

Test green in `node --run check`; comment on this issue with the test name and its output.

issues.title: Keep a long agent run from blocking its entity's other messages
issues.description:
## Goal

A long-running agent step never blocks other messages to the same entity (cancel, status, user input, approvals).

## Context

* Found in <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" />. Evidence: `/mnt/project-files/eve-18/killnorestart/analysis.txt`, "per-entity outage" section.
* Cluster entity mailboxes process one message at a time by default. While `Long` (25s) ran on entities e-000..e-003, every `Deliver` to those entities waited behind it. Worst case e-003: 73s with no deliveries (36s failover plus a re-run of the 25s job plus queueing). Other entities saw at most 36s.
* For agents this means a "stop" or "approve" button would wait until the current step finishes.

## Work

1. Split the agent surface into two entity types: `AgentRun` (the workflow handle from the restart issue, one per run) and `AgentSession` (one per conversation, short handlers only: start run, cancel run, read status, post user input).
2. Handlers on `AgentSession` must return in under 1s; enforce with a test that sends `Cancel` while a run is mid-step and asserts the cancel reply arrives in under 1s.
3. If a handler legitimately needs concurrency, use `Entity.toLayer(..., { concurrency })` and document why.

## Acceptance

Cancel-while-busy test passes with the latency assertion.

## Out of scope

UI for cancel and approve.

## Done signal

Test green in `node --run check`; comment with the measured cancel latency.

issues.title: Stream agent output from a durable log, not volatile RPCs
issues.description:
## Goal

Agent token and event streams survive shard moves: a client that reconnects gets every chunk exactly once by offset.

## Context

* Found in <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" />. Evidence: `/mnt/project-files/eve-18/*/analysis.txt`, "volatile" sections.
* Non-persisted RPCs (`ClusterSchema.Persisted=false`, which is how `DemoEntity.Shoot` is declared today) are dropped when their shard is moving: 332 of 10,000 lost during a graceful drain, 1,751 lost on SIGKILL with a 20s restart, 4,238 lost on SIGKILL with failover. Persisted RPCs lost 0 in every run.
* Streaming RPC chunks are volatile by nature, so a stream that rides an entity RPC breaks on every shard move.

## Work

1. Each agent run appends output events to a Postgres table keyed by `(runId, offset)` from inside its activities (see the restart issue), in the same transaction as the step result where possible.
2. The client reads with "events after offset N" plus a notify (Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY` or polling at 200ms); on reconnect it resumes from its last offset.
3. Test: kill the runner that owns the run mid-stream; assert the client receives offsets 0..N with no gaps and no repeats.

## Acceptance

Gap-and-duplicate test passes against two runners.

## Out of scope

Choosing the client transport (SSE, WebSocket); AI SDK UI integration.

## Done signal

Test green; comment with the test output.

issues.title: Remove the shard-manager process that owns shards with no entities
issues.description:
## Goal

The compose and Kubernetes demo stacks run only processes that host the entities they own shards for.

## Context

* Found in <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" />. Evidence: `/mnt/project-files/eve-18/emptyrunner/`.
* @effect/cluster 0.56.4 has no shard manager; shard ownership is advisory locks in Postgres (`SqlRunnerStorage`). `packages/platforms/postgresql/src/shardManager.ts` launches `NodeClusterSocket.layer({ storage: "sql" })` with no entities, so it registers as a full runner and takes its share of shards.
* Reproduced with one entity runner plus `shardManager.ts`, 30 shards, 40 entities: 21 of 40 entities failed every message with `Entity type 'Probe' not registered`.
* `packages/cluster-compose/docker-compose.postgresql.yaml` runs a `shard-manager` service and `SHARDS_PER_GROUP=2`, so the demo loses roughly half its traffic once the shard-manager holds a shard.

## Work

1. Delete `packages/platforms/postgresql/src/shardManager.ts` and the MySQL equivalent if present; remove the `shard-manager` service and `depends_on` entries from the compose file and the Kubernetes manifests rendered by `platforms-postgresql:cluster:render`.
2. Replace it with a second `battleships` runner (`CLUSTER_APP_MODE=runner`) so the demo shows two runners.
3. Update `packages/cluster-tooling/cli/verify-cluster-demo-logs.ts` to assert both runners logged `Boom!` and no `not registered` errors.
4. Update people docs (`docs/parts/local-dev/three-tier-platform-runtime.md`) and agent docs.

## Acceptance

`pnpm cluster:compose:up` then `pnpm cluster:compose:verify-demo-logs` passes and shows two runners.

## Done signal

Comment with the verify output.

issues.title: Cut runner-loss failover from 36s and expose the cluster settings in config
issues.description:
## Goal

Runner loss is detected and its shards reassigned within a stated target (proposed: 10s), set through the platform's configuration schema, with sensible shard counts.

## Context

* Found in <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" />. Evidence: `/mnt/project-files/eve-18/killnorestart/`.
* SIGKILL of a runner: its shards were reassigned 36.2s later (kill 22:22:03.1, first delivery on the survivor 22:22:39.4), which is the 35s `shardLockExpiration` default. With a fast restart (20s) the killed runner reclaimed its own shards and the survivor never took them.
* SIGTERM: shards moved as soon as in-flight handlers finished or `entityTerminationTimeout` (15s) passed.
* `SHARDS_PER_GROUP` defaults to 2 in compose, `local-colocated-cluster-stack.ts` and FPK: at most two runners can ever hold shards. The library default is 300.
* `ShardingConfig` reads constant-case env vars (`HOST`, `PORT`, ...). `packages/databases/pg/src/pg-client-layer.ts` falls back to `PORT` and `HOST` for Postgres, so a runner without `PGPORT` tries to reach Postgres on its own cluster port (seen in <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" />: ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:34431).

## Work

1. Add a `cluster` section to the platform configuration schema (Effect `Config`, not ad hoc `process.env`): `shardsPerGroup` (default 300), `shardLockRefreshInterval` (default 3s), `shardLockExpiration` (default 10s), `entityTerminationTimeout` (default 15s), `runnerHealthCheckInterval`. Feed it into `NodeClusterSocket.layer({ shardingConfig })`.
2. Remove the `PORT` and `HOST` fallbacks from `pgClientConfigFromEnv`; Postgres reads `DB_*` only, matching `postgresClusterSqlLayer`.
3. Fix `makeClusterSqlRunnerLayer` and `makeClusterSqlClientLayer` in `packages/core/src/cluster/sql-socket-layers.ts`: their types claim to output `SqlClient` but they use `Layer.provide`, so callers fail at runtime with `Service not found: @effect/sql/SqlClient`. Use `Layer.provideMerge` and drop the casts.
4. Re-run the <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" /> `killnorestart` scenario and record the new failover time.

## Acceptance

Failover at or under the configured `shardLockExpiration` plus 3s, measured with the <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" /> harness; docs list every option with its default.

## Done signal

Comment with before and after timings.

issues.title: Make every entity action idempotent and persisted by default
issues.description:
## Goal

Every action that reaches an entity is persisted and carries an idempotency key, so the at-least-once delivery the cluster gives can never double-apply a change.

## Context

* Found in <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" />. Evidence: `/mnt/project-files/eve-18/kill/analysis.txt`.
* Persisted RPCs with a `PrimaryKey` lost nothing in any scenario and arrived in order per entity, but SIGKILL produced 12 duplicate handler executions out of 10,000 (messages in flight when the runner died were replayed on the new owner).
* Non-persisted RPCs are dropped during moves (up to 42%).
* `DemoEntity.Shoot` is declared `Persisted=false`, which is the wrong default to copy.

## Work

1. In the shared action contract (<issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> actions, Effect Schema), require an `idempotencyKey` on every mutating action and make it the RPC `PrimaryKey`.
2. Entity handlers write a `(entity, idempotencyKey)` row in the same transaction as the change and skip if it exists. Provide this as one core helper, not per handler.
3. Make `ClusterSchema.Persisted` true the default in the core entity helper; volatile needs an explicit opt-in with a comment.
4. Test with two SQL runners: kill one mid-stream and assert zero double-applied changes (count rows, not log lines).

## Acceptance

Duplicate test passes; the helper is used by the demo entity.

## Done signal

Comment with the test output.

issues.title: P1.1 Build the action contract and inventory in Effect Schema
issues.description:
## Binding action-boundary approval — 2026-11-14

Jonathan approved this architecture on 2026-11-14 after the <issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" />, <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />, <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> and <issue id="57425d1f-fae5-49c9-af1e-51cd26f64d20" label="EVE-244" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-244/scaffold-the-fresh-nx-expo-effect-and-testing-foundation" /> research review. This is architecture approval only: it does not start implementation, approve unlisted dependencies, provision services, change spending limits, or re-enable paid AI gates.

The action contract belongs in `@eventiva/contracts`, separate from Effect handlers. Portable specifications contain stable IDs, Effect Schema inputs/outputs, typed errors, descriptions, permissions, approvals and side-effect classes. Feature-owned handlers register one-to-one against those specifications and execute through `@eventiva/runtime`.

UI, mobile MDT, desktop/web, built-in/external agents and HTTP/MCP/ACP/other adapters are thin interfaces over the same authorized runtime invocation. The runtime resolves current identity and delegation for every call, enforces permissions/approvals, applies idempotency, emits audit/receipts and never exposes a privileged agent path. Capability parity means every supported operation is discoverable across interfaces under the caller's actual permissions.

Registration is scoped and all-or-nothing with typed duplicate/compatibility errors. Dynamic modules can register and unregister actions and manifests safely; disposal removes registrations and resources without changing core. Provider wire names may adapt stable canonical IDs without changing their meaning.

This supersedes any text that puts action definitions in the schema package, embeds backend handlers in client-imported specifications, or duplicates UI/agent logic.

## Goal

Every capability in Eventiva is one action, defined once in Effect Schema, listed in one inventory used by every supported surface (UI, HTTP, MCP, ACP, Effect AI Toolkit adapters and CLI).

## Context

* Phase-1 step 1 of the [S2 capability map](<https://linear.app/resnovas/document/s2-agent-native-capability-map-and-protocol-conformance-matrix-9a000bdd8953>). Upstream reference: BuilderIO/agent-native `@agent-native/core@0.222.2` (6b5cf68), root files of `packages/core/src` (defineAction, caller, invocation, receipts, input coercion, output contract, action-ui, framework tools), `shared/`, `json-schema/`.
* <issue id="07c58289-6f1c-488e-a130-5f718b473fce" label="EVE-14" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-14/s1-prove-one-effect-action-serves-ui-mcp-and-ai-sdk-from-one-inventory" /> (S1) proves the shape on one action; this issue builds the real package from its result.
* <issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" /> creates the portable contracts, shared schema and backend runtime boundaries. Action specifications live in `@eventiva/contracts`; handlers and invocation live in `@eventiva/runtime`.

## Scope

1. `defineAction` taking an Effect Schema input and output, a typed error union (`Data.TaggedError`), required permissions, approval policy (none, confirm, always), side-effect class (read, write, external) and a description written for the agent.
2. An inventory service (`Context.Tag`) listing every action with its metadata; registration fails at startup on duplicate names.
3. Provider-safe JSON Schema derived from the Effect Schema, carrying upstream's quirks from `json-schema/` (no unions at the root, flattened composed schemas, string formats the providers accept).
4. Action receipts: every call returns a receipt (who, what, input hash, outcome, duration) consumed by audit (P1.4) and the agent (P1.8).
5. A parity check (`nx` target) that fails when an action has no description, no permission, or is not reachable from every registered surface.

## Acceptance criteria

* Three sample actions (one read, one write, one external) defined and listed; JSON Schema output for each matches a committed snapshot accepted by Anthropic, OpenAI and Google tool schemas (snapshot test per provider rule).

comments.body:
## PROPOSAL - product decision cards (not approved)

These cards preserve the approved three-package architecture and the single authorized action path. They do not authorize implementation, dependencies or spending.

### Settled requirements - do not reopen

- Portable Effect action specifications are separate from feature-owned handlers; every UI, MDT, agent and protocol adapter uses the same runtime invocation.
- Identity and delegation resolve on every call; authorization is coarse-before-decode and resource-specific-after-decode.
- Approval policy can raise but never lower an action's floor. Only an interactive human can approve; an agent cannot approve its own call.
- Every mutating action has an idempotency key. The authoritative mutation and idempotency result are persisted together. Replays cannot double-apply.
- Every outcome has a receipt/audit record. PowerSync/Yjs does not create a bypass around the server Effect action.

### A1 - Integrity transaction boundary (most consequential)

**Recommend:** one authoritative transaction commits the domain mutation, idempotency record, state transition/history, outbox event and successful receipt together. Authorization and approval are rechecked before returning a replayed result. Keep financial, payment, ticket, stock and dispatch idempotency records for the business record's lifetime; lower-risk records may expire only after the compatibility/audit window.

**Alternatives:** separate stores or a short universal TTL.

**Consequences:** retries, runner failover, webhooks and offline MDT uploads cannot duplicate charges, allocations, stock deltas or dispatch transitions. Separate stores are simpler initially but permit partial success and ambiguous retries.

### A2 - Human and AI approval policy

**Recommend:** direct human low-risk reversible actions need no second confirmation; agent writes default to `confirm`; irreversible, financial, permission, payment/refund, ticket-capacity, stock-commitment and live-production actions use `always` with fresh human approval/step-up. Bind approval to principal, tenant, action version, canonical input hash, maximum amount/quantity and expiry. A planned batch may use one approval only when the exact item set and aggregate limits are bound.

**Alternatives:** confirm every write, or let each tenant lower defaults.

**Consequences:** agents remain useful for routine work while money, scarce capacity and live operations cannot be silently committed. Tenants may raise policy, never lower the action floor.

### A3 - Offline MDT, dispatch and scheduled execution

**Recommend:** ordinary reversible edits may queue offline. Guarded stock, tickets, assignments and lifecycle changes queue only an intent carrying expected version/state plus idempotency key; the server revalidates and conflicts become an explicit user task, never silent last-write-wins. Payments and live show/dispatch control are online-only. A dispatch request may queue only with an action-specific deadline and must never execute after expiry. Scheduled work stores `notBefore`, deadline, dependency state and approved bounds; execution rechecks permission, approval validity, capacity and state.

**Alternatives:** auto-apply queued guarded changes, or forbid all offline writes.

**Consequences:** MDT users can keep working without falsely promising tickets, stock, payment or live-control success. Production dependencies fail closed instead of executing stale instructions.

### A4 - Audit availability

**Recommend:** writes and privileged/sensitive reads fail closed when their durable receipt cannot be recorded. Low-risk reads may proceed only through a bounded local audit spool with a visible degraded-health signal and eventual persistence; exhausting the spool fails closed.

**Alternatives:** fail every call closed, or treat audit as best effort.

**Consequences:** integrity operations remain provable without turning a temporary audit outage into a total read outage. Best-effort audit would contradict EVE-43.

**Owner decisions requested:** approve/amend A1-A4. The auth-provider choice remains a separate EVE-43 card.

comments.body:
## APPROVED - three offline execution categories (2026-11-14)

Jonathan approved this policy as the Eventiva default. This approval is limited to the three categories below; A1, A2, A4 and every S-card remain proposals unless separately approved.

1. **Routine work:** crew task/status updates, checklists and notes may queue durably offline and synchronize with visible conflicts.
2. **Authoritative operations:** dispatch allocation, stock reservations, ticket capacity and payment/financial commitments require an authoritative service. Offline preparation is allowed, but an unconfirmed allocation or commitment must never be shown as successful.
3. **Safety-sensitive operations:** show control and safety-critical output follow explicitly approved procedures, current authorization, and validated local-execution/degraded-mode requirements. Offline access never relaxes safety policy.

Tenants may configure policy where safe. Mandatory safeguards are immutable and cannot be weakened by tenant configuration, feature flags, agents or offline mode.

This aligns with [EVE-71](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-71/f7-fleet-and-live-operations-vehicles-maintenance-units-dispatch-and) and [EVE-147](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-147/f77-build-the-incident-control-log-and-dispatch-for-live-events): crew status/log work may queue, while dispatch assignment remains authoritative and online-only; safety-critical control needs a separate validated safety case.
