comments.body:
## APPROVED - A1 integrity transaction boundary (2026-11-14)

Jonathan approved A1 as recommended.

For each successful authoritative mutation, one transaction atomically commits:

- the domain change;
- the deduplication/idempotency result;
- the state transition and append-only history;
- the outbox event; and
- the receipt/audit record.

Retries and replays revalidate current authorization and any required approval before a stored result is returned. Idempotency evidence for payments, ticketing, stock and dispatch is retained for the lifetime of the business record.

This decision binds the action runtime to [EVE-39](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-39/make-every-entity-action-idempotent-and-persisted-by-default) and the transactional storage work in [EVE-42](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state). It preserves the separately approved three offline execution categories: a queued intent is not an authoritative success.

A2, A4 and S1-S4 remain PROPOSAL unless separately approved. This is a product decision, not implementation authorization.

comments.body:
## APPROVED — A2, A3 and A4 foundation policy (2026-11-15)

Jonathan approved all three together.

### A2 — Human and AI approvals
Direct human low-risk reversible writes need no extra confirmation. Agents may execute only preauthorized bounded routine work under the caller's live scopes; other agent writes default to `confirm`. Irreversible, financial, payment/refund, permission, ticket-capacity, stock-commitment and live-production actions require `always` with fresh human approval/step-up as applicable. Approval binds principal, tenant, action/version, canonical input/hash, amount/quantity limits and expiry; batches bind exact items and aggregate limits. Tenants may raise but never weaken the floor. Agents cannot self-approve.

### A3 — Offline, MDT and scheduled execution
Routine reversible edits durably queue as pending. Guarded assignments, stock, tickets and lifecycle work queue explicit intents with expected state/version, idempotency key and deadline, then receive online authoritative revalidation and visible conflicts—never silent LWW. Payments and live dispatch/show control are online-only unless a separately validated safety-specific local profile governs its own behavior. Expired dispatch instructions never execute. Scheduled jobs recheck `notBefore`, deadline, dependencies, permissions, capacity, state and approval validity, and preserve immutable baseline versus live forecast.

### A4 — Audit outage
Mutations and privileged/sensitive reads fail closed if their durable receipt cannot be recorded. Low-risk reads may use only a capacity-bounded durable local audit spool with visible degradation and eventual persistence; exhaustion fails closed. Protected audit is never best effort.

### Acceptance tests
- Agent self-approval, stale approval, wrong principal/tenant/action/version/input, expired approval and bound-limit overflow are denied.
- A batch changed after approval is denied; tenants can raise but cannot lower the floor.
- Guarded offline intents reject stale state visibly; expired dispatch never runs; scheduled work rechecks every gate at execution.
- Mutations and sensitive reads fail when receipt persistence fails; low-risk reads spool durably until capacity and then fail closed; recovery drains exactly once.

Architecture approval only: no new dependency, provider, infrastructure, spending or security exception is approved. [Decision sheet](https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-architecture-decisions-3169b540-652d-4795-ae9c-7ad78a534f17).

issues.title: P1.2 Build app config, settings, secrets and credentials
issues.description:
## Goal

One place for configuration, per-user and per-tenant settings, and secrets and credentials that agents can use without ever seeing them.

## Context

* Phase-1 step 2 of the S2 capability map. Upstream reference at 6b5cf68: `app-config/`, `settings/`, `secrets/`, `credentials/` in `packages/core/src`.
* Credentials are what user-owned AI subscriptions (<issue id="a904aa60-b3c7-4bfa-8d2d-995d1e679389" label="EVE-20" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-20/s7-find-which-ai-providers-allow-users-to-bring-their-own-subscription" />) and external connections hang off.

## Scope

1. App config resolved through Effect `Config` and validated by Effect Schema; no environment-variable feature switches (house feature-flags rule).
2. Settings store with scopes user, tenant and app, each setting declared with a schema and exposed as read and write actions (P1.1).
3. Secrets store: encrypted at rest with a key from config, write-only to the UI, never returned in action output, prompts, logs or telemetry (a redaction test proves this).
4. Credentials: a secret bound to an endpoint, owner and scope, with expiry and revocation; agent tools receive a handle, not the value, and the HTTP client resolves it at call time.

## Acceptance criteria

* A test sets a secret, uses it through a credential handle in an outbound call against a stub server, and asserts the value appears in no log, span, action output or agent message.
* Revoking a credential makes the next call fail with a typed `CredentialRevoked` error.
* Settings read and write actions appear in the inventory and pass the parity check.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; no vendor secret manager coupling (a port with an in-database default); no new dependency without approval here; ship to main with check results.

## Done signal

Merged to main with the redaction test green, and a comment listing the setting and credential actions.

## Modular-platform implementation increment (2026-11-15)

Canonical spec: [https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c>). Preserve the full settings/credential scope above; this adds the required kernel bootstrap seam. Decode versioned external manifests/composition with Schema; load deployment/provider config through Config and layer-local ConfigProvider, never raw env reads in features. ModuleDefinition.validate is typed Effect, uses redacted failures and performs no feature mutation. Instance Config is namespaced by {module,instance}; no mutable global provider choice. Secrets use Config.redacted/Redacted or opaque credential handles and cannot appear in Schema errors, JSON/string/inspect/Cause trees, prompts, telemetry, projections or events. Invalid required config fails before any module registration/layer publication; valid config composes two independent provider instances.

Acceptance evidence: valid and invalid bootstrap/config matrices, unknown/missing fields, revoked/expired credential handles, secret canary negative serialization at every named surface, no partial registration and no provider-instance contamination. Config settings are not feature flags or authorization. Pure portable schemas/ports in contracts; any secret provider in integrations, wiring in app composition. Reserve concrete new paths with coordinator before coding; shared manifests/generated docs stay held. <issue id="ceb453e5-ab8e-4566-bf54-47d742b0f425" label="EVE-257" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-257/implement-the-composable-module-kernel-and-safe-lifecycleprovider" /> can checkpoint its validate seam before full credential-store delivery, but full <issue id="b025ea11-9298-48b2-9bd4-d44decabcab4" label="EVE-261" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-261/integrate-the-modular-platform-and-prove-every-owner-required" /> acceptance remains blocked on this evidence. AI-authored planning addition; no package/crypto/provisioning approval implied.

## Modular extensions: configuration, capability and secret boundary (2026-11-15)

Extensions declare typed, versioned, namespace-scoped config defaults and overrides; validation occurs before activation and on hot update, with audit, safe rollback, feature-flag gate and no raw env/secret access. Tenant/user settings use authorized actions. Subscriptions to <issue id="afb95d96-359d-4c0f-a462-a7ce41e2c988" label="EVE-262" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-262/implement-governed-observation-only-execution-and-lifecycle-hooks-with" /> events never grant decryption, credentials or keys. Restricted/Vault event projection is a separate policy-mediated, minimally disclosed service; credentials are resolved only by approved adapters and revoked before any subsequent side-effect delivery. Test malicious config, logs/spans/console leakage, revoked grants, failure to validate, isolated module instances and pre-telemetry bootstrap redaction. Align <issue id="4f5ecaa3-aedf-446d-8993-0c07c98d4bb4" label="EVE-251" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251/decide-marketplace-service-attestation-and-cryptographic-trust" /> and <issue id="ceb453e5-ab8e-4566-bf54-47d742b0f425" label="EVE-257" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-257/implement-the-composable-module-kernel-and-safe-lifecycleprovider" />. No provider/dependency authorization implied.

issues.title: P1.3 Build the storage layer: Drizzle on Postgres and SQLite, state machines and tenant guards
issues.description:
## Binding storage architecture — 2026-11-15

Jonathan approved S1-S4 and the three offline execution categories. <issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" /> and the migration guard are landed. The approved SQL-only first increment was delivered to main on 2026-11-15 with exact-head CI green at [e0914e34](<https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/commit/e0914e34450e6f6c103e0ae3d2d83134484e0273>).

This issue remains In Progress, not Done: deferred Drizzle/device scope, production least-privilege acceptance and <issue id="55c2d64a-d779-41d9-b74e-dcc7d062b86b" label="EVE-252" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-252/implement-effect-cluster-sharding-and-multi-runner-recovery-in-the" /> Phase B SQL/process recovery are not completed by this increment. [Delivery evidence](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eve-42-sql-evidence-6f270af4-a889-4337-98aa-0ff0f25804db>).

## Goal

Provide one portable storage contract with Postgres/Neon server and SQLite Node conformance, typed state machines and tenant database routing, while keeping drivers out of shared/client packages.

## Approved rules

* S1: one logical operational database per tenant, selected only after authentication through explicit scoped routing; a narrow shared control plane holds identity/routing/provisioning metadata. No routine cross-tenant operational queries.
* S2: authoritative append-only ledgers/deltas, expiring reservations and typed CAS state machines for scarce resources; online-only provider payment actions plus idempotent reconciliation; dispatch/scheduled production leases, deadlines and transition history; exact money values.
* S3: typed raw PowerSync tables and explicit device migrations for canonical offline records; JSON only for projections; explicit guarded command envelopes and visible conflicts through the same server Effect action.
* S4: forward-only checksum-verified expand-and-contract migrations, compatibility windows and tested restore/branch recovery; UUIDv7, Postgres `timestamptz`, SQLite epoch milliseconds, exact decimal strings and no tenant ID in physically isolated tenant primary keys.
* The old tenant-predicate query guard is superseded by tenant database routing. The old mandatory down-migration guard is superseded by S4.

## Planned scope

* Portable database capabilities, errors and state-machine contracts.
* Tenant database router and scoped current-tenant context.
* Database-neutral column/sync declarations in `@eventiva/schema`.
* Driver integrations for approved Postgres and SQLite packages, dialect projections and platform integrity tables.
* Forward-only migration generation and a dependency-free storage guard rejecting `drizzle push`, changed applied checksums and unannotated destructive changes.
* One conformance suite for SQLite in memory and PostgreSQL in CI; a Postgres service job feeds required `application check`.

## Acceptance

* Both dialect suites pass the same storage conformance contract.
* Concurrent reservation tests prove no oversell/negative availability; stale CAS, illegal transitions and expired leases fail with typed errors.
* Payment retries reconcile exactly once; rollback leaves no receipt or outbox record; replay returns the stored receipt.
* Device migrations and explicit guarded-envelope fields are verified; stale offline commands surface visible conflicts.
* Tenant routing cannot cross operational databases; control-plane access remains explicitly scoped and audited.
* UUIDv7, temporal and exact-decimal round trips pass.
* The dependency-free storage guard runs in root `check`; package-backed conformance runs in `verify` and required `application check`.

## Dependency gate

The owner approved only @effect/sql@0.52.2, @effect/sql-pg@0.53.1, @effect/sql-sqlite-node@0.54.1, development-only @types/pg@8.23.1, locked pg@8.23.1 and better-sqlite3@13.0.3, PostgreSQL 17, and the exact Bookworm image digest recorded in delivery evidence. No better-sqlite3 build script was authorized or enabled; its bundled prebuild executed.

The exact postgres:17.12-bookworm digest 40865bc877a289da75963d97d72b59633f639fc5af7a4e856bfa3714cae5b536 has a bounded owner exception only for isolated disposable synthetic local/CI testing, expiring 2026-11-22 UTC or earlier on a relevant exploit/input/fix/rebuild trigger. Its 4 critical/140 high/231 medium/190 low/11 unknown scan findings remain unsuppressed. No production use, Trixie adoption, provider/paid infrastructure, CDC or broader waiver is authorized. Fixtures use generated SCRAM credentials, loopback/dedicated bridge, resource/time limits and teardown; CI fails closed at expiry and for PR/dispatch code rather than skipping conformance.

Other dependencies and the deferred scope still require their own owner approval.

## Delivery

After <issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" /> and the dependency gate, implement on current main under Eventiva's direct-to-main exception, preserve Smartcloud/$0 AI safeguards, run required checks and record evidence here.

## Verified SQL-only delivery evidence (2026-11-15)

Agent-authored delivery record. ## PROPOSAL - storage and consistency decision cards (not approved)

These cards preserve the approved package architecture and EVE-17 decision. They do not authorize implementation, dependencies, provisioning or spending.

### Settled requirements - do not reopen

- PowerSync self-hosted Open Edition handles record sync; Yjs handles text/canvas with updates carried through PowerSync. Electric/TanStack DB is only the licence fallback.
- Every authoritative write passes through the same server Effect action, permission check and audit path.
- Default record fields merge per field; guarded status/money/assignment/dispatch changes use expected state/version and reject conflicts; quantities use append-only deltas; Yjs governs documents/canvas; live operations are online-only.
- Revocation immediately removes the bucket and destroys open Yjs documents, presence and undo state.
- Effect v3 and portable schema/runtime boundaries are already approved.

### S1 - Tenant isolation topology (most consequential)

**Recommend:** one logical database/branch per tenant for tenant data, selected by an authenticated routing service; a narrowly scoped shared control-plane database holds tenant directory/routing only. Use RLS as defence in depth on shared control-plane tables, not as the primary tenant boundary. PowerSync gets a separate replication role and bucket authorization.

**Alternatives:** shared tenant tables with RLS, or database-per-tenant with no control-plane RLS.

**Consequences:** a missing query predicate cannot cross tenant data boundaries, while routing and lifecycle operations remain manageable. This increases provisioning/migration orchestration and requires explicit cross-tenant administration paths.

### S2 - Integrity model for tickets, stock, payments and production state

**Recommend:** tickets/stock/capacity are server-authoritative ledgers: append-only deltas plus expiring reservation state machines; availability is derived and cannot go below zero. Payments are online-only external actions with idempotent authorization/capture/refund commands and a local reconciliation ledger. Dispatch and scheduled production dependencies use typed compare-and-set state machines with leases, deadlines and append-only transition history. Money uses currency plus exact decimal/minor-unit representation, never floating point.

**Alternatives:** mutable counters/LWW, provider-only payment state, or generic status strings.

**Consequences:** offline MDT may draft or queue requests but cannot promise scarce inventory or payment success. Concurrent winners are explicit; stale requests return typed conflicts. Reconciliation and audit remain possible after provider or runner failures.

### S3 - Device schema and guarded-write envelope

**Recommend:** use raw PowerSync tables for authoritative typed offline records and explicit device migrations; reserve JSON projections for derived/read models. Carry expected version/state, idempotency key, client mutation ID and deadline in an explicit command envelope, not hidden metadata.

**Alternatives:** PowerSync JSON views everywhere, `trackMetadata`, or `trackPreviousValues`.

**Consequences:** stronger type/index support and inspectable conflict semantics across MDT/web/server, at the cost of device migration work. Hidden metadata is easier initially but couples correctness to sync-engine internals.

### S4 - Migration and canonical value policy

**Recommend:** forward-only expand-and-contract migrations with checksum enforcement and restore/branch rollback; no routine hand-written down migration promise. Use UUIDv7 IDs, Postgres `timestamptz`, SQLite epoch milliseconds behind one temporal schema, exact decimal strings at portable boundaries, and no tenant ID in domain primary keys when tenant data is physically isolated.

**Alternatives:** mandatory handwritten down SQL, ISO timestamp text on SQLite, composite `(tenant_id,id)` keys.

**Consequences:** safer evolution for old offline clients and fewer misleading rollback guarantees. Destructive changes require staged compatibility windows and explicit recovery plans.

**Owner decisions requested:** approve/amend S1-S4. PostgreSQL major, native package versions and service provisioning remain later implementation approvals.

## APPROVED - three offline execution categories (2026-11-14)

Jonathan approved this policy as the Eventiva default. This approval is limited to these categories; S1-S4 and the remaining A-cards are still proposals unless separately approved.

1. **Routine work:** crew task/status updates, checklists and notes may queue durably offline and synchronize with visible conflicts.
2. **Authoritative operations:** dispatch allocation, stock reservations, ticket capacity and payment/financial commitments require an authoritative service. Offline preparation is allowed, but an unconfirmed allocation or commitment must never be shown as successful.
3. **Safety-sensitive operations:** show control and safety-critical output follow explicitly approved procedures, current authorization, and validated local-execution/degraded-mode requirements. Offline access never relaxes safety policy.

Tenants may configure safe behaviour, but mandatory integrity and safety safeguards are immutable. Storage and sync must represent pending, confirmed, rejected and expired outcomes distinctly; a queued intent is not a committed allocation.

Product examples: [EVE-71](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-71/f7-fleet-and-live-operations-vehicles-maintenance-units-dispatch-and) and [EVE-147](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-147/f77-build-the-incident-control-log-and-dispatch-for-live-events). ## APPROVED — S2, S3 and S4 foundation policy (2026-11-15)

Jonathan approved all three together.

### S2 — Integrity
Tickets, stock and capacity use authoritative append-only deltas/ledgers, expiring reservations and typed compare-and-set state machines; availability cannot oversell or become negative. Payments are online-only provider actions with idempotent local reconciliation. Dispatch and scheduled production use CAS state machines with leases, deadlines and transition history. Money uses exact currency minor units or decimal strings, never binary floating point.

### S3 — Offline device contract
Canonical offline records use typed raw PowerSync tables with explicit device migrations; JSON projections are only derived/read models. Guarded command envelopes explicitly carry expected state/version, idempotency key, client mutation ID and deadline, and use the same Effect server action path with visible conflicts.

### S4 — Migration and values
Migrations are forward-only, checksum-verified expand-and-contract with offline-client compatibility windows and tested restore/branch recovery. This supersedes the blanket down-step requirement. IDs are UUIDv7; Postgres uses `timestamptz`; SQLite uses epoch milliseconds behind one temporal contract; portable decimals are exact strings; physically isolated tenant DB primary keys omit tenant ID while routing/auth remains tenant-scoped.

### Acceptance tests
- Concurrent reservation/ledger tests prove no oversell or negative availability; stale CAS and expired leases fail with typed errors; payment retries reconcile once.
- Raw device tables migrate explicitly; guarded envelopes expose every required field; stale offline commands become visible conflicts through the server action path.
- Migration checks reject changed applied checksums, `drizzle push`, and unannotated destructive changes; old-client compatibility and restore/branch recovery are tested.
- UUIDv7 ordering/uniqueness, Postgres/SQLite temporal round trips, exact decimal round trips and tenant-router isolation are covered.

Architecture approval only. EVE-42 dependency versions, PostgreSQL major, providers and infrastructure remain unapproved. [Decision sheet](https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-architecture-decisions-3169b540-652d-4795-ae9c-7ad78a534f17).

## BINDING Neon CDC / PowerSync cost and compatibility gate — 2026-11-15

Fresh official Neon guidance confirms logical replication is enabled per project, permanently changes `wal_level` to `logical`, cannot be reverted, and restarts every compute. A connected subscriber prevents scale-to-zero and can create continuous compute cost. Inactive slots are removed after about 40 hours without acknowledged `flush_lsn`; branch restore removes slots. Neon supports at most 10 WAL senders and 10 replication slots by default.

For Eventiva/PowerSync, CDC must use a direct Neon endpoint without the `-pooler` suffix and a correctly privileged dedicated replication role; persistent replication is incompatible with PgBouncer pooling. Runtime Effect SQL queries must test pooled and direct paths separately. Do not enable replication or run tests on the existing historical PG16 Frankfurt project.

Plan the first London PG17 synthetic test project with replication disabled. Any later PowerSync/CDC integration trial requires separate owner approval, synthetic-only data, direct endpoint, measured active time, slot lag/retention and cost evidence before broad enablement. This is especially material for the project-per-tenant production model. A Neon branch remains a test-isolation mechanism, not equivalent production tenant isolation.

Official sources refreshed 2026-11-15:
- https://neon.com/docs/guides/logical-replication-guide (updated 2026-10-21)
- https://neon.com/docs/guides/logical-replication-neon (updated 2026-10-09)

Do not silently discard the approved PowerSync design if economics or scaling fail. Return an evidence-backed architecture proposal for owner decision.

Enumerate identities/integrity/provenance/licences/SBOM/vulnerabilities before use; preserve the security gates and escalate materially different components or findings. No production provisioning, paid infrastructure or weakened security policy is authorized. Older comments remain intact as historical evidence.

## BINDING OWNER DECISION — Keycloak as the Eventiva identity provider (2026-11-15)

Jonathan explicitly chose **Keycloak** as Eventiva's primary identity and SSO platform and authorized starting <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" /> implementation. **Pin the implementation/proof target to candidate Keycloak 26.8.2**, subject to verifying the exact container manifest, supply chain, protocol behavior and compatibility before using it; do not silently upgrade/change its version. ZITADEL is no longer a co-equal selection candidate, though standard provider-neutral interfaces and documented exit/migration paths remain mandatory.

**Architecture and operating models**

* Keycloak operates as Eventiva's central authentication/identity service: interactive login, credentials, sessions, MFA/passkeys and SSO. It must be usable in self-hosted Community without Eventiva Cloud as well as in Cloud/Production (independent resilience/HA topology).
* Keycloak must act **outbound** as an OpenID Connect provider/OAuth 2 authorization server and SAML 2.0 IdP for authorized first-party and external application clients, and **inbound** as identity broker for enterprise OIDC/SAML IdPs, social logins, and LDAP/Active Directory/Kerberos where available.
* Test enterprise federation, realm/organization selection, user account linking, SCIM user/group provisioning/deprovisioning where supported, passkeys/WebAuthn MFA and step-up, logout, rotation/revocation, client/service credentials, tokens/audiences/scopes, and correct degraded operation when upstream IdPs fail.
* Document **non-universal** coverage of legacy SSO/SSO-like protocols and variants (e.g. WS-Federation, CAS, SAML 1.x), and separately scope any extensions/bridges. No unsupported claim that *all* possible SAML or OAuth implementations are compatible.
* Eventiva itself owns canonical identity-to-tenant membership mapping, resource-level RBAC/ABAC/capability policies, agent delegation, human approval gates, tenant database routing and durable audit; Keycloak-issued token claims are not an authorization bypass. A user can belong to multiple tenants, potentially with different federated enterprise IdPs.
* Enforce the same delegated-authorized Effect action pathway for human UI, API, agents and all protocols. No direct client DB/API access or automatic identity claims granting rights in other tenant databases. Prevent implicit self-approval, unsafe token exchange impersonation, and tenant cross-link collisions.
* Keep vendor adapters in backend integration packages: portable contracts, portable schema and authorized core runtime must not directly depend on Keycloak SDK APIs. Supports standards-based OIDC/SAML independent interface and a documented replacement path.

**Implementation authorization and dependency gate**
Owner authorization covers choosing Keycloak and progressing <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" /> implementation, including code and tests that use already-approved dependencies and nonconflicting paths, with signed, checked conventional direct-to-main delivery under Eventiva's exception. It does **not** automatically approve unlisted npm dependencies, image versions/digests, new paid infrastructure, external accounts, paid services, changing Neon/production settings, or lowering security gates. Verify the exact version/security/SBOM and submit any new package/version and container digest for explicit approval in a consolidated batch. Synthetic, local-only proof planning and implementation scaffolding need no new provider provisioning. If executable Keycloak container proof needs an unapproved image, ask for its digest acceptance before pulling/running.

* Prioritize <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" /> after completed <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />, <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> and <issue id="55c2d64a-d779-41d9-b74e-dcc7d062b86b" label="EVE-252" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-252/implement-effect-cluster-sharding-and-multi-runner-recovery-in-the" /> SQL foundation. Initial implementation slices: portable identity/subject/federation models and stable IDs; Eventiva-owned org/member/role/user-profile actions with SQL-authoritative membership, authorized action binding and audit; standards-focused token issuer/audience and scope validation seam with mock/test provider; first-party/third-party SSO, SCIM, enterprise federation and step-up conformance matrix, then Keycloak concrete adapter and executable integration tests once exact components are approved.
* Keep schema, tenant routing, gateway and runner boundaries consistent with <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" />/<issue id="55c2d64a-d779-41d9-b74e-dcc7d062b86b" label="EVE-252" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-252/implement-effect-cluster-sharding-and-multi-runner-recovery-in-the" />; do not overwrite dirty work of any concurrent orb. No PRs.

Previous <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" /> text that says the auth provider is undecided is superseded by this explicit owner choice; remaining work is exact version/dependency/security validation and implementation, not provider selection.

## Goal

One permission check that people and agents both pass through, with every call audited and tenants fully isolated.

## Context

* Phase-1 step 4 of the S2 capability map. Upstream reference at 6b5cf68: `org/` (orgs, teams, SCIM on better-auth), `authorization/`, `user-profile/`, `audit/`.
* Decided D2: Eventiva owns auth. Keycloak 26.8.2 is selected; the 2026-11-16 owner comment governs the reviewed exact image/OIDC dependency batch. Provider-neutral tenant membership, authorization and audit remain Eventiva-owned.

## Scope

1. Tenants, members, teams and roles as Eventiva tables (P1.3) with actions for membership changes.
2. An authorization service evaluated once per action call (P1.1) for any principal: user, agent acting for a user, service, or external agent; the agent never gets more than the user it acts for.
3. Approvals: actions marked confirm or always pause and wait for the user, on screen and through every protocol surface.
4. Audit log of every action call from the receipt, with redaction of secret-marked fields and read scopes for tenant admins.
5. User profile actions.

## Acceptance criteria

* A test matrix proves: cross-tenant read denied; agent acting for a viewer cannot write; an approval-required action does not run until approved; every call writes one audit row.
* Verify the selected Keycloak 26.8.2 integration against its reviewed exact image/dependency batch and protocol/security matrix; report unexecuted lanes and unresolved security findings without claiming production readiness.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; no vendor lock-in to an auth SaaS without the decision; no new dependency without approval here; ship to main with check results.

## Done signal

Merged with the matrix green and the audit table queryable by a tenant admin action.

## Modular lifecycle/resource/hook audit boundary (2026-11-15)

Spec [https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c>); <issue id="b025ea11-9298-48b2-9bd4-d44decabcab4" label="EVE-261" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-261/integrate-the-modular-platform-and-prove-every-owner-required" /> integration gate. Preserve approved Keycloak direction/version/supply-chain gates and all existing identity scope; no new provider selection here. KernelAuthority uses existing Caller; Resources checks tenant/principal/authorization per operation; hook release checks current scoped grant/revocation every attempt. Tamper-evident mandatory audit is separate from optional telemetry and cannot be disabled by telemetry opt-out. Atomic write/outbox/history/audit uses same Storage.transaction; sensitive/privileged operations fail closed when required durable evidence cannot persist. Tests include self-approval, tenant switching, revoked subscription/credential, secret/Cause serialization, audit sink outage vs telemetry outage and replay. Four independent protected-release gates and assurance floors remain <issue id="4f5ecaa3-aedf-446d-8993-0c07c98d4bb4" label="EVE-251" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251/decide-marketplace-service-attestation-and-cryptographic-trust" />/13 constraints. No cryptographic algorithm/dependency/provisioning approved by this addition. AI-authored planning addition.

## Session identifier versus authentication proof — acceptance requirement (2026-11-17)

A `SessionId` UUID is a non-secret correlation identifier, never a credential or bearer capability. Knowing or supplying a session UUID must grant no access. Every externally reachable caller must prove possession of a separately protected credential (for example a verified short-lived token, signed service assertion or equivalent approved mechanism); trusted identity resolution then maps that proof to the subject and session before Eventiva authorization runs.

The fixed `shellCaller` / `ShellIdentity` UUID in `apps/server/src/access.ts` is permitted only inside the current non-networked registration diagnostic. Replace or isolate that exact-value resolver before any HTTP, RPC, agent or other untrusted transport can invoke it. Acceptance tests must prove that a copied/guessed SessionId without valid credential proof is denied, expired/revoked proof is denied, and authenticated identity still receives only Eventiva-owned tenant membership and action permissions. Session IDs may appear in source, traces or logs only under the normal correlation/redaction policy; credentials, tokens and proof material must never do so.

## EVE-43 enterprise identity and federation acceptance requirements — 2026-11-15

Owner clarified that Eventiva needs an identity platform capable of **both central user/login management and acting as an external-facing SSO/OAuth/OIDC identity provider**, **while also brokering/federating external enterprise identities**. The provider must be evaluated in BOTH directions; simply supporting login *to* Eventiva does not satisfy the requirement.

**Required protocol/capability matrix for the bounded provider comparison and test plan:**
- **Outbound provider role:** Eventiva authentication authority must act as OIDC OpenID Provider / OAuth 2 authorization server for first-party clients and permitted third-party applications, and as SAML 2.0 Identity Provider for SAML service providers; confirm scopes, clients, credentials, refresh/revocation, logout, signing, metadata/discovery and SSO.
- **Inbound broker role:** consume enterprise SAML 2.0 Identity Providers and OIDC (and compatible OAuth 2 where identity attributes can be safely resolved), plus social IdPs; map external subject identity into stable Eventiva identities with explicit account linking and collision prevention.
- **Federated directories:** LDAP/Active Directory/Kerberos where supported, including local-account fallback, MFA/passkey/step-up, enterprise conditional policies and secure authentication-context propagation.
- **Provisioning:** SCIM 2.0 inbound create/update/deprovision for users and groups where supported; explicitly distinguish outbound SCIM client/synchronization and unsupported optional SCIM capabilities. Keycloak 26.8.2 documentation confirms supported SCIM Realm API, enabled at server level by default but still configured per realm; test access boundaries and org group semantics.
- **Multi-organization account model:** one stable human identity may belong to multiple Eventiva tenant organizations; individual customer organizations may bring distinct external SAML/OIDC providers, and membership/delegation must not imply cross-tenant operational DB access. Evaluate Keycloak Organizations and realm organization mapping, self-hosted Community deployment, migrations and account lifecycle.
- **Agents:** OAuth2 service identity, user-delegated authority, consent, token audience and scoped permissions; do not rely on preview/legacy token-exchange impersonation to bypass Eventiva's own authorized Effect action path, fresh human approvals or audit. Eventiva remains authoritative over tenant/resource/action permission grants.
- **Legacy/edge standards:** identify unsupported protocols/profile variants (e.g., SAML v1, WS-Federation, CAS, nonstandard enterprise SAML claims, proprietary SSO APIs) instead of asserting universal compatibility; document vetted bridges/adapters, certificates, logout/rotation and compliance limitations.
- **Security acceptance tests:** SAML both directions, OIDC both directions, cross-tenant account linking, role and membership revocation, SCIM deprovision, logout/back-channel logout, passkeys/MFA/step-up with authn context, issuer/audience validation, failure/availability and IdP outage.

**Research status:** Keycloak 26.8.2 is the current recommended candidate; ZITADEL 4.20.3 is an alternative. Keycloak provider selection, new dependencies, container execution, identity database provisioning and production rollout remain separately approval-gated. This comment defines evaluation scope rather than authorizing deployment.

Official references:
- https://www.keycloak.org/docs/26.8.0/server_admin/
- https://www.keycloak.org/docs/26.8.2/upgrading/
- https://www.keycloak.org/securing-apps/token-exchange
- https://www.keycloak.org/2026/07/keycloak-2670-released

issues.description:
## Goal

Every action, agent turn and protocol call is traced through OpenTelemetry, and product analytics, errors and flags go through a port with PostHog as the default adapter.

## Context

* Phase-1 step 5 of the S2 capability map. Upstream reference at 6b5cf68: `observability/`, `tracking/` (includes `posthog-exception.ts`), `packages/otel` (replace with `@effect/opentelemetry`).
* <issue id="dacc06d5-e888-47f3-8eae-91a9e0f60172" label="EVE-21" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-21/remove-sentry-from-core-and-make-telemetry-export-vendor-neutral" /> removes Sentry; <issue id="a5a3ce16-9f4f-484c-9a58-4562bfc9e5b3" label="EVE-19" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-19/s6-map-posthog-and-opentelemetry-support-across-web-native-and-backend" /> (S6) maps what PostHog supports per platform. D4: vendor-neutral, easy to switch.

## Scope

1. `@effect/opentelemetry` layer with OTLP export configured by `Config`; no vendor SDK in core.
2. Automatic spans for action calls (name, principal kind, outcome, duration), agent turns, model calls (tokens, model, provider) and protocol requests; secret fields never in attributes.
3. A tracking port (events, identify, exceptions, feature flags) with a PostHog adapter in an integration module and a no-op default.
4. Failure context for agent runs (upstream `observability/` failure context) attached to the span.

## Acceptance criteria

* An in-memory exporter test asserts the span tree for one action called by the agent: turn, model call, tool call, action.
* Swapping the tracking adapter to no-op changes no other code (test).
* No Sentry, LaunchDarkly or Amplitude import anywhere (lint).

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; PostHog provisioning or production changes need Jonathan's go-ahead; no new dependency without approval here; ship to main with check results.

## Done signal

Merged with the span-tree test green.

## Owner continuity addendum — 2026-11-15 (binding implementation requirements)

This is part of the coordinated Eventiva modular-extension platform gate, not a completion claim. Original context: `Examples/preamp` historical extension/HookRegistry/onLoad/Effect.logInfo/structured annotations/Eventiva ASCII word-art; inspect exact archived source before implementing or copying artwork. Preserve original banner bytes/layout where compatible, do not fabricate an equivalent. User-approved directions: strict central typed database API for features; centrally approved declaration migrations; hybrid safe hot changes with controlled restarts; observational and additive hook events only (never mutation, veto, override, synchronous critical-path blockers); additional approval/security boundaries for accounting, payment, emergency and vault-protected operations. No module registration grants decryption rights. Existing security taxonomy Baseline/Sensitive/Restricted-Regulated/Vault-Zero-Knowledge and assurance A1-A5 take precedence; no competing independently granted hook trust taxonomy. Protected notifications only via explicitly authorized, minimized, audited boundary service, not arbitrary plugin callbacks inside protected execution.

Cross-cutting acceptance: install sample extension with manifest + lifecycle registration, receive platform.ready, print *exact archived Eventiva word art* through central structured console logging, emit OTel correlated spans/logs, observe execution and step events, provide an allowed declarative UI extension, and uninstall cleanly, all with NO modifications to host/core or original feature module. Verify hot enable/disable and replacement without listeners/leaks/duplicates; in-flight execution pinned to correct version, emergency operation never delayed; first-party/third-party boundary negative tests. Console and time/date-rotated file exporters, pluggable adapters, output routing and sanitation need explicit tests; UI extension telemetry must correlate actions, screen projections, hook delivery and errors under viewer permissions. Synchronous collection MUST NOT run arbitrary plugin code inside committed transactions; reliable notifications use outbox after commit, idempotent delivery and backpressure. Test authorization, field minimization, revocation, metadata leaks, tenant isolation, offline behavior, failure/retry/cancellation, shutdown/drain, upgrade recovery, exact-version compatibility, and PostgreSQL/SQLite gaps honestly. No unapproved dependencies, provisioning, payment activation, production migrations or settings changes. Code review, full checks, evidence and owner approval required before main integration. Details and gaps must remain self-contained in these Linear briefs even if Amp chat context disappears.

### Required observability/logging service expansion

Provide a single vendor-neutral Effect-native telemetry and logging service for platform and extensions: structured log levels, attributes, trace/span/execution/step/module/tenant correlation, console sink, date-rotated file sink for appropriate server/node targets, configurable bounded redaction/sampling/backpressure/retention, pluggable OTLP/PostHog etc adapters and safe no-op test target. File sink is target-dependent; mobile/web require supported alternatives, not file-system promises. Hook registration/delivery/failure, module transitions, UI extension lifecycle, action calls and per-step execution must emit telemetry without logging secrets or vault/regulated payloads. Pre-Amp Eventiva ASCII word-art startup sample must invoke central Effect.logInfo/structured logger via a platform.ready extension; verify exact archived banner, once-per-generation emission and sanitized output. Tests: exporter swap with no feature edits, trace tree across UI -> authorized action -> execution -> step -> hook event -> async side effect, console/file fixture, rotation boundary, exporter outages never break emergencies or payment transactions, sensitive payload non-disclosure. Existing policy requiring separate approval for new dependencies/providers remains.

## Modular-platform observability acceptance (2026-11-15)

Canonical spec [https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c>). Add core-controlled Effect spans/loggers/metrics around bootstrap, all module lifecycle transitions, dependency/provider decisions, resource transactions, durable hooks, workflow lease/update/recovery and failures. Correlation crosses runner/workflow/hook boundaries; metric labels are bounded, payloads/principal PII/keys excluded.

No production OTLP/PostHog ingestion or provisioning without approval, no assumption every OTel signal is supported by each vendor/target.

Add tests for clock rollover, bounded buffers/outage, flush/interruption, no duplicate instrumentation after update, secret canary redaction, audit-vs-telemetry toggle and action->resource->observer correlation; inspect console/file output. Proposed portable constants remain contracts/telemetry.ts, orchestration runtime/telemetry.ts, node sinks integrations/telemetry.server and server/bootstrap composition, subject to coordinator path reservation/new dependency approval. issues.title: P1.6 Build the change flow: domain events and a durable resource change feed
issues.description:
## Binding <issue id="ee08644c-eb3c-4a46-aea7-745864ad4263" label="EVE-45" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change" /> producer decisions — 2026-11-17

Jonathan approved all three producer semantics:

1. **Runtime restart identity:** every runtime restart creates a fresh durable runtime-incarnation UUID linked to a stable logical runtime identity. Never reuse an unfenced incarnation/session identity.
2. **Callback crash ambiguity:** callback success followed by a crash before durable result confirmation is recorded as unresolved and reconciled through an idempotency key and authoritative status/reconciliation path. Never replay blindly.
3. **Event meaning and provenance:** lifecycle events represent committed state transitions. Invocation attempts/outcomes are separate observations. Trusted producer binding comes from authoritative tenant, purpose, security profile, module version and generation; never infer identity or provenance from snapshots.

These decisions authorize implementation and tests within the existing safety, security and delivery gates.

## Goal

Anything that changes emits a typed event that the UI, the agent, sync, schedules and webhooks can all subscribe to, without losing events on restart.

## Context

* Phase-1 step 6 of the S2 capability map. Upstream reference at 6b5cf68: `event-bus/` (registerEvent with standard-schema), `resource-changes/` (durable change feed via a SQL function).

## Scope

1. Event definitions in Effect Schema, registered in an inventory like actions (P1.1).
2. In-process delivery on Effect `PubSub`; durable delivery through a transactional outbox table written in the same transaction as the change (P1.3).
3. A resource change feed per tenant with a cursor, so a client or agent can ask "what changed since X".
4. Write actions emit their event automatically from the receipt.

## Acceptance criteria

* A test kills the process between commit and delivery and proves at-least-once delivery after restart with one applied observer effect per event/subscription id through durable idempotency; delivery itself is not claimed exactly once.
* A cursor read returns exactly the changes after the cursor, scoped to the tenant.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; works on Postgres and SQLite; no new dependency without approval here; ship to main with check results.

## Done signal

Merged with the restart test green.

## Modular-platform observation-only hooks (2026-11-15)

Canonical spec [https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c>). This issue owns durable domain/resource/module/platform lifecycle observations; do not create another hook/event engine. Hooks are after-commit observations and additive side effects, NEVER authorization, blocking guard/veto, transaction control or trigger input/result mutation. Failures/retries do not rerun or change the originating action. Event envelope carries stable event id/version, tenant-safe reference, correlation/causation, module/version/generation; no secrets/plaintext protected data. Actual event/Hook public names follow the active lane handoff.

Owned active paths: packages/contracts/src/hook.ts, packages/runtime/src/hook.ts, tests/contracts/src/hook.spec.ts, tests/runtime/src/hook.spec.ts. Shared export-map hold for @eventiva/contracts/hook and @eventiva/runtime/hook. Production outbox dispatcher/store/app wiring requires a separate coordinated checkpoint; an in-memory PubSub or callback is not durable proof.

Observer/subscription lifecycle must explicitly register/validate/activate/pause-or-drain/deactivate/unregister with Scope cleanup and no duplicate registration; retries have independent idempotency, bounded backpressure, per-resource ordering, dead-letter/quarantine and operator replay. Pinned module/version/generation persists across retry; revocation is rechecked at delivery. platform.ready is produced once per runtime generation durably and repeated ready returns emitted:false; observer delivery may repeat, durable consumer dedup proves one applied banner effect. Keep registration of observers before ready; word-art work starts only after verified ready.

Security: registration grants no decrypt access. Protected profiles/assurance floors from <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" />/251 apply. Sensitive metadata is minimized; Restricted/Vault arbitrary third-party subscriptions default deny, never raw payload/reference enabling unauthorized reads. No untrusted callbacks inside decrypting transaction or emergency/live-control path. <issue id="5beffe53-7de1-44a4-9d23-3166327dc2b1" label="EVE-253" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-253/build-shared-guided-sop-procedures-and-governed-step-execution" /> forbids autonomous incident/alarm actuation of dispatch/audio/lights/PA/emergency; observer may notify/propose only, separately approved human action is required.

Acceptance: crash after commit/before delivery, crash after side effect/before ack, multi-runner claim/fence/replay and backpressure/revocation tests prove at-least-once delivery plus idempotent effects, tenant cursor isolation and no source rerun; lifecycle removal drains safely; redaction tests cover hook/outbox/error/dead-letter/log/projection. Durable outbox binding and authorized production release fail closed until supplied. <issue id="b025ea11-9298-48b2-9bd4-d44decabcab4" label="EVE-261" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-261/integrate-the-modular-platform-and-prove-every-owner-required" /> remains open until these run. AI-authored planning addition; no package/provisioning approval.

## Explicit hook-delivery dependency and protected event gate (2026-11-15)

<issue id="afb95d96-359d-4c0f-a462-a7ce41e2c988" label="EVE-262" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-262/implement-governed-observation-only-execution-and-lifecycle-hooks-with" /> owns typed observation-only hook enrollment/dispatch policy; this issue owns atomic domain-state/outbox commit, durable event/version record, per-tenant cursors, subscription-specific idempotent worker retries, bounded queue/backpressure, poison-message dead letter, safe checkpoint/cancel/replay and multi-runner lease/fencing integration. Subscriber execution always after authoritative commit, never blocking original transaction, and failed observer never re-executes original operation. Check latest grant/revocation and data-classified redaction at delivery; event metadata itself may be protected. Test crash before/after enqueue, duplicate delivery, loss/recovery, disabled subscription, worker redeploy, critical emergency timing and protected-data non-disclosure. Process-local PubSub delivery alone does NOT pass readiness.

## Nonduplicating hook issue split and written API

Coordinator created <issue id="afb95d96-359d-4c0f-a462-a7ce41e2c988" label="EVE-262" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-262/implement-governed-observation-only-execution-and-lifecycle-hooks-with" /> for governed subscription/dispatcher/protected gateway implementation; this issue retains durable producer/outbox/change-feed storage and recovery. One shared engine, no duplicate registry. <issue id="afb95d96-359d-4c0f-a462-a7ce41e2c988" label="EVE-262" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-262/implement-governed-observation-only-execution-and-lifecycle-hooks-with" /> tentative HookDefinition/HookSubscription prose maps to actual HookDeclaration/HookPin/HookEvent contracts; do not create duplicate API names. The active hook lane paths are implemented under that increment; durable SQL adapter still belongs this issue's coordinated integration.

Written API: HookPin/HookObservation/HookEvent/HookDeclaration/HookClaim/HookSettlement; HookModuleIdentity/HookCapability/HookDeliveryState; HookDenied/HookOutboxFailure/HookObserverFailure; HookReleasePolicy.authorize, HookOutbox.stage/claim/settle, fail-closed HookReleaseDeny/HookOutboxUnavailable, hookReleaseRequirements/hookFlag default false. Runtime HookSink.deliver, HookSinkUnavailable, HookDispatcher.register scoped -> dispatch/drain, HookDispatcherLive. Pin {tenant,owner:{module,version,generation},hook,revision}; nonnegative observation generation uses actual kernel snapshot (register normally advances first module from0 to1), never blanket preactivation0. Serving/workflow pins need verified ready generation. Production durable stage/fencing/reclaim/capacity/dedup/CAS/dead-letter remain adapter obligations, not volatile model proof.

issues.title: P1.7 Build the HTTP API, streaming and the typed client from the action inventory
issues.description:
## Goal

Every action is callable over HTTP with OpenAPI output, agent chat streams over the same server, and front ends get a typed client generated from the inventory.

## Context

* Phase-1 step 7 of the S2 capability map. Upstream reference at 6b5cf68: `server/` (action-routes, action-batch, short-lived tokens, agent chat SSE) and `agent-native/` (createAgentNativeClient). Decided D2: Eventiva owns the server on Effect HTTP.

## Scope

1. `@effect/platform` HttpApi built from the inventory: one route per action, batch route, OpenAPI document.
2. Auth: session for people, short-lived tokens and service principals for machines, all resolving to a principal for P1.4.
3. Streaming endpoint for agent turns using the AI SDK UI message stream format over Effect HttpServer.
4. Typed client (Effect RPC or HttpApi client) usable from React Native and web, with offline queueing left to S4's engine.

## Acceptance criteria

* Contract test: every inventory action has a route and appears in OpenAPI.
* A stream test receives text, tool call and tool result parts in order and can be cancelled mid-turn (fiber interruption).
* The client compiles in the React Native app package.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; no Nitro or h3; no new dependency without approval here; ship to main with check results.

## Done signal

Merged with the contract and stream tests green.

## Session identifier versus authentication proof — acceptance requirement (2026-11-17)

A `SessionId` UUID is a non-secret correlation identifier, never a credential or bearer capability. Knowing or supplying a session UUID must grant no access. Every externally reachable caller must prove possession of a separately protected credential (for example a verified short-lived token, signed service assertion or equivalent approved mechanism); trusted identity resolution then maps that proof to the subject and session before Eventiva authorization runs.

The fixed `shellCaller` / `ShellIdentity` UUID in `apps/server/src/access.ts` is permitted only inside the current non-networked registration diagnostic. Replace or isolate that exact-value resolver before any HTTP, RPC, agent or other untrusted transport can invoke it. Acceptance tests must prove that a copied/guessed SessionId without valid credential proof is denied, expired/revoked proof is denied, and authenticated identity still receives only Eventiva-owned tenant membership and action permissions. Session IDs may appear in source, traces or logs only under the normal correlation/redaction policy; credentials, tokens and proof material must never do so.

The agent knows what is on the user's screen and can do anything the user can do there, because every screen and interactive element is registered against an action.

## Context

* Phase-1 step 11 of the S2 capability map; the <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> screen awareness requirement. ## Scope

1. Screen context: each screen declares an Effect Schema projection of what it shows (records, selection, filters), published to application state the agent reads.
2. Interaction registry: every button, menu item and form submit binds to an action id; an unbound interactive element fails a lint or test.
3. Navigation as actions (go to screen, open record), shared by the command menu and the agent.
4. On web only, the same registry is exposed through WebMCP.

## Acceptance criteria

* On web and Android: the agent answers "what am I looking at" from the projection, and performs a visible button's action by its id with the same result as the tap.
* The unbound-element check fails on a fixture.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 for anything with IO; WCAG 2.2 AA for UI; depends on <issue id="a7a66a5c-e747-4245-bc84-3232ef65a16c" label="EVE-16" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-16/s3-prove-runtime-loading-and-switching-of-a-remote-module-on-expo-web" /> for the Expo stack; no new dependency without approval here; ship to main with check results.

## Done signal

Merged with the web and Android checks recorded.

## Declarative substrate split (2026-11-15)

Canonical spec [https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c>). <issue id="71b3a3b5-09a5-45f1-9c59-512c9368036e" label="EVE-259" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-259/implement-the-initial-declarative-ui-module-registry-over-approved" /> owns only initial constrained declarative module schema/registry/renderer. This issue retains general screen awareness, app state/navigation, WebMCP and actual native evidence; reuse <issue id="71b3a3b5-09a5-45f1-9c59-512c9368036e" label="EVE-259" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-259/implement-the-initial-declarative-ui-module-registry-over-approved" />, do not build a second registry. Every interactive element maps to an existing authorized action and emits viewer-filtered declared projection with canonical concepts plus rendered terminology. Unknown/unbound actions and protected-node modification are negative fixtures. Activation/update/disposal follows kernel Scope/generation/lease policy; offline/stale/denied states cannot expose hidden data. Existing <issue id="a7a66a5c-e747-4245-bc84-3232ef65a16c" label="EVE-16" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-16/s3-prove-runtime-loading-and-switching-of-a-remote-module-on-expo-web" /> relation is retained for its native/executable support matrix; it is not a reason to postpone portable data-only schema work or claim executable federation accepted. <issue id="71b3a3b5-09a5-45f1-9c59-512c9368036e" label="EVE-259" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-259/implement-the-initial-declarative-ui-module-registry-over-approved" /> can checkpoint without that spike, but this issue's web/Android proof is still mandatory. issues.title: P1.12 Build collaboration: Yjs for text and canvas with record sync and authorization at sync
issues.description:
## Goal

People and agents edit the same records and the same text or canvas together, offline or online, with permissions enforced on what syncs.

## Context

* Phase-1 step 12 of the S2 capability map. Upstream reference at 6b5cf68: `collab/` (Yjs, y-protocols, diff-match-patch; Wrap). D1: both editing models, designed together.
* <issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" /> (S4, Done 2026-11-09) chose PowerSync (self-hosted Open Edition, Postgres bucket storage) for records and Yjs for text and canvas, with Yjs updates sent as rows through PowerSync. This issue implements that choice. Spike code and gotchas: <issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" /> comments and project files `eve-s4-sync/`.

## Scope

1. A Yjs document service behind one Effect boundary: load, apply update, presence, undo, persisted per resource.
2. Record sync on the engine S4 picks, on SQLite on device and Postgres on server.
3. Authorization at sync: a user or agent only receives and can only push what P1.4 allows; revocation removes data from the device.
4. Agent edits go through the same path as a person's edits, attributed in the audit log.

## Conflict rules

From the <issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" /> conflict policy, which this issue implements as written:

| Data kind | Rule |
| -- | -- |
| Record fields (default) | Per-field merge in the server action: PATCH carries only changed fields, and the last write to arrive wins. |
| Guarded fields (status transitions, money, assignments, dispatch state) | The action checks a precondition (expected version or state-machine transition). A conflict is rejected and shown to the user; never silent last-write-wins. |
| Quantities (stock, capacity, tickets) | Append-only delta rows; totals derived on the server. |
| Lists and ordering | Membership rows with client-generated ids; fractional index per item; delete wins over a concurrent edit. |
| Documents (rich text) | Yjs `Y.Text` / `Y.XmlFragment`; append-only update rows, compacted on the server. Always merges. |
| Canvas objects | Yjs `Y.Map` per object, merged per property; z-order by fractional index; delete wins. **Concurrent edits to the same property resolve by Yjs CRDT merge order, not last-writer-wins**: every device converges to the same value, which is not necessarily the edit that reached the server last (seen on the Android device test). UI copy and docs must not promise "last edit wins" for canvas. |
| Live ops (dispatch, show control, hardware) | Online-only actions. An offline client may queue a request with a TTL, re-validated on reconnect, never auto-applied after the window closes. |

## Revocation teardown

When PowerSync removes a sync bucket from a client (access revoked or scope narrowed), the client tears down every open Yjs document from that bucket immediately: destroy the in-memory `Y.Doc`, unmount or close its editors, drop presence and discard undo history. It must not wait for a reload or restart. The Android device test showed revoked text and canvas staying on screen until the app restarted, so this is a required behaviour, not an optimisation.

## Known gotchas from S4

* Each PowerSync database in one process needs a unique `dbFilename`.
* The connector must `complete()` a rejected transaction and surface the rejection to the user; never drop it silently.
* Debounce Yjs updates on the client and compact them into snapshot rows on the server.
* lib0 (Yjs) imports a webcrypto provider on React Native. Production maps it to an `expo-crypto` backed module, which needs dependency approval here.
* A fully offline cold start on web needs an app-shell service worker.

## Acceptance criteria

* Two clients and the agent edit one document and one record concurrently, one client offline, and all converge after reconnect.
* Revoking access removes the record from the revoked device on next sync, and any open text or canvas document from the removed bucket disappears from screen without a restart.
* Two clients moving the same canvas object concurrently converge to the same value on every device.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; no new dependency without approval here; ship to main with check results.

## Done signal

Merged with the convergence and revocation tests green.

comments.body:
## BINDING Neon CDC / PowerSync cost and compatibility gate — 2026-11-15

Fresh official Neon guidance confirms logical replication is enabled per project, permanently changes `wal_level` to `logical`, cannot be reverted, and restarts every compute. A connected subscriber prevents scale-to-zero and can create continuous compute cost. Inactive slots are removed after about 40 hours without acknowledged `flush_lsn`; branch restore removes slots. Neon supports at most 10 WAL senders and 10 replication slots by default.

For Eventiva/PowerSync, CDC must use a direct Neon endpoint without the `-pooler` suffix and a correctly privileged dedicated replication role; persistent replication is incompatible with PgBouncer pooling. Runtime Effect SQL queries must test pooled and direct paths separately. Do not enable replication or run tests on the existing historical PG16 Frankfurt project.

Plan the first London PG17 synthetic test project with replication disabled. Any later PowerSync/CDC integration trial requires separate owner approval, synthetic-only data, direct endpoint, measured active time, slot lag/retention and cost evidence before broad enablement. This is especially material for the project-per-tenant production model. A Neon branch remains a test-isolation mechanism, not equivalent production tenant isolation.

Official sources refreshed 2026-11-15:
- https://neon.com/docs/guides/logical-replication-guide (updated 2026-10-21)
- https://neon.com/docs/guides/logical-replication-neon (updated 2026-10-09)

Do not silently discard the approved PowerSync design if economics or scaling fail. Return an evidence-backed architecture proposal for owner decision.

* Sign-in flows that bill the user: OpenRouter (OAuth PKCE) and GitHub Copilot (Copilot SDK over GitHub OAuth, per-session token provider).
* Ollama: local endpoint on desktop and self-hosted only, plus Ollama Cloud keys.
* Desktop ACP for the user's own Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI (Eventiva holds no credential).
* ChatGPT plan usage (Sign in with ChatGPT) only after OpenAI approves Eventiva as a private client; until then OpenAI users bring an API key.
* Not supported: Claude, Gemini or Mistral consumer subscriptions inside Eventiva.
* The <issue id="a904aa60-b3c7-4bfa-8d2d-995d1e679389" label="EVE-20" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-20/s7-find-which-ai-providers-allow-users-to-bring-their-own-subscription" /> credential model applies: envelope-encrypted per-tenant storage, per-run identity, Eventiva-side quotas, typed `CredentialRevoked` pausing the run, audit per call, and no environment-variable or payer fallback.

## Scope

1. An engine service (`Context.Tag`) with AI SDK providers as layers; model catalog with capabilities (tools, reasoning, images, context size).
2. Model selection per tenant, user and task, with explicit defaults.
3. User-owned credentials through P1.2 handles; if the user's credential fails, the run stops with a typed error and asks the user, it never switches payer.
4. Failure taxonomy and retry policy (retryable vs not) as Effect `Schedule`; first-event timeout.
5. Usage metering per run (tokens, cost, payer) feeding quotas.

## Acceptance criteria

* A test with a failing user credential proves no call is made on Eventiva's credential.
* Retry tests for a retryable and a non-retryable provider error.
* Usage rows recorded for each model call.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; only sanctioned login or key flows from S7, never cookies or unofficial tokens; dependencies need approval here; ship to main with check results.

## Done signal

Merged with the no-silent-fallback test green.

issues.title: P1.8c Build durable agent runs on Effect Cluster and Workflow
issues.description:
## Goal

An agent run survives a crash, a deploy or a runner loss and resumes exactly where it stopped, without repeating a write.

## Context

Upstream reference at 6b5cf68, `agent/`: `run-store.ts` (6k lines), `run-manager.ts` (4k), `run-loop-with-resume.ts`, `durable-background.ts`, `auto-continue.ts`, `execution-fence.ts`, `tool-call-journal.ts`, `reaped-run-thread.ts`, `run-terminal-tracking.ts`, `abort-reasons.ts`, `turn-resume-context.ts`. D3: Effect Cluster and Workflow, sharding first. <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" /> (S5) proves two runners.
S2 flagged that `effect` latest is 4.x while `@effect/cluster` 0.60 and `@effect/workflow` 0.19 are on the v3 line; <issue id="07c58289-6f1c-488e-a130-5f718b473fce" label="EVE-14" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-14/s1-prove-one-effect-action-serves-ui-mcp-and-ai-sdk-from-one-inventory" /> must confirm 3.19 works first.

## Scope

1. One Cluster entity per run, with run state as a P1.3 state machine (queued, running, waiting for approval, completed, failed, cancelled).
2. Each tool call is a Workflow activity journaled before and after, so replay never re-runs a completed write (upstream `tool-call-journal`, `execution-fence`).
3. Cancel from any surface maps to interruption; stale runs reaped and resumed.
4. Background runs (started by schedules or events) use the same path.

## Acceptance criteria

* Kill the runner mid-turn after a write: on resume the write is not repeated and the turn completes (test on two runners from S5).
* Cancel from HTTP, MCP and ACP each end the run as cancelled.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; ship to main with check results.

## Done signal

Merged with the kill-and-resume test green on two runners.

## Safe module updates with durable runs (2026-11-15)

Spec [https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c>). Preserve this issue's durable agent-run/workflow intent; coordinate <issue id="55c2d64a-d779-41d9-b74e-dcc7d062b86b" label="EVE-252" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-252/implement-effect-cluster-sharding-and-multi-runner-recovery-in-the" /> and <issue id="ceb453e5-ab8e-4566-bf54-47d742b0f425" label="EVE-257" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-257/implement-the-composable-module-kernel-and-safe-lifecycleprovider" /> rather than implement another execution engine. Kernel.workflow returns scoped {module,version,generation}; local mutation rejects workflow-active before preflight. Workflow engine may checkpoint/suspend safely, release and retry, but may not cancel/repin/force-migrate active work merely to accept an update. Persist selected composition/provider/schema epoch and owner fencing, stable effect idempotency and approval bounds. Resume rechecks grants/revocation/deadline/state; exact predecessor compatibleWith and additive schema proof required for hot update. Staged/restart returns no-mutation restart-required; incompatible code/data recovery repairs forward. Evidence: long-lived workflow survives rejected update, safely resumes/releases then replacement succeeds; runner crash at every checkpoint preserves one applied business effect and audit; absent persisted adapter remains fail-closed. AI-authored planning addition.

issues.title: Telemetry F1: Spike Effect OTLP export of traces and metrics from Expo on Hermes
issues.description:
## Goal

Prove that `@effect/opentelemetry` `Otlp.layer` can export traces and metrics from the Expo / React Native app on Hermes, because PostHog's React Native SDK has no tracing or metrics API (<issue id="a5a3ce16-9f4f-484c-9a58-4562bfc9e5b3" label="EVE-19" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-19/s6-map-posthog-and-opentelemetry-support-across-web-native-and-backend" /> matrix).

## Context

* Decided contract: <issue id="a5a3ce16-9f4f-484c-9a58-4562bfc9e5b3" label="EVE-19" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-19/s6-map-posthog-and-opentelemetry-support-across-web-native-and-backend" /> comment "S6 findings" (accepted by Jonathan 2026-10-31): traces, logs and metrics are vendor-neutral by OTLP config; no collector.
* `Otlp.layer({ baseUrl, headers, resource })` appends `/v1/traces`, `/v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs` to `baseUrl` and runs on Effect `HttpClient` (`@effect/opentelemetry@0.61.0`, `dist/esm/Otlp.js`). PostHog base URL: `https://<region>.i.posthog.com/i`.
* House rules: Effect-TS, `@effect/vitest`, spikes on `spike/*` branches only (Eventiva AGENTS.md house:local).

## Work

1. On a `spike/eve-telemetry-hermes` branch, create a minimal Expo app (or use the existing app if one exists by then) that provides `Otlp.layer` with `FetchHttpClient.layer`.
2. Emit one `Effect.withSpan` span with a child span and one `Metric.counter` and one `Metric.histogram`.
3. Point `baseUrl` at a local OTLP receiver (an OTel Collector in Docker with the `debug` exporter, or any OTLP HTTP sink), not PostHog. No PostHog project is authorised for this spike.
4. Run on iOS simulator and Android emulator in a Hermes release build. Try JSON and protobuf serialisation (`layerJson`, `layerProtobuf`).
5. Test: app backgrounded mid-batch, airplane mode then reconnect, app killed with a pending batch. Record what is lost.
6. Record bundle size added by the exporter.

## Acceptance

* A comment on this issue with: works / does not work per platform and serialisation, payload received at the sink (pasted), the loss behaviour from step 5, the bundle size delta.
* If it does not work: the fallback is native metrics sent as PostHog events behind the same Effect `Metric` API, and native spans dropped or sent from the server only. State which and why.

## Out of scope

PostHog provisioning, code on main, offline queue design (only measure behaviour).

## Done signal

Comment with results and one recommendation: use Effect OTLP on native, or use the fallback.

issues.title: Telemetry F3: Implement Early Access enrollment on native and server through the Flags service
issues.description:
## Goal

Give every runtime the house-required Early Access capability, even though only posthog-js exposes it (`getEarlyAccessFeatures`, `updateEarlyAccessFeatureEnrollment`); posthog-react-native 4.85.1 and posthog-node 5.61.1 have no API for it.

## Context

* Decided contract: <issue id="a5a3ce16-9f4f-484c-9a58-4562bfc9e5b3" label="EVE-19" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-19/s6-map-posthog-and-opentelemetry-support-across-web-native-and-backend" /> comment "S6 findings" (accepted 2026-10-31). `Flags` is a `Context.Tag` service in core with `evaluate(flag: FlagDef<A>)` and `enrolEarlyAccess(flag, on)`; vendors are Layers in `packages/integrations/*`.
* House: `feature-flags` skill (safe in-code defaults, offline cached values); Effect-TS rule 3.

## Work

1. Read posthog-js `updateEarlyAccessFeatureEnrollment` source to get the exact event name and person property it sends (expected `$feature_enrollment_update` with `$feature_flag`, `$feature_enrollment`, and `$set` of `$feature_enrollment/<flag>`). Record the source file and version in a comment.
2. In the PostHog native and Node Layers, implement `Flags.enrolEarlyAccess` by sending that same capture, then reload flags.
3. Listing features: serve the list from Eventiva's server (one Effect action, permission-checked, agent-invocable like every action) that calls the PostHog early access API with a server-side key; clients call that action, not PostHog.
4. Web Layer keeps using posthog-js directly.
5. Tests with `@effect/vitest`: the native and Node Layers emit the same payload as posthog-js for a given flag (golden test); the Noop Layer is a no-op.

## Acceptance

Enrolling from web, native and server flips the same flag for the person in PostHog; tests pass; docs updated per house rule 6.

## Out of scope

UI for the early access list (belongs to the screen that hosts it).

## Done signal

Merged to main per the Eventiva ship-direct rule, with tests and docs.
