issues.title: Telemetry F4: Propagate session and person context from clients into server spans, logs, errors and AI spans
issues.description:
## Goal

Every server-side span, log line, captured error and AI span carries the caller's PostHog session id and distinct id, so logs link to Session Replay and Person and AI Observability links to replay and errors (house telemetry must-haves).

## Context

* Decided contract: [EVE-19](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-19/s6-map-posthog-and-opentelemetry-support-across-web-native-and-backend>) comment "S6 findings" (accepted 2026-10-31).
* posthog-js has a `tracingHeaders` extension that adds session id and distinct id headers to fetch/XHR (`lib/src/extensions/tracing-headers.d.ts`, posthog-js 1.444.0). posthog-react-native 4.85.1 has the same option, `addTracingHeaders` (adds `X-POSTHOG-DISTINCT-ID` and `X-POSTHOG-SESSION-ID` to matching fetch requests; corrected 2026-10-31, see <issue id="a5a3ce16-9f4f-484c-9a58-4562bfc9e5b3" label="EVE-19" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-19/s6-map-posthog-and-opentelemetry-support-across-web-native-and-backend" /> recheck comment).
* posthog-node has no log API, so server logs go out as OTLP via Effect and need these attributes to link.

## Work

1. Read posthog-js `tracing-headers` to get the exact header names. Record them in a comment.
2. Clients: enable `addTracingHeaders` (native) and the web equivalent for Eventiva's API hostnames only, and confirm Effect `FetchHttpClient` requests go through the patched global fetch. If they do not, add the two headers in the app's `HttpClient` layer instead.
3. Server: one Effect middleware for the HTTP and RPC entrypoints that reads the headers through `Schema`, validates them, and puts them on a `FiberRef` / span attributes (`posthog.distinct_id`, `$session_id`) and `Effect.annotateLogs`, so every span and log below inherits them.
4. `ErrorReports.report` and AI span creation read the same context; AI spans set the attributes PostHog uses to link generations to sessions (confirm names from `@posthog/ai` source).
5. Agents calling actions without a browser session: use the agent run id as the session-like id and the delegating user as the distinct id; document it.
6. Respect `telemetry: false`: no headers sent, no attributes set.
7. Tests with `@effect/vitest` for header parsing, inheritance into child spans and logs, and the telemetry-off path.

## Acceptance

A request from web and from native produces a server span, a log line and an error event that all show the same session and person in PostHog (verify once F2's dev project exists; until then, verify with an OTLP debug sink).

## Done signal

Merged to main with tests and docs (people docs and ai-docs).

issues.title: F12 Payroll: pay staff and crew from rosters and approved timesheets
issues.description:
Status: Proposed (2026-11-01). Feature set F12 from the [Feature set spec template and list](<https://linear.app/resnovas/document/feature-set-spec-template-and-list-26b9f78cf17a>). Planning only: no code, no new dependency, no vendor sign-up until Jonathan approves the decisions below.

## 1. Goal

An organiser pays every person who worked an event correctly and on time, from the shifts they were rostered for and the hours they actually worked, with each cost landing on the right event and the right ledger account.

## 2. Users and jobs

| User | Jobs |
| -- | -- |
| Organiser or production manager | Approve timesheets for their event, see labour cost against budget per event and phase |
| Payroll administrator (finance) | Set pay rules and rate cards, run and lock a pay period, resolve exceptions, send to the payroll provider, post to accounts |
| Crew member or staff (employee) | Clock in and out on site (offline too), check and submit a timesheet, see payslips and pay history |
| Freelancer or contractor | Confirm hours, receive a self-billed invoice or submit their own, see payment status |
| Crew chief or department head | Approve hours for their team on the day, add allowances (meal, travel, late finish) |
| Accountant (external, read-only) | Download pay run reports and journals |
| Agent | Draft timesheets from rosters, flag anomalies, prepare the pay run, explain any line of pay; never submits or pays without approval |

## 3. Market check

Checked 2026-11-01. Names stay out of customer-facing copy.

* **Workforce tools with timesheets (Deputy, Rotaready, [workforce.com](<http://workforce.com>))**: rostering, clock-in with geofencing, timesheet approval, then an export or connector into a separate payroll product. They do not file tax themselves. Eventiva matches this shape for time capture and goes further by tying hours to event, phase and budget.
* **Payroll engines (Xero Payroll, Sage, BrightPay, PayFit)**: gross-to-net, payslips, statutory pay, pensions auto-enrolment and real-time filing to the tax authority. In the UK, software that files PAYE RTI must hold HMRC PAYE recognition ([gov.uk guidance](<https://www.gov.uk/guidance/paye-recognition-for-payroll-software-developers>)), and the recognition is re-tested every tax year.
* **Payroll APIs (Staffology Payroll API)**: an HMRC-recognised engine exposed as an API so another product can embed payroll ([staffology.co.uk](<https://staffology.co.uk/?p=20>)).

Where Eventiva differs: the event is the unit of cost; freelancers and employees are paid from one approved-time source; the agent can do every step a person can. Where Eventiva does not compete: filing tax returns itself (see decision D1).

## 4. Capabilities as actions

Every operation is an inventory action ([EVE-40](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40>)) with Effect Schema input and output, typed errors, one permission check, audit receipt and change record with undo where it mutates. Approval policy follows <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" /> (none, confirm, always).

| Action | Input | Output | Permission | Approval |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `payroll.payRule.upsert` | rule id?, name, kind (hourly, day rate, fixed fee, overtime, allowance, deduction, holiday accrual), formula params, effective from | PayRule | `payroll:rules:write` | confirm |
| `payroll.rateCard.upsert` | role, grade, event? or org default, rates, currency, effective dates | RateCard | `payroll:rules:write` | confirm |
| `payroll.rateCard.list` | filters | RateCard\[\] | `payroll:rules:read` | none |
| `payroll.worker.setPayProfile` | worker ref and Engagement ref (F13), pay schedule, rate card, provider worker ref | PayProfile | `payroll:profiles:write` | confirm |
| (consumed) `timesheet.export` | F2 action ([EVE-138](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-138/f29-build-time-capture-and-timesheets>)): approved, locked timesheets per period as a versioned, idempotent batch | lines with worker, engagement type, Event, Phase, Department, hours, source refs | owned by F2 | owned by F2 |
| `payroll.allowance.add` | worker, event, kind, amount or quantity, reason | PayLine | `time:approve` | confirm |
| `payroll.period.open` | pay schedule, start, end | PayPeriod | `payroll:run` | confirm |
| `payroll.run.calculate` | period id | PayRun (draft) with lines and exceptions | `payroll:run` | none |
| `payroll.run.explainLine` | pay line id | Explanation (rule, rate, source entries) | `payroll:read` or own line | none |
| `payroll.run.lock` | run id | PayRun (locked) | `payroll:run` | always |
| `payroll.run.submitToProvider` | run id | ProviderSubmission | `payroll:submit` | always |
| `payroll.run.importResults` | submission id | PayRun (net figures, payslip refs) | `payroll:submit` | none |
| `payroll.selfBill.issue` | run id, freelancer ids | SelfBillInvoice\[\] | `payroll:run` | always |
| `payroll.payment.prepare` | run id | PaymentBatch (bank file or payment-port request) | `payroll:pay` | always |
| (event) `payroll:run_approved` | emitted on the change feed ([EVE-45](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change>)) when a run reaches completed (net results imported) | per cost dimension (Event, Phase, Department): gross, employer NI, employer pension, employee deductions (PAYE, employee NI, pension, student loan, other), net; freelancer self-bill totals separately; integer minor units plus currency | n/a | n/a (follows the always-approved lock and submit) |
| (event) `payroll:run_reversed` | emitted when a run is reversed | the correcting amounts in the same shape | n/a | n/a |
| `payroll.run.reverse` | run id, reason | PayRun (reversed) + correcting entries | `payroll:run` | always |
| `payroll.payslip.list` / `payroll.payslip.get` | worker? period? | Payslip\[\] / Payslip | own, or `payroll:read` | none |
| `payroll.report.labourCost` | event?, phase?, period?, group by | LabourCostReport | `payroll:read` or event budget read | none |

## 5. Data model

Tenant scope: every row carries `org_id`; tenant guards from [EVE-42](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42>).

Referenced, not redefined: **Event**, **Phase**, **Department**, **TeamMember** (the person's role on an event), **RunOfShow** and **Itinerary** (F1, names fixed in [EVE-73](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73>) section 5); **Shift**, **Assignment**, **Availability**, **TimeEntry** and **Timesheet** (F2, [EVE-67](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-67/f2-scheduling-and-rosters-crew-availability-shifts-offers-call-sheets>); F2 owns time capture and timesheet approval via [EVE-138](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-138/f29-build-time-capture-and-timesheets>) and records engagement type on each Assignment; scheduling base [EVE-33](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33>)); **Worker**, **Engagement** (type, payBasis, individual rate, contractedHours, offPayrollStatus, versioned), **SensitiveProfile** (bank details, tax and NI ids, encrypted, <issue id="636f7592-553b-41f2-adb0-9a336d0188e3" label="EVE-116" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-116/f132-build-the-sensitive-profile-with-field-masking-reveal-audit-and" />), the leave ledger and approved absence (<issue id="5ca54321-0f0a-461c-ade1-89cf3197dc48" label="EVE-179" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-179/f137-build-leave-policies-the-leave-ledger-requests-and-absence" />) and the final-pay flag at offboarding (<issue id="576185f3-f438-43c7-b694-e5afff0605e7" label="EVE-153" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-153/f134-build-onboarding-and-offboarding-runs" />), all F13 (<issue id="253839bc-c987-416b-92ea-206c9e9e8d2e" label="EVE-80" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-80/f13-human-resources-worker-records-onboarding-qualifications-and-leave" />). Rate precedence: an individual Engagement rate overrides the F12 rate card for that worker; the rate card supplies role and event rates, overtime and allowances. F12 calculates holiday pay from F13's approved leave, and a final-pay flag becomes a pay run exception; **Contact** and **Organisation** (F4, for agencies and freelancers trading as companies); **Account**, **Journal** and **Budget line** (F11).

Owned by F12:

| Entity | Key fields | Relations | Offline | Conflict rule |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| PayRule | kind, params, effective range, version | used by RateCard | read-only offline | server wins; versioned, never edited in place once used |
| RateCard | role, grade, rates, currency, effective range | org or Event | read-only offline | server wins |
| PayProfile | pay schedule, rate card, provider worker ref (engagement type and status read from F13 Engagement) | Worker, Engagement | read-only offline | server wins |
| PayPeriod | schedule, start, end, status | PayRun | no | server only |
| PayRun | status (draft, locked, submitted, completed, reversed), totals, exceptions | PayLine\[\], ProviderSubmission | no (read cache only) | server only; locked runs are immutable, corrections are new lines in a later run |
| PayLine | kind, quantity, rate, amount, cost centre (Event, Phase, Department), source refs | PayRun, Worker, TeamMember? | read cache | server only |
| SelfBillInvoice | number, lines, tax treatment | PayRun, Worker, Organisation? | read cache | server only |
| Payslip | period, gross, deductions, net, document ref | Worker, PayRun | read cache, encrypted at rest on device | server only |
| ProviderSubmission | provider, request hash, status, response refs | PayRun | no | server only |

Money is integer minor units plus ISO currency; no floats. Embedded documents: payslip PDFs and self-bill invoices are files ([EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25>)); no collaborative text or canvas in this set.

## 6. Screens

All components from Rambo-UI. Every screen declares a screen-context projection and binds every control to an action ([EVE-50](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50>)). Pay figures are masked in projections for viewers without `payroll:read`.

| Screen | Components | Projection | Controls to actions |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Clock in and timesheets | owned by F2 (<issue id="522cf0df-8126-444d-8833-1e31bf21345e" label="EVE-138" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-138/f29-build-time-capture-and-timesheets" />) | n/a | n/a |
| My pay | payslip list, payslip viewer | own payslips (no other workers) | `payroll.payslip.*` |
| Allowances | list and form on the pay run | allowances per worker and event | `payroll.allowance.add` |
| Pay rules and rate cards | form, versioned history | rules, effective dates | `payroll.payRule.upsert`, `payroll.rateCard.upsert` |
| Pay run | stepper (open, calculate, review exceptions, lock, submit, pay, post), exception list, line explainer drawer | run status, totals, exceptions, selected line | one action per step, `payroll.run.explainLine` |
| Labour cost | chart and table by event and phase against budget | report rows | `payroll.report.labourCost` |

## 7. Agent behaviour

* On request: draft timesheets from the roster, explain a pay line in plain words, prepare a pay run and summarise exceptions, answer "what did the load-out cost in crew pay".
* Proactively (behind the flag, as suggestions, never applied): flag a timesheet whose hours differ from the roster by more than a threshold, a missing clock-out, a worker past a working-time limit, a rate below the statutory minimum, a freelancer with no engagement status recorded, a run that differs from the last comparable run by more than a threshold.
* Always needs a human: locking a run, submitting to the provider, issuing self-bills, preparing payments, posting journals, reversing a run, changing a pay rule or rate card. Approval is the action policy `always`, not an agent prompt.
* The agent works under the invoking user's permissions only; an agent acting for a crew member sees that member's pay and nobody else's.

## 8. Integrations

Each behind a neutral Effect port in its own integration package; switching vendor changes composition only.

* `PayrollProvider` port: send approved gross inputs per worker, receive net pay, deductions, payslip documents and filing status. First adapter is decision D1.
* `PaymentRail` port: produce a bank payment file (UK Bacs Standard 18 or similar) or call a payment provider. Phase 1 is file export only.
* Accounting: F12 does not post journals. It emits `payroll:run_approved` and `payroll:run_reversed` on the change feed; F11 ([EVE-69](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-69>), posting rules [EVE-90](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-90>)) maps them to wages expense and control accounts and reconciles the net wages payment ([EVE-157](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-157>)). Agreed with the F11 spec 2026-11-01.
* Calendar and location: none new; clock-in location uses the device location permission only when the org turns it on.

## 9. Permissions and roles

| Role | Sees | Changes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Worker | own time, timesheets, payslips, self-bills | own draft entries, submit |
| Crew chief | team time for their events | approve or reject, allowances |
| Organiser | labour cost for their events, timesheets for their events, no individual net pay or deductions | approve timesheets for their events |
| Payroll admin | everything in payroll for the org | rules, profiles, runs |
| Finance approver | runs, reports | lock, submit, pay, post (separate from the person who calculated when the org enables two-person approval) |
| Accountant (external) | reports and journals | nothing |
| Agency (external org) | its own workers' approved hours | nothing |

Bank details and tax or NI ids live only in F13's encrypted SensitiveProfile (<issue id="636f7592-553b-41f2-adb0-9a336d0188e3" label="EVE-116" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-116/f132-build-the-sensitive-profile-with-field-masking-reveal-audit-and" />). F12 reads them when it builds a provider submission or a payment file and never stores them; they never appear in action payloads, telemetry or prompts.

## 10. Telemetry and flags

* Flag: `payroll` (default off), plus `payroll-agent-suggestions` (default off) and `payroll-clock-location` (default off).
* Events (time and timesheet events are F2's): `pay_run_calculated`, `pay_run_locked`, `pay_run_submitted`, `pay_run_exception_resolved`, `agent_payroll_suggestion_accepted`. No amounts, names or identifiers beyond pseudonymous ids.
* Success metric: median time from period end to submitted run, and share of runs with zero post-lock corrections (target 95 percent after three months of use).

## 11. Compliance

To validate per jurisdiction before launch; the UK is the first target market (assumed from Resnovas being UK-based).

* Tax filing: PAYE RTI is filed only by HMRC-recognised software (D1). Eventiva keeps the audit trail of inputs it sends.
* Worker status: off-payroll working rules (IR35) for freelancers; Eventiva records the status determination and who made it, it does not decide it.
* Minimum wage and working time: check effective hourly pay against the statutory minimum for the worker's age band, and working-time limits and rest breaks; warn, never block silently.
* Holiday pay for irregular-hours and part-year workers: accrual rule as a PayRule kind; the rule values come from current guidance at build time, not from this spec.
* Pensions auto-enrolment: handled by the provider in D1 option A; Eventiva passes pensionable pay.
* Record keeping: pay records kept at least 3 years after the tax year (UK), configurable longer; locked runs immutable.
* Personal data: payroll data is special handling under UK GDPR; least-privilege access, encryption at rest, retention schedule, masking in screen projections and replay.
* Self-billing: needs a written self-billing agreement per freelancer stored as a file before the first self-bill.

## 12. Acceptance

* Approved timesheets from F2's `timesheet.export` (offline clock-ins included) are paid once: re-importing the same batch version adds no lines.
* A 30-minute late finish approved in F2 gets a late-finish allowance in F12 and shows on the pay line explanation.
* A pay run for 50 workers across two events calculates gross pay matching a hand-checked fixture to the penny, with overtime, a day rate, a fixed fee and an allowance.
* Every pay line explains itself back to the rule, rate and time entries it came from, through the UI and through the agent with the same answer.
* Locking, submitting and paying each need an explicit human approval; the agent's attempt without one fails with a typed error and an audit entry.
* Labour cost per event and phase reconciles to the run total, and one `payroll:run_approved` event per run carries the same totals to F11.
* An organiser cannot read an individual's net pay; a worker cannot read another worker's payslip, on every interface (UI, HTTP, MCP, ACP).
* Reversing a locked run creates correcting lines in the next run and leaves the locked run unchanged.

## 13. Out of scope

Filing tax returns directly with HMRC or another authority (unless D1 changes); payroll outside the UK in the first release (the model is currency and jurisdiction aware so others plug in later); expenses and reimbursement claims (F11); recruitment, contracts and leave requests (F13); benefits administration; tips and tronc schemes; on-demand or early wage access.

## 14. Dependencies

* Phase 1: [EVE-40](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40>) actions, [EVE-41](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-41>) config and secrets (provider credentials), [EVE-42](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42>) storage, state machines and tenant guards, [EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43>) identity, roles and audit, [EVE-44](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44>) telemetry and flags, [EVE-45](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45>) change feed, [EVE-46](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-46>) HTTP API, [EVE-50](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50>) screen awareness, [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51>) record sync, [EVE-52](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-52>) and [EVE-54](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54>) agent loop and durable runs.
* Port later: [EVE-24](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24>) notifications (payslip ready, timesheet reminders), [EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25>) files (payslips, self-bills, agreements), [EVE-28](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-28>) localisation, [EVE-33](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33>) scheduling.
* Feature sets: F1 events ([EVE-73](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73>): cost centres Event, Phase and Department; TeamMember role drives the rate card), F2 rosters (shifts), F11 accounting (journals, budgets), F13 HR (worker records, leave, right to work), F4 contacts (agencies).

## 15. Decisions for Jonathan

Each has a recommendation; the first is on the decision card in the payroll thread, the rest are proposed defaults that stand unless he flips them.

* **D1 Who calculates net pay and files tax.** A: Eventiva calculates gross, a recognised payroll provider calculates net and files, behind the `PayrollProvider` port (recommended). B: build an HMRC-recognised engine in Eventiva. C: export only, no provider connection.
* **D2 First jurisdiction.** UK only (recommended), with currency and jurisdiction fields from day one; or UK plus one more.
* **D3 Freelancer pay.** Self-billed invoices generated by Eventiva (recommended); or freelancers upload their own invoices only.
* **D4 Two-person approval.** Off by default and an org setting (recommended); or always on.
* **D5 Clock-in location.** Org opt-in, captured only at clock in and out, never tracked between (recommended); or no location at all.

## 16. Child issues (build order)

1. [EVE-82](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-82/f121-build-pay-rules-rate-cards-and-pay-profiles>) F12.1 Pay rules, rate cards and pay profiles
2. <issue id="e08704c6-b901-4fc2-8753-73aaf09f694f" label="EVE-83" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-83/f122-build-time-capture-clock-in-and-out-and-time-entries-offline" /> and <issue id="6d951ef7-861e-43b3-aaa8-3f2ba0d53f56" label="EVE-85" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-85/f123-build-timesheets-draft-from-roster-submit-and-approve" /> (old F12.2 time capture and F12.3 timesheets) closed as duplicates of F2's <issue id="522cf0df-8126-444d-8833-1e31bf21345e" label="EVE-138" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-138/f29-build-time-capture-and-timesheets" />, which owns time capture and timesheets; payroll needs listed there.
3. [EVE-87](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-87/f124-build-pay-run-calculation-on-durable-runs>) F12.4 Pay run calculation and allowances (after F12.1 and [EVE-138](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-138/f29-build-time-capture-and-timesheets>))
4. [EVE-88](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-88/f125-build-the-payroll-provider-port-and-the-first-adapter>) F12.5 Payroll provider port and first adapter (after F12.4)
5. [EVE-92](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-92/f126-build-freelancer-self-billing-and-worker-status-records>) F12.6 Freelancer self-billing and worker status records (after F12.4)
6. [EVE-96](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-96/f127-build-the-payments-file-and-journal-posting-to-accounting>) F12.7 Payments file and pay run events for accounting (after F12.5, F12.6)
7. [EVE-101](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-101/f128-build-labour-cost-reporting-per-event-and-phase>) F12.8 Labour cost reporting per event and phase (after F12.4)
8. [EVE-104](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-104/f129-build-the-payroll-agent-explanations-anomaly-suggestions-and>) F12.9 Payroll agent: explanations, anomaly suggestions and approval gates (after F12.7, F12.8)

issues.title: F3 Tasks: task lists, assignments, dependencies and checklists per event
issues.description:
Status: Approved (2026-11-08). Jonathan chose "Approve, add a rule builder": decisions 1 to 6 as recommended, decision 7 option B (rule builder in F3, <issue id="cbcfb707-a7d4-4089-8e84-d9e2a2bd4d94" label="EVE-235" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-235/f310-build-the-task-rule-builder-when-x-then-y-on-a-generic-rule" />). Planning only; no implementation until Jonathan asks. Follows the [Feature set spec template](<https://linear.app/resnovas/document/feature-set-spec-template-and-list-26b9f78cf17a>). F1 (Events and production planning, <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> section 5) owns Event, Phase, Department, Segment (of a RunOfShow), ItineraryItem and TeamMember; this set references them by id and does not redefine them. F1's readiness checks read open tasks per Department.

## 1. Goal

Everyone working on an event, people and agents alike, knows what has to be done, by whom, by when and in what order, and can tick it off on site with no signal.

## 2. Users and jobs

| User | Jobs |
| -- | -- |
| Organiser / producer | Plan the work for an event from a template, assign it, see what is late or blocked, reschedule everything when the event date moves |
| Department head (lighting, sound, rigging, staging) | Own a task list for a discipline, break work into subtasks, set dependencies on other departments |
| Crew | See "my tasks" across events and shifts, claim open tasks, run on-site checklists (load-in, safety, show-ready, load-out) offline, attach photo evidence |
| Vendor / freelancer (external) | See and complete only the tasks assigned to them, without seeing the rest of the event |
| Finance / admin | Track admin tasks (contracts, deposits, insurance) tied to the event timeline |
| Agent (first-party or external) | Draft task plans from a brief, chase overdue work, answer "what is blocking load-in", apply templates, keep dates in step with the event, all through the same actions |

## 3. Market check

Names stay internal; customer-facing copy is whitelabel.

| Tool | What it does | Eventiva |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Asana | Tasks, subtasks, "waiting on" dependencies drawn on a timeline, rules, and AI Teammates that act on projects ([dependencies](<https://asana.com/inside-asana/dependencies>), [Winter 2026 release](<https://asana.com/inside-asana/winter-release-2026>)) | Match: subtasks, finish-to-start dependencies, agent that acts. Differ: the agent uses the same actions as the UI ([EVE-13](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and>) parity), and tasks hang off the event record instead of a free-floating project |
| ClickUp | Tasks with dependency types, Brain and Super Agents for dependency tracking and prioritisation ([AI task manager](<https://clickup.com/features/ai-task-manager>), [dependency agent](<https://clickup.com/p/ai-agents/dependency-management>)) | Match: agent prioritisation and dependency alerts. Differ: offline-first on mobile, which general work tools treat as secondary |
| Aisle Planner / Planning Pod (event-specific) | Checklist templates with due dates relative to the event date that move when the event is rescheduled ([template due dates](<https://integration-tag-api.aisleplanner.com/blog/feature-spotlight/introducing-checklist-due-dates-template-level>), [rescheduling](<https://aisleplanner.com/blog/work-life/rescheduling-made-easy-aisle-planner>), [Planning Pod checklists](<https://planningpod.com/checklists-and-task-management>)) | Match: event-relative templates and cascade on reschedule. Differ: anchors can be any F1 date (Phase start, Segment), not only the event day, and on-site checklists carry sign-off and evidence |

Gap none of them fill well: crew checklists that work offline at a venue and sync with evidence, with the same tasks visible to an agent.

## 4. Capabilities as actions

Every operation is an inventory action (<issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />): Effect Schema input and output, typed errors, one permission check (<issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />), receipt, change record with undo where it mutates. Side-effect class in brackets.

| Action | Input | Output | Permission | Approval |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `taskList.create` \[write\] | name, scope (Event, Phase or tenant), owner | TaskList | `tasks:manage` on scope | none |
| `taskList.update` / `taskList.archive` \[write\] | id, fields | TaskList | `tasks:manage` | none |
| `task.create` \[write\] | listId, title, description?, assignees?, due?, priority?, parentId?, links? | Task | `tasks:write` on list | none |
| `task.update` \[write\] | id, patch of fields | Task | `tasks:write`, or assignee for status and checklist | none |
| `task.assign` / `task.unassign` \[write\] | id, principalIds | Task | `tasks:assign` | confirm when an agent assigns someone other than the requester |
| `task.claim` \[write\] | id | Task | `tasks:claim` (crew on the event) | none |
| `task.setStatus` \[write\] | id, status | Task | `tasks:write` or assignee | none |
| `task.complete` / `task.reopen` \[write\] | id, note? | Task | `tasks:write` or assignee | none |
| `task.move` \[write\] | id, listId, position | Task | `tasks:write` on both lists | none |
| `task.delete` \[write\] | id | receipt with undo | `tasks:manage` | confirm for agents; always when deleting more than 10 |
| `task.bulkUpdate` \[write\] | ids, patch | Task\[\] | per task | confirm when more than 10 tasks |
| `task.get` / `task.list` / `task.search` \[read\] | id or filters (assignee, status, due range, Event, Phase, label) | Task / page | `tasks:read` | none |
| `task.myTasks` \[read\] | range, include shifts? | Task page | self | none |
| `task.link` / `task.unlink` \[write\] | id, resource ref (Event, Phase, Segment, Shift, kit item, vehicle, map pin) | Task | `tasks:write` and read on target | none |
| `dependency.add` / `dependency.remove` \[write\] | fromTaskId, toTaskId, lag? | Dependency | `tasks:write` on both | none |
| `dependency.blockers` \[read\] | taskId or Event | blocking chain | `tasks:read` | none |
| `checklist.addItem` / `checklist.updateItem` / `checklist.reorder` / `checklist.removeItem` \[write\] | taskId, item | Checklist | `tasks:write` | none |
| `checklist.toggleItem` \[write\] | itemId, done, evidence? | ChecklistItem | assignee or `tasks:write` | none |
| `checklist.signOff` \[write\] | taskId, signature note | SignOff | role named on the checklist (for example safety lead) | always (a person signs; an agent cannot) |
| `template.create` / `template.update` / `template.archive` \[write\] | name, tasks with relative offsets and anchors | TaskTemplate | `tasks:templates` | none |
| `template.apply` \[write\] | templateId, Event (and Phase map) | TaskList with tasks | `tasks:manage` on Event | confirm when it creates more than 25 tasks |
| `task.reschedule` \[write\] | Event or anchor change, mode (cascade or preview) | change set | `tasks:manage` | confirm for cascade |
| `reminder.set` / `reminder.clear` \[write\] | taskId, when (absolute or before due) | Reminder | assignee or `tasks:write` | none |
| `recurrence.set` / `recurrence.clear` \[write\] | taskId, rule | Recurrence | `tasks:manage` | none |
| `task.watch` / `task.unwatch` \[write\] | id | Watch | `tasks:read` | none |
| `guest.inviteToTask` \[external\] | taskId, contact | invite | `tasks:assign` and `guests:invite` | confirm |

Comments and mentions use <issue id="b7f17f15-c893-46e9-9b3b-2aefae473802" label="EVE-27" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-27/port-comments-mentions-and-review-suggestions-on-any-resource" /> (`comment.*`), attachments <issue id="8d8d301b-d679-4dac-95bb-c24889179cd0" label="EVE-25" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import" />, navigation <issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" /> (`nav.open` with a Task id).

## 5. Data model

All tables tenant-scoped (<issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> tenant guard), soft delete with undo, attributed edits.

* **TaskList**: id, tenantId, scope (Event id, or tenant-level), optional Phase id and Department id, name, owner, archivedAt.
* **Task**: id, tenantId, listId, parentId (subtask, max depth 3), title, optional Phase, Department and Segment refs (F1), description (Yjs document embedded in the record per [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>)), status (category: todo, in_progress, blocked, done, cancelled; tenant-renameable label), priority (none, low, medium, high, urgent), due (absolute instant or relative: anchor ref plus offset), start (same shape), estimateMinutes, labels, position (fractional index), completedAt, completedBy, createdBy (person or agent on behalf of person).
* **TaskAssignee**: taskId, principalId (member or guest), assignedBy, assignedAt. Many per task.
* **TaskDependency**: fromTaskId, toTaskId, type (finish-to-start), lagMinutes. Cycles rejected.
* **ChecklistItem**: id, taskId, text, position, done, doneBy, doneAt, evidence (attachment refs, [EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>)), required.
* **SignOff**: taskId, role, principalId, at, note. Immutable once written; a reopen adds a new row.
* **TaskTemplate** and **TemplateTask**: tasks, checklists, dependencies and assignee roles (mapped to F1 TeamMember roles and Departments on apply) with offsets relative to an anchor (Event start or end, Phase start or end, Segment time, ItineraryItem).
* **Reminder**, **Recurrence** (rule from [EVE-33](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters>)), **TaskWatch**, **TaskLink** (task to any resource ref).

Offline sync and conflict rules per field (S4 engine, <issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" />):

| Field | Syncs offline | Conflict rule |
| -- | -- | -- |
| title, priority, due, start, labels, estimate | yes | last writer wins per field, both values kept in the change log |
| description | yes | Yjs merge |
| status | yes | completion wins: a `done` from any client beats a concurrent non-done change; only an explicit `task.reopen` after it undoes it |
| assignees | yes | set merge (add and remove as separate ops); a remove beats a concurrent add of the same person only if later |
| checklist items | yes | per item: done is monotonic until untoggled by a later op; order uses fractional index |
| sign-off | yes, queued | append-only; never overwritten |
| dependencies | yes | add-wins set; a cycle created by two offline adds is rejected at sync and flagged to both editors |
| relative due recalculation | computed on server and device | server result wins on reconnect; device shows a "dates updated" notice |

Authorization at sync: a guest's device only receives tasks assigned to them; revocation removes them on next sync (<issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" />).

## 6. Screens

All components from Rambo-UI; every control binds to an action id; each screen declares a screen-context projection (<issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" />).

| Screen | Platforms | Rambo-UI parts | Projection | Controls to actions |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| My tasks | all | list, group header, checkbox, chip, filter bar | visible tasks (ids, titles, status, due), filters, selection | tick: `task.complete`; claim: `task.claim`; open: `nav.open` |
| Event tasks (list and board) | all; board on wide screens | list, board columns, drag handle, avatar stack | Event id, grouping (Phase or status), visible tasks, selection | drag: `task.move` / `task.setStatus`; add: `task.create`; apply template: `template.apply` |
| Task detail (sheet) | all | sheet, rich text editor, date picker, assignee picker, checklist, comment thread | the task, its checklist, blockers, focus field | each field: `task.update`; assign: `task.assign`; add blocker: `dependency.add` |
| Checklist run (on site) | mobile first | large checkbox rows, camera button, sign-off panel, offline badge | task, items, which are done, pending sync count | tick: `checklist.toggleItem`; sign: `checklist.signOff` |
| Dependencies and timeline | web and desktop; mobile shows a blockers list | timeline, connector lines | visible range, tasks, links | draw link: `dependency.add`; drag dates: `task.update` |
| Templates library and editor | all; editor best on wide screens | list, editor, offset picker | template, its tasks | `template.*` |

Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA; drag has a keyboard and menu alternative (move to column action); offline and sync state announced to screen readers.

## 7. Agent behaviour

When asked: break a brief into a task plan for an Event (preview, then `template.apply`-style creation with confirm over 25 tasks); answer "what is blocking X" from `dependency.blockers`; reassign a person's tasks when they drop out (confirm); reschedule after an Event date change (preview then confirm); fill a checklist from a document (<issue id="8d8d301b-d679-4dac-95bb-c24889179cd0" label="EVE-25" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import" /> import).

Proactive (behind the flag, opt-in per user): a daily digest of the user's overdue and due-soon tasks; a warning when a dependency chain makes a due date impossible; a nudge when an on-site checklist is incomplete at its Segment anchor. Proactive work only reads and suggests; any write it proposes waits for the user.

Approvals: as in section 4. An agent never signs off a checklist, never deletes another person's task without confirm, and never assigns a third party without confirm. Offline, the device agent can use local task actions; anything needing a remote model says it is offline.

## 8. Integrations

None required for phase 1. Each later integration sits behind a neutral port:

* Calendar feed of my tasks (ICS out, then Google and Microsoft through the <issue id="97915f03-fb56-4efc-bb5a-15e8b62b96b2" label="EVE-33" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters" /> calendar providers).
* Import from CSV and from other task tools (port `TaskImport`; vendors later, each approved on its issue).
* Notifications through <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" /> channels (push, email, chat platforms).

## 9. Permissions and roles

| Role | See | Change |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Tenant admin | all task lists | everything, templates |
| Event manager | tasks on their Events | `tasks:manage`, `tasks:assign`, templates apply |
| Department lead | lists they own plus read on the Event's other lists | `tasks:write` on own lists, assign within their team |
| Crew member | tasks on Events they are rostered for (F2) | own tasks, claim open tasks, toggle checklists, sign off where their role is named |
| Guest (vendor, freelancer) | only tasks assigned to them, with the Event name and the relevant date | status, checklist, comments on those tasks |
| Attendee | nothing in F3 | nothing |
| Agent | exactly what the person it acts for can see and do (<issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />) | same, plus the approvals above |

## 10. Telemetry and flags

* Flags (PostHog, safe in-code default off): `tasks` (the set), `tasks-dependencies`, `tasks-templates`, `tasks-agent-proactive`, `tasks-guests`, `tasks-rules`.
* Events: `task created`, `task completed`, `task reopened`, `task assigned`, `template applied`, `checklist signed off`, `dependency added`, `tasks rescheduled`, `task created offline` (with sync delay), each with source (ui, agent, api, mcp) and no task text.
* Spans on every action from <issue id="a03acb76-125b-4ead-815e-10ec986d8413" label="EVE-44" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor" />; metric for sync conflict count per field.
* Success metric: share of Event tasks completed by their due date, and share of task writes made by agents that the user keeps (not undone within 24 hours).

## 11. Compliance

* Personal data: assignees, comments and evidence photos are personal data (UK GDPR). Export and erase per person through the tenant's data subject actions; erased people show as "former member".
* Retention: sign-offs and evidence on safety checklists are kept for the tenant's configured retention (default 6 years) and cannot be edited, only superseded. Eventiva records the evidence; it does not claim the checklist meets any specific safety regulation.
* Guest access: guests accept terms on invite; their data is limited to their tasks.

## 12. Acceptance

* Every operation in section 4 is in the inventory and the parity check passes; the agent can do each one through MCP and the UI with the same result.
* A crew member completes a checklist with a photo on a phone in airplane mode, restarts the app, reconnects, and the organiser sees it complete with the evidence.
* Two people change the same task offline (one completes, one renames), and after reconnect it is complete with the new name.
* Moving an Event start date by 7 days moves every relative task by 7 days in preview, and on confirm, with absolute-date tasks untouched.
* A dependency cycle is rejected online and flagged when created by two offline edits.
* A guest sees only their tasks; revoking them removes the tasks from their device on next sync.
* An agent acting for a crew member cannot assign someone else or sign off.

## 13. Out of scope

Time tracking and timesheets (F12), shift rosters (F2), rules over non-task triggers and actions (F14 extends the <issue id="cbcfb707-a7d4-4089-8e84-d9e2a2bd4d94" label="EVE-235" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-235/f310-build-the-task-rule-builder-when-x-then-y-on-a-generic-rule" /> engine), portfolio and resource-levelling views across tenants, Gantt baselines, dependency types other than finish-to-start, public task boards for attendees.

## 14. Dependencies

* Phase 1: [EVE-40](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema>) (actions), [EVE-42](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state>) (storage, state machines, tenant guard), [EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>) (permissions, approvals, guests), [EVE-44](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor>) (telemetry), [EVE-45](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change>) (change feed), [EVE-46](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-46/p17-build-the-http-api-streaming-and-the-typed-client-from-the-action>) (HTTP), [EVE-48](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-48/p19-build-inbound-mcp-from-the-action-inventory>) (MCP), [EVE-50](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen>) (screen awareness), [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>) (sync and Yjs), [EVE-52](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-52/p18a-build-the-agent-turn-loop-with-actions-as-tools>) and [EVE-54](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow>) (agent loop and durable runs). Spikes: [EVE-16](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-16/s3-prove-runtime-loading-and-switching-of-a-remote-module-on-expo-web>), [EVE-17](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and>).
* Port later: [EVE-24](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email>) (notifications), [EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>) (attachments), [EVE-26](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-26/port-search-and-embeddings-across-every-resource>) (search), [EVE-27](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-27/port-comments-mentions-and-review-suggestions-on-any-resource>) (comments), [EVE-33](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters>) (recurrence and calendars).
* Feature sets: F1 (Event, Phase, Segment, ItineraryItem as anchors), F2 (Shift links and who is on the Event), F4 (guests as contacts), F6, F7 and F10 (link targets), F14 (custom fields, custom views, and extending the F3 rule engine to other sets).
* Rambo-UI has no components yet; the screens need its list, board, sheet, checkbox, date picker and rich text editor.

## 15. Decisions for Jonathan

Decided 2026-11-08 on one card: 1A, 2A, 3A, 4A, 5A, 6A, 7B.

1. **Offline status conflicts.** A: completion wins until an explicit reopen (recommended: a ticked safety check must not be silently un-ticked). B: last writer wins.
2. **Dependency types.** A: finish-to-start with lag only (recommended: covers event work; the others add UI weight with little use). B: all four types now.
3. **Statuses.** A: five fixed categories with tenant-renameable labels; custom workflows come with F14 (recommended). B: fully custom workflows in F3.
4. **Task description.** A: Yjs rich text embedded in the record (recommended: same model as other documents, co-editable). B: plain text field.
5. **External assignees.** A: guests in F3, limited to their own tasks (recommended: vendors and freelancers are a large share of event work). B: wait for F4 and F5.
6. **Agent writes.** A: agent creates and edits for the requester freely (undoable), confirm for assigning others, bulk over 10 or 25 for templates, never signs off (recommended). B: confirm every agent write.
7. **Automation rules.** A: no rule builder in F3; F3 emits events and the agent plus F14 rules act on them (was recommended). B: build a "when X then Y" rule builder in F3. **Chosen: B.** Built as a domain-agnostic rule engine that F14 extends, so there is still only one engine (<issue id="cbcfb707-a7d4-4089-8e84-d9e2a2bd4d94" label="EVE-235" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-235/f310-build-the-task-rule-builder-when-x-then-y-on-a-generic-rule" />).

## 16. Child issues

In build order. F3.2, F3.3, F3.6, F3.7 and F3.8 can run in parallel once F3.1 lands.

 1. <issue id="d63643eb-423b-4502-b0a5-e4b99c887f54" label="EVE-64" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-64/f31-build-task-lists-and-tasks-as-synced-records-with-actions" /> F3.1 Task lists and tasks as synced records
 2. <issue id="f941b8f6-0309-45e0-9d56-60feddd2f985" label="EVE-70" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-70/f32-build-checklists-with-photo-evidence-and-sign-off-that-work" /> F3.2 Checklists, evidence and sign-off
 3. <issue id="b092122b-6aea-4fec-b8c4-e1baf084c342" label="EVE-72" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-72/f33-build-subtasks-and-finish-to-start-dependencies-with-blocker" /> F3.3 Subtasks and dependencies
 4. <issue id="5a6f845d-5c7a-450c-8e8d-cef1b7ddbc80" label="EVE-84" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-84/f34-build-event-relative-due-dates-task-templates-and-reschedule" /> F3.4 Event-relative dates, templates and rescheduling
 5. <issue id="1bd1df6b-b667-44f0-a5c5-5c560cec94e4" label="EVE-86" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-86/f35-build-the-task-screens-with-screen-projections-on-web-and-mobile" /> F3.5 Task screens
 6. <issue id="d838fcc2-59de-47d6-a932-ab003b58cbab" label="EVE-89" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-89/f36-build-task-reminders-watchers-and-notifications" /> F3.6 Reminders, watchers and notifications
 7. <issue id="f473bd5a-7c18-4d18-9c69-ef2e48648a7d" label="EVE-93" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-93/f37-build-recurring-tasks-on-the-shared-scheduling-rules" /> F3.7 Recurring tasks
 8. <issue id="a4c6a5ee-ff88-4b6c-b564-dee9d8c82f59" label="EVE-109" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-109/f38-build-guest-assignees-so-vendors-and-freelancers-see-only-their" /> F3.8 Guest assignees
 9. <issue id="ce4d47c5-899a-4972-b02e-c6297c0c3a40" label="EVE-110" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-110/f39-build-agent-behaviour-for-tasks-planning-blockers-digests-and" /> F3.9 Agent behaviour for tasks
10. <issue id="cbcfb707-a7d4-4089-8e84-d9e2a2bd4d94" label="EVE-235" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-235/f310-build-the-task-rule-builder-when-x-then-y-on-a-generic-rule" /> F3.10 Rule builder (after F3.1 and F3.3; can run alongside F3.4 to F3.9)

comments.body: Cross-feature requirement from Eventiva live-operations design (Jonathan, 2026-11-13; canonical discussion on EVE-71): Event-relative task templates are needed for repeatable production jobs on tours/multi-venue events. Example: "Rig sound system in Space X" for Crew A, repeated across tour stops with per-venue assignments, locations and dates. Tasks scheduled ahead of time remain in **Scheduled/Upcoming**, then become eligible for the active CAD dispatch board near their planned start; active dispatch and completed history remain distinct. Preserve the association between the Task/template/event milestone and its operational assignment/status/log; don't duplicate separate task execution logic inside F7. Rescheduling an event should recompute future relative deadlines, flag conflicts, and preserve in-progress/completed history. Exact release/activation semantics (automatic vs controller confirmation) remain open for Jonathan's decision. This comment clarifies product requirements only, not implementation approval.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
## Live-operations scheduling and dependency decision — Jonathan, 13 Nov 2026

**User-approved design direction:** Support both release modes for pre-scheduled production tasks: **automatic is the preferred default**, and **controller approval before dispatch** is configurable for an organisation/event/task according to its policy. Crew can be assigned to their planned tasks in advance, so work is visible and prepared without requiring controllers to manually dispatch every routine job. An already assigned/scheduled item is **not necessarily active or safe to start**.

**Hard dependency gate:** A scheduled task may activate only when (a) its planned start/release condition is satisfied, (b) **every required predecessor dependency is completed and any required sign-off is valid**, and (c) any configured controller release/approval has occurred. For example **Install power → Install lighting rig**: even when the lighting task's scheduled start time arrives, it must remain blocked if power installation is incomplete. Neither a timer nor an agent may bypass this gate. When prerequisites clear after the scheduled start, auto-release the eligible task in automatic mode; in manual mode place it in the controller's ready-for-release queue. Detect cycles and do not silently ignore broken references, revoked sign-offs or failed completion validation. For work already active when a predecessor is later reopened or invalidated, surface a safety/blocker alert and require a documented operational decision rather than silently rewinding its history.

**CAD/MDT presentation:** Distinguish Upcoming/Scheduled, Blocked/Waiting, Ready-to-release, Active/In progress, Complete and Cancelled in views/status projections, without replacing F3's canonical Task status categories or F7's separate Incident statuses. A task behind schedule with unmet dependencies remains **blocked and late**, not active; display its scheduled time, elapsed delay, precise blocker(s), responsible crew and downstream jobs at risk. Surface this in both the controller's CAD board and the assigned crew's MDT. Use colour + text/icon (not colour alone), with accessible high-contrast and screen-reader status. Make upcoming and blocked tasks visible to assignees but prevent 'start', operational dispatch and unsafe next-step actions until unblocked. Show critical downstream consequences, and consider configurable notifications/escalation while avoiding alert floods.

**Technical boundaries:** Use the F3 canonical TaskTemplate/TaskDependency model, Event/Phase relative dates and F7 operations action inventory, with one auditable workflow rather than duplicating separate task engines. Repeated tour dates instantiate independent task schedules and dependencies with per-venue substitutions. Offline state may show last-known readiness but must not fabricate a verified dependency completion or initiate privileged dispatch without current authorization. Agent proposals remain subject to the same dependency and approval gates; live incident dispatch still requires controller approval. Clarify state-vs-eligibility and exact notification thresholds during implementation planning.

This records UX/functional policy, not approval for code changes or dependencies; do not interrupt the four currently researching foundation orbs.

**F3 scope:** Own dependency truth, relative start timing, blocked-state derivation, wait reasons, audit receipts, and task projections. Avoid separate scheduler flags that drift from task completion, status and sign-off.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
Decision from Jonathan (13 November 2026): **Automatically and continuously recalculate the working/forecast schedule of dependency-linked tasks as their predecessors run late. Preserve the original planned schedule unchanged for comparison and audit.** This supersedes the earlier proposal for human confirmation of each automatic cascade, but does not grant any agent authority to bypass execution approvals or safety-critical sign-offs.

Required model and behaviour:
- Persist an immutable original/baseline scheduled start and finish (or original duration/offset); retain subsequent plan revisions and the reasons/actor/time for changes, rather than overwriting history. Distinguish this baseline from the current forecast/effective planned times and actual start/finish.
- Forecast dependent tasks against predecessor completion/forecast completion, duration, any finish-to-start lag, task's earliest permitted start, and relevant constraints. Recompute downstream critical paths on fresh status/estimate changes; propagate delays through the dependency graph. Don't assume a precise new time when predecessor ETA is unknown: indicate uncertainty/awaiting estimate.
- **Delay = working/forecast start minus original baseline start**, displayed explicitly as a duration, alongside original time, current forecast time, blocking predecessor(s), and affected downstream tasks. Keep an accessible CAD and crew MDT presentation with conspicuous textual/icon overdue/blocked and knock-on indicators; use colour as supplement.
- Keep dependency gating separate from timetable forecasting: scheduled tasks may be preassigned and visible but must not become active before prerequisites/sign-off and applicable release approval. Recalculation must not silently shift actual/historical completions, override a manually locked commitment or erase the original schedule.
- Repeated tour/event templates instantiate per-event baselines. Preserve cross-event visibility without silently modifying a different show's locked commitments.

Example: power work originally due to complete 10:00; lighting originally scheduled to begin 10:00, forecast power completion changes to 10:45 -> lighting forecast start becomes 10:45 or later according to other prerequisites, displayed +45 min versus its original 10:00 baseline. If power ETA changes, update the lighting forecast and downstream impacts accordingly.

This is a product-spec decision, not an instruction to implement now or approve dependencies; foundation AMP orbs remain on their existing tasks.

F3 owns persisted baseline/revision history, dependencies, and forecast computation exposed through a single task projection to other surfaces.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
**Product decision, 13 Nov 2026 (Jonathan): delay tolerance for automated dependency rescheduling.** Set default tolerance to **10 minutes** (correcting initial verbal suggestion of five). It must be configurable as **any numeric minute value from 5 to 60 inclusive**, with range validation; do not limit to preset options such as 5/10/15-minute increments. Expose an editable tolerance in the appropriate authorised scheduling configuration, inherited as the default for new schedules/events, with effective value visible in the UI.

**Semantics:** Continuously calculate and display actual/estimated lateness, original baseline, current projected times and knock-on effects, even below the tolerance. The configured threshold controls when a newly predicted delay should **trigger an automatic rescheduling cascade / revision of the working schedule and corresponding notifications**, not whether users can see the delay. At or above the tolerance, apply the automatic cascade; do not overwrite the immutable original baseline or actual historical times. Required finish-to-start dependencies and any safety/approval gates remain strictly enforced **regardless of tolerance**: a 9-minute delay under a 10-minute tolerance never authorises an otherwise blocked dependent task to start. If a prerequisite is not done, display it as blocked even if no cascade has yet been triggered. Avoid repeatedly duplicating schedule revisions while a delay remains unchanged; use idempotent updates and clearly show a live forecast distinct from the last committed working schedule when relevant.

Avoid making per-person terminology/preferences override tenant operational governance; decide the exact configuration scope as part of the UI/policy design. This is a requirements decision, not permission to change code, introduce packages or interrupt the foundation orbs.
F3 owns the tolerance setting, forecast computation, automatic cascade trigger, revision history and validation.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

issues.title: F6 Warehousing and inventory: equipment, stock, availability, purchasing and maintenance
issues.description:
Status: Approved (2026-11-08, Jonathan approved D1 to D6 as recommended). Planning only; no implementation until Jonathan asks. Follows the [Feature set spec template](<https://linear.app/resnovas/document/feature-set-spec-template-and-list-26b9f78cf17a>). F1 entities (Event, Phase, run of show, itinerary, venue or site) are referenced by name and owned by F1.

## 1. Goal

A production company always knows what equipment and stock it owns, where every item is, whether it is free for an event, what it needs to buy or hire in, and whether it is safe to use, and the agent can do all of that through the same actions as the crew.

## 2. Users and jobs

| User | Jobs |
| -- | -- |
| Warehouse manager | Keep the catalogue and locations, approve adjustments, plan prep, resolve discrepancies, run stock counts |
| Warehouse crew | Prep, pick, scan out, scan in, report damage, move items between bins, often offline |
| Production manager or organiser (F1) | Put equipment on an event, see shortages, approve sub-hire and purchases |
| Event crew (F2 rostered) | Receive kit on site, check what is on the truck, report missing or damaged items |
| Technician or inspector | Run inspections (electrical, lifting), log repairs, release or quarantine assets |
| Purchaser | Raise purchase requests and orders, chase suppliers, receive goods |
| Finance (F11) | Asset register value, depreciation, purchase accruals, write-offs |
| Supplier (external) | View and confirm a purchase order or sub-hire sent to them |
| Agent | Everything above within the delegated user's permissions; proactive shortage, maintenance and reorder alerts |

## 3. Market check

From public product pages and listings (Current RMS, Flex Rental Solutions, Rentman, plus Odoo Inventory as the ERP reference), not hands-on trials. Names stay out of customer-facing copy.

* Rental and production tools (Current RMS, Flex, Rentman) all model products with serialised and bulk stock, kits and containers, availability over date ranges against jobs, barcode check-out and check-in on a mobile app, sub-rental (rent in) from other companies, and repair and inspection tracking. Rentman and Current RMS sell crew scheduling and warehouse in one product; Flex is strongest on warehouse workflow and container nesting.
* Odoo Inventory models stock as double-entry moves between locations (including virtual locations for suppliers, customers, scrap and adjustments), with routes, reorder rules and purchase integration. It is the clearest reference for a ledger that accounting can trust.
* Where Eventiva matches: serialised, bulk and consumable tracking; kits and nested containers; availability calendar; scan out and in; sub-hire; inspections; purchasing with reorder points.
* Where Eventiva differs: (1) one append-only stock ledger shared by people and agents, which merges offline without conflicts; (2) equipment comes from the F1 production plan, so a lighting or rigging plan produces the pick list; (3) warehouse, vehicles (F7), site maps (F10) and accounting (F11) are one platform rather than integrations; (4) every operation is an agent action, so "what am I short for Saturday and hire it in" is one request with approval.
* Gaps we do not chase in phase 1: marketplace for renting spare stock to other companies (F5 later), EDI or punchout with suppliers, RFID portals.

## 4. Capabilities as actions

## 5. Data model

All tables carry `org_id` (tenant guard, <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" />) and audit columns; ids are client-generated (UUIDv7) so offline writes are idempotent (<issue id="1b79a257-9ea0-40b5-a8f7-23e1c09221be" label="EVE-39" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-39/make-every-entity-action-idempotent-and-persisted-by-default" />).

| Entity | Key fields | Relations | Offline sync | Conflict rule |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Product | name, sku, category, tracking (`serialised`, `bulk`, `consumable`), unit, weight, dimensions, power draw, replacement value, required inspection types | Kit components, SupplierProduct, images (<issue id="8d8d301b-d679-4dac-95bb-c24889179cd0" label="EVE-25" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import" />) | Synced read to all warehouse devices; edits online or offline | Last writer wins per field, audit keeps both |
| Kit | kit product, component lines (product, qty, optional) | Product | Synced | Replace whole component list; later write wins, with a conflict note |
| Asset | product, serial, tag code (barcode or QR), cost, purchase ref, in-service date, condition, quarantine flag, retired | Product, Location (derived), Movement | Synced for assets on the device's scopes | Per field last writer wins; quarantine set wins over release until an explicit online release |
| Location | type (`warehouse`, `zone`, `bin`, `vehicle`, `event-site`, `supplier`, `repair`, `virtual`), parent, refs to F7 Vehicle or F1 Event | Tree | Synced | Last writer wins per field |
| StockMovement | product, asset (optional), qty, from, to, reason, refs (Event, Reservation, PickList, PO, SubHire, Count), actor (person or agent), device, occurred_at | append-only | Insert only, synced everywhere it is scoped | No conflicts: inserts commute; duplicates rejected by id |
| StockLevel | product, location, qty | derived from movements | Projection, rebuilt locally | Never written directly; negative levels raise a Discrepancy |
| Reservation | F1 Event, Phase, window (out date, return due), lines (product qty or asset), status (`hold`, `confirmed`, `picking`, `out`, `returned`, `cancelled`), source (`manual`, `plan`, `sales`) | PickList | Synced to event crew and warehouse | Server re-checks availability on sync; an overbooked line becomes `conflict` and raises a shortage, never silently dropped |
| PickList | reservation, assigned people (F2), lines with expected and scanned counts, status | Movements | Synced to assigned devices | Scans are movements, so they merge; line counts are derived |
| Discrepancy | type (`missing`, `extra`, `damaged`, `wrong-item`, `double-checkout`, `negative-stock`), refs, notes (Yjs text, <issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" />), photos, resolution | Asset, Movement | Synced | Notes merge as text; resolution is last writer wins with audit |
| MaintenanceJob, Inspection | asset, type, due date, result, certificate file, inspector, next due | Asset | Synced | Append-only results; due date last writer wins |
| SupplierProduct | F4 Organisation, product, supplier sku, price, currency, lead time | Product | Synced read | Last writer wins |
| PurchaseRequest, PurchaseOrder, GoodsReceipt | lines, status, totals, refs to Event | Supplier, Movements, F11 bill | Drafts editable offline; approve, send and cancel need connectivity | Per line last writer wins on drafts; status changes are server-ordered |
| SubHire | supplier, lines, window, event, PO ref, return state | Movements (into `supplier` location) | As PurchaseOrder | As PurchaseOrder |
| StockCount | location, expected snapshot, counted lines, adjustments | Movements | Synced to counting devices | Counts are per device then summed; finalise is online only |

Documents embedded in records: discrepancy and repair notes are Yjs text on the record (<issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" />), permissioned and versioned with the record. Warehouse floor plans are F10 site maps, not F6.

Sync scopes: a warehouse device gets its warehouse's catalogue, locations, levels and open pick lists; an event crew device gets only its event's reservation, pick lists and those assets; costs and supplier prices sync only to purchaser and finance roles.

## 7. Agent behaviour

Asked: "What am I short for the festival on Saturday?", "Put the lighting plan on the event and hire in what we are missing", "Where is case 0412?", "Which hoists are due for inspection this month?", "Reorder haze fluid".

Proactive, as suggestions in the agent inbox (never silent writes):

* Shortage found when a reservation, plan change or returned-damaged item leaves an event short; offers sub-hire, purchase, substitute product, or moving stock from another warehouse.
* Inspection or service coming due on an asset reserved for an upcoming event; offers to schedule it before the out date.
* Consumable below its reorder point; drafts a purchase request.
* After check-in, items still out past the return date; drafts discrepancies and a message to the crew lead.

Approval: the agent may create holds, draft pick lists, draft requests and orders, and record scans when the user drives it. It needs confirm for adjustments above the threshold, finalising counts, retiring assets and releasing quarantine; it always needs approval to send an order or sub-hire to a supplier or cancel a sent one. The agent can never release a failed safety inspection; only a person with `inventory:inspection:release` can.

## 8. Integrations

Each behind a neutral Effect port in its own integration package; no vendor chosen yet.

* Scanner port: camera barcode and QR (new dependency, approval on F6.5); hardware scanners in keyboard mode need no dependency; RFID is a later adapter.
* Label printer port: PDF labels first (no vendor); networked label printer adapter later.
* Supplier delivery port: send purchase orders and sub-hires by email through [EVE-24](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email>) with a PDF; supplier portal link for confirm. EDI and punchout out of scope.
* Accounting (agreed with F11, <issue id="158ba369-976e-47ea-9f86-a8df608cb4d0" label="EVE-69" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-69/f11-accounting-ledgers-invoices-bills-event-budgets-and-tax" />): each goods receipt emits `inventory:goods_received` on the change feed at the time (PO id, PO line ids, quantities, unit cost in integer minor units, currency, F1 Event id, supplier F4 Contact id) for three-way matching; `inventory.valuation.exportToAccounts` emits `inventory:valuation_exported` per period for depreciation, average-cost movements, asset additions and retirements, and write-offs. F6 stores F11 tax code ids, never its own rates.
* Production plans (agreed with F1, <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" />): `inventory.reservation.fromPlan` reads F1 `EquipmentRequirement` rows (event_id, phase_id, department_id, catalogue_ref = F6 Product id, quantity, needed_from, needed_to), handed over by F1's `requirement.sendToWarehouse`. Event-site locations reference an F1 `Event` or `Space`.
* Tax and currency: from F11 settings.

Sales contract with F9 (agreed with the F9 thread, 2026-11-01): F9 registers line kind `stock` and calls `inventory.reservation.create` on add to cart (returns reservation id and expiry, keyed by an F6 Product and a Location such as a warehouse or an event booth), `commit` when the order is paid, and `release` on cart expiry, cancel or refund with restock. Holds from carts carry an expiry and source `sales`. Offline point of sale cannot reserve live: the device writes commutative sale movements, and an oversell shows as negative stock and a `negative-stock` Discrepancy on sync rather than rejecting the sale. An F9 sellable product links to an F6 Product by id and never redefines it.

## 10. Telemetry and flags

* Flag: `f6-inventory` (default off) gates the set; per-slice flags `f6-purchasing`, `f6-subhire`, `f6-maintenance`, `f6-valuation`.
* Events: `inventory_reservation_created`, `inventory_shortage_detected`, `inventory_scan_recorded` (with offline true or false), `inventory_pick_completed` (variance count), `inventory_discrepancy_raised`, `inventory_inspection_recorded`, `purchasing_order_sent`, `inventory_agent_suggestion_accepted`.
* Spans on every action (<issue id="a03acb76-125b-4ead-815e-10ec986d8413" label="EVE-44" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor" />); scan latency and offline queue depth as metrics.
* Success metric: share of events whose kit goes out and returns with zero unresolved discrepancies after 7 days; target 95 percent. Guard metric: median scan-to-confirm under 300 ms on device.

## 11. Compliance

Rules are configuration per jurisdiction; the UK is the first set and is verified against current guidance before F6.7 is built.

* Lifting equipment (rigging, hoists, truss accessories): thorough examination intervals and records under LOLER 1998 (6 months for equipment lifting people and for accessories, 12 months otherwise), and use of work equipment under PUWER 1998. A failed or overdue examination blocks check-out.
* Portable electrical equipment: in-service inspection and testing records (IET Code of Practice); failed test quarantines the asset.
* Hazardous consumables (haze and smoke fluids, pyrotechnics): storage limits and safety data sheets; pyrotechnic storage licensing is flagged as out of scope for phase 1 and blocks marking pyro as stock until reviewed.
* Purchase and asset records kept 6 years for tax (HMRC); VAT handled by F11.
* Personal data: custody records name people (who scanned what); retained under the org's retention policy, exportable and erasable per GDPR without breaking the ledger (actor pseudonymised on erasure).
* Disposal of electrical equipment recorded for WEEE.

## 12. Acceptance

* A product with serialised, bulk and consumable variants can be catalogued, received on a purchase order, reserved on an F1 Event, picked, scanned out offline on two devices, scanned in, and the levels match on every device after reconnect.
* Two devices scanning the same serialised asset out offline produce one `double-checkout` discrepancy after sync, and no lost movement.
* An overbooked reservation made offline is flagged as a shortage on sync with sub-hire and purchase options.
* An asset with an overdue lifting examination cannot be scanned out; the agent cannot override it.
* The agent completes "short for Saturday, hire it in" end to end through actions, stopping for approval before sending the sub-hire.
* Every control on every F6 screen is bound to an action (<issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" /> check passes) and every action passes the <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" /> parity target.
* Valuation export for a period balances against the movement ledger.

## 13. Out of scope

Selling or renting equipment to customers (quotes and prices are F9, invoices are F11; F6 supplies availability and reservations), vehicle maintenance (F7), warehouse floor plans (F10), the general ledger (F11), RFID portals, EDI and punchout, marketplace hire to other companies (F5 later), manufacturing or bills of materials beyond kits, multi-currency landed cost.
