| D3 | Scanning in phase 1 | (a) camera barcode and QR plus hardware scanners in keyboard mode, RFID later; (b) include RFID now | (a): no hardware vendor needed to start |
| D4 | Offline check-out of a serialised item already out | (a) accept and raise a discrepancy on sync; (b) block offline check-out of serialised items | (a): crews in basements and venues keep working; the ledger keeps both scans |
| D5 | Purchasing scope | (a) F6 owns requests, orders, receiving and reorder points; supplier bills go to F11; (b) purchasing moves wholly to F11 | (a): receiving is a warehouse job |
| D6 | Valuation | (a) cost per serialised asset with straight-line depreciation, average cost for bulk and consumables, exported to F11; (b) FIFO for everything | (a): matches how rental fleets are valued |

## 16. Child issues

In build order:

 1. <issue id="eaa9fbf7-7a3c-4c1c-9470-a76edd5316ff" label="EVE-81" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-81/f61-build-the-equipment-catalogue-products-tracking-modes-and-kits" /> F6.1 Equipment catalogue: products, tracking modes and kits
 2. <issue id="606e799c-90cf-4e59-a1b8-77e6f0dad633" label="EVE-103" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-103/f62-build-locations-and-the-append-only-stock-movement-ledger" /> F6.2 Locations and the append-only stock movement ledger
 3. <issue id="cb4c273f-1a14-4e3d-a8de-fb3cf1afa4d7" label="EVE-118" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-118/f63-build-the-serialised-asset-register-containers-and-labels" /> F6.3 Serialised asset register, containers and labels
 4. <issue id="676ab6ef-a290-4e84-a999-c4b8975eeb89" label="EVE-123" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-123/f64-build-availability-and-reservations-against-events-carts-and" /> F6.4 Availability and reservations against events, carts and production plans
 5. <issue id="1796f4cf-9de8-49b9-962f-825f58d9adc7" label="EVE-149" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-149/f65-build-prep-pick-lists-and-offline-scan-out-and-scan-in" /> F6.5 Prep, pick lists and offline scan out and scan in
 6. <issue id="439edb35-70a7-4cfc-8ef2-d1999be94377" label="EVE-150" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-150/f66-build-discrepancies-damage-reports-and-asset-quarantine" /> F6.6 Discrepancies, damage reports and asset quarantine
 7. <issue id="a30ae0e7-1f07-450d-be07-f6951c016315" label="EVE-151" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-151/f67-build-maintenance-repairs-and-safety-inspections-for-lifting-and" /> F6.7 Maintenance, repairs and safety inspections
 8. <issue id="1399347c-26db-4939-8de9-b75f95a6c6bf" label="EVE-187" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-187/f68-build-purchasing-supplier-products-requests-orders-receiving-and" /> F6.8 Purchasing: supplier products, requests, orders, receiving and reorder points
 9. <issue id="68cc7f08-be03-4b3b-8533-13124aafab5a" label="EVE-188" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-188/f69-build-sub-hire-renting-in-equipment-from-other-suppliers-for-an" /> F6.9 Sub-hire
10. <issue id="e7a50ec7-4e4c-4031-ad8e-988787e6717a" label="EVE-189" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-189/f610-build-stock-counts-and-cycle-counts-with-offline-counting" /> F6.10 Stock counts and cycle counts
11. <issue id="34869faa-3669-491c-b2a0-f104a1be1812" label="EVE-190" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-190/f611-build-stock-valuation-asset-depreciation-and-the-per-period" /> F6.11 Valuation, depreciation and export to accounting
12. <issue id="12170955-2a99-42eb-b6a5-e460ad492a78" label="EVE-198" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-198/f612-build-the-inventory-agent-behaviours-shortages-inspections-due" /> F6.12 Inventory agent behaviours

New dependencies to approve when their slice starts: a barcode and PDF label library (F6.3) and camera barcode reading on Expo (F6.5).

### Planning coordination D6-7 - product/spec evidence and supplier-driven catalogue import (2026-11-13)

Keep tenant-owned inventory Product, Asset, Kit and stock ledger separate from a potentially shared manufacturer/model specification reference and supplier listing projections. A supplier can select a known model for a quotation or upload a new one and supporting datasheet; use structured category-specific fields (intended use, dimensions/weight, compatibility, interfaces, power/RF, kit contents), units, document provenance, revision and verification state. Detect duplicates before creating a new reference; incomplete/unverified data remains clearly indicated. Do not automatically promote a supplier statement or extracted document to a verified reference. Historical quotes point at the evidence version originally evaluated.

F6 reservations/holds/hire-out, dispatch, returns and maintenance determine actual supplier stock state; F5 receives only permission-controlled, as-of availability/capacity projections for specific date/quantity requests. Avoid exposing other customers' jobs, serials, private counts or valuation across tenant boundaries. Procurement comparison owns context-specific equivalence results, not F6 master identity. Include explicit technical/availability freshness and test matching plus no cross-tenant leakage. See <issue id="f08bafe4-f32d-4906-9e87-5d69df56d6a0" label="EVE-124" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-124/f58-build-quotes-quote-comparison-and-the-acceptance-handoff-to-the" /> D5-14. Planning only.

## Planning decision D6-8 - private-first supplier inventory capture and independent directory disclosure (2026-11-13; coordinates F5 D5-15)

### Confirmed scope

Encourage suppliers to manage detailed, accurate structured stock and product specs within their **own** Eventiva tenant (including movements, hired-out/reserved units, returns and maintenance), even when they choose not to show this information to buyers. Separate F6's private authoritative data from F5's revocable, policy-generated public/customer projections. D5-16/D6-9 supersede the earlier matching restriction: directory recommendation matching is default-enabled under transparent supplier-facing terms with an explicit opt-out, but storing data does not permit unrestricted cross-tenant disclosure, unrelated processing or shared-model training.

### Policy

* F5 inventory display preference has three supplier-configurable levels: detailed inventory/product + permitted stock availability; date-based availability only without counts; private/no buyer-facing inventory information. Support organisation default with category/product overrides and permission-controlled changes. Do not equate 'detailed' with disclosing serials, client identities, warehouse bins, valuation, cost/margin or other tenant-private operational fields.
* Track a **default-enabled, explicit supplier opt-out** for eligible directory matching, with clear onboarding notice, controlled purpose and audit. A hidden-stock supplier may be included in generic recommendations but private equipment/quantity/date reasoning must not leak via search/re-ranking/agent APIs. Confirm lawful basis and terms before enabling for existing tenants. Its own tenant agent still uses its private stock within its roles.
* Provide low-friction data capture: import/select manufacturer/model references, validate specifications, enter owned quantities and movements, reconcile duplicates and accept updates with provenance. Offline stock workflows remain supported. Missing inventory is not automatically a negative business signal.
* Public/read projections must be derived through tenant- and action-scoped permissions, include data freshness, and avoid using an unapproved or stale signal to promise a hire. Publishing, changing permissions and revoking sharing are auditable; invalidate active search/index/cache projections on revocation. Historical contractual snapshots persist under separate lawful/approved access.
* Product reference contributions must not expose a supplier's private SKU, usage, stock count, prices or customer projects. Technical product specs and supplier private inventory remain separate records. Do not use private data for general-purpose AI training by default; any such purpose requires a separate explicit authorisation and policy.

### Validation

* A supplier manages 50 microphones, 10 reserved and 15 out on hire internally. Under 'dates only' an organiser sees permitted date availability but not private counts or hire movements; under 'private' the supplier may still receive a generic public-category/area recommendation using protected internal eligibility signals, but no counts, dates, stock-specific rationale or reconstructable ranking data is exposed.
* Product-specific sharing overrides the tenant default without changing underlying stock ledger or related bookings. Unauthorised API, MCP, external agent and search routes cannot bypass disclosure.
* Visibility reduction halts public stock disclosures without automatically switching off default recommendation matching. Explicit **matching opt-out** halts cross-tenant stock-derived candidate ranking and invalidates relevant caches within a defined bound; ordinary public directory search, private stock operations and private agents remain available.

### Open decision

**Resolved by D5-16 and D6-9:** inventory-backed matching is default-on with clear supplier notice and explicit opt-out; even for hidden inventory, buyer-facing content may use only independently public general supplier attributes. Exposure/inference protection and applicable lawful basis remain implementation checks, not permission to reveal private stock. F6 stays authoritative for stock; F5 owns directory presentation. Planning only.

## Planning decision D6-9 - default-on internal supplier matching, explicit opt-out, independent stock visibility (2026-11-13)

### Goal / supersession

The supplier may maintain full F6 stock records and configure what buyers see, while F5 can use eligible supplier stock and availability internally for recommendations **by default**, until the supplier explicitly opts out. This supersedes D6-8's proposed opt-in gate. A 'hidden inventory' display level suppresses detailed buyer-facing disclosures, **not** internal matching. Do not treat this as permission to train shared models or disclose information from other clients.

### Permission and information-flow contract

* Make directory matching participation a supplier-level default-enabled setting with clear onboarding/import notice and one-action opt-out. Supplier agreement and lawful basis must be checked, particularly before any rollout to existing tenants. Use a tenant-aware server action to evaluate eligibility, not expose raw private F6 inventory to a consuming organiser tenant or its AI agent.
* Publishable field projection remains detailed, date-only or hidden, independently configurable by supplier and optionally category/product. The policy evaluation supplies F5 a **non-disclosing recommendation eligibility result** and only the explicitly publishable evidence permitted by the chosen visibility setting.
* If visibility is hidden, candidate inclusion is allowed, but public justification can rely only on independently public supplier listing facts (category, geography/service area etc.). Never reveal a hidden model, count, date, stock status, estimated capability, booking clash or 'technically meets your specific item' claim. Guard against repeated-query and ranking inference; if unsafe, use only ordinary publicly grounded eligibility for that query.
* An opt-out removes private-stock signals from F5 cross-tenant candidate generation/ranking and derived caches, without deleting inventory records or removing ordinary public supplier listings. Existing authorised quotes/commitments retain legitimate historic snapshots. All actions, agents, APIs and integrations enforce the same view.
* Internal agents may continue using the supplier's own data within its tenant under normal permissions. No default shared-model training from privately managed inventory; a separate governance decision is needed for that.

### Validation

A supplier whose inventory indicates availability but whose public setting is hidden may be shown as a general service-area supplier, not as 'stock confirmed'. Switching to dates-only shows only permitted time windows, detailed shows only approved stock fields, and opting out ends inventory-derived cross-tenant matching even if the public supplier listing remains searchable. Synthetic repeated-query tests must fail to recover hidden quantities/date coverage. All paths (UI, API, MCP, external agent) agree. Planning only.

issues.title: F3.1 Build task lists and tasks as synced records with actions
issues.description:
Status: Approved (2026-11-08, <issue id="4e19a499-139f-4016-88c4-264d3a0f7c33" label="EVE-62" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-62/f3-tasks-task-lists-assignments-dependencies-and-checklists-per-event" /> decisions). Planning only until Jonathan asks for implementation.

## Goal

People and agents create, assign, update and complete tasks on any Event, offline or online, through one set of actions.

## Context

* Parent spec: [EVE-62](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-62/f3-tasks-task-lists-assignments-dependencies-and-checklists-per-event>) sections 4 (actions), 5 (data model and conflict rules), 9 (permissions). Decisions 1, 3 and 4 there set the status rule, status categories and description model.
* F1 (<issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> section 5) owns Event, Phase, Department and Segment; a TaskList scopes to an Event (optionally a Phase and Department) or to the tenant, and a Task may carry Phase, Department and Segment refs. Reference them by id only. F1 readiness checks read open tasks per Department, so `task.list` must filter by Department.
* Record sync and Yjs come from [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>) on the engine [EVE-17](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and>) picks; tenant guards and state machines from [EVE-42](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state>); actions from [EVE-40](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema>).

## Scope

1. A `tasks` extension package (Nx `type:extension`), schemas in the shared schema package (<issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" />), no driver imports.
2. Tables: TaskList, Task, TaskAssignee, TaskLink, on Postgres and SQLite through Drizzle, tenant-scoped, soft delete.
3. Task status as an <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> state machine over the five categories (todo, in_progress, blocked, done, cancelled) with tenant-renameable labels.
4. Actions: `taskList.create`, `taskList.update`, `taskList.archive`, `task.create`, `task.update`, `task.assign`, `task.unassign`, `task.claim`, `task.setStatus`, `task.complete`, `task.reopen`, `task.move`, `task.delete`, `task.bulkUpdate`, `task.get`, `task.list`, `task.search` (filter-based; full text arrives with <issue id="2cd1c920-450c-487e-b4c8-e860a382a6b0" label="EVE-26" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-26/port-search-and-embeddings-across-every-resource" />), `task.myTasks`, `task.link`, `task.unlink`, with the permissions and approval policies in <issue id="4e19a499-139f-4016-88c4-264d3a0f7c33" label="EVE-62" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-62/f3-tasks-task-lists-assignments-dependencies-and-checklists-per-event" /> section 4.
5. Description as a Yjs document embedded in the Task record (<issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" /> embedded-document rules).
6. Field conflict rules from <issue id="4e19a499-139f-4016-88c4-264d3a0f7c33" label="EVE-62" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-62/f3-tasks-task-lists-assignments-dependencies-and-checklists-per-event" /> section 5, including "completion wins until explicit reopen".
7. Domain events (`task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.completed`, `task.assigned`) through <issue id="ee08644c-eb3c-4a46-aea7-745864ad4263" label="EVE-45" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change" />.
8. Feature flag `tasks`, default off.

## Acceptance criteria

* Every action is in the inventory and the parity check passes; each is callable through HTTP (<issue id="0ab161c4-ed9c-4581-86fe-91fa1f4216aa" label="EVE-46" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-46/p17-build-the-http-api-streaming-and-the-typed-client-from-the-action" />) and MCP (<issue id="37c126a9-64e0-4235-88f0-494533c8e3a2" label="EVE-48" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-48/p19-build-inbound-mcp-from-the-action-inventory" />) with identical results to the UI path in a test.
* Offline test: client A completes a task while client B renames it, both offline; after reconnect the task is done with B's title.
* Assignee set merge: A adds X and B adds Y offline; both are assigned after sync.
* Permission matrix test: crew can complete own task, cannot delete; an agent acting for a crew member cannot assign others; cross-tenant read denied.
* Undo of `task.delete` restores the task with its assignees and links.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 house rules (`Data.TaggedError`, `Context.Tag` services, Schema, `@effect/vitest`); no zod; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; docs for people and agents; graph refreshed; ships to main per the AGENTS.md delivery exception with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged to main with the offline, merge and permission tests green, and a comment here listing the actions and their JSON Schema snapshots.

## Blockers

[EVE-40](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema>), [EVE-42](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state>), [EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>), [EVE-45](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change>), [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>), [EVE-17](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and>), [EVE-23](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared>); F1 Event, Phase and Department records (<issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" />).

issues.title: F4 Contacts and CRM: people, organisations, relationships and history
issues.description:
Status: Proposed (2026-11-01). Follows the [feature set spec template](<https://linear.app/resnovas/document/feature-set-spec-template-and-list-26b9f78cf17a>). Planning only: no code, no new dependency and no vendor sign-up until Jonathan approves the decisions in section 15.

## 1. Goal

Every person and organisation an event business deals with (clients, vendors, venues, artists, crew, attendees, suppliers) lives once in Eventiva, with their relationships, their role on each event and their full history, so a person or the agent can answer "who is this, what have we done with them and what is next" from one record.

## 2. Users and jobs

| User | Jobs |
| -- | -- |
| Organiser or account manager | Capture an enquiry, track it to a booked event, see a client's history, plan follow-ups, find the right venue contact |
| Production manager | Find the vendor, venue and artist contacts attached to an event and their roles; share a contact sheet with crew |
| Crew member | See the contacts on today's event (venue manager, site security) on mobile, offline |
| Vendor or client (external) | Keep their own details and preferences current; see the events they are on |
| Attendee (external) | Manage their consent and contact preferences; request a copy or deletion of their data |
| Finance | Use the organisation record as the billing party (F11) without retyping details |
| Admin | Control who sees which contacts, run imports, merges and privacy requests |
| Agent | Log interactions, dedupe, summarise a relationship, draft follow-ups, move an opportunity, all through the same actions and approvals as a person |

## 3. Market check

Checked 2026-11-01 from public product pages and docs; names stay out of customer-facing copy.

* **Generic CRM (HubSpot style):** standard objects (contacts, companies, deals) plus custom objects, joined by typed associations with labels; a timeline of activities per record; pipelines with stages; consent and GDPR tooling (lawful basis, delete). Eventiva matches the object and association model and the per-record timeline. Differs: associations reach event records (F1) natively, and custom objects come from F14 rather than a CRM-only builder.
* **Modern relationship CRM (Attio style):** flexible records and lists, automatic enrichment of people and companies from email domains, mailbox and calendar sync that builds the relationship graph and "last interaction" automatically, and a strong API that agents drive. Eventiva matches mailbox-derived history and lists, and is agent-first by architecture rather than through an API add-on. Differs: no third-party enrichment by default (privacy and cost; decision D4).
* **Event and venue sales tools (Tripleseat style):** lead capture forms, leads converted to bookings with proposals, contracts and payments, accounts and contacts tied to each event, and reporting on lead sources and conversion. Eventiva matches enquiry to event conversion and per-event contact roles. Differs: proposals, contracts and payments live in F9 and F11, not in the CRM, and crew and vendor contacts share the same model as clients.

Gap none of them close and Eventiva targets: one identity per human across sales, production, crew, ticketing and HR, usable offline on a phone at the venue.

## 4. Capabilities as actions

Every operation is an inventory action (<issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />): Effect Schema input and output, typed errors, one authorization check, a receipt, audit, and a change record with undo where it mutates. Names use `crm.<entity>.<verb>`. Permissions: `crm:read`, `crm:write`, `crm:admin`, `crm:sensitive` (sensitive fields), `crm:privacy` (privacy requests). Approval: none unless stated.

| Action | Input | Output | Permission | Approval | Offline |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `crm.person.create` / `update` / `archive` / `restore` | person fields, contact points | Person | crm:write | none | yes |
| `crm.person.get` / `list` / `search` | id or filter, page | Person or page | crm:read | none | yes (local data) |
| `crm.organisation.create` / `update` / `archive` / `restore` / `get` / `list` | org fields | Organisation | crm:write or read | none | yes |
| `crm.affiliation.add` / `end` | person, org, title, dates | Affiliation | crm:write | none | yes |
| `crm.relationship.add` / `remove` | from, to, type | Relationship | crm:write | none | yes |
| `crm.eventRole.assign` / `unassign` | Event (F1) id, party, role | EventRole | crm:write plus event write | none | yes |
| `crm.interaction.log` / `update` / `delete` | party, kind, time, summary, links | Interaction | crm:write | none | yes |
| `crm.note.create` / `update` | party, document | Note (Yjs doc) | crm:write | none | yes |
| `crm.timeline.get` | party, filter, page | timeline entries | crm:read | none | yes (synced part) |
| `crm.tag.apply` / `remove`, `crm.list.create` / `update` / `addMembers` / `removeMembers` | tags, list def | Tag or List | crm:write | none | yes |
| `crm.smartList.evaluate` | saved filter | members page | crm:read | none | yes (local data) |
| `crm.duplicate.find` | party or all | candidate pairs with score | crm:read | none | yes |
| `crm.party.merge` / `unmerge` | survivor, merged ids, field choices | merged Party, merge record | crm:admin | confirm | no |
| `crm.import.start` / `crm.import.commit` | file ref ([EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>)), mapping | import report | crm:admin | confirm on commit | no |
| `crm.export.run` | filter, format | file ref | crm:admin | confirm | no |
| `crm.enquiry.capture` / `resolve` | form payload, source; or outcome won or lost | Enquiry | public form token, crm:write, or the F5 directory system principal for that tenant (audited) | none | yes (internal) |
| `crm.opportunity.create` / `update` / `moveStage` / `markWon` / `markLost` | opportunity fields, stage | Opportunity | crm:write | none | yes |
| `crm.opportunity.convertToEvent` | opportunity id, event template | Event (F1) id | crm:write plus event create | confirm | no |
| `crm.pipeline.define` / `update` | stages | Pipeline | crm:admin | none | no |
| `crm.mailbox.connect` / `disconnect` / `sync` | provider, scopes | MailboxConnection | own user | confirm on connect | no |
| `crm.consent.record` / `withdraw` / `get` | party, purpose, channel, basis, source | ConsentRecord | crm:write; party self | none | yes (queued) |
| `crm.privacy.requestExport` / `requestErasure` / `fulfil` | party, request | PrivacyRequest | crm:privacy; party self | always on fulfil erasure | no |
| `crm.followUp.schedule` | party, due, note | Task (F3) id | crm:write plus task write | none | yes |
| `crm.portal.invite` / `revoke` | party, scope | external principal ([EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>)) | crm:admin | confirm | no |
| `crm.relationship.summarise` | party | summary text and sources | crm:read | none | no (needs model) |

Navigation actions (<issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" />): `nav.crm.open`, `nav.crm.person.open`, `nav.crm.organisation.open`, `nav.crm.pipeline.open`.

## 5. Data model

All tables are tenant scoped (<issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> tenant guard) and carry the standard created and updated columns. IDs are typeids.

* **Party**: the supertype for Person and Organisation, so every relation, tag, timeline entry and event role points to one `party_id`. Fields: kind, display name, owner (member), visibility (`tenant`, `team`, `private`), archived at, merged into.
* **Person**: given name, family name, preferred name, pronouns (optional, free text), date of birth (sensitive), language, time zone, photo ([EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>) file), optional `user_id` link to an identity ([EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>)). A Person is not a login; a User is not a Person (decision D1).
* **Organisation**: legal name, trading name, kind (client, vendor, venue, agency, supplier, other; multi-select), registration and tax numbers (finance reads these in F11), website, domain list.
* **ContactPoint**: party, kind (email, phone, address, social, website), value, label, primary flag, verified at. Addresses use a structured schema with country, localised by [EVE-28](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-28/port-localization-for-people-and-for-the-agent>).
* **Affiliation**: person, organisation, title, department, start, end, primary flag.
* **Relationship**: from party, to party, type (reports to, assistant of, agent for, partner of, refers, other with label).
* **EventRole**: Event (F1), party, role (booker, venue contact, vendor, artist, artist management, promoter, sponsor, security, other), notes, on-site flag. The primary client is F1's `Event.client_ref` (a Party id), shown first in the event contacts tab and not duplicated as an EventRole. F1's TeamMember (`contact_ref` to a Person) is the internal event team and Rider performer `contact_ref` the artist; F4 keeps those Party ids stable (merge rewrites them through the reference owner contract). EventRole covers the other external business contacts. Crew shifts stay in F2.
* **Interaction**: party links (many), kind (call, meeting, email, message, visit, note), direction, occurred at, duration, summary, source (manual, mailbox, agent, system), external message id, links to Event (F1), Opportunity, Task (F3).
* **Note**: a Yjs document embedded in a Party record ([EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>)), with its own version history.
* **Tag**, **List** (static members) and **SmartList** (saved filter, evaluated on read). Named SmartList, not Segment, because Segment is an F1 run of show entity.
* **Enquiry**: source, raw payload, matched party, status (new, qualified, discarded, converted, won, lost), external ref (for example the F5 directory thread id).
* **Pipeline** and **Stage**; **Opportunity**: party, organisation, title, stage, value and currency, expected date, probability, owner, lost reason, converted Event (F1) id.
* **MailboxConnection**: member, provider, scopes, credential ref ([EVE-41](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-41/p12-build-app-config-settings-secrets-and-credentials>), never in the record), sync cursor, status.
* **ConsentRecord**: party, purpose (marketing email, SMS, photos, data sharing with vendors), channel, lawful basis, state, source, captured at, evidence. Append only.
* **PrivacyRequest**: party, kind (export, erasure, rectification), status, due at, fulfilled by, result file.
* **MergeRecord**: survivor, merged ids, field choices, reference rewrites, undo payload.

Timeline is a projection, not a table: it reads Interactions, Notes, ConsentRecords, Opportunities, EventRoles and domain events from other sets on the change feed (<issue id="ee08644c-eb3c-4a46-aea7-745864ad4263" label="EVE-45" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change" />) that name a party (an order in F9, a ticket in F8, an invoice in F11).

**Offline and conflicts (**<issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" />**,** <issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" />**):**

| Data | Syncs offline | Conflict rule |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Person and Organisation scalar fields | yes, per field | last writer wins per field, with both values kept in the change record so undo can restore either |
| ContactPoints, Affiliations, Relationships, EventRoles | yes, per row | row level add wins; concurrent edits of one row resolve per field as above |
| Tags and List members | yes | set merge, add wins, remove of an unseen add does not remove it |
| Notes | yes | Yjs merge |
| Interactions | yes, append mostly | per field last writer wins; delete wins over edit |
| Opportunity stage | yes | server orders stage moves by server receive time; a move to won or lost from a stale stage is rejected and returned to the user |
| ConsentRecord | queued only | append only; the latest captured at wins; withdrawal received offline is applied the moment it syncs and before any send |
| Merge, import, export, privacy fulfilment, mailbox sync, convert to event | no | online only; shown disabled offline with the reason |
| Sensitive fields | synced only to devices of members with `crm:sensitive` |  |

Local sync scope per device: contacts linked to the member's events in the next 30 days plus their owned and recently opened records, so a crew phone has the venue contacts without holding the whole CRM.

## 6. Screens

UI comes from Rambo-UI (no components exist yet at b47a58c; the components named below are the list F4 needs from it). Every control binds to an action; every screen declares a screen-context projection (<issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" />).

| Screen | Rambo-UI components | Projection | Controls and actions |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Contacts list | DataTable, FilterBar, SearchField, Tabs (people, organisations), BulkActionBar | visible rows (id, name, kind, tags, owner), filter, selection | new (`crm.person.create`), search (`crm.person.search`), tag (`crm.tag.apply`), add to list, archive, export, open (`nav.crm.person.open`) |
| Person detail | Header with Avatar, Card, FieldList, Timeline, Tabs (overview, events, opportunities, consent), RichTextEditor | person fields minus masked ones, active tab, timeline page | edit field (`crm.person.update`), add contact point, add affiliation, log interaction, add note, schedule follow-up, merge, invite to portal |
| Organisation detail | as Person plus PeopleList | org fields, people list, events | same pattern with organisation actions |
| Event contacts tab (inside F1 event) | RoleList, PartyPicker | event id, roles and parties | assign and unassign role, call, email, open party |
| Pipeline board | KanbanBoard, Card, StageColumn, SummaryBar | pipeline, stage counts and values, visible cards | create, move stage, mark won or lost, convert to event |
| Enquiry inbox | List, Detail pane, MatchSuggestion | enquiries, suggested matches | qualify, match to party, discard, convert to opportunity |
| Duplicates review | ComparePane, FieldChooser | candidate pair, chosen fields | merge (confirm), dismiss |
| Import wizard | FileDrop, ColumnMapper, Preview, ProgressBar | mapping, preview counts, errors | start, map, commit (confirm) |
| Consent and privacy (admin) | DataTable, Badge, Dialog | requests, due dates | record consent, fulfil request (approval) |
| Portal profile (external) | Form, ConsentToggles | own record only | update own details, change consent, request export or erasure |
| Mobile event contact sheet | List, CallButton, OfflineBadge | today's event roles | call, message, open on map (F10) |

## 7. Agent behaviour

* **When asked:** find people and organisations, summarise a relationship with cited sources, log a call from dictation (<issue id="7bd596ca-10db-4e11-bced-7aa22fc64269" label="EVE-31" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-31/port-voice-input-and-transcription-for-the-agent" />), draft a follow-up email (sent through <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" /> only with the user's confirm), build a list from a description, move an opportunity, attach the right contacts to an event.
* **Proactive (suggest, never act silently):** propose duplicates after an import or a create; suggest a follow-up Task (F3) when an opportunity has had no interaction for a configurable number of days (default 14); flag an event in the next 7 days with no venue contact; flag a privacy request approaching its due date.
* **Approvals:** merge, import commit, export, convert to event and portal invite need confirm; erasure fulfilment always needs a human approval, even when the agent prepared it; any send to an external person needs confirm.
* **Limits:** the agent only reads fields the user it acts for can read; sensitive fields are masked in its context unless the user has `crm:sensitive` and the action needs them. No agent SQL; only actions.

## 8. Integrations

Each behind a neutral Effect port in its own integration package; switching vendor changes composition only.

| Port | Purpose | Candidate adapters (need approval on the child issue) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `MailboxSync` | read message headers and bodies for linked parties, send through the user's mailbox | Google (Gmail API), Microsoft (Graph); IMAP later |
| `CalendarSync` | meetings with known parties become Interactions | Google Calendar, Microsoft Graph |
| `ContactExchange` | import and export | CSV and vCard in-house (no vendor) |
| `AddressLookup` | address autocomplete and validation | none in phase 1; reuse the F10 maps vendor if chosen there |
| `Enrichment` | company and person data from a domain | none (decision D4) |
| Messaging and email send | follow-ups and consent confirmations | <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" /> port |

## 9. Permissions and roles

* Tenant roles map to permissions: Viewer (`crm:read`), Member (`crm:read`, `crm:write`), CRM admin (adds `crm:admin`, `crm:privacy`), Owner (all). `crm:sensitive` is granted separately.
* Record visibility: `tenant` (default), `team`, `private` (owner and admins). Visibility is enforced in the authorization service (<issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />) and at sync (<issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" />), not only in the UI.
* Event scoped access: a member who can read an Event (F1) can read the business contact details of parties with an EventRole on it (name, role, work phone and email), even without `crm:read`, so crew get the venue contacts. Personal contact points stay hidden.
* External principals (<issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />): a portal user is linked to one Person and can read and edit only that Person, its consent, and the names of events they hold a role on. A vendor organisation admin can manage the people affiliated with their organisation.
* Agents act with the permissions of the user they act for, never more.

## 10. Telemetry and flags

* Feature flags (PostHog, safe in-code default off): `crm` for the set, plus `crm-pipeline`, `crm-mailbox-sync`, `crm-portal`, one per slice that adds user-visible behaviour.
* Events (no personal data in properties; party ids are pseudonymous): `crm_party_created` (kind, source), `crm_party_merged` (count, source), `crm_interaction_logged` (kind, source), `crm_opportunity_stage_changed` (from, to), `crm_opportunity_converted`, `crm_import_committed` (rows, errors), `crm_privacy_request_fulfilled` (kind, days taken), `crm_agent_suggestion_accepted` (suggestion kind).
* Spans on every action come from <issue id="a03acb76-125b-4ead-815e-10ec986d8413" label="EVE-44" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor" />; mailbox sync jobs add `crm.mailbox.sync` spans with counts only.
* Success metrics: share of upcoming events with a client and a venue contact attached (target 90 percent); duplicate rate after import (under 2 percent); median days from enquiry to converted event; privacy requests fulfilled inside the legal deadline (100 percent).

## 11. Compliance

* UK GDPR and EU GDPR: lawful basis recorded per purpose; data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure, portability, objection) fulfilled within one month; records of processing; data minimisation (date of birth optional and sensitive); retention policy per tenant (default: archived parties purged after 7 years for finance links, 2 years otherwise, configurable).
* PECR (UK) and the ePrivacy rules: marketing email and SMS need recorded consent or soft opt-in; every marketing send checks ConsentRecord at send time. CAN-SPAM and CCPA/CPRA honoured where the tenant operates in the US (opt-out, do-not-sell flag).
* Special category data (health, for example access needs or dietary needs) is out of F4 (section 13); it belongs to the set that needs it, with explicit consent.
* Erasure keeps finance and legal records required by law (F11 invoices) by replacing the party with a tombstone that holds only what the law requires.
* Mailbox sync: users connect their own mailbox with least scopes; message bodies are stored only for messages with a known party; the provider's terms for API use are recorded on the child issue.
* Telemetry and logs never carry names, emails, phones or note text (<issue id="a03acb76-125b-4ead-815e-10ec986d8413" label="EVE-44" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor" /> redaction).

## 12. Acceptance

* Every action in section 4 is in the inventory, passes the parity gate (<issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />) and is callable from UI, HTTP, MCP and the agent with identical results and permissions.
* A person created offline on Android and edited on web while offline converges after reconnect under the rules in section 5, with undo available for both edits.
* A crew member with no `crm:read` sees the venue contact for their event, offline, and cannot see that contact's personal phone.
* Merging two people moves every reference (event roles, interactions, opportunities, tasks, orders, invoices) to the survivor, and unmerge restores them.
* A consent withdrawal recorded on the portal blocks a marketing send queued before it.
* An erasure request removes personal data everywhere except legally retained finance records, and the audit log shows who approved it.
* The agent answers "who is the venue contact for Saturday and when did we last speak" from the screen projection and the timeline, citing sources.
* A deliberately unbound control on any F4 screen fails the <issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" /> check.

## 13. Out of scope

* Marketing campaigns, newsletters and automation journeys (a later set; F4 only records consent and lists).
* Quotes, proposals, contracts and payments (F9, F11).
* Crew employment records, qualifications and payroll identity (F13 Worker, F12); they reference the Person.
* Public directory listings and reviews (F5); they reference the Organisation.
* Third-party enrichment, social scraping and lead databases.
* Special category data.
* A telephony dialler or call recording.
* Custom fields and custom objects (F14 provides them for every set; F4 ships the fixed schema above).

## 14. Dependencies

* **Phase 1:** [EVE-40](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema>) actions; [EVE-41](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-41/p12-build-app-config-settings-secrets-and-credentials>) secrets and credentials (mailbox tokens); [EVE-42](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state>) storage and tenant guards; [EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>) identity, authorization, approvals, audit and external principals; [EVE-44](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor>) telemetry; [EVE-45](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change>) change feed (timeline); [EVE-46](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-46/p17-build-the-http-api-streaming-and-the-typed-client-from-the-action>) HTTP API; [EVE-48](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-48/p19-build-inbound-mcp-from-the-action-inventory>) MCP; [EVE-50](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen>) screen awareness; [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>) record sync and Yjs notes; [EVE-52](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-52/p18a-build-the-agent-turn-loop-with-actions-as-tools>) agent loop; [EVE-54](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow>) durable runs (mailbox sync, import, erasure jobs). Sync engine choice [EVE-17](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and>).
* **Port later:** [EVE-24](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email>) notifications and email; [EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>) files and import; [EVE-26](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-26/port-search-and-embeddings-across-every-resource>) search; [EVE-27](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-27/port-comments-mentions-and-review-suggestions-on-any-resource>) comments and mentions; [EVE-28](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-28/port-localization-for-people-and-for-the-agent>) localisation of names and addresses; [EVE-30](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-30/port-data-widgets-saved-dashboards-and-brand-kits>) dashboards; [EVE-31](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-31/port-voice-input-and-transcription-for-the-agent>) voice capture.
* **Other sets:** F1 (names fixed in [EVE-73](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show>) section 5: Event with `client_ref`, TeamMember `contact_ref`, Rider performer `contact_ref`; EventRole and convert to event build on them); F2 rosters (crew link by Person); F3 Task (follow-ups); F5 directory (Organisation); F8 and F9 (attendees and buyers become Persons); F10 maps (address on map); F11 (billing party is an Organisation or Person); F13 (<issue id="253839bc-c987-416b-92ea-206c9e9e8d2e" label="EVE-80" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-80/f13-human-resources-worker-records-onboarding-qualifications-and-leave" />: Worker references Person by party id, agency crew via Worker.supplierOrgId to an Organisation, special category data in F13 SensitiveProfile; F13 registers as a reference owner in <issue id="7cc5c061-dd2d-4963-8e03-f0175a4f12b9" label="EVE-98" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-98/f131-build-worker-records-engagements-and-organisation-structure" />); F5 (<issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" />: Listing.organisationRef, crmEnquiryRef via crm.enquiry.capture and resolve); F14 (custom fields).

## 15. Decisions for Jonathan

* **D1 Person and user.** A. Person (CRM record) and User (login, <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />) are separate, with an optional link; every human Eventiva knows about is one Person, and other sets reference Person. B. One table for both. **Recommended: A**, because most contacts never log in and the old `contact` extension, which made contact the creator table, mixed the two.
* **D2 Sales pipeline home.** A. Enquiries and opportunities live in F4 and convert into an Event (F1). B. Leave pipeline to F9. **Recommended: A**, as in event sales tools, where the lead belongs with the contact.
* **D3 Mailbox and calendar sync.** A. Build the ports and Google and Microsoft adapters in F4.7, each dependency approved on that issue. B. Manual logging plus a per-tenant forwarding address only. C. Defer sync entirely. **Recommended: A**, because automatic history is the main thing modern CRMs do better than manual entry; B ships first inside F4.7 as the no-vendor fallback.
* **D4 Enrichment.** A. No third-party enrichment; the agent can look up a public website on request with the user's approval. B. A paid enrichment vendor. **Recommended: A** (privacy, cost, no vendor sign-up).
* **D5 Duplicates.** A. Always suggest, merge on confirm, with unmerge. B. Auto-merge exact email matches. **Recommended: A**; auto-merge loses data silently when two people share an inbox.

## 16. Child issues (build order)

 1. <issue id="d71c315c-52d0-4e04-b37a-88b4e1db7827" label="EVE-68" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-68/f41-build-people-organisations-and-contact-points-as-crm-actions" /> F4.1 People, organisations and contact points
 2. <issue id="2e57e1c4-1d58-43b1-bc1e-be0c74986f29" label="EVE-91" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-91/f42-link-contacts-to-events-with-roles-and-to-each-other-with" /> F4.2 Event roles and relationships
 3. <issue id="c3695c62-5106-4bd6-8ce1-c7dff1d14427" label="EVE-95" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-95/f43-build-the-activity-timeline-interactions-notes-and-history-from" /> F4.3 Activity timeline, interactions and notes
 4. <issue id="7692d04c-3444-4989-b2aa-b73a1a69ab02" label="EVE-99" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-99/f44-find-and-merge-duplicate-contacts-and-import-and-export-them" /> F4.4 Duplicates, merge, import and export
 5. <issue id="4b6f8805-b1b2-40f7-99e9-089c9adb8002" label="EVE-105" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-105/f48-record-consent-and-fulfil-privacy-requests-for-contacts" /> F4.8 Consent and privacy requests (built fifth: F4.5, F4.7 and F4.9 need its consent check)
 6. <issue id="5049ee23-9ed6-4a9d-a129-c881611a5f90" label="EVE-102" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-102/f45-organise-contacts-with-tags-lists-and-smart-lists" /> F4.5 Tags, lists and smart lists
 7. <issue id="aa5aaa4a-23e6-4982-bde3-b771cf4bf000" label="EVE-137" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-137/f46-capture-enquiries-and-track-opportunities-through-a-pipeline-into" /> F4.6 Enquiries, pipeline and convert to event
 8. <issue id="1389fdd4-c847-469a-96c4-b469e8fda737" label="EVE-139" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-139/f47-sync-mailbox-and-calendar-history-into-the-contact-timeline" /> F4.7 Mailbox and calendar sync
 9. <issue id="72403895-aec7-4187-943d-ad7df0566e6d" label="EVE-141" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-141/f49-let-external-contacts-manage-their-own-details-and-consent-in-a" /> F4.9 External contact portal
10. <issue id="18171bfa-18f0-4fe1-89ff-499f1fb5d4be" label="EVE-144" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-144/f410-give-the-agent-crm-skills-summaries-follow-up-suggestions-and" /> F4.10 Agent CRM skills and suggestions

issues.title: F5 Directory and marketplace: vendor, venue and professional listings, search, enquiries, quotes and reviews
issues.description:
Status: Proposed (2026-11-01). Planning only, no implementation until Jonathan asks. Template: [Feature set spec template and list](<https://linear.app/resnovas/document/feature-set-spec-template-and-list-26b9f78cf17a>). Decisions D5-1 to D5-6 recorded 2026-11-08 (section 15).

## 1. Goal

An organiser finds, compares and engages vendors, venues and freelance professionals inside the same app they plan the event in, and a vendor wins work from a listing they manage in the same app they run their business in.

## 2. Users and jobs

| User | Jobs |
| -- | -- |
| Organiser (planner, producer) | Search by category, location, date, capacity and budget; shortlist; send one enquiry (RFP) to several suppliers; compare quotes side by side; accept one and have it land on the F1 Event; review afterwards |
| Vendor or venue (a business with its own Eventiva tenant) | Publish and maintain a listing (venue rooms, services, packages, media, service area); answer enquiries; send and revise quotes; respond to reviews; see listing performance |

| Platform moderator (Eventiva staff role) | Verify businesses, handle reports, remove unlawful content, manage the category taxonomy |
| Agent (first-party or external, acting for one of the above) | Everything that person can do, through the same actions, with approvals on anything that contacts another business |

## 5. Data model

F5 owns these entities. F1 Event and F4 Organisation and Contact are referenced by id, not redefined. Shared columns from <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> (tenantId, created, updated, version, deleted).

* **Listing**: tenantId (publisher), kind, slug, name, summary, description (rich text), categories, status (draft, pending verification, published, unpublished, suspended, archived), verification badge, contact channel settings, response-time stat, rating summary, organisationRef (the publisher's own F4 Organisation Party id, per [EVE-65](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-65/f4-contacts-and-crm-people-organisations-relationships-and-history>); legal name, address and contact details are read from it, not copied). One tenant may publish several listings (a company and its venues).
* **VenueRoom** (venue only; named so it does not clash with the per-event F1 Space): listingId, name, area, ceiling height, capacities per layout (standing, theatre, banquet, cabaret, classroom), rigging points and load, power supply, load-in access, step-free access and accessible facilities, floor plan file. Links to an F10 site map when the venue maintains one. F1 references F5 by id only ([EVE-73](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show>) section 5): Event.venue_ref is a Listing id of kind venue, and an F1 Space may carry an optional venue_room_ref to a VenueRoom; referenced VenueRooms are archived, never deleted.
* **Offering**: listingId, name, description, unit (per event, per day, per hour, per head, per item), price from, currency, inclusions. Professionals use offerings for day rates.
* **ProfessionalProfile** (kind professional): skills, qualifications (references F13 qualification records when the professional is staff of a tenant; self-declared otherwise, marked as such), languages, travel radius.
* **MediaItem**: listingId, fileId ([EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>)), alt text (required), order.
* **ServiceArea**: listingId, geometry (point plus radius, or region code list).
* **Category**: platform-owned taxonomy, versioned, localised labels ([EVE-28](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-28/port-localization-for-people-and-for-the-agent>)).
* **VerificationCase**: listingId, trader name, registered address, registration number, VAT number, contact, evidence files, outcome, reviewer, decided at.
* **Shortlist** and **ShortlistItem**: organiser tenant, optional F1 Event id, listing ids, notes.
* **Enquiry**: organiser tenant, optional F1 Event id, brief fields, attachments, status (draft, sent, closed, withdrawn).
* **EnquiryRecipient**: the cross-tenant record. enquiryId, listingId, organiserTenantId, vendorTenantId, status (new, viewed, responded, declined, quoted, won, lost, expired), message thread, crmEnquiryRef. On send, F5 calls crm.enquiry.capture ([EVE-137](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-137/f46-capture-enquiries-and-track-opportunities-through-a-pipeline-into>)) in the vendor tenant so the enquiry lands in the vendor's CRM pipeline; F5 keeps the cross-tenant thread and quotes, F4 keeps the lead.
* **Message**: enquiryRecipientId, author principal (person or agent for person), body, attachments, read receipts.
* **Quote** and **QuoteLine**: enquiryRecipientId, version, lines (offeringId optional, description, quantity, unit price, tax rate code), totals, validity date, terms, status (draft, sent, accepted, declined, expired, superseded).
* **EngagementHandoff**: produced on acceptance. Creates in the organiser tenant: an F4 Organisation and Contact link for the supplier (found or created), a booking hold through [EVE-33](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters>) primitives on the F1 Event dates, and a commitment record F11 reads. In the vendor tenant the enquiry already exists as an F4 lead (see EnquiryRecipient); acceptance calls crm.enquiry.resolve (<issue id="aa5aaa4a-23e6-4982-bde3-b771cf4bf000" label="EVE-137" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-137/f46-capture-enquiries-and-track-opportunities-through-a-pipeline-into" />) with won, and the other recipients' leads are resolved lost with a reason. Both CRM calls run as the F5 directory system principal, scoped in each vendor tenant to crm.enquiry.capture and crm.enquiry.resolve only, and audited with the F5 thread id. F5 owns only the handoff record and its status; the targets are owned by their sets.
* **ReviewInvitation**, **Review**, **ReviewResponse**: review tied to exactly one EngagementHandoff (verified by construction), ratings per dimension, body, moderation status, published at.
* **ModerationCase**: target ref, reporter, reason, outcome, statement of reasons, appeal state.
* **Seeded listing fields** on Listing: ownership (claimed, unclaimed), seededBy, seedSource, lastCheckedAt. Unclaimed listings sit in a platform directory scope, hold public business facts only (vendor and venue kinds; professionals are never seeded), and take no offerings, prices, reviews or availability. Claiming moves the same Listing id to the claimant tenant, so F1 references survive.
* **ClaimCase**: listingId, claimant tenant, evidence (domain email or documents), outcome, statement of reasons, dispute state. Plus a do-not-seed list and an invitation suppression list.
* **CommissionPlan** (platform scope, versioned: rate in basis points, minimum, cap, categories, effective from), **CommissionTermsAcceptance** (vendor tenant, plan version, accepted by, at), **PaymentRequest** (quote id, schedule line, amount, due date, status due, paid, overdue, refunded, cancelled, settled off platform), **CommissionCharge** (payment id, base excluding VAT, rate, amount, plan version, status collected, refunded, adjusted), **CommissionAdjustment**. Commission records are vendor and platform scope only; organisers never read them.

Tenant scope. Listings, venue rooms, offerings and media are tenant-owned and publicly readable only through the public projection when published. EnquiryRecipient, Message, Quote and EngagementHandoff are two-party records: the row stores both tenant ids, and the authorization rule ([EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>)) is "principal belongs to one of the two tenants and holds the enquiry or quote permission there". This is the first cross-tenant record type in Eventiva and needs a test matrix of its own. Reviews are public once published. Moderation cases are platform scope.

Offline sync ([EVE-17](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and>), [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>)). Synced to device: own listings and children (vendor), own shortlists, own enquiries, threads and quotes (both sides), last search result pages cached read only. Not synced: the public index. Conflict rules: listing scalar fields last-writer-wins per field with version check; listing description is a Yjs text document embedded in the record ([EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>)) so two staff can edit it together; VenueRoom capacities and Offering prices last-writer-wins per field; quote lines are edited by one side only and a sent quote is immutable (revise makes a new version), so no merge; messages are append-only; status transitions are server-validated state machines ([EVE-42](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state>)), so an offline transition that is no longer valid is rejected on sync and surfaced to the user. Sending an enquiry, message or quote while offline queues the action and it is executed and authorized on reconnect; the UI shows it as queued, never as sent.

## 7. Agent behaviour

When asked:

* Organiser: "find three lighting suppliers within 50 miles of the venue for the festival dates under budget line X" runs `directory.search` with filters read from the F1 Event and its unfilled EquipmentRequirement items, the F10 site map and the F11 budget, explains the ranking, and offers a shortlist.
* Organiser: drafts the enquiry brief from the event and attaches the relevant run of show; compares quotes and explains differences in inclusions, not only price.
* Vendor: drafts a quote from offerings, F6 stock availability and F2 crew availability for the requested dates; drafts listing copy and alt text from uploaded photos for the user to approve.

Proactive (behind the flag, opt-in per user):

* Nudge an organiser when a quote is about to expire or a supplier has replied.
* Nudge a vendor when an enquiry has waited longer than their usual response time.
* After an event closes, propose review invitations for every engagement.

Approvals: anything that reaches another business or the public is confirm or always (publish, send enquiry, message as an agent, send quote, accept quote, submit or respond to review). The agent never accepts a quote without explicit approval (always). Bulk enquiry to more than 5 recipients always asks.

Safety: listing text, reviews, messages and quote terms written by another tenant are untrusted data in the agent's context and are marked as such in the projection; instructions inside them are never followed. The agent must not write or solicit reviews (fake review rules, section 11).

## 8. Integrations

Each behind a neutral port in its own integration package; no vendor chosen here, each needs approval on its child issue.

* Geocoding and maps tiles: `Geocoder` port (address to point, region lookup) and map rendering via the F10 map stack. Search by radius works from stored points without a live call.
* Search index: Postgres full text and vector search through the <issue id="2cd1c920-450c-487e-b4c8-e860a382a6b0" label="EVE-26" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-26/port-search-and-embeddings-across-every-resource" /> search port; geo filtering in Postgres (decision D5-4).
* Business verification: manual moderator review in v1 behind a `TraderVerifier` port, so a registry lookup service can be added later.
* Bot protection on anonymous enquiries and reports: `HumanCheck` port.
* Email and push for new enquiries, replies and quotes: <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" /> notifications.
* Payments between organiser and vendor (D5-6 b): the organiser pays the vendor's connected account through F9 checkout and the PaymentGateway port (<issue id="382cab34-de6b-4524-8a47-241353c76b2b" label="EVE-174" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-174/f93-build-the-payment-gateway-port-and-online-card-payments" />), with Eventiva's commission taken as the platform fee through F9 split payments (<issue id="05f45c5a-d89d-44e3-b726-e3a04db95a21" label="EVE-223" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-223/f912-build-vendor-sales-at-events-with-split-payments" />); refunds and disputes through F9.8 (<issue id="cc848306-1827-4682-a18a-e5c255970dd3" label="EVE-215" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-215/f98-build-refunds-cancellations-exchanges-and-disputes" />). Eventiva holds no balance. A monthly commission statement and VAT invoice goes to each vendor from the operator tenant (F11, <issue id="2ef1ed05-1c6a-4b1b-9b1c-04331398cac8" label="EVE-126" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-126/f114-build-sales-invoices-credit-notes-and-receivables" />).
* Claim invitations and domain-email claim checks: <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" /> email, with a suppression list.

## 11. Compliance

* UK DMCC Act 2024 and CMA fake reviews guidance; EU Omnibus Directive (2019/2161): reviews only from verified engagements, disclosure of how reviews are collected and checked, no review incentives, no suppression of negative reviews.
* EU Digital Services Act and UK Online Safety Act where applicable: notice and action for illegal content, statement of reasons for moderation decisions, trader traceability (verified trader details before a business can publish to consumers).
* EU Platform-to-Business Regulation (2019/1150): publish the main ranking parameters (including that unclaimed listings rank below claimed ones at equal relevance, and that commission never affects ranking), disclose that paid placement does not exist in v1, and give commission terms in plain language with 15 days notice before any change.
* UK GDPR and EU GDPR: professionals are individuals, so their public profile is published only with explicit consent, can be unpublished and erased; enquiry messages are personal data with retention rules; data subject export covers threads.
* Accessibility: public pages meet WCAG 2.2 AA; venue access information is structured fields, not free text.
* Consumer law: quote terms carry the vendor's identity and cancellation terms; Eventiva is not a party to the contract and says so.
* Seeded listings: business facts only, from the business's own public material entered by a person; no scraping or third-party directory imports (terms and database right); a clear unclaimed label (CMA guidance on misleading information); removal on request within 30 days; claim invitations to business addresses carry an unsubscribe and honour a suppression list (PECR).
* Payments and commission: payments run on a regulated provider's connected accounts with the vendor as merchant of record, so funds never sit in an Eventiva balance; check the chosen provider's terms on <issue id="382cab34-de6b-4524-8a47-241353c76b2b" label="EVE-174" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-174/f93-build-the-payment-gateway-port-and-online-card-payments" /> to confirm Eventiva needs no payment institution or safeguarding authorisation (Payment Services Regulations 2017) before the flag is turned on. The provider runs vendor identity checks at onboarding. VAT on the commission goes on a monthly invoice from F11. Consumer organisers get the vendor's cancellation and refund terms before paying.

## 12. Acceptance

* A vendor publishes a verified listing with venue rooms, offerings and media; an anonymous visitor finds it on the public web by category and radius.
* An organiser sends one enquiry to three listings from an F1 Event, each vendor sees only its own thread, two quote, the organiser compares and accepts one, and the handoff creates the F4 link, the [EVE-33](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters>) hold and the F11 commitment.
* The same flow runs end to end through the agent with approvals shown on screen and through MCP, with identical audit rows.
* A review can only be submitted from an engagement; a vendor can respond; a reported review goes to moderation with a statement of reasons.
* Cross-tenant negative tests: recipient A cannot read recipient B's thread or quote; a vendor cannot read the organiser's other enquiries; an agent for a planner without quote:accept cannot accept.
* Offline: an enquiry sent offline shows as queued and is sent on reconnect; a quote accepted after it expired while offline is rejected on sync with a clear message.
* An unclaimed listing is claimed by domain email, keeps its id, and an F1 Event that referenced it still resolves; a dispute can reverse the transfer.
* An organiser pays the deposit and balance of an accepted quote in Eventiva; each payment lands with the vendor less commission, a partial refund reverses commission in proportion, and organisers cannot see commission.

## 13. Out of scope

Escrow or Eventiva-held balances; payment plans beyond deposit and balance; paid placement and advertising; instant booking without a quote; contract e-signature (port later if needed); ticket resale; hotel room blocks; external marketplace syndication; automated background checks on professionals.
