issues.title: F8 Ticketing: ticket types, capacity, issuance, admissions and scanning
issues.description:
Status: Approved (2026-11-08, Jonathan, decision card): D1, D2, D4 and D5 as recommended; D3 changed to (b), a seat map editor inside F8 now. Planning only; no implementation until Jonathan asks. Follows the [Feature set spec template](<https://linear.app/resnovas/document/feature-set-spec-template-and-list-26b9f78cf17a>). F1 entities from <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> (Event, Phase, Space, Segment) are referenced by id, not redefined; Venue is F5's record. A ticket admits to an Event, optionally narrowed to a Phase (for example day 2), a Space (zone) or a Segment with audience public (for example a workshop slot); this issue calls that the admission scope. F9 line-provider contract agreed with the F9 thread: kind ticket maps reserve to ticketing.hold.create, commit to ticketing.ticket.issueForOrder and release to ticketing.hold.release (unpaid) or ticketing.ticket.void (paid); offline box office uses a pre-allocated per-device quota from a capacity pool.

## 1. Goal

An organiser can sell, issue and admit tickets for any F1 Event (optionally narrowed by admission scope) from one app, and the gate keeps admitting people safely when the network drops, with no oversell and no double entry.

## 2. Users and jobs

| User | Jobs |
| -- | -- |
| Organiser / ticketing manager | Design ticket types and prices, set capacity and sales windows, release holds, open and close sales, watch sales, run the waiting list, void or reissue tickets |
| Box office staff | Sell and print or send tickets in person, look up and reissue tickets, change holder names, sell from an offline quota when the network is down |
| Gate staff (crew) | Scan tickets at an entry point, see a clear admit or reject result, handle re-entry, admit manually by lookup, keep scanning offline |
| Attendee / ticket holder | Find tickets, show the code, fill in attendee details, transfer to a friend, join a waiting list, return a ticket for resale |
| Buyer | Buy several tickets, name each holder, see order status (order itself is F9) |
| Finance | Read sales and admission totals per event, reconcile with F9 orders and F11 ledgers |
| Vendor / promoter (later) | Sell an allocation through their own link or access code |
| Agent | Every job above under the delegating user's permissions: draft a ticket structure from the event brief, watch sell-through and capacity, chase incomplete attendee details, answer holder questions, prepare the gate briefing |

## 3. Market check

Checked 2026-11-01 (names stay out of customer copy):

* **pretix** (open source): check-in lists limited to products; its scanner app has an "asynchronous" mode that keeps a local copy of attendee data and scans without internet, syncing in the background; badge printing after a scan; a ticket vending kiosk app. ([check-in features](<https://pretix.eu/about/en/features/checkin>))
* **DICE**: app-only tickets to fight touting, a waiting list that resells returned tickets at face value, tight limits on transfer and resale. ([summary](<https://www.tickettailor.com/blog/dice-reviews-summary-pros-cons>))
* **Ticket Tailor**: low flat fees, seating charts with seat choice, a waitlist after sell-out, free check-in app with camera or external scanner, organiser connects their own payment provider (Stripe, Square, PayPal). ([how it works](<https://tickettailor.com/how-it-works>))
* **Eventbrite** (from memory, not re-checked): discovery marketplace plus self-serve ticketing; marketplace reach is its edge.

Where Eventiva matches: ticket types with capacity pools, waitlist, organiser-owned payments (through F9), offline scanning with background sync (pretix model), badges.
Where Eventiva differs: tickets are part of the same Event record that production, crew, fleet and site maps use, so the gate briefing, crew roster and capacity on the site map come from one source; the agent can do every ticketing job through the same actions; one app serves organiser, gate crew and attendee by role (no separate scanner app); tickets are signed so a device can verify a ticket it has never synced (stronger than list-only offline mode); face-value official resale through the waiting list is built in. Discovery marketplace reach is F5's job, not F8's.

## 4. Capabilities as actions

All actions follow [EVE-40](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema>) (Effect Schema input and output, typed errors, one permission, approval policy, side-effect class, receipts). Scope is the org ([EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>)); every input carries the F1 Event (optionally narrowed by admission scope) id it acts on. Approval: none / confirm (agent must ask the user) / always (agent needs explicit approval every time).

| Action | Input | Output | Permission | Agent approval |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| ticketing.ticketType.create | event or admission scopes, name, price tiers (amount, currency, valid from/to), pool id, per-order min/max, visibility (public, hidden, access-code), attendee questions, transferable flag, re-entry rule | TicketType | ticketing:manage | none (draft) |
| ticketing.ticketType.update | id, patch | TicketType | ticketing:manage | confirm if on sale |
| ticketing.ticketType.publish / unpublish | id | TicketType | ticketing:manage | confirm |
| ticketing.ticketType.archive | id | TicketType | ticketing:manage | confirm |
| ticketing.pool.create / update | admission scope, name, capacity, optional parent pool | CapacityPool | ticketing:manage | confirm if lowering capacity |
| ticketing.pool.availability | pool or ticket type id | available, held, sold, admitted | ticketing:read or public for published types | none |
| ticketing.salesWindow.set | ticket type id, opens at, closes at, on-sale queue on/off | TicketType | ticketing:manage | confirm |
| ticketing.accessCode.create / revoke | event id, code, unlocks ticket type ids, max uses, expiry | AccessCode | ticketing:manage | none / confirm |
| ticketing.hold.create | lines (ticket type id, qty), purpose (checkout, manual, offline-quota), ttl | Hold with expiry | ticketing:sell or public checkout | none |
| ticketing.hold.release / extend | hold id | Hold | ticketing:sell (own) or ticketing:manage | none |
| ticketing.ticket.issueForOrder | F9 order id, lines with hold ids, holder details | Ticket\[\] | system (F9 order-paid event) or ticketing:sell | not agent-callable directly |
| ticketing.ticket.issueComp | ticket type id, qty, holder details, reason | Ticket\[\] | ticketing:manage | always |
| ticketing.ticket.get / list / search | ids or filters | Ticket(s), masked by role | ticketing:read, holder for own | none |
| ticketing.ticket.updateHolder | ticket id, name, email, answers | Ticket | holder (if allowed) or ticketing:sell | confirm |
| ticketing.ticket.void | ticket id, reason (refund, fraud, reissue, cancel) | Ticket | ticketing:manage or system (F9 refund) | always |
| ticketing.ticket.reissue | ticket id | new Ticket, old voided | ticketing:sell | confirm |
| ticketing.ticket.deliver | ticket ids, channel (email, in-app, pdf, wallet) | delivery receipts | ticketing:sell or holder for own | confirm for bulk |
| ticketing.transfer.offer / accept / cancel | ticket id, recipient email | Transfer | holder | confirm |
| ticketing.waitlist.join / leave | ticket type id or admission scope, qty, contact | WaitlistEntry | public or holder | none |
| ticketing.waitlist.offer | entry ids or next N | offers with hold and expiry | ticketing:manage | confirm |
| ticketing.resale.list / withdraw | ticket id | ResaleListing (face value) | holder | confirm |
| ticketing.checkInList.create / update | admission scope, name, ticket type ids, gates, time window, re-entry rule | CheckInList | ticketing:manage | confirm |
| ticketing.scan.submit | device id, list id, code payload, scanned at, offline flag | ScanResult (admitted, rejected with reason, warning) | ticketing:scan | not agent-callable (device only) |
| ticketing.checkIn.manual | ticket id, list id, reason | ScanResult | ticketing:scan | always |
| ticketing.checkIn.undo | scan id, reason | ScanResult | ticketing:manage | always |
| ticketing.device.register / revoke | name, gate, list ids, offline quota | ScannerDevice with device key | ticketing:manage | confirm / none |
| ticketing.device.snapshot | device id | signed validity snapshot for offline use | ticketing:scan (registered device) | not agent-callable |
| ticketing.boxOffice.allocateOfflineQuota | device id, ticket type id, qty | Hold (purpose offline-quota) | ticketing:manage | confirm |
| ticketing.report.sales / admissions | event or admission scope, range, grouping | report rows | ticketing:read or finance:read | none |
| ticketing.export.attendees | admission scope, fields | file reference ([EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>)) | ticketing:manage | confirm (personal data) |
| ticketing.gateBriefing.generate | admission scope | document: lists, gates, expected arrivals, rules | ticketing:read | none |
| ticketing.seatPlan.create / update / generateRows / assignZone / setSeatState / publish / duplicate (F8.11) | space id, plan patch ops, row spec, zone to ticket type, seat state | SeatPlan (Yjs document, versioned) | ticketing:manage | confirm for publish and for killing seats on sale |

Navigation to every ticketing screen is an action too (<issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" />).

## 5. Data model

Tenant scope: org. Every row carries org id and the F1 Event id; admission scope (phase id, space id or public segment id) where capacity applies.

* **CapacityPool**: admission scope, name, capacity, parent pool (for nested limits, e.g. venue total over standing and seated). Counters (held, sold, admitted) are owned by a cluster entity per pool, not by rows edited by clients.
* **TicketType**: event id, admission scopes, pool id, name, description (rich text document, Yjs, embedded per [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>)), price tiers, currency, sales window, visibility, per-order limits, attendee questions (schema), transferable, resale allowed, re-entry rule, status (draft, on sale, paused, sold out, closed, archived).
* **AccessCode**: code hash, unlocks ticket types, max uses, used count, expiry.
* **Hold**: lines, purpose, owner (checkout session, user, device), expires at, status (active, converted, released, expired).
* **Ticket**: ticket type id, admission scope, F9 order id and line id (null for comps), holder name and email, answers, status (valid, void, transferred-out), secret (random 128-bit), signed payload version, issued at, seat ref (F8.11 SeatPlan seat).
* **SeatPlan** (F8.11): F1 Space ref, sections, rows, seats, tables, general-admission areas, price zones; a collaborative Yjs document per <issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" />, versioned, locked to a published version while on sale.
* **Transfer**, **WaitlistEntry**, **ResaleListing**: as named in section 4.
* **CheckInList**: admission scope, ticket types, gates (F1 Space or F5 Venue refs), time window, re-entry rule (single, unlimited, n times, with exit scan).
* **Scan**: append-only admission ledger: ticket id or raw payload, list id, device id, gate, scanned at (device clock and server receive time), result, reason, offline flag, user.
* **ScannerDevice**: name, user, gate, list ids, public key, offline quota hold id, last sync, revoked at.

Offline and conflict rules per field:

| Data | Offline on device | Conflict rule |
| -- | -- | -- |
| TicketType and pool settings | read-only copy | server wins; edited only online |
| Pool counters | never edited offline | owned by the pool entity; offline sales only consume a pre-allocated device quota hold, so they cannot oversell |
| Ticket validity snapshot (id, type, status, holder name, secret hash) | read-only, signed, refreshed on sync | server wins; void on server beats an offline admit, which is then flagged for review, not silently reverted |
| Scan ledger | append-only, queued | union of all scans (no edits); for single-entry lists the earliest server-ordered admit is the valid one, later admits of the same ticket become duplicate-entry alerts |
| Holder name and answers | editable at box office offline | last writer wins per field with audit; holder's own edits rank equal |
| TicketType description | Yjs document | merges per <issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" /> |

## 6. Screens

All components from Rambo-UI (names are the expected component kinds; Rambo-UI has none yet). Every control binds to the action shown; every screen declares a screen-context projection (<issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" />) filtered by role.

| Screen | Components | Projection | Actions behind controls |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Event tickets (tab on the F1 Event) | data table, form sheet, status badge, price input | event id, ticket types with status, price, pool availability, selection | ticketType.*, pool.*, salesWindow.set, navigation |
| Capacity board | stacked bar, tree of pools | pools with held/sold/admitted, selected pool | pool.update, hold.release |
| Ticket type editor | form, rich text, question builder | the type being edited, dirty fields, validation errors | ticketType.create/update/publish |
| Attendee list | data table with filters, search, row sheet | filters, visible rows (masked), selected ticket | [ticket.search/updateHolder/void/reissue/deliver](<http://ticket.search/updateHolder/void/reissue/deliver>), export.attendees |
| Ticket detail | card, timeline (scans, transfers) | ticket, status, history | ticket.\*, checkIn.manual/undo |
| Check-in setup | list, gate picker (F1 Space or F5 Venue), rule picker | lists, gates, devices | checkInList.\*, device.register/revoke |
| Scanner | camera scanner, large result banner, counter, offline indicator | list, last result, admitted count, sync state (no attendee data beyond name and type) | scan.submit, checkIn.manual |
| Box office | product grid, cart (F9), holder form, print button | admission scope, available types, offline quota left | hold.create, F9 checkout, ticket.deliver |
| Waiting list | data table, offer button | entries, positions, offers outstanding | waitlist.offer |
| Sales dashboard | charts ([EVE-30](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-30/port-data-widgets-saved-dashboards-and-brand-kits>) widgets) | totals, sell-through, pace vs target | report.sales/admissions |
| My tickets (attendee, same app) | ticket cards with code, transfer and resale buttons | own tickets only | ticket.get, transfer.*, resale.*, waitlist.\* |
| Public ticket picker (on F14 sites) | ticket list, quantity steppers | published types and availability | pool.availability, hold.create then F9 checkout |

## 7. Agent behaviour

When asked: build a ticket structure from the event brief (drafts only), change prices or windows (confirm), produce sales and admission reports, find and fix a holder's ticket, prepare the gate briefing, offer waiting list places (confirm).
Proactively (as suggestions in the agent thread, never acting alone): capacity at 80 and 95 percent, sell-through pace behind target, expiring holds blocking sales, attendee details missing within 48h of doors, duplicate-entry alerts after offline sync, devices not synced for over 10 minutes during doors.
Always needs approval: comps, voids, check-in undo, manual admits, bulk delivery or messages, lowering capacity, exports of personal data. Never: scanning on behalf of a device, issuing tickets for an unpaid order, raising capacity above the F1 Space or F5 Venue safe capacity.

## 8. Integrations

Each behind a neutral Effect port in an integration package (<issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> rule 4); none is chosen here.

* **Payments, orders, refunds**: F9's ports, not F8's. F8 only reacts to F9 order events.
* **Delivery**: email and push through <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" />.
* **PDF tickets and badges**: <issue id="8d8d301b-d679-4dac-95bb-c24889179cd0" label="EVE-25" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import" /> files; rendering library needs approval.
* **Wallet passes** (Apple Wallet, Google Wallet): WalletPass port; needs vendor accounts and approval (slice F8.10).
* **Barcode/QR rendering and decoding**: library choice needs approval; camera through Expo on native, web camera on web.
* **Hardware**: USB/Bluetooth scanners in keyboard mode (no SDK); receipt and ticket printers through the OS print path first; native printer SDKs only on approval.
* **Outbound webhooks**: ticket issued, voided, scanned, through the platform webhook surface (<issue id="cc5eba91-a4f7-4542-b332-10d3e1d70ed8" label="EVE-15" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-15/s2-build-the-upstream-agent-native-capability-map-and-protocol" /> matrix).

## 9. Permissions and roles

Permissions: ticketing:read, ticketing:manage, ticketing:sell, ticketing:scan, finance:read, plus holder rights on own tickets. Default roles: Organiser owner (all), Ticketing manager (manage, sell, scan, read), Box office (sell, scan, read), Gate staff (scan only; sees holder name and ticket type, never email, answers or order), Finance (finance:read, ticketing:read), Attendee (own tickets, transfers, waiting list), Public (published types and availability only). Agents act as the delegating user and inherit exactly that role (<issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />). Revoking a device or a role stops scans at the next request and invalidates the device key; an offline device keeps working until its snapshot expires (default 24h, set per list).

## 10. Telemetry and flags

Flag `ticketing` (default off) with sub-flags `ticketing-offline-scan`, `ticketing-waitlist-resale`, `ticketing-box-office`, `ticketing-wallet`, `ticketing-seating` (all default off). PostHog events (no personal data, ids pseudonymous): ticket_type_published, hold_created, hold_expired, ticket_issued, ticket_voided, ticket_transferred, waitlist_joined, waitlist_offer_accepted, scan_result (result, offline, latency bucket), offline_sync_completed (queued count, duplicates), device_registered. Spans on every action (<issue id="a03acb76-125b-4ead-815e-10ec986d8413" label="EVE-44" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor" />); metrics: scan latency, pool contention, hold expiry rate.
Success metrics: zero oversold pools; scan-to-result p95 under 300 ms offline and 800 ms online; duplicate admits under 0.1 percent of scans after offline sync; organiser can go from event to tickets on sale in under 10 minutes.

## 11. Compliance

Verify with legal before launch; this list is a starting point.

* **All-in pricing**: UK DMCC Act 2024 (drip pricing) and US FTC rule on unfair or deceptive fees (live-event tickets): the first price shown includes mandatory fees. F8 shows prices from F9's price breakdown.
* **Secondary ticketing**: UK Consumer Rights Act 2015 s.90 to 95 information duties apply to resale; F8 only offers face-value official resale; track proposed UK resale price caps.
* **Cancellation rights**: EU and UK distance-selling cooling-off exemption for date-specific leisure services; refund policy is the organiser's, enforced through F9.
* **Personal data**: UK GDPR and GDPR: data minimisation at the gate, retention limit for attendee data after the event (default 12 months, configurable), export and deletion through [EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>), consent for marketing separate from ticket delivery.
* **Payments**: PCI DSS stays out of F8 (no card data); F9 owns it.
* **Accessibility**: companion and accessible tickets as ticket types with questions; screens meet WCAG 2.2 AA; scanner result banner readable in sunlight and by colour-blind staff (shape and text, not colour alone).
* **Safety**: capacity cannot exceed the F1 Space or F5 Venue safe capacity; admitted count per gate available for safety officers.

## 12. Acceptance

* Two buyers racing for the last ticket: one succeeds, one gets a sold-out error; 10,000 concurrent holds against a 1,000-capacity pool never sell more than 1,000 (load test).
* A ticket bought through F9 is issued, delivered and admitted at a scanner; a refund in F9 voids it and the next scan rejects it.
* Two devices scan offline for 30 minutes, one admits a ticket the other also admits; after sync, one admit stands, the other is a duplicate-entry alert, and both devices show it.
* A device that has never synced a ticket verifies its signature and admits it offline; a forged code is rejected.
* Box office sells offline from a quota and cannot exceed it; sales reconcile with F9 on reconnect.
* The agent drafts ticket types for a sample event, asks before publishing, and cannot void or comp without approval; every screen's projection lets it see what the user sees.
* Gate staff cannot see holder email or order details through any surface (UI, HTTP, MCP, agent).
* Parity check (<issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />) passes for all ticketing actions and UI bindings (<issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" />).

## 13. Out of scope

Checkout, payments, discount codes, refunds and tax (F9). Accounting entries (F11). Discovery marketplace listing (F5). Event sites and page design (F14; F8 provides the ticket picker). Dynamic or demand pricing, auctions, memberships and season tickets, distribution to third-party sales channels, open resale at buyer-set prices, RFID or NFC wristbands and turnstile integration (candidates for a later slice once hardware is chosen), and identity verification at the gate.

## 14. Dependencies

* Phase 1: [EVE-40](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema>) actions, [EVE-41](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-41/p12-build-app-config-settings-secrets-and-credentials>) secrets (signing keys), [EVE-42](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state>) storage, [EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>) identity and access, [EVE-44](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor>) telemetry, [EVE-45](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change>) change feed, [EVE-46](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-46/p17-build-the-http-api-streaming-and-the-typed-client-from-the-action>) HTTP API, [EVE-50](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen>) screen awareness, [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>) sync and collaboration, [EVE-52](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-52/p18a-build-the-agent-turn-loop-with-actions-as-tools>) and [EVE-54](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow>) agent and durable runs. Spike [EVE-17](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and>) (sync engine) decides the offline transport. [EVE-39](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-39/make-every-entity-action-idempotent-and-persisted-by-default>) (idempotent entity actions) and [EVE-38](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-38/cut-runner-loss-failover-from-36s-and-expose-the-cluster-settings-in>) (failover) matter for the pool entity.
* Port-later: [EVE-24](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email>) notifications and email, [EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>) files, [EVE-26](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-26/port-search-and-embeddings-across-every-resource>) search, [EVE-28](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-28/port-localization-for-people-and-for-the-agent>) localization, [EVE-30](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-30/port-data-widgets-saved-dashboards-and-brand-kits>) dashboards, [EVE-27](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-27/port-comments-mentions-and-review-suggestions-on-any-resource>) comments (on ticket types).
* Feature sets: F1 <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> (Event, Phase, Space, Segment, TeamMember for gate crew), F5 (Venue), F9 (orders, payments, refunds, box office checkout), F2 (gate staff rosters), F4 (holders as contacts), F10 (gate positions; optional backdrop for the F8 seat map editor), F11 (revenue), F14 (public ticket picker).

## 15. Decisions for Jonathan

* **D1 Boundary with F9**: (a) F8 owns ticket types, capacity, holds, tickets and admission; F9 owns checkout, orders, payments and refunds. (b) F8 has its own ticket checkout. **Recommend (a)**: one checkout for tickets, merchandise and services.
* **D2 Offline scanning**: (a) signed tickets plus a synced validity snapshot and an append-only scan ledger. (b) synced list only (pretix style). (c) online only. **Recommend (a)**: works for tickets issued after the last sync and resists forgery.
* **D3 Reserved seating**: (a) general admission and capacity zones first, seats later on F10 site maps. (b) build a seat map editor inside F8 now. (c) no seating. **Decided (b)** on 2026-11-08: F8.11 builds an F8 seat map editor now; it may show an F10 site map as a backdrop but does not wait for F10.
* **D4 Resale and transfer**: (a) organiser-controlled transfers plus face-value resale through the waiting list. (b) transfers only. (c) open resale at any price. **Recommend (a)**: protects fans and stays inside UK resale rules.
* **D5 Ticket delivery**: (a) in-app and email QR plus PDF first, wallet passes as a later slice. (b) wallet passes from the start. **Recommend (a)**: no vendor accounts needed to start.

## 16. Child issues (build order)

 1. F8.1 <issue id="befba1e2-7fb2-4ab8-a9fa-a0efcf2ebfae" label="EVE-112" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-112/f81-build-the-ticket-catalogue-ticket-types-capacity-pools-sales" /> Ticket catalogue: ticket types, capacity pools, sales windows, access codes
 2. F8.2 <issue id="eed7c2f7-0dc7-43cb-8b86-6324a06e36d5" label="EVE-114" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-114/f82-build-the-capacity-engine-oversell-proof-holds-on-a-cluster-entity" /> Capacity engine: oversell-proof holds on a cluster entity per pool, F9 line provider, on-sale queue
 3. F8.3 <issue id="55f17a19-e0f5-4a67-b779-0d118ecd75da" label="EVE-117" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-117/f83-build-ticket-issuance-and-delivery-signed-tickets-from-paid-orders" /> Issuance and delivery: signed tickets from paid orders, comps, voids, reissue
 4. F8.4 <issue id="b11d671d-2a5f-4e92-a9a4-da4d61c3d64d" label="EVE-122" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-122/f84-build-the-attendee-view-my-tickets-holder-details-and-transfers-in" /> Attendee view: my tickets, holder details, transfers
 5. F8.5 <issue id="57212326-6c0e-4711-a80a-d34efa6ffd87" label="EVE-162" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-162/f85-build-check-in-lists-and-online-scanning-in-the-app" /> Check-in lists and online scanning
 6. F8.6 <issue id="257d6693-f9de-4779-a911-c07895c8f06e" label="EVE-192" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-192/f86-build-offline-scanning-validity-snapshots-local-scan-ledger-sync" /> Offline scanning: snapshots, local ledger, sync, duplicate alerts
 7. F8.7 <issue id="2a381308-d018-4984-a018-c3a7453e3e4b" label="EVE-193" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-193/f87-build-the-box-office-in-person-ticket-sales-reprints-and-offline" /> Box office: in-person sales, reprints, offline quota sales
 8. F8.8 <issue id="6618b76f-19ed-47a6-8dd9-cf73789d5d85" label="EVE-194" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-194/f88-build-the-waiting-list-and-face-value-resale" /> Waiting list and face-value resale
 9. F8.9 <issue id="325c1b43-063c-49a1-a818-f8be8db0cd91" label="EVE-195" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-195/f89-build-ticketing-reports-the-sales-dashboard-and-attendee-exports" /> Reports, sales dashboard, attendee exports, retention
10. F8.10 <issue id="a3ce723f-5587-4670-909a-5e1a335c8e8a" label="EVE-209" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-209/f810-add-wallet-passes-for-tickets-behind-a-neutral-port" /> Wallet passes behind a neutral port (needs vendor approval)
11. F8.11 <issue id="3682ce53-f6e7-41d9-a911-2fb44d73f7c6" label="EVE-211" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-211/f811-add-reserved-seating-on-f10-site-maps" /> Seat map editor and reserved seating in F8 (D3 b)
12. F8.12 <issue id="96e3bf8c-3a1b-4b1e-920e-4a6d89e14752" label="EVE-212" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-212/f812-build-ticketing-agent-behaviour-watchers-gate-briefing-and" /> Agent behaviour: watchers, gate briefing, approval tests

issues.title: F5.2 Build the listing editor screens for vendors, venues and professionals
issues.description:
Status: Proposed (2026-11-01), part of <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> (F5 Directory and marketplace).

## Goal

A vendor builds and previews their listing on phone, desktop or web, and the agent sees and can operate every part of the editor.

## Context

* <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> section 6 (Listing editor row) lists the screen, components, projection and controls.
* Actions come from F5.1. Screen awareness rules from <issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" />: every control binds to an action id, every screen declares a projection.
* UI comes from Rambo-UI (D8); no local component library.

## Scope

1. Listing editor screen with sections: profile, venue rooms (venue), offerings, professional profile (professional), media manager, service area, preview.
2. Venue room editor with a capacity-per-layout grid, rigging and power fields, accessibility checklist and floor plan upload.
3. Offering editor with unit and price from, inclusions list.
4. Media manager: upload via [EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>), reorder, required alt text with an inline error.
5. Service area: point plus radius input with a map preview (map rendering from the F10 stack; if F10 is not built, a plain address and radius form ships first).
6. Preview that renders the `ListingPublic` projection exactly as F5.5 will.
7. Publish blockers panel listing what stops publishing (missing verification, missing alt text, no category), each item a navigation action.
8. Screen-context projection: listing id, active section, dirty fields, publish blockers, selected venue room or offering.
9. Offline: edits work offline and show a pending-sync badge.

## Acceptance criteria

* Every interactive element is bound; the unbound-element check from [EVE-50](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen>) passes, and a fixture with an unbound button fails.
* The agent answers "what is missing before I can publish" from the projection and fixes a missing alt text by calling `directory.media.attach` with the same result as the UI.
* WCAG 2.2 AA: axe or Lighthouse run on the web build recorded here; keyboard-only completion of the venue room editor.
* Verified on web and Android (record commands and device).

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 for anything with IO; Rambo-UI components only; whitelabel ASCII copy; flag `directory-marketplace`; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; ships to main with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged with web and Android checks recorded and an accessibility report attached.

## Blockers

F5.1, <issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" /> (screen awareness), <issue id="a7a66a5c-e747-4245-bc84-3232ef65a16c" label="EVE-16" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-16/s3-prove-runtime-loading-and-switching-of-a-remote-module-on-expo-web" /> (Expo stack).

issues.title: F5.3 Build business verification, publishing and content moderation
issues.description:
Status: Proposed (2026-11-01), part of <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> (F5 Directory and marketplace).

## Goal

Only verified traders publish to the directory, anyone can report unlawful or misleading content, and every moderation decision is recorded with a statement of reasons.

## Context

* <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> section 11: trader traceability and notice and action (EU DSA, UK Online Safety Act where applicable), DMCC fake review rules.
* Verification is manual in v1 behind a `TraderVerifier` port so a registry lookup service can be added later without domain changes (<issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> no vendor coupling).
* Professionals are individuals: publishing their profile needs explicit consent (UK GDPR).

## Scope

1. VerificationCase entity and actions `directory.verification.request` (trader name, registered address, registration number, VAT number optional, contact, evidence files) and `directory.verification.decide` (platform:moderate).
2. `directory.listing.publish` and `.unpublish`: publish requires an approved verification for the tenant and, for professionals, a recorded consent; approval policy confirm.
3. ModerationCase entity and actions `directory.content.report` (signed-in, or anonymous through a `HumanCheck` port) and `directory.moderation.decide` with outcomes keep, edit request, remove, suspend listing, plus a mandatory statement of reasons sent to the affected tenant.
4. An appeal: the affected tenant can contest once; a second moderator decides.
5. Moderation queue screen (platform role) with projection and bound controls.
6. Notifications through <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" /> to the reporter and the affected tenant.
7. A platform role `moderator` in <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" /> that can read reported content only, never other private threads.

## Acceptance criteria

* A listing without approved verification cannot be published (typed error), and the agent gets the same error.
* A report creates a case, a decision sends the statement of reasons, and an appeal is decided by a different moderator (test enforces this).
* A moderator cannot read an unreported enquiry thread (negative test).
* Audit rows for every decision.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; manual verification only, no verification vendor without Jonathan approving it here; whitelabel copy; flag `directory-marketplace`; ships to main with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged with the tests green and the moderation policy text (people docs) committed.

## Blockers

F5.1, <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" /> (roles and approvals), <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" /> (notifications; in-app only until it lands).

issues.title: F5.4 Build directory search, filters, geo radius and transparent ranking
issues.description:
Status: Proposed (2026-11-01), part of <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> (F5 Directory and marketplace).

## Goal

Organisers and anonymous visitors find the right supplier by text, category, location, date, capacity and budget, and can see why results are ranked as they are.

## Context

* <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> sections 4 (`directory.search`, `directory.listing.get`), 8 and 11 (P2B ranking transparency).
* Text and semantic search come from the <issue id="2cd1c920-450c-487e-b4c8-e860a382a6b0" label="EVE-26" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-26/port-search-and-embeddings-across-every-resource" /> search port (Postgres full text plus vectors).
* Decision D5-4 default: PostGIS on Neon for radius and polygon service areas. PostGIS on Neon was approved by Jonathan on 2026-11-08 (decision card on <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" />, D5-4 a), so it may be enabled for this issue.

## Scope

1. A search read model fed from the change feed (<issue id="ee08644c-eb3c-4a46-aea7-745864ad4263" label="EVE-45" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change" />) with published `ListingPublic` rows only.
2. `directory.search` input: query text, kind, categories, location (point or place resolved by a `Geocoder` port), radius, date range, capacity per layout, budget ceiling, sort (relevance, distance, rating, response time), cursor. Output: ListingSummary page plus a ranking explanation per result (matched terms, distance, rating, response time weight).
3. Ranking formula documented and published as the "main ranking parameters" page; no paid boosts, commission never used as a ranking input (F5.14), and an unclaimed listing ranks below a claimed one at equal relevance (F5.13); all three are stated on the page.
4. Service area matching: a listing appears when the search point lies inside its service area, or within radius of its point.
5. Search screen per <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> section 6 with list and map toggle, projection with result ids, ranks and reasons.
6. Offline: last result pages cached read-only with a "results from <time>" banner; search itself requires connectivity and says so.
7. Anonymous access with rate limiting.

## Acceptance criteria

* Fixture of 200 listings: category, radius, capacity and budget filters each have a test; results outside a service area never appear.
* The ranking explanation matches the documented formula in a property test.
* p95 under 300 ms for the fixture on the CI database (recorded).
* The agent answers "why is this first" from the projection.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; PostGIS approved; no geocoding vendor until Jonathan approves on this issue; flag `directory-marketplace`; ships to main with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged with tests and the performance number recorded here, and the ranking page committed to the people docs.

## Blockers

F5.1, <issue id="2cd1c920-450c-487e-b4c8-e860a382a6b0" label="EVE-26" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-26/port-search-and-embeddings-across-every-resource" /> (search port), <issue id="ee08644c-eb3c-4a46-aea7-745864ad4263" label="EVE-45" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change" /> (change feed), decision D5-4.

issues.title: F13 Human resources: worker records, onboarding, qualifications and leave
issues.description:
Status: Approved (2026-11-08, Jonathan chose decisions 1a, 2a, 3a, 4a, 5a, 6a and 7b on the decision card). Follows the [Feature set spec template](<https://linear.app/resnovas/document/feature-set-spec-template-and-list-26b9f78cf17a>). Planning only until Jonathan asks for implementation; no new dependency or vendor sign-up without approval on the child issue.

## 1. Goal

Every person who works on an event (employee, freelancer, volunteer or agency crew) has one trusted record in Eventiva, is onboarded with signed paperwork, and can only be put on a job they are qualified, entitled and available to do.

## 2. Users and jobs

| User | Jobs |
| -- | -- |
| HR admin (owner, office manager) | Create workers, set engagements and positions, run onboarding and offboarding, keep documents, check right to work, set leave policies, answer audits |
| Line manager / head of department | Approve leave, verify certificates, see their team's onboarding and expiry status |
| Crew coordinator / production manager | See who is eligible for a role on an Event (F1) before rostering (F2); never sees sensitive fields |
| Worker (employee) | Keep own profile, sign documents, upload certificates, request leave, see balances |
| Freelancer or volunteer | Same app and same self-service, scoped to their own record and the tenants they work for |
| Crew agency / supplying vendor | Upload and maintain qualification evidence for the people they supply; sees only their own people |
| Finance and payroll (F12) | Read engagement terms and approved absence that pay runs need |
| Site supervisor at a venue | Check offline that the rigger in front of them holds a valid certificate and completed the site induction |
| Agent (acting for any of the above) | Everything that user can do, through the same actions, with approvals where marked |

## 3. Market check

Names stay out of customer-facing copy.

* **General SME HR platforms (HiBob, Personio)**: strong employee records, org charts, onboarding checklists, document templates with e-signature (often through a partner), leave policies with accruals and approval chains, self-service apps, reporting. They assume salaried employees on fixed contracts; freelancers and volunteers are weak or absent, and there is no link between qualifications and who can be put on a job.
* **Event and rental crew tools (Rentman crew scheduling, CrewBrain)**: built for freelance crew pools: availability requests, crew portals, skills and certificates, rates per function, project-based planning. HR depth is thin: little document signing, basic or no leave accrual, no right-to-work workflow.
* **Shift workforce tools (Deputy and similar)**: qualifications with expiry that block rostering, leave feeding availability, mobile-first self-service, time and attendance feeding payroll.

**Where Eventiva matches**: records, onboarding, documents, leave accrual and approvals, self-service, qualification expiry that gates rostering.

**Where Eventiva differs**: one record type for employees, freelancers, volunteers and agency crew; qualifications checked against the actual role on an Event (F1) and roster (F2), including per-Event site inductions; offline eligibility checks at the venue; and every HR operation is an agent action with the same permissions, approvals and audit as the UI (<issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> parity rule), so the agent can onboard a crew of 30 freelancers or chase every expiring certificate before a show.

## 4. Capabilities as actions

## 5. Data model

All tables live in an `hr` extension through the shared schema package (<issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" />), tenant-scoped with the <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> tenant guard on every row. Identity of the human comes from F4 (Person); a Worker is the HR view of a Person within one tenant, so a freelancer who works for two tenants has two Worker rows and one Person per tenant, never a shared record across tenants.

## 7. Agent behaviour

When asked, the agent can do anything the user can through the actions above, for example "onboard these 30 freelancers for the festival", "who is qualified to rig on the main stage on Saturday", "book me Friday off".

Proactive (each behind its own flag, results go to a review queue, never silent changes):

* Expiry watch: a durable scheduled run (<issue id="a626308a-598f-41ba-accd-4004cbbd9932" label="EVE-54" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow" />) lists qualifications and right-to-work follow-ups expiring within 60 days and before any rostered Event date, drafts reminders to the worker (<issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" />) and flags affected F2 roster slots.
* Roster guard: when someone is put on a role, the agent runs `hr.eligibility.check` and explains any failure in plain words with the fix (upload certificate, verify, override request).
* Onboarding chase: overdue steps produce a suggested reminder and a summary for HR each morning.
* Leave clash: on `hr.leave.request`, report clashes with F2 rosters and F1 Event dates to the approver.
* Evidence reading: when a certificate image or PDF is uploaded, the agent proposes issuer, reference and dates for a person to confirm; it never verifies its own extraction.

Always needs a human: signing, acknowledging policies, verifying a qualification the agent extracted, approving leave (unless the tenant sets an auto-approve rule), ending an engagement, offboarding, revoking access, eligibility overrides, data subject exports started by HR, and purges. The agent never reads sensitive fields unless the user it acts for could and the purpose is recorded; sensitive values are excluded from prompts, telemetry and agent memory by default (<issue id="e00f04b6-a68b-41ed-8aa3-263fb8721b32" label="EVE-56" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-56/p18e-build-the-agent-harness-outbound-acp-agent-memory-and-context" />).

## 9. Permissions and roles

Default role grants per tenant (editable in F14 customisation, enforced by <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />):

| Role | Grants |
| -- | -- |
| HR admin | All `hr:*` grants, including sensitive read with purpose |
| HR officer | hr:workers:write, hr:documents:write, hr:onboarding:write, hr:qualifications:write, hr:rtw:write, hr:leave:write, no admin, sensitive read with confirm |
| Line manager | Read own reports (non-sensitive), approve their leave, verify their qualifications, complete onboarding steps they own |
| Crew coordinator / production manager | crew:eligibility:read (status and reasons only), set Event requirements, record inductions |
| Site supervisor | Offline eligibility and emergency contacts for workers rostered on their Event on the day; record inductions |
| Finance | Read engagement pay fields and approved absence; no sensitive profile except bank details when F12 needs them |
| Worker (any type) | Own record, own documents, own leave, own qualifications; never another worker's data |
| Supplying agency (external) | Add and maintain qualifications and documents for workers whose supplierOrgId is their organisation; see eligibility for those workers only |
| Agent | Exactly the grants of the user it acts for, minus actions marked human-only in section 7 |

Field masking: SensitiveProfile fields are masked in every projection unless the caller holds hr:sensitive:read and has revealed them for a recorded purpose; reveals are audited and expire after the screen closes.

## 10. Telemetry and flags

* Feature flag: `hr-module` (default off in code), with child flags `hr-agent-expiry-watch`, `hr-agent-roster-guard`, `hr-agent-evidence-reading` (default off).
* PostHog events (no personal values, ids pseudonymous): `hr_worker_created`, `hr_onboarding_started`, `hr_onboarding_completed` (with duration), `hr_document_signed`, `hr_qualification_added`, `hr_qualification_verified`, `hr_eligibility_checked` (outcome, reason codes), `hr_eligibility_overridden`, `hr_leave_requested`, `hr_leave_decided`, `hr_site_check_offline`.
* Spans on every action from <issue id="a03acb76-125b-4ead-815e-10ec986d8413" label="EVE-44" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor" />; sensitive fields marked secret are never attributes.
* Success metrics: share of rostered people with all required qualifications valid at call time (target 100 percent, overrides counted separately); median days from `hr.onboarding.start` to completion; share of leave requests decided within 2 working days.

## 11. Compliance

Requirements to validate with a qualified adviser before launch; the rules below are the starting point, UK first (decision 6), behind a jurisdiction rule port.

* **Data protection (UK GDPR, EU GDPR)**: lawful basis per field, special category data (health, diversity) separated, consent for optional diversity data, data subject access and export (`hr.dataExport.subject`), rectification, retention schedules with purge (`hr.retention.purge`), records of processing, encryption at rest for SensitiveProfile and files, access audit on every reveal.
* **Right to work (UK)**: checks recorded before work starts, copies kept securely for the engagement plus two years after it ends, then deleted; follow-up checks for time-limited permission.
* **Employment terms**: a written statement of particulars from day one for employees and workers (generated from templates).
* **Working time**: store the 48-hour opt-out signature; rest and weekly limits are enforced in F2 rosters using data held here.
* **Holiday**: statutory minimum 5.6 weeks for full-time staff; rolled-up holiday pay and the 12.07 percent accrual method allowed for irregular-hours and part-year workers in leave years starting on or after 1 April 2024; bank holiday handling per policy.
* **Freelancers**: store the off-payroll (IR35) status determination and its reasoning where the tenant must make one; Eventiva does not decide employment status.
* **E-signatures**: simple electronic signatures are admissible in the UK and EU for most employment documents; evidence must show who signed, when, and that the document was not changed.
* **Safeguarding**: record check type and date for roles that need criminal record checks; never store the certificate content beyond what the tenant's policy allows.
* All customer-facing text is whitelabel and ASCII only.

## 12. Acceptance

* A freelancer, an employee and a volunteer are each created, onboarded from a template with a signed document and an uploaded certificate, and appear as active, by a person in the UI and separately by the agent, with identical audit rows.
* Rostering a worker with an expired or unverified required qualification onto an F2 role for an F1 Event fails with a reason; an override requires approval and is audited.
* A site supervisor's phone, offline, shows the correct eligibility and induction status for every worker rostered on that Event that day, and records an induction that syncs on reconnect.
* A leave request offline is accepted locally, approved online with balance and roster clash re-checked, writes a ledger entry and blocks availability in <issue id="97915f03-fb56-4efc-bb5a-15e8b62b96b2" label="EVE-33" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters" />.
* A crew coordinator and the agent acting for them can never read any SensitiveProfile field (negative tests across UI, HTTP, MCP and ACP).
* A data subject export contains every HR record for the worker; a purge removes right-to-work copies after the retention date.
* The parity gate passes for every action and every screen control in this set.

## 13. Out of scope

* Pay runs, payslips, tax and pension calculations, timesheets and expenses (F12 and F11).
* Shift building, availability requests and call sheets (F2), beyond the eligibility check and leave block this set provides.
* Recruitment and applicant tracking (job adverts, candidate pipelines); a Worker starts at candidate status when hiring is decided.
* Engagement surveys and compensation planning. Performance reviews, goals and feedback are in scope (decision 7b, <issue id="17b3f12a-4684-475c-8204-fb320edf05fe" label="EVE-239" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-239/f1310-build-performance-reviews-goals-and-feedback" />).
* Health and safety incident reporting (belongs with live operations).
* Deciding employment status or giving legal advice.

## 15. Decisions for Jonathan

Decided 2026-11-08 by Jonathan: 1a, 2a, 3a, 4a, 5a, 6a, 7b (reviews added as F13.10, <issue id="17b3f12a-4684-475c-8204-fb320edf05fe" label="EVE-239" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-239/f1310-build-performance-reviews-goals-and-feedback" />).

1. **Who has an HR record**: (a) one Worker record for employees, freelancers, volunteers and agency crew, recommended, because event crews are mostly freelance; (b) employees only, freelancers stay contacts in F4.
2. **Identity**: (a) Worker extends the F4 Person per tenant, recommended, one human one contact record; (b) a separate HR person record.
3. **Qualification gate on rostering**: (a) hard block with an approved, audited override, recommended for safety-critical work like rigging and electrics; (b) warning only; (c) no check.
4. **E-signature in phase one**: (a) built-in simple e-signature with an evidence record behind the `ESignature` port, recommended, no vendor or cost; (b) integrate an external provider first.
5. **Right-to-work checks in phase one**: (a) manual check record with document capture and follow-up reminders, provider port later, recommended; (b) integrate a certified identity provider now.
6. **Leave rules**: (a) UK statutory rule pack first, other jurisdictions as configurable policies, recommended; (b) generic configurable policies only.
7. **Performance reviews**: (a) out of F13 for now and listed as a future set, recommended; (b) add a reviews slice to F13. **Chosen: (b).**

## 17. Alignment with other feature sets (2026-11-01)

* **F1 (**[EVE-73](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show>)**)**: people on an event are F1 TeamMember (event_id, contact_ref to F4, role, departments, external flag). F13 exposes `hr.qualifications.holds` (personRef, qualificationTypeKey, at) returning holds, expiry, verified and a reason, so F1 can gate `rigging.signOff` (f1:rigging:certify) on the seeded `rigging-competent-person` qualification. Built in [EVE-154](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-154/f135-build-qualifications-requirements-and-the-eligibility-check>). Requirement targets use F1 Event and Space.
* **F4 (**[EVE-65](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-65/f4-contacts-and-crm-people-organisations-relationships-and-history>)**)**: every human is one F4 Person (Party, typeid), separate from the login User in [EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>). A Worker references the Person by party id and holds employment data only; special category data stays in F13 SensitiveProfile, never in F4. F13 registers as a PartyReferenceOwner ([EVE-99](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-99/f44-find-and-merge-duplicate-contacts-and-import-and-export-them>)) so Person merges rewrite Worker references. Built in [EVE-98](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-98/f131-build-worker-records-engagements-and-organisation-structure>).
* **F2 (**[EVE-67](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-67/f2-scheduling-and-rosters-crew-availability-shifts-offers-call-sheets>)**)**: F2 reads F13 only through a QualificationReader port (qualifications, age band derived from date of birth without exposing it, contract type) and treats approved leave as an availability exception of kind unavailable ([EVE-128](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-128/f21-build-crew-profiles-roles-and-availability>), [EVE-130](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-130/f23-build-working-time-rules-and-conflict-checks>)). F2 stores no right-to-work documents. Working-time rule packs (UK first) live in F2 and read contract type from F13. F13 implements QualificationReader in [EVE-154](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-154/f135-build-qualifications-requirements-and-the-eligibility-check>) and the leave exception in [EVE-179](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-179/f137-build-leave-policies-the-leave-ledger-requests-and-absence>).
* **F7 (**[EVE-71](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-71/f7-fleet-and-live-operations-vehicles-maintenance-units-dispatch-and>)**)**: driving licences live in F13 as Qualifications; F7 reads them through the same QualificationReader port for driver eligibility ([EVE-97](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-97/f72-build-driver-eligibility-checks-from-staff-qualifications>)). Each Qualification carries category key (for example UK licence categories B, C1, D1 and extras such as 4x4 or forklift as their own types), validFrom, expiresAt (valid to) and restrictions (list of codes and free text). Built in [EVE-154](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-154/f135-build-qualifications-requirements-and-the-eligibility-check>).
* **F12 payroll (**<issue id="1eff75a6-04b4-446b-a29c-816c50dd169f" label="EVE-92" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-92/f126-build-freelancer-self-billing-and-worker-status-records" />, <issue id="dd0fdf5c-47be-46e5-a9ac-ba072c3a43a5" label="EVE-88" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-88/f125-build-the-payroll-provider-port-and-the-first-adapter" />, <issue id="a060ed52-422b-4a20-ba8e-cc47ca2a79de" label="EVE-96" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-96/f127-build-the-payments-file-and-the-pay-run-events-for-accounting" />): the individual rate stays on Engagement and overrides the F12 rate card (role and event rates, overtime, allowances) for that worker. F12 reads engagement type and offPayrollStatus from Engagement and keeps no status record of its own. F12 reads bank details and tax and NI ids from SensitiveProfile only when building a provider submission or payment file, and never stores them. F12 calculates holiday pay from approved leave (<issue id="5ca54321-0f0a-461c-ade1-89cf3197dc48" label="EVE-179" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-179/f137-build-leave-policies-the-leave-ledger-requests-and-absence" />). The final-pay flag from offboarding (<issue id="576185f3-f438-43c7-b694-e5afff0605e7" label="EVE-153" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-153/f134-build-onboarding-and-offboarding-runs" />) becomes an F12 pay run exception.
* Naming: the HR record is **Worker** (not Staff); certificates, licences, trainings and inductions are all **Qualification** of a **QualificationType**.

comments.body:
Training, competency and permission decision confirmed by Jonathan:

Evidence levels remain distinct:
1. Viewed/participated.
2. Knowledge demonstrated by assessment.
3. Practical competency signed by an authorised assessor.
4. Operational authorisation for a defined role/resource/action/scope/time.

Credential model:
- Completion, assessment, practical competency, qualification, licence, induction and certification are versioned signed credential/claim records on the worker profile with issuer, subject, scope, evidence, source content/version/profile, issue/valid-from/expiry, renewal, status and revocation.
- A credential is not itself an unrestricted role. Tenant policy explicitly maps an accepted credential type/issuer/level to one or more permission groups, role memberships, feature flags/surfaces or eligibility conditions.
- Roles/permission groups remain live relationship subjects. Prefer conditional/dynamic membership based on valid credentials rather than copying permanent grants.
- When the credential expires, is suspended/revoked, its issuer loses trust, required training changes or evidence is invalidated, derived access is automatically suspended/removed and affected assignments are surfaced.

Grant policy:
- Tenant administrators define whether an outcome auto-activates access, requires assessor approval, requires manager/security approval or only contributes to an eligibility decision.
- Low-risk product training may automatically unlock UI/features after passing.
- Sensitive, regulated, financial, permissions, live-control and safety capabilities require the configured practical assessment/independent approval and cannot be granted merely by viewing or passing a quiz.
- Policy declares scope: tenant, module, event, site, resource class, individual resource, shift/time window and permitted actions.
- Every derived grant shows an explain-access path such as: Jane → signed Event Controller competency → Live Operations role → dispatch action on Event A.
- Permission simulator supports hypothetical credential completion/expiry/revocation and previews gained/lost access before policy publication.

Operational checks:
- Eligibility also considers qualification validity, site/event induction, role/resource permission, required supervision, suspension/restrictions, assurance level and refresher/recency requirements where lawful.
- Assignments re-evaluate at planning time, shift start and sensitive action time according to policy. Offline clients use bounded signed eligibility evidence and reconcile changes visibly.
- Agents may recommend training or initiate an authorised grant workflow but cannot self-issue competency, approve their own evidence or bypass separation of duties.

This is a core EVE-13 authorisation requirement; direct EVE-245 training and EVE-154 qualification/eligibility requirement; related EVE-80 HR and EVE-244 credential/policy contract requirement.

comments.body:
External qualification verification decision confirmed by Jonathan:

- Accept Eventiva-issued signed credentials, standards-based verifiable credentials, trusted issuer API/registry evidence, QR/digital signatures and uploaded certificate/licence evidence.
- Uploaded/unverified evidence may be stored provisionally but cannot activate Sensitive/Restricted operational permissions or eligibility until the tenant’s configured verification policy succeeds.
- Low-risk policy may permit bounded provisional access with explicit expiry/supervision, but this must be visible, auditable and never the default for regulated/safety capability.

Verification states:
- Unverified
- Evidence submitted/pending
- Automatically verified
- Manually verified
- Verification failed/rejected
- Expired
- Suspended
- Revoked
- Superseded

Evidence and trust:
- OCR/AI extracts issuer, subject, qualification, scope, dates, restrictions and identifiers as proposed data only; it never establishes authenticity by itself.
- Verify cryptographic signatures/QRs, issuer endpoints, trusted registries and revocation/status lists where available. Manual verification records named verifier, method, source, timestamp, confidence, notes and evidence.
- Tenant-managed issuer trust registry defines accepted issuers, credential types, assurance/verification methods, jurisdictions, refresh frequency and which permission scopes they may unlock.
- Show credential validity separately from evidence verification and issuer trust. A genuine credential from an untrusted issuer does not automatically satisfy policy.
- Prefer hashes, issuer references and minimised extracted fields over retaining unnecessary document copies. Original evidence uses the declared security/retention/residency profile and subject-erasure/legal-hold rules.
- Periodically revalidate revocation/expiry where supported. Changes immediately re-evaluate live conditional permissions, assignments and eligibility, with offline bounded evidence/degraded behaviour.
- User can inspect and challenge a verification outcome; corrections preserve immutable provenance.
- Import/export uses portable credential/evidence/status representations and does not falsely claim another system’s assurance.

This is a direct EVE-154 qualification/eligibility and EVE-245 training requirement; related EVE-80 HR, EVE-13 authorisation and EVE-244 credential contracts.

comments.body:
Training content versioning/retraining decision confirmed by Jonathan:

All published training:
- Immutable published versions; edits create a new draft/version.
- Completion/evidence records retain exact course/module/content/question/profile versions.
- Learner/admin views show version, publication date, supersession and available change notes.

Change-impact classes:
- Editorial: wording/presentation only; existing completion remains valid.
- Minor: useful content change without changed competency; optional notification/review.
- Material: procedure, answer or expected behaviour changed; focused delta training/assessment may be assigned.
- Critical: safety, security or regulatory change; affected competency/access may be suspended until required retraining completes.

Eventiva/default course packs:
- Impact classification, structured changelog, source/standard changes, affected lessons/questions/competencies/roles, learner-facing explanation and migration/retraining policy are mandatory before publication.
- Show a clear version-to-version diff and explain how internal Eventiva changes alter training, assessment, qualification and live conditional permissions.
- Generate focused delta paths containing changed mandatory material rather than requiring the entire course where safe.
- Eventiva-owned critical/regulated defaults can impose minimum retraining consequences that tenants cannot silently weaken; they remain transparent and versioned.

Tenant/user-authored courses:
- Exact versioning remains mandatory, but change-impact classification, retraining assignment and access consequence are optional authoring fields by default.
- Authoring UI prompts for impact, suggests a classification/diff using deterministic analysis/AI assistance, and explains consequences. It does not silently enforce retraining when the tenant leaves the optional fields unset.
- Tenants may configure policy requiring impact classification for selected authors, modules, regulated content or integrity profiles.

Governance:
- Named authorised publisher approves classification; AI may propose but not approve critical/regulated impact.
- Changing impact after publication is audited and notifies affected administrators/learners.
- Offline clients receive signed version/impact manifests and cannot present obsolete critical training as current.
- Agents explain why retraining/access changed using the course diff and canonical policy evidence.

This is a direct EVE-245 requirement and refines EVE-154 live competency, EVE-80 HR and EVE-13 authorisation/audit contracts.
