issues.title: F5.8 Build quotes, quote comparison and the acceptance handoff to the event
issues.description:
Status: Proposed (2026-11-01), part of <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> (F5 Directory and marketplace).

## Planning addendum - 2026-11-12

Decision D5-7 confirmed 2026-11-13: support both acceptance of a whole supplier quote and **mixed-supplier awards with individual line/product selection and a separate supplier contract, commitment and payment schedule for every winning supplier**. The organiser requires requirement-level comparison across three or more supplier specifications, exact products, approved functional alternatives, many-to-many package breakdowns, price allocation without invented unit costs, quote revision redlines and comparison of awarded scope against later supplier invoices. The existing total-only comparison is insufficient. Partial selection from an indivisible supplier package requires a supplier-confirmed re-quote; never invent contractual component pricing. Full requirements, proposed data model, action contracts and validation are in the attached Linear document **F5.8 - Requirement-level supplier quote comparison, equivalence and invoice redlines**. Planning only; no implementation authorised.

## Goal

Vendors send priced, versioned quotes. The organiser compares requirements and products side by side, then either accepts a complete supplier quote or builds one mixed-supplier award plan selecting individual offered lines. Each awarded supplier receives a separate contract, booking/capacity commitment and payment schedule; no quote is silently divided into new legally binding prices.

## Context

* <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> sections 4 (`directory.quote.*`), 5 (Quote, QuoteLine, EngagementHandoff) and 12.
* F5 owns the quote and the handoff record. The targets are owned elsewhere: F4 Organisation and Contact (supplier link in the organiser tenant, customer link in the vendor tenant), the <issue id="97915f03-fb56-4efc-bb5a-15e8b62b96b2" label="EVE-33" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters" /> booking hold on the F1 Event dates, and the F11 commitment. Until a target set exists, the handoff records a pending step and completes it when that set ships.
* Decisions D5-2 and D5-6 (b) (2026-11-08): organisers pay accepted quotes through Eventiva via F9 split payments, with commission deducted at source per payment. The handoff creates the PaymentRequests from the quote's payment schedule as an idempotent step (F5.14, <issue id="7dba7530-e7b6-4259-be26-9924f9ebddcb" label="EVE-237" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-237/f514-build-marketplace-commission-on-accepted-quotes" />), as an idempotent handoff step.

## Scope

1. Quote and QuoteLine tables on the EnquiryRecipient (two-party scope from F5.7). Lines: optional offeringId, description, quantity, unit, unit price, tax rate code, line total; quote totals, currency, validity date, terms text, vendor trader identity snapshot.
2. Actions `directory.quote.create`, `.revise` (new version, previous becomes superseded), `.send` (confirm), `.compare`, `.accept` (always), `.decline`. A sent quote is immutable.
3. Quote comparison: normalises totals to the enquiry currency (exchange rates through a neutral `FxRates` port, shown as indicative), aligns inclusions, flags expiring quotes.
4. EngagementHandoff as a durable workflow (Effect Workflow on the cluster, [EVE-54](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow>) pattern): find or create the F4 records, place the [EVE-33](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters>) hold, create the F11 commitment, mark other recipients lost (with an optional polite decline message), call crm.enquiry.resolve (<issue id="aa5aaa4a-23e6-4982-bde3-b771cf4bf000" label="EVE-137" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-137/f46-capture-enquiries-and-track-opportunities-through-a-pipeline-into" />) in each vendor tenant with won for the accepted recipient and lost with a reason for the others (F5 directory system principal, scoped to crm.enquiry.capture and crm.enquiry.resolve only), notify both sides. Each step idempotent and retryable; failures visible on the handoff record.
5. Screens: quote editor (vendor) with lines from offerings; comparison grid and accept flow (organiser) with an approval dialog showing totals and terms.
6. Offline: a quote can be drafted offline; send and accept require connectivity at execution and are queued; accept of an expired quote is rejected on sync.
7. Statement on every quote that Eventiva is not a party to the contract.

## Decision D5-7: mixed-supplier awards (2026-11-13)

* F5 owns a versioned AwardPlan across supplier quote revisions, AwardSelections linked to organiser requirement lines, and one SupplierAward per participating supplier. The same model must also support a one-supplier whole-quote acceptance.
* A selected subset is only a proposed partial award until that supplier confirms scope, minimums, discounts, dates, price, taxes and binding contract terms. An opaque quoted kit is never automatically split into contractual per-product prices.
* Each SupplierAward uses the existing durable EngagementHandoff, F9 order/line-provider model, F6 stock or hire availability, F11 cost commitment and supplier-specific invoice, F5.14/<issue id="0bb5afb4-c634-4b0a-a364-648e1ea650ef" label="EVE-246" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-246/define-provider-neutral-connected-account-invoicing-and-settlement" /> payment and commission flows; one supplier remains merchant of record for its own contract.
* AwardPlan coverage checks prevent unintentional double-awards, missing mandatory requirements and duplicated reservations; also expose cross-supplier technical compatibility and integration responsibility gaps.
* Supplier awards may commit independently. A failed or rejected second supplier must not silently reverse another supplier's accepted contract; preserve partial-commit status, retry safely and require authorised amendments/cancellation where necessary.
* Supplier A never receives Supplier B's private quotes or organiser comparison notes. Agents can propose mixed awards, but each supplier contract requires authorised human confirmation.
* The attached detailed specification has test cases and action-contract candidates for this decision. Existing `directory.quote.accept` must reuse SupplierAward/Handoff rather than implement an unrelated second acceptance path.

## Acceptance criteria

* Accept runs once even when retried (idempotency test) and leaves F4, <issue id="97915f03-fb56-4efc-bb5a-15e8b62b96b2" label="EVE-33" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters" /> and F11 steps either done or recorded as pending.
* Two vendors quote; the organiser compares; accepting one marks the other lost; vendors see only their own quote.
* Agent: drafts a quote from offerings for a vendor user; cannot accept for an organiser user without quote:accept; accept always waits for the user's approval on screen and through MCP.
* Revised quote keeps the history of versions (test).

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; no zod; no payment or FX vendor without Jonathan approving it on this issue; flag `directory-marketplace`; ships to main with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged with the handoff workflow tests green, and a comment here listing which handoff steps are live and which are pending on F1, F4 or F11.

## Blockers

F5.7 (enquiries), <issue id="a626308a-598f-41ba-accd-4004cbbd9932" label="EVE-54" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow" /> (durable runs), <issue id="97915f03-fb56-4efc-bb5a-15e8b62b96b2" label="EVE-33" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters" /> (booking holds), F1 Event, F4 Organisation and Contact, F11 commitments.

## Added 2026-11-08: payment schedule (D5-6 b)

* The quote editor holds an optional payment schedule: a deposit (percentage or amount, due date or days after acceptance) and a balance (due date relative to the F1 Event start). Default when blank: one payment of the full total, due on acceptance.
* The schedule is part of the sent quote version, so it is immutable once sent and shown to the organiser before acceptance with the vendor's cancellation and refund terms.
* On acceptance the EngagementHandoff creates one PaymentRequest per schedule line (F5.14, <issue id="7dba7530-e7b6-4259-be26-9924f9ebddcb" label="EVE-237" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-237/f514-build-quote-payments-with-commission-deducted-at-source" />). Paying, commission and refunds are built in F5.14, not here; this issue only stores the schedule and emits the requests.
* Commission is never shown on the organiser side of the quote or comparison.

## Decision D5-8 - progressive comparison and planning-driven quote impact (2026-11-13)

### Goal

Make complex supplier comparisons usable from a stage-level overview down to the exact quoted product or service, while keeping supplier quote validity aligned with the organiser's changing event requirements. This extends D5-7 whole-quote and mixed-supplier awards and the attached requirement-level comparison specification; it does not replace those contracts.

### Progressive disclosure and visual status

* Default overview presents event areas such as Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3, or the equivalent organiser-defined plan hierarchy. Show comparable cost roll-ups, supplier coverage, quotation freshness and a small, non-intrusive issue indicator. Do not force the full equipment matrix on initial load.
* Drill path: event -> stage/area -> category or discipline (audio, lighting, video, etc.) -> requirement -> individual proposed product/service, bundle components, evidence and quote revision differences. Support navigating back without losing filters, selection or context.
* Derive parent warning state and counts from affected descendants. Use concise accessible icons and labels, and avoid flooding the overview with per-line warnings. Provide filters such as 'show issues only' and clear visual distinctions for 'not supplied', 'not quoted', 'not applicable', 'non-equivalent', 'partially covered', 'price anomaly', 'outdated quote', 'awaiting supplier confirmation', and 'resolved'. Never rely on colour, grey-out or strikethrough alone. Suppressed/non-applicable lines must remain accessible for audit.
* Coverage is defined relative to current requirement versions, quantities, units and technical criteria. Do not treat an item as covered merely because a supplier used a similar product name. Multi-line kits and functional-equivalence approvals must roll up without double-counting prices or coverage.
* Major deficiencies (e.g. half the required audio equipment missing) show a conspicuous but restrained deficiency count or coverage summary at stage level; reveal exact missing lines upon drill-down. Percentages must be based on a disclosed denominator, not an unexplained score.
* Preserve accessibility, keyboard navigation, screen-reader status, responsive layouts and offline access to the most recently synchronised comparison, clearly labelled if stale. Large comparisons should load detail incrementally without requiring full materialisation in the initial view.

### Planning-to-sourcing dependency and change impact

* The F1 event plan/production requirements own the authoritative versioned requirement tree, including stable requirement ID, stage/category linkage, quantity, units, specification, timing and constraints. F5 comparisons and supplier quote lines reference requirement IDs and the exact requirement revision they were priced against. Integrate with F1/F5.7/F5.8 and F6 inventory requirements rather than creating a second source of truth.
* When a requirement changes, emit a durable, idempotent change event and recompute affected coverage, equivalence, pricing assumptions, selection plans and supplier response status. Changes to quantity, product, specifications, dates, venue/stage or removed/added requirements must be distinguishable.
* Example: Stage 2 vocal microphone requirement changes from 20 to 10. Existing supplier quotes for 20 are preserved as immutable supplier versions and flagged 'needs review / quoted against earlier requirement' with before/after quantities. A unit-price multiplication may be shown only as a clearly labelled non-binding estimate when valid; discounts, minimum hire quantities, bundle pricing, freight and crew impacts require supplier reconfirmation. Do not silently rewrite or accept supplier quotes.
* Scope impact detection traverses bundles, shared equipment, staffing, hire dates, dependencies, substitutions and mixed-supplier selections. A changed requirement need not invalidate unrelated areas or quotes. The system should distinguish automatic clear matches from uncertain impacts needing human review.
* Buyer can review impact, approve suggested supplier clarification, request revised quotes, compare revisions and accept or dismiss an issue with reason. Supplier receives only their own affected requirement changes and approved communication, never competitors' prices. Maintain immutable history, actor, time, previous/new requirement versions, impacted quote IDs, supplier responses and final resolution.
* Already accepted supplier contracts and commitments must not be edited by a changed plan: create a change-request/amendment workflow with authorised approval, supplier confirmation and independent accounting/booking adjustments. Agent tools use the same authorised operations as UI and cannot auto-commit changes or contact suppliers without the requisite permissions and approval.
* Offline plan edits may queue and sync, but stale comparisons cannot be represented as current; reconcile concurrent planning edits with version checks and conflict handling. Recompute asynchronously and show pending/stale indicators when needed without blocking the planning UI.

### Validation

1. On opening a comparison covering three stages, only stage-level summary rows render initially, with correct totals, coverage and issue count; selecting Stage 2, then Audio, then Microphones exposes individual supplier lines without loss of context.
2. A supplier omitting 50% of the defined Stage 2 audio requirements produces a visible deficiency indication at Stage 2 and Audio, with exact missing requirements identifiable on expansion. 'Not applicable' and 'not supplied' never merge into a misleading status.
3. Changing a requirement from 20 microphones to 10 marks only affected supplier quotes and award selections stale, preserves prior sent quote versions and prices, and offers a supplier re-quote workflow; no binding price, contract or invoice changes automatically.
4. Supplier bundles covering more than one requirement are represented without duplicated monetary totals; changing one bundled requirement flags the whole price dependency when it cannot be safely separated.
5. A previously accepted contract remains unchanged until a separately approved amendment. Failed change processing is retryable, auditable and cannot duplicate notifications, commitments or awards.
6. The same impact details and navigation are available through Agent-Native actions to appropriately authorised agents, with cross-supplier confidentiality and negative permission tests.
7. Mobile/web, screen-reader, keyboard, offline/stale-data and large-comparison performance tests prove the summary remains usable and warnings are perceivable beyond colour.

### Out of scope / escalation

This decision does not authorise auto-awarding, auto-renegotiation or an unapproved redesign of the F1 planning schema. Before implementation, align F1 requirement versioning and event production planning issue ownership, plus existing F5.8 detailed document/action contracts. Escalate ambiguity around requirement-tree ownership, mixed-unit coverage denominators, discounts or bundled repricing rather than inventing values. Planning only.

## Decision D5-9 - multi-round supplier quote redlines and discount regression detection (2026-11-13)

### Goal

Organisers can compare successive quotation rounds from the same supplier, separately from cross-supplier comparisons, and identify additions, removals, specification changes and unexpected price changes without manually rereading every line. Detect the real-world failure in which a supplier revises a quote and an agreed discounted price silently returns to its default rate.

### Context and scope

* A sourcing exercise has requirement revisions and optional named quotation rounds (Round 1, Round 2, Round 3); each supplier has its own immutable sequence of sent quote versions, timestamp, attached original proposal and supplier identity. Round membership is explicit, and a supplier may submit multiple versions within one round or decline a round. Do not assume all suppliers submit simultaneously.
* Provide two distinct comparisons: (a) supplier A revision N versus supplier A revision N-1 or any selected historical baseline; (b) supplier A, B and C against a common requirement revision in a selected round. Provide a toggle to compare against the last quote, first quote, latest agreed commercial baseline or a user-selected version. Preserve requirement-version differences when comparing changed criteria.
* Match line items by durable supplier line identity, product/catalogue identity and requirement identity, using explicit human-confirmed continuity when supplier identifiers are regenerated, descriptions change, items split/merge, bundles are restructured or products are substituted. Matching confidence is not proof; ambiguous matches must be marked for review. Deleted lines and unpriced additions remain visible in the redline and audit trail.
* Every change receives a typed, accessible label: added, removed, quantity/unit changed, product/substitution changed, scope changed, unit price changed, discount changed, tax changed, fee changed, bundle repriced, total changed, and unchanged. Show old/new values, absolute and percentage deltas when mathematically meaningful; distinguish unit-price change from quantity-driven extended-total change, and include all applicable taxes/fees with currency and FX basis indicated. Avoid misleading percentages when a baseline is zero or prices are opaque.
* Persist the agreed or supplier-confirmed commercial pricing baseline per stable line or negotiated package: price basis, list price if explicitly supplied, agreed net unit/package rate, discount type/value, currency, quantity tiers, validity/effective dates, and supplier confirmation/evidence. Distinguish a negotiated rate from an inferred discount. Negotiated rates may change legitimately when the scope, volume or validity changes; do not assume rates are perpetual.
* Flag any unchanged or comparably matched line whose new net unit rate exceeds an applicable previously confirmed negotiated rate, particularly where it appears to revert to list/default price. A potentially expired or quantity-conditioned discount is flagged as 'requires confirmation', not automatically labelled supplier error. Highlight unexpected discount removal even if another line reduces the overall quote total. Do not auto-correct supplier-owned quote versions, invent discounts, or declare a binding agreed price without evidence.
* For a revised round, split overall financial movement into at least: quantities, net unit prices/discounts, added/removed scope, bundle/fee effects, tax, and unallocated/unexplained residual. The decomposition must reconcile to the old/new totals on a like-for-like currency/tax basis; where decomposition is impossible, mark it unknown rather than invent numbers. Whole proposal totals and stage/category roll-ups reflect these differences.
* In the stage-first progressive view established by D5-8, show a subtle summary such as '3 changes, 1 price regression' or 'discount needs confirmation'; drill through stage -> category -> line to see old/new quotes and supplier evidence. Filters include 'changes only', 'price increases', 'discount regressions' and 'unresolved'. Explicit icons/labels must work without relying on colour alone.
* Enable the organiser to acknowledge a change, flag a suspected regression, attach notes/evidence, request supplier clarification or re-quote, mark a variance accepted with an authorised reason, and retain all resolutions across later rounds. Suppliers see only their own quote and approved requests, never competing supplier commercial terms. Agent-Native actions expose the same history and review workflow under equivalent permissions; no autonomous acceptance or supplier messaging without relevant approval.
* Quote revisions are supplier-submitted immutable snapshots; round/comparison results and human review notes are separately versioned. Changes after contract acceptance require supplier amendment/approval, not mutation of an executed commitment. Support offline review of cached versions marked stale, but sending and accepting require online checks and current authorisation.

### Validation and example

* Illustrative: Round 1 quotes 20 microphones at a supplier-confirmed discounted net rate of GBP 40 each (GBP 800 pre-tax). Round 2 still quotes 20 identical microphones but unit rate silently becomes GBP 50 (GBP 1,000). Display +GBP 10/unit, +GBP 200 total and +25% with 'possible discounted-rate regression', even if the total quotation fell because unrelated lines were removed. Historical discount evidence is linked and the user's review remains unresolved until explicitly addressed.
* When requirements change from 20 to 10 microphones and the quoted rate changes, show quantity movement separately from price movement; check whether the confirmed rate applied at 10 units before labelling a regression. Never assume the total must be half.
* One line split into two lines or combined into a supplier kit cannot disappear from history or double-count money; incomplete matching is flagged for manual confirmation.
* Adding/removing items, scope substitutions, tax/fee changes and the complete round-by-round comparison are testable. Selection of any historical baseline reproduces the same deltas. Quote history, agreements, evidence, notes and approvals remain immutable/auditable.
* A three-supplier two-round exercise shows both each supplier's own revision history and current cross-supplier coverage on the same requirements, with no leakage of confidential prices.

### Boundaries and escalation

Use the F5 quote/QuoteLine versioning and the requirement-level comparison model already specified; integrate F1 requirements, F6 catalogue and F11 commitments without creating parallel commercial sources of truth. Supplier-confirmed discounts and packages must be distinguished from assumptions or calculator estimates. Escalate ambiguity over tier pricing, currencies, partial kits, matching, contract amendments and expired concessions. Planning only; do not implement or send supplier requests yet.

## Decision D5-10 - neutral bidirectional change markers and quick review (2026-11-13)

User correction to D5-9: any material price difference, whether increase **or decrease**, should carry the same neutral visual 'Changed - review' indication. A change is not inherently an error or a warning; show direction and amount separately from status. Never use a red icon simply because a unit price rose, nor a green icon simply because it fell. Reserve escalated severity for separately evidenced risks (e.g. violated supplier-confirmed pricing baseline, missing mandatory scope, incompatibility).

* Mark both price increases and reductions across quote rounds, even when total quote movement masks them. Compare quantities, unit prices, discounts, line totals and applicable tax/fees; separate price and quantity causes as specified in D5-9.
* Default UI: compact neutral change icon and accessible 'Changed' label in overview, stage/category roll-ups and line-level detail; drill down to old value -> new value with signed difference, percentage where valid, source quote revision and change reason if known. Changes remain discoverable without reliance on colour.
* Provide single-action 'Reviewed / Dismiss' for ordinary differences without requiring a note or multistep dialogue. Keep an option to add a note or request clarification. Dismissing clears the pending attention indicator, **not** the immutable record of the underlying difference. Allow reopening, and track reviewer, time, compared versions and optional reason. A subsequent new revision creates a fresh review item; no permanent suppression of future changes.
* Distinguish 'unreviewed change', 'reviewed change', and 'verified issue' as separate concepts; flagging an unexpected price regression remains possible, but not every increase automatically becomes a regression. Drops can be favourable or can indicate missing scope, changed specification, removed labour or a quotation mistake, so they merit the same quick check.
* Configurable materiality thresholds may reduce noise in top-level roll-ups but must never hide line-level changes in an explicit complete-diff view; no threshold value is assumed.

Acceptance: two otherwise identical revisions where an item goes GBP 40 -> GBP 50 and GBP 50 -> GBP 40 both show equivalent neutral change markers and accurate signed deltas. Reviewer can dismiss either with one action; overview attention count drops while change history remains accessible, auditable and visible in full diff. Changes in quantity or bundle scope are separately explained. An independently confirmed breach can still be escalated without treating all price increases as errors. Same actions and permissions apply to human and agent interfaces. Planning only.

## Decision D5-11 - hybrid planning propagation with manual supplier re-quote release (2026-11-13)

### Goal and real workflow

Internal changes to event specifications must immediately propagate as **impact information** to sourcing and quote comparisons, while supplier communication and commercial changes remain deliberate. Event planning may be exploratory (e.g. leadership proposes scope before a sale is secured); drafting many changes must not bombard suppliers with repeated re-quote requests. Product planning decision: **hybrid**, not automatic supplier outreach and not fully manual change discovery.

### Automatic internal propagation

* F1 remains the owner of versioned event requirement records. Every draft or approved requirement revision produces an internal change event with durable requirement ID, revision, provenance, author/time and correlation to the event, stage and sourcing package. Other modules update derived views, not the authoritative F1 requirement.
* Mark affected supplier quote lines, coverage, equivalence, stage/category totals and previous comparison baselines as 'review against revised requirement' or 'potentially outdated'. Detect incompatibilities and gaps as soon as the requirement changes; do not treat flags as supplier-confirmed mismatches or rewrite the supplier's immutable quote.
* Update internal forecasts, planning budget scenarios and procurement impact lists as appropriate, distinguishing exploratory vs approved scenario numbers, and preserving accepted contractual prices. Show a unified, unobtrusive change-impact queue across quotes, supplier enquiries, allocations and commitments; distinguish 'changed but not sent', 'supplier action requested', 'waiting for revised quote', 'resolved', and 'requires contract amendment'.
* Flag impacted stock/reservations and scheduling implications for review. Never silently release confirmed reservations or modify purchase orders, signed contracts, approved commitments or actual accounting entries.

### Explicit supplier action gate

* A planning change **never automatically** sends a supplier an updated brief, re-quote request, cancellation, revised contract or commercial instruction. Such externally consequential actions require deliberate authorised release of a selected, version-locked change set after manual review. This applies equally to humans and agents using the same Agent-Native action/permission/approval path.
* Users can classify event ideas, proposals or scenarios as **exploratory / not for procurement**, and can defer a specific quote revision indefinitely, until a sale, scope approval or other business milestone. These can continue changing and being costed internally without supplier notifications.
* Support collecting multiple revisions into one pending change set, previewing the cumulative delta against the last brief *actually sent to that supplier*, selecting relevant supplier(s) and requirements, and releasing **one** consolidated re-quote when ready. Do not compare only to the most recent draft; separate 'latest plan' from 'supplier has seen version'.
* Before release show the old supplier-visible brief, the proposed replacement, added/removed/changed requirements, exclusions, quote impact, recipient(s), any outstanding dependencies and optional message. User can edit, split, hold, dismiss, or approve the selected batch. Approval records actor/authority, time, exact version, recipients and released content. Dispatch is idempotent, retries do not send duplicates, failures are visible.
* Concurrent changes after user approval must not silently join an already-approved transmission. If further changes occur while a release is pending, preserve them as new unsent differences and require re-review before another outbound communication. If a batch has changed between preview and approval, block stale approval and ask for refreshed review.
* Support explicit 'do not request re-quote yet', 'waiting for sale', 'on hold', and later 'ready to send' states without automated deadlines or forced sends. Reminders may be configured separately, but no default auto-send after a timer/debounce.
* Supplier replies link to a specific released request package, supplier, requirement baseline and quote revision. Preserve every round and use the existing D5-9/D5-10 neutral bidirectional change markers and one-action internal acknowledgement; acknowledgement of a price difference is **not** permission to contact a supplier.

### State/authority model

* Distinguish internal event plan versions, procurement-released requirement baseline per supplier, quote revisions received, winning award plan, and executed contract baselines. This prevents conceptual proposals from being mistaken for purchased scope.
* Approval to release sourcing requests and approval to award/contract are separate entitlements and transitions. Agents can prepare impact summaries, draft requests and suggest consolidation, but cannot bypass release approval, signer authority, revocation or supplier isolation.
* Consider approval policies configurable by organisation/event, including delegation to an authorised procurement role; do not presume only one named individual can approve, and do not assert a sale is always required for all event types.

### Verification examples

* An exploratory change from 20 microphones to 10 marks existing quotes potentially outdated and updates internal scenario comparisons immediately; no supplier is contacted and original supplier quote totals stay immutable.
* A further change ten minutes later adjusts that same scope and adds lighting. The organiser sees cumulative changes from the last supplier-visible brief, with a single optional re-quote request after approval, not two automatic emails.
* If the sale falls through, the changes can remain exploratory, be cancelled or retained as scenarios; nothing has been transmitted or contracted.
* A released Round 2 request links to a fixed requirement snapshot. Changes made while a send is awaiting approval require re-review. A supplier Round 2 response is compared against Round 1 and the scope sent in Round 2; discount regressions and both price increases/decreases are tracked without treating every difference as an error.
* Signed commitments remain unchanged until a separately approved amendment; audit log reconstructs who saw, approved and sent exactly which change set and when.

### Integration and boundaries

Apply as F5 sourcing/quote orchestration and F1-derived impact views, linked to <issue id="03bd23d1-9da5-4272-8f2e-0b0bf4f7f846" label="EVE-119" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-119/f57-build-cross-tenant-enquiries-rfps-and-private-message-threads" /> (enquiries), <issue id="f08bafe4-f32d-4906-9e87-5d69df56d6a0" label="EVE-124" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-124/f58-build-quotes-quote-comparison-and-the-acceptance-handoff-to-the" /> (comparisons), <issue id="a58abd97-6c1f-4235-a66f-e5e161edebc7" label="EVE-229" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-229/f111-build-equipment-requirements-roll-up-placed-elements-and-hand" /> (equipment), <issue id="0bb5afb4-c634-4b0a-a364-648e1ea650ef" label="EVE-246" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-246/define-provider-neutral-connected-account-invoicing-and-settlement" /> (settlement), and existing booking/commitment workflows. Avoid a second master requirement database. Out of scope: implementing auto supplier notifications, revising signed agreements without amendment, or deciding specific organisation approval roles without further requirements. Planning only; no supplier contact or code changes.

## Decision D5-12 - supplier-by-supplier re-quote selection, multi-supplier batches and flexible scope views (2026-11-13)

### Goal

Organisers and tenants can run procurement in the way their event works: request revisions from one selected supplier or several at once; obtain quotes covering a single technical discipline or multiple disciplines; and compare, combine, group or split those supplier quotes into whatever view helps them make a decision. A supplier's submitted quotation and commercial terms remain the immutable source record regardless of how they are displayed.

### Supplier selection and approval

* In the internal review queue from D5-11, show an independent selection control per eligible supplier, with select-all/selected-subset and one-at-a-time operation. Allow selecting one supplier or many for a consolidated **user-triggered** review-and-release batch; do not infer that all originally invited suppliers should be contacted.
* When an organiser has identified a preferred supplier, they can hold, exclude or close out other supplier re-quote requests without losing those other suppliers' quotes, history or ability to resume procurement. The award may still be mixed across suppliers and categories under D5-7.
* Preview each selected supplier's **own** proposed scope changes relative to the last brief actually released to that supplier, draft request, recipients and latest relevant quote. A single bulk confirmation may approve the selected batch if the actor is authorised for **each** supplier/action, but each outbound supplier request has its own individually traceable recipient, version lock, approval, dispatch outcome and error/retry status. Partial batch failure must not cause duplicate sends or misleading success claims.
* Selection is not the same as authorisation; selecting, previewing, approving and dispatching are distinct steps. Changes made after preview require refreshing the impacted recipient's content. Never send unsolicited changes just because an internal plan, view or supplier selection changed. Agents share the same authorised actions and approval gate.

### Different suppliers, overlapping categories and workflows

* Model supplier capability/scope as a flexible **many-to-many** relationship with requirement IDs: a supplier can quote video only, audio only, video + audio, or a broader combination. A requirement may be offered by multiple suppliers; a supplier response can include lines that cover multiple requirements or categories, including indivisible bundles.
* Support different request types **per supplier and sourcing package**: organiser-specified item/quantity pricing (RFQ), design/specification-led proposal (supplier proposes a video-wall solution), budget/option-led proposals, and mixed-discipline proposals. A supplier can respond with options, alternative designs, partial coverage, exclusions or a bundled quote. Organiser can select request scope and expected response format without forcing all suppliers into the same workflow.
* An organiser may group several requirements into one supplier enquiry, split into separate enquiries, or invite different supplier sets by stage, equipment category, work package, or user-defined tags. Preserve durable requirement relationships across grouping changes and supplier-generated proposals; distinguish proposed alternative coverage from verified technical equivalence.
* Every supplier receives only its own approved brief and discussion. Never expose competing quotes, negotiated discounts, competing suppliers' proposals or other tenants' data merely because the comparison view combines them.

### Flexible presentation and quote integrity

* Store immutable source proposal/version, document/attachments, supplier-defined hierarchy, lines and totals with provenance. Maintain separate **derived projections/view definitions** (group by event stage, category, requirement, work package, supplier, supplier proposal, comparison round, or tenant-defined grouping). Support expand/collapse, saved tenant defaults and optional user overrides. These are presentation preferences, not edits to supplier evidence or accounting records.
* **Split for viewing:** one 'Audio + Video' proposal can appear under both Audio and Video categories while still remaining one submitted quote with one supplier total and intact bundling terms. Show source quote link and how displayed slices map back to original lines. A quote can span multiple stages/categories, and user-defined views can regroup it without changing scope or prices.
* **Combine for viewing:** show a composite solution from video-only supplier A plus audio-only supplier B alongside supplier C's combined audio+video quote; clearly identify quote provenance, coverage, gaps, overlaps, compatibility and provisional vs confirmed allocations. Combining display rows never combines legal entities, supplier contracts, invoice obligations or unquoted prices.
* Do **not** allocate an undivided bundle price into audio/video line prices, infer individual discounts, or sum the full combined quote once under each category. When supplier provides priced components, use them. Otherwise show 'bundle: price not allocated' and count its total **once** at the parent/commercial package level; comparative category subtotals must show incomplete/unknown rather than inventing apportioned values.
* Distinguish informative grouping from partial supplier acceptance. If the user selects only audio from a bundled proposal, preserve original terms and require an authorised supplier re-quote/confirmation before treating the partial price as binding (D5-7). Multiple supplier awards retain separate contracts and commitments.
* Keep supplier-to-supplier and round-over-round redlines from D5-9/D5-10 consistent across every view, using stable requirement/line identities and neutral 'changed' marks. Saved views must not hide excluded requirements, multi-category overlaps, unmatched lines or changes when complete comparison is requested.

### Verification examples

* Supplier A bids video wall only, supplier B audio only, and supplier C video + audio in one quote. The organiser can display all three by supplier, split by audio/video, or view an A+B composite against C. Same source quote IDs and original prices appear across views, with no duplicate counted bundle totals.
* User selects C alone for a Round 2 request, leaving A and B untouched; alternatively selects A and B together and approves one batch, with separate authorised request and dispatch records and supplier-isolated content.
* Supplier C quotes one unpriced-split audio/video bundle. Both categories show coverage with clear bundle lineage, but no made-up category price. A requested partial audio award stays pending commercial confirmation.
* A tenant's saved default grouping and an organiser's different personal view can coexist; changing views or suppliers selected never edits quote records nor dispatches an email.
* A supplier-developed video-wall proposal maps to the event's video requirement through verified coverage and alternatives, while an itemised supplier maps its own equipment lines; neither is forced to mimic the other supplier's document.

### Boundaries

Planning specification only. Do not create a separate duplicate quote master, modify contracts, allocate supplier bundle prices without evidence or contact suppliers. Coordinate the RFP/request-side behaviour with <issue id="03bd23d1-9da5-4272-8f2e-0b0bf4f7f846" label="EVE-119" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-119/f57-build-cross-tenant-enquiries-rfps-and-private-message-threads" />, retain the F1 event requirement authority, and apply <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> agent-native action parity and permission controls.

## Decision D5-13 - exact-model versus function-based requirements, supplier alternatives and contextual equivalence (2026-11-13)

### Goal and confirmed choice

The organiser can choose, **per individual event requirement line**, whether procurement must match an exact specified product/model (e.g. performer rider) or may accept supplier-recommended products that achieve an agreed function (e.g. one handheld microphone for speech). Supplier suggestions are welcome for functional requirements and can also be explicitly submitted as **non-compliant alternatives** to exact requirements, without silently being presented as compliant. Comparison should put functionally acceptable offers together even when manufacturers and models differ.

### Core model and buyer UX

* F1/<issue id="a58abd97-6c1f-4235-a66f-e5e161edebc7" label="EVE-229" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-229/f111-build-equipment-requirements-roll-up-placed-elements-and-hand" /> owns the authoritative, versioned requirement. Add a required fulfilment policy at line level: **Exact item** or **Functional / equivalent allowed**; allow a sensible tenant/category default but an explicit override per requirement. Do not flatten complex stage/rider specifications into a single exact/generic flag across the entire quote.
* Exact: record manufacturer, specific model/variant and applicable revision/SKU where provided, quantity, units, rider/source and hard constraints. The supplier's compliant bid must provide the designated item; a different product is a separate alternative with a visible 'deviation from exact' classification requiring organiser-authorised approval/waiver, not a silently 'equal' match. Availability/substitution requests do not alter the rider requirement.
* Functional: record the requested **job/outcome** (e.g. one handheld speaking microphone), quantity/units, and explicit hard/soft criteria such as form factor, wireless or wired, intended use, connection/interface, required accessories, safety/compliance, compatibility, performance floor, environment, power/frequency and rental/services scope as applicable. No manufacturer/model need be preselected. 'Generic' must not mean missing functional constraints or no technical check.
* The same event can mix both policies line-by-line and can switch policies through versioned, authorised requirement revisions. Previously sent RFQs or signed contracts are not rewritten; D5-11 impacts and supplier re-quote release approval apply.

### Supplier proposal capture and matching

* Supplier may bid the exact requested item, supply a specific brand/model for a functional request, offer multiple candidate products/options or a design-led solution, each explicitly linked to one or more requirement IDs/versions and source quote lines. Preserve supplied manufacturer/model, quantity, accessories, stock/availability claim and original quote price/conditions separately from organiser's requirement. A proposal can be more detailed than the buyer specification without turning the proposal into the master requirement.
* Group bids by **shared requirement/outcome** in the comparison view. Supplier A offering a Shure microphone, supplier B a RODE microphone and supplier C another named model can be displayed as competing candidates for 'one handheld microphone for speaking', provided they satisfy the hard criteria. Do not mark product identities as literally identical or universally interchangeable: equivalence is **contextual to this requirement**, not a global product master-data assertion.
* Explicit candidate match states: exact match; functionally meets hard criteria (verified); likely fit / proposed alternative (pending review); partially meets; incompatible / material deviation; unable to assess because evidence is missing. Include the reason, criterion/evidence, reviewer or agent provenance, and required accessories/service scope. Never auto-approve uncertain spec claims or rider exceptions, and never treat supplier marketing names as proof of technical suitability. Agents may suggest classification with evidence and confidence but follow authorised human review for ambiguity.
* A supplier may quote an alternative that is better, cheaper, or different, with its rationale and effects on scope, compatibility and price. The organiser may accept the alternative as a **bid choice** without automatically rewriting the original requirement; there is a separate explicit action to adopt it into a new plan/spec revision, with F1 change-impact review and supplier notification gate where applicable.
* Keep price, quantities, taxes, bundle/kit composition, included labour/services and omissions visible alongside equivalence. Comparable in function does not mean commercially equivalent. Do not fabricate component prices for indivisible bundles (D5-7/D5-12). Display competing candidate rows in the same functional grouping, with clear technical differences and quote provenance. Continue neutral bidirectional price-change markers (D5-9/D5-10) across rounds.

### Acceptance checks

* A line requiring an exact microphone model from a performer's rider: only that model/variant meets 'Exact item'; a supplier's different brand/model is visibly a proposed deviation even when acoustically similar. Organiser can review/authorise an exception with an audit trail but no silent rider/spec rewrite.
* A line for '1 handheld microphone, spoken-word stage' with approved functional criteria: distinct supplier-branded products can all be matched to that one requirement and shown side-by-side. Missing evidence gives 'pending review', not presumed equivalent.
* A generic lapel requirement and a handheld requirement are **not** grouped as interchangeable unless criteria explicitly permit both. Wireless frequency/licensing, connectors, power, receiver, supplied accessories and use-case requirements can disqualify superficially similar items.
* All original supplier quotes and F1 requirement versions remain immutable/auditable; accepting an option vs adopting a plan revision are distinct authorised actions. Grouping changes do not alter pricing, awards or notify suppliers.

### Ownership and boundaries

<issue id="a58abd97-6c1f-4235-a66f-e5e161edebc7" label="EVE-229" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-229/f111-build-equipment-requirements-roll-up-placed-elements-and-hand" />/F1 owns requirement policy/constraints; <issue id="03bd23d1-9da5-4272-8f2e-0b0bf4f7f846" label="EVE-119" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-119/f57-build-cross-tenant-enquiries-rfps-and-private-message-threads" />/F5.7 transports the approved requirement policy and supports supplier alternatives; <issue id="f08bafe4-f32d-4906-9e87-5d69df56d6a0" label="EVE-124" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-124/f58-build-quotes-quote-comparison-and-the-acceptance-handoff-to-the" />/F5.8 owns comparison, evidence, review and award mapping. <issue id="eaa9fbf7-7a3c-4c1c-9470-a76edd5316ff" label="EVE-81" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-81/f61-build-the-equipment-catalogue-products-tracking-modes-and-kits" /> catalogue links may assist with product identities, but do not put event-specific equivalence judgements into a permanent global identity map. Plan only; no implementation or supplier outreach.

## Decision D5-14 - F6 product specifications and supplier inventory drive equivalence and recommendation (2026-11-13)

### Decision

Following D5-13, equivalence evaluation should preferentially use **structured, evidence-backed technical specifications** from the F6 product/reference catalogue, not solely text similarity or a model's unsourced opinion. When a supplier creates/revises a quote, it can select a known product/kit linked to its inventory or import a new product/datasheet through the controlled F6 product-intake workflow; F5 retains the supplier's immutable original quote/line evidence and links to a specific specification version.

Keep four questions separate in quote comparison: (1) is this the exact required model or a contextually acceptable functional alternative; (2) what technical evidence and gaps support that conclusion; (3) does the supplier's inventory/kit include the required **quantity and components**; (4) is that quantity potentially available for this event window and has the supplier confirmed it? 'Equivalent' never means 'same SKU', 'owned', 'available' or 'contracted'.

Show source-labelled fields (maker, model, variant, type, intended use, specifications, dimensions/weight, electrical/RF/interfaces and accessories where relevant), missing/contradictory values and a comparison of hard vs preferred criteria. Match statuses from D5-13 remain distinct: exact, verified fit, proposed/pending review, partial, incompatible, unknown. An agent may suggest a fit with evidence; missing required data cannot be silently inferred. A supplier manufacturer's marketing text is supporting context, not technical certification. Exact rider models remain exact absent explicit authorised exception.

Supplier stock and availability are tenant-scoped F6 data; the **internal matching process is default-on with explicit supplier opt-out** under <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> D5-16, while all buyer-facing stock/availability evidence remains separately publication-controlled, freshness-labelled and never a wholesale sharing of stock records. A quantity known to be hired out, reserved, unavailable through damage/maintenance or incomplete within a kit must not be counted as freely available. Stale or non-shared inventory becomes 'needs confirmation', not 'available' or 'unavailable'. Do not commit, hold, award or send a re-quote merely because the automated check changes; D5-11 manual supplier contact and D5-7 contractual controls remain.

**Test:** Three suppliers offer distinct microphone models for a speaking requirement. Two models meet documented criteria and one lacks a required interface. View compares technical suitability, independently sourced prices, and availability status for event dates; one supplier's last 8 units are reserved, so 5 required is insufficient despite 8 stock owned. A new uploaded model stays pending verification until evidence review. The supplier's underlying quotes, bundle totals and tenant-private data remain untouched.

Cross-feature contract: F6/<issue id="eaa9fbf7-7a3c-4c1c-9470-a76edd5316ff" label="EVE-81" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-81/f61-build-the-equipment-catalogue-products-tracking-modes-and-kits" /> product/model evidence, F6/<issue id="928dc098-5cc9-4586-88bb-50abbe03071a" label="EVE-63" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-63/f6-warehousing-and-inventory-equipment-stock-availability-purchasing" /> inventory and booking calendar, F5/<issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> recommendations and directory, F5/<issue id="03bd23d1-9da5-4272-8f2e-0b0bf4f7f846" label="EVE-119" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-119/f57-build-cross-tenant-enquiries-rfps-and-private-message-threads" /> supplier quote intake; F1/<issue id="a58abd97-6c1f-4235-a66f-e5e161edebc7" label="EVE-229" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-229/f111-build-equipment-requirements-roll-up-placed-elements-and-hand" /> requirement criteria. Planning only.

### Planning coordination D5-16 - quote comparison never infers disclosed stock from default private matching (2026-11-13)

Supplier-private inventory can inform internal matching by default (with transparent notice and explicit supplier opt-out), independently of public stock visibility. However a buyer-facing quote comparison may show specific model, quantities, technical evidence and dates only to the extent they are explicitly included in a quote or permitted supplier publication. A hidden-inventory supplier can be generally recommended without the comparison revealing why internal stock may have contributed. Supplier-submitted quotes remain the canonical disclosed commercial evidence; any unconfirmed availability is 'confirmation needed', not 'available'. The default recommendation setting does not grant cross-tenant raw inventory/API/MCP access or auto-contact suppliers. See <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> D5-16 and <issue id="928dc098-5cc9-4586-88bb-50abbe03071a" label="EVE-63" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-63/f6-warehousing-and-inventory-equipment-stock-availability-purchasing" /> D6-9. Planning only.

issues.title: F11.3 Build event dimensions, budgets and budget vs actual
issues.description:
## Goal

An event manager sets a budget per F1 Phase, edits it offline, gets it approved, and always sees budget, committed and actual side by side.

## Context

* Parent [EVE-69](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-69/f11-accounting-ledgers-invoices-bills-event-budgets-and-tax>) sections 4 to 7. Uses F1 Event (anchor), EventSeries, Phase and Department by id as dimension values; does not redefine them (names fixed in <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> section 5). F1 EquipmentRequirement (event, phase, department, F6 catalogue ref, quantity, dates) feeds forecast equipment cost.
* Record sync and conflict rules from [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>) and the engine chosen in [EVE-17](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and>); screen awareness from [EVE-50](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen>).
* Committed cost comes from F6 purchase orders ([EVE-63](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-63/f6-warehousing-and-inventory-equipment-stock-availability-purchasing>)) and approved bills not yet paid (F11.5).

## Scope

1. Dimensions on every journal line: event (F1 Event), event series (F1 EventSeries), phase (F1 Phase), department (F1 Department), plus custom dimensions (F14 custom fields can add values). Dimension values are created automatically when an F1 Event, EventSeries, Phase or Department is created (consume F1 domain events).
2. `Budget` and `BudgetLine` with versions; states draft, submitted, approved, superseded ([EVE-42](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state>) state machine). Approved versions are immutable; a revision creates a new version.
3. Actions: `accounting.dimension.*`, `accounting.budget.draft` / `update` / `submit` / `approve` (always) / `variance`.
4. Variance service: budget, committed (open F6 POs and approved unpaid bills), planned (F1 EquipmentRequirement priced from the F6 catalogue, not yet ordered), actual (posted journals) and forecast (actual plus committed plus planned) per account and phase, as of a date.
5. Screens: Event finance tab inside the F1 Event screen, Budget editor (offline capable grid). Each with projections; the agent reads exactly the figures on screen.
6. Agent rule: flag an F1 Event when forecast passes a tenant-set share of budget (default 90 percent); approval not needed to flag.

## Acceptance criteria

* Two people edit different budget lines offline on two devices; both edits survive reconnect. Same-line edits resolve last-writer-wins and the losing value is shown in history.
* Approving needs a second person with `accounting:budget:approve`; the drafter cannot approve (segregation test).
* Variance numbers for a seeded F1 Event match a hand-computed fixture.
* The agent, asked "how is the stage phase doing against budget", answers with the same figures as the Event finance tab (projection test).

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; no new dependency; Rambo-UI components only; flag `f11-accounting`; ship to main with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged with the offline merge and variance fixtures green, and a screen recording of the Event finance tab linked here.

issues.title: F11.4 Build sales invoices, credit notes and receivables
issues.description:
## Goal

A finance user or the agent drafts an invoice from an F1 Event or an F9 order, issues it with a gapless number and a VAT-compliant PDF, sends it, and sees it paid off in receivables.

## Context

* Parent [EVE-69](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-69/f11-accounting-ledgers-invoices-bills-event-budgets-and-tax>) sections 4 to 7 and 11. Customers are F4 Parties (Organisation or Person, <issue id="ad791a38-f528-4aec-9433-c36977bbe8e2" label="EVE-65" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-65/f4-contacts-and-crm-people-organisations-relationships-and-history" />); invoices copy legal name, address and tax number from the Party at issue so the issued document never changes. F11 registers as a PartyReferenceOwner (<issue id="7692d04c-3444-4989-b2aa-b73a1a69ab02" label="EVE-99" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-99/f44-find-and-merge-duplicate-contacts-and-import-and-export-them" />) and holds a legal hold against erasure (<issue id="4b6f8805-b1b2-40f7-99e9-089c9adb8002" label="EVE-105" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-105/f48-record-consent-and-fulfil-privacy-requests-for-contacts" />). F9 hands pay-on-account orders to F11 with `sales.order.invoiceOnAccount` and waits for `accounting:invoice_settled` on the change feed (agreed with F9, 2026-11-01).
* Tax codes from F11.7; until F11.7 lands, a seeded UK standard, reduced, zero and exempt set is used.
* Files and PDFs from [EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>); email from [EVE-24](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email>); the customer link is served through [EVE-46](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-46/p17-build-the-http-api-streaming-and-the-typed-client-from-the-action>).

## Scope

1. `Invoice`, `CreditNote`, `DocumentLine`, `TaxLine`; states draft, issued, part paid, paid, void (<issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> state machine). Drafts sync offline; issue is online only.
2. Numbering sequences per tenant (prefix, next number), assigned in the issue transaction; never reused, never gapped.
3. Actions: `accounting.invoice.draft` / `update` / `issue` / `send` / `remind` / `void`, `accounting.creditNote.issue`, `accounting.invoice.fromEvent` (lines from F1 Event quote items when F1 defines them), `accounting.invoice.fromOrder` (the F9 hand-off), `accounting.invoice.view` (token-scoped for customers), `accounting.receivable.statement`.
4. On issue: post receivable and revenue and VAT through F11.1; render PDF with all UK VAT invoice fields; store via <issue id="8d8d301b-d679-4dac-95bb-c24889179cd0" label="EVE-25" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import" />.
5. On settlement (payment allocations from F11.6 or F9 payments): emit `accounting:invoice_settled`.
6. Screens: invoices list, invoice editor with PDF preview, customer invoice view (external link). Projections and bound controls.
7. Agent: draft invoices on request; list overdue invoices daily and propose reminders (sending needs approval unless a standing rule exists).

## Acceptance criteria

* 1,000 concurrent issues across two runners produce 1,000 distinct consecutive numbers (concurrency test).
* An issued invoice cannot change; a credit note reverses it fully or partly and posts the reversal.
* The PDF includes every field on the HMRC VAT invoice checklist (snapshot test against a fixture list).
* The customer link shows only that invoice; a tampered token is denied.
* An F9 pay-on-account order becomes an invoice and F9 marks it paid after settlement (contract test with an F9 fixture).

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; no new dependency (PDF rendering uses what <issue id="8d8d301b-d679-4dac-95bb-c24889179cd0" label="EVE-25" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import" /> provides, or asks here first); customer-facing text whitelabel and ASCII; flag `f11-accounting`; ship to main with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged with the numbering, PDF and F9 contract tests green, and a sample PDF attached here.

issues.title: F11.5 Build bills, expense claims, approvals and payables
issues.description:
## Goal

Supplier bills and crew expenses reach the books with a receipt, the right event and an approval, and the agent does the typing.

## Context

* Parent [EVE-69](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-69/f11-accounting-ledgers-invoices-bills-event-budgets-and-tax>) sections 4 to 7. Suppliers are F4 Parties (<issue id="ad791a38-f528-4aec-9433-c36977bbe8e2" label="EVE-65" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-65/f4-contacts-and-crm-people-organisations-relationships-and-history" />), covered by the same PartyReferenceOwner registration and legal hold as F11.4; claimants are F13 staff members. F6 ([EVE-63](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-63/f6-warehousing-and-inventory-equipment-stock-availability-purchasing>)) owns purchase orders and goods receipts and emits `inventory:goods_received`; F11 owns supplier bills (agreed 2026-11-01).
* Approvals and segregation of duties use [EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>). Receipt extraction uses the agent on the user's model engine ([EVE-52](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-52/p18a-build-the-agent-turn-loop-with-actions-as-tools>), [EVE-53](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-53/p18b-build-model-engines-model-selection-and-user-owned-subscriptions>)), decision D4 on [EVE-69](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-69/f11-accounting-ledgers-invoices-bills-event-budgets-and-tax>).

## Scope

1. `Bill`, `ExpenseClaim`, `DocumentLine`; states draft, submitted, approved, rejected, scheduled, paid (<issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" />). Drafts and claims work offline, including the photo.
2. Three-way match: a bill line can link to F6 PO lines and goods receipts; price or quantity differences beyond a tenant tolerance (default 2 percent) block approval with a typed reason.
3. Approval policies: by amount bands, by F1 Event (event manager approves their events), by department; the drafter can never approve their own bill or claim.
4. Actions: `accounting.bill.draft` / `update` / `submit` / `approve` / `reject`, `accounting.bill.extract` (proposal only), `accounting.expense.submit` / `approve` / `reject`, `accounting.payable.aged`, `accounting.payment.batch.prepare` (bank upload file, UK Bacs standard 18 CSV or the bank's CSV; no payment initiation in this slice).
5. On approval: post payable, expense or asset, VAT, and clear GRNI where matched.
6. Screens: bills list and editor with file viewer, expense capture (mobile first, camera), approvals inbox. Projections and bound controls.
7. Agent: from an uploaded or emailed receipt, propose supplier, date, lines, tax and F1 Event with confidence; never approves.

## Acceptance criteria

* A claim captured in airplane mode with a photo syncs on reconnect and appears in the right approver's inbox.
* A bill 5 percent above its PO price is blocked; within 2 percent it passes.
* The drafter approving their own bill is denied on every surface (UI, HTTP, MCP, ACP).
* Extraction on a fixture set of 20 receipts fills supplier, date, total and VAT correctly on at least 18 (evaluation tracked in <issue id="bef04957-8bec-479e-85ee-5880dfc9fc8c" label="EVE-29" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-29/port-agent-evaluations-linked-to-posthog-datasets" /> when it exists).

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; no OCR vendor (D4) and no new dependency without approval here; receipts are private files (<issue id="8d8d301b-d679-4dac-95bb-c24889179cd0" label="EVE-25" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import" />); flag `f11-accounting`; ship to main with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged with the offline claim, tolerance and segregation tests green, and the extraction score posted here.

issues.title: F2.1 Build crew profiles, roles and availability
issues.description:
## Goal

Every person who can be rostered has a crew profile with roles, and states when they can and cannot work, so schedulers and agents can ask "who is free" and get a trustworthy answer.

## Context

* Slice 1 of F2 (parent <issue id="1c8c53a0-396b-43a7-8fb9-c138dbbc70b2" label="EVE-67" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-67/f2-scheduling-and-rosters-crew-availability-shifts-offers-call-sheets" />, sections 4 and 5). Builds on the generic Resource and availability tables of <issue id="97915f03-fb56-4efc-bb5a-15e8b62b96b2" label="EVE-33" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters" /> (Resource kind `person`).
* Qualifications are owned by F13 (decision 2 in <issue id="1c8c53a0-396b-43a7-8fb9-c138dbbc70b2" label="EVE-67" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-67/f2-scheduling-and-rosters-crew-availability-shifts-offers-call-sheets" />, recommended); until F13 exists this slice ships a `QualificationReader` port with an in-memory adapter.
* Leave approved in F13 appears here as an AvailabilityException of kind `unavailable` through the same port.

## Scope

1. Tables CrewProfile and Role through the shared schema package (<issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" />), `org_id` on every row.
2. Actions `crew.profile.get`, `crew.profile.update`, `crew.role.define`, `availability.set`, `availability.exception.add`, `availability.request.send`, `availability.request.respond`, `availability.query` with the inputs, outputs and permissions in <issue id="1c8c53a0-396b-43a7-8fb9-c138dbbc70b2" label="EVE-67" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-67/f2-scheduling-and-rosters-crew-availability-shifts-offers-call-sheets" /> section 4.
3. `availability.query` ranks people by role match, qualifications, availability kind (free over tentative), travel distance from home base when known, and returns a reason list per person.
4. Privacy: exception reasons visible only to the person and admins; schedulers see free, busy or tentative.
5. Offline: a person's own availability and the scheduler's in-scope people sync to SQLite (<issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" /> engine); overlapping offline edits are both kept and flagged.
6. Screens: Availability calendar and Availability request composer with projections (<issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" />).

## Acceptance criteria

* Weekly pattern plus an exception across a DST change returns correct free ranges in two timezones (`@effect/vitest` property test).
* `availability.query` for "rigger, 14th, 09:00 to 18:00" returns the same ranked list through the UI, HTTP and MCP surfaces.
* A scheduler cannot read an exception reason; an admin can (negative test).
* An availability request sent to 3 people records each per-range answer; the agent must confirm before sending.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 (Effect services, `Data.TaggedError`, Schema, `@effect/vitest`); pure availability helpers stay plain TypeScript; behind flag `f2-scheduling`; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; WCAG 2.2 AA; whitelabel ASCII copy; ships to main per the AGENTS.md delivery exception with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged to main, tests green, the actions listed in the inventory, and a comment here with the check output.

## Blockers

<issue id="97915f03-fb56-4efc-bb5a-15e8b62b96b2" label="EVE-33" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters" /> (engine), <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />, <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" />, <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />, <issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" /> (sync engine choice).

issues.title: F2.2 Build crew requirements and shifts on events
issues.description:
## Goal

A production manager states what crew an Event needs (role, count, times, place) per Phase, and Eventiva turns that into concrete shifts that can be filled.

## Context

* Slice 2 of F2 ([EVE-67](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-67/f2-scheduling-and-rosters-crew-availability-shifts-offers-call-sheets>)). Attaches to F1 entities (<issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> section 5) Event, Phase, Department, Space and RunOfShow by id; F2 does not redefine them. Shifts must be readable per TeamMember and Phase so F1 `itinerary.generate` can build ItineraryItem kind `shift`.
* Shifts are [EVE-33](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters>) booking slots on a person resource, so conflicts with vehicles (F7) and kit (F6) use one engine.
* Run of show changes arrive through the change feed ([EVE-45](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change>)).

## Scope

1. Tables CrewRequirement (eventId, phaseId?, departmentId?, spaceId?, roleId, count, times, qualifications) and Shift; `org_id` and Event scope on every row. A read action `shift.listForItinerary` (by Event, TeamMember, Phase) for F1.
2. Actions `requirement.create`, `requirement.update`, `requirement.delete` (agent confirm), `requirement.fromRunOfShow` (drafts requirements from a Run of show and a crew template; agent confirm), `shift.generate` (split a requirement into shifts by count and split rules such as maximum shift length), `shift.update`, `shift.cancel` (approval always when assigned).
3. Requirement templates per org (for example "Standard load-in: 4 riggers, 2 lighting, 1 crew chief").
4. When a Phase moves, a domain event marks affected shifts `needs_review` rather than moving them silently.
5. Conflict rule: a count decrease below the number already assigned is rejected at sync with a typed error.
6. Screen: Event staffing with filled versus needed per Phase, projection and bindings per [EVE-67](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-67/f2-scheduling-and-rosters-crew-availability-shifts-offers-call-sheets>) section 6.

## Acceptance criteria

* From a Run of show with three Phases, `requirement.fromRunOfShow` drafts requirements matching the template; applying it creates shifts with correct times in the venue timezone.
* Moving a Phase by 2 hours flags its shifts `needs_review` and emits one change record.
* Decreasing count below assigned fails offline-replay with `RequirementBelowAssigned`.
* The Event staffing screen passes the unbound-element check.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; behind flag `f2-scheduling`; F1 entities referenced, not redefined (if F1 is not built, use a minimal Event and Phase read port and say so here); no new dependency without approval on this issue; WCAG 2.2 AA; ships to main with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged to main, tests green, a comment here with the check output and the list of actions added.

## Blockers

F2.1, F1 Event and Phase, <issue id="97915f03-fb56-4efc-bb5a-15e8b62b96b2" label="EVE-33" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters" />, <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />, <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" />, <issue id="ee08644c-eb3c-4a46-aea7-745864ad4263" label="EVE-45" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change" />.

issues.title: F2.3 Build working-time rules and conflict checks
issues.description:
## Goal

Every proposed assignment is checked against overlaps, qualifications and working-time law before anyone is booked, with clear reasons and an audited override.

## Context

* Slice 3 of F2 (<issue id="1c8c53a0-396b-43a7-8fb9-c138dbbc70b2" label="EVE-67" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-67/f2-scheduling-and-rosters-crew-availability-shifts-offers-call-sheets" /> sections 4, 5 and 11). Rule packs are data; UK Working Time Regulations first, EU next (decision 4, recommended).
* Rules are pure functions so they run on device offline and in the solver (F2.11).

## Scope

1. A pure rules engine in plain TypeScript (no IO): input an assignment set plus context (person age band, contract type, qualifications, existing bookings across person, vehicle and kit resources), output RuleResult\[\] with severity block, warn or info and a human-readable reason.
2. Built-in rules: overlap (any resource), travel buffer between locations (fixed minutes until a TravelTime port exists), qualification missing, daily rest, weekly rest, break entitlement, weekly hours average over the reference period with opt-out flag, young worker limits, maximum consecutive days.
3. Rule pack `uk-wtr-1998` with the limits listed in <issue id="1c8c53a0-396b-43a7-8fb9-c138dbbc70b2" label="EVE-67" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-67/f2-scheduling-and-rosters-crew-availability-shifts-offers-call-sheets" /> section 11; pack `eu-wtd-2003` as a second pack; org overrides per contract type, versioned.
4. Actions `rules.check` (read), `rules.override` (approval always, justification required, audit record), `rules.pack.update` (admin).
5. RuleResults recomputed on the server after every sync and stored; device results are advisory.

## Acceptance criteria

* Table-driven tests for every rule, including a shift ending 23:00 followed by one starting 08:00 (block under UK pack) and a 17-year-old on a 9-hour shift (block).
* An override by a user without `roster:approve` fails; one with it records who, why and when in audit.
* The same input gives the same result on device and server (shared fixtures).
* Rule check of a 200-person event roster finishes under 500 ms on the server.

## Constraints

Rules stay pure plain TypeScript (house exemption for pure functions); services around them in Effect; no new dependency; legal limits cited in code comments with the regulation; ships to main with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged to main with both packs, tests green, and a comment listing every rule and its source.

## Blockers

F2.1, F2.2, <issue id="97915f03-fb56-4efc-bb5a-15e8b62b96b2" label="EVE-33" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters" />, <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />, <issue id="9d08c369-bac9-4eb7-b8a7-329b5ec9bff0" label="EVE-41" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-41/p12-build-app-config-settings-secrets-and-credentials" /> (config for packs).
