issues.title: F1.11 Build equipment requirements: roll up placed elements and hand them to warehousing
issues.description:
## Goal

Everything a plan needs (fixtures, truss, speakers, cable, risers) becomes a list of equipment lines per phase and department that warehousing reserves, the marketplace can source, and accounting can cost.

## Context

* Parent: <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> sections 4, 5 (EquipmentRequirement, canonical), 7 (stock check).
* Agreed with F6 (<issue id="928dc098-5cc9-4586-88bb-50abbe03071a" label="EVE-63" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-63/f6-warehousing-and-inventory-equipment-stock-availability-purchasing" />): F6's `inventory.reservation.fromPlan` reads EquipmentRequirement filtered by event and phase. Agreed with F5 (<issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" />, <issue id="d4cc9e14-e41b-494a-a236-d205dd9c47b1" label="EVE-165" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-165/f512-build-agent-sourcing-for-organisers-and-quote-drafting-for" />): F5 reads unfilled lines to drive supplier search. F7 reads lines for transport, F11 for cost.
* Sources: DesignElements from F1.6 (with `catalogue_ref` to an F6 product), rider suggestions from F1.2, and hand-entered lines.

## Scope

1. Table `equipment_requirement` (event_id, phase_id optional, department_id, catalogue_ref to F6 product id, quantity, needed_from, needed_to, source: rollup or manual, source_element_ids, fulfilment: unfilled, reserved, hired, notes).
2. Pure roll-up function: groups DesignElements by department, catalogue_ref and phase window; adds spares by a per-department spare percentage from the org configuration schema (default 0); never deletes manual lines; marks rollup lines whose elements were removed as `stale` instead of deleting them.
3. Actions: `requirement.rollUp` (idempotent), `requirement.update`, `requirement.addManual`, `requirement.remove`, `requirement.sendToWarehouse` (confirm; emits `requirement.sent` on the change feed for F6), `requirement.setFulfilment` (called by F6 and F5 only, permission `f1:requirement:fulfil`).
4. Elements with no `catalogue_ref` are reported, not guessed; the agent may suggest a match from the F6 catalogue for confirmation.
5. Screen: Requirements tab in the Department workspace (grouped list, stale and unmatched markers, fulfilment status, send button) with projection and bound controls.

## Acceptance criteria

* Placing 24 of one fixture and 6 truss sections and rolling up gives two lines with the right quantities; rolling up again changes nothing.
* Removing 4 fixtures and rolling up updates the quantity; a manual line is untouched.
* `requirement.sendToWarehouse` produces one change-feed event F6 can consume (contract test with a fake consumer).
* Only F6 and F5 service identities can call `requirement.setFulfilment`.
* Screen passes the unbound-control check and axe.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 house rules (roll-up is pure TypeScript); every operation is an inventory action with one permission check, audit and change record; UI from Rambo-UI, WCAG 2.2 AA; behind PostHog flag `f1-production-plans`; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; whitelabel ASCII copy; people docs and ai-docs in the same commit; ships to main with `node --run check` results here.

## Done signal

Merged with roll-up, idempotency and contract tests green, and the change-feed event schema posted here for F6 and F5.

## Blockers

F1.1 (<issue id="43e4e4e4-42e9-4d64-8201-aa65787fe66c" label="EVE-166" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-166/f11-build-the-event-record-event-eventseries-phase-space-team-and" />), F1.6 (<issue id="f3615509-1ebf-4495-9f61-e5a0544e56f4" label="EVE-201" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-201/f16-build-production-plans-a-collaborative-canvas-per-space-and" />), <issue id="ee08644c-eb3c-4a46-aea7-745864ad4263" label="EVE-45" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change" />, F6 catalogue product ids (<issue id="928dc098-5cc9-4586-88bb-50abbe03071a" label="EVE-63" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-63/f6-warehousing-and-inventory-equipment-stock-availability-purchasing" />).

### Planning decision - exact versus functional requirement policy (2026-11-13; coordinate D5-13 in <issue id="f08bafe4-f32d-4906-9e87-5d69df56d6a0" label="EVE-124" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-124/f58-build-quotes-quote-comparison-and-the-acceptance-handoff-to-the" />)

* Each versioned EquipmentRequirement has a line-level procurement/fulfilment policy: **exact specified manufacturer/model/variant** where mandated by a performer rider or technical requirement, or **functional/equivalent permitted** when the organiser specifies an outcome rather than a brand (e.g. one handheld microphone for spoken-word use, or one lapel microphone). Tenant/category defaults may prefill but explicit per-line settings prevail.
* Exact requirements record specific model/variant, quantity, rider provenance and hard constraints. Functional requirements record usage/outcome and required hard/soft acceptance criteria (type/form factor, wiring/connectivity, compatible accessories, RF/environment/safety/performance where relevant), even when no model is prescribed.
* Supplier-branded candidate products and evaluated equivalence are **proposals linked to the requirement ID/version**, not replacements of the F1 source record. An alternate to an exact rider is a visible non-compliant proposal pending separately authorised waiver, never automatically equivalent.
* A user may explicitly adopt a supplier's proposed alternative to the event plan, creating a new version with change-impact propagation and existing manual supplier-release approval. Merely choosing an option for quote review or grouping alternatives does not rewrite a plan or executed commitment.
* Verify: one event carries an exact rider mic and a generic spoken-word handheld concurrently; different branded candidates match the second by verified constraints, not the first; changes and exceptions are recorded and auditable. Do not force an exact catalogue SKU for a function-based line.

issues.title: F1.12 Build live show calling and show sequences: run the run of show, live drift, timecode timelines and the show log
issues.description:
## Goal

A stage manager calls the show from Eventiva: starts segments, sees over and under run live, stands by and goes cues, and every device on the team follows the same clock, with a full log afterwards.

## Context

* Parent: <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> sections 4 (`show.*`, `sequence.*`), 5 (ShowRun, ShowRunEntry, ShowSequence, live behaviour without internet), 6 (Show caller, Show sequence), 7 (approvals), decision D3.
* This slice works without any hardware: cues are called by voice from the screen. Sending cues to devices is F1.13. Live data is never queued offline (<issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> section 5).
* The live clock lives on the show bridge when one is paired (F1.13); without a bridge, the caller's device is the clock and others follow over the live channel (<issue id="0ab161c4-ed9c-4581-86fe-91fa1f4216aa" label="EVE-46" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-46/p17-build-the-http-api-streaming-and-the-typed-client-from-the-action" /> streaming).

## Scope

1. Tables `show_run` (run_of_show_id, started_by, started_at, ended_at, armed_by, clock source) and `show_run_entry` (at, kind: segment_go, cue_standby, cue_fire, cue_result, adjust, stop; actor person or agent; outcome) and `show_sequence` (event_id, timecode format 24, 25, 29.97 drop frame, 30; start offset; cues placed at timecode).
2. Actions: `show.start`, `show.goSegment`, `show.adjust` (add or remove time, re-plan the rest), `show.end`, `cue.standby`, `sequence.create`, `sequence.placeCue`, `sequence.preview` (plays the timeline on screen only, no output).
3. Live drift: pure function from planned times (F1.3 timing engine) and actual go times to projected end and per-segment over or under.
4. Live channel: followers subscribe to a show run stream; if the stream drops they keep counting locally, mark timings stale and stop showing standby as current.
5. Show log: every entry with actor and time; exported as CSV after the show; synced when back online.
6. Agent: can be delegated a show run by a person, after which it may `show.goSegment` and `cue.standby` on schedule; the delegating person can take it back at once. `show.arm` and firing rules are in F1.13.
7. Screens: Show caller (big clock, current and next, drift, cue stack, keyboard shortcuts with large targets, never colour alone) and Show sequence (timeline with timecode ruler, playhead, preview) with projections and bound controls.

## Acceptance criteria

* Drift tests: segment runs 2 minutes over, the projected end moves by 2 minutes; `show.adjust` minus 2 recovers it.
* Three followers stay within 100 ms of the caller's clock on a LAN; one follower losing the stream shows stale timing within 2 seconds.
* With the internet off but the LAN up, a show run completes and its log syncs when the internet returns.
* Timecode conversion tests for every supported frame rate including 29.97 drop frame.
* A delegated agent goes segments on time in a simulated run, and a person taking control back stops it within one tick.
* Both screens pass the unbound-control check and axe, and the caller screen is fully usable by keyboard.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 house rules (drift and timecode maths are pure TypeScript; the live channel is an Effect stream); every operation is an inventory action with one permission check, audit and change record; UI from Rambo-UI, WCAG 2.2 AA; behind PostHog flag `f1-show-control`; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; whitelabel ASCII copy; people docs and ai-docs in the same commit; ships to main with `node --run check` results here.

## Done signal

Merged with drift, timecode, follower and offline tests green and a recorded sample show run attached here.

## Blockers

F1.3 (<issue id="cb0f80d4-48f4-4e2c-8957-26f36f9a838f" label="EVE-169" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-169/f13-build-the-run-of-show-segments-fixed-and-relative-timing" />), F1.5 (<issue id="cab9223d-ac24-4174-99b4-092df552d509" label="EVE-173" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-173/f15-build-department-cue-lists-with-numbering-segment-links-and" />), <issue id="0ab161c4-ed9c-4581-86fe-91fa1f4216aa" label="EVE-46" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-46/p17-build-the-http-api-streaming-and-the-typed-client-from-the-action" />, <issue id="a03acb76-125b-4ead-815e-10ec986d8413" label="EVE-44" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor" />, <issue id="3deaef52-8db8-490c-8143-b293ab5656a8" label="EVE-52" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-52/p18a-build-the-agent-turn-loop-with-actions-as-tools" /> (agent delegation).

issues.title: F1.13 Build the show bridge: a local process that fires cues to consoles, playback and media servers over OSC, MIDI, MSC and timecode
issues.description:
## BINDING owner decision — 15 November 2026: human-in-the-loop for ALL operational emergency actions

**Never automatically actuate a show-control or operational response from an incident, alarm, emergency sensor, issue classification, agent interpretation, integration alert or rules-engine event.** An alarm/event may be ingested, classified, displayed, logged, correlated, escalated to people, propose a configured SOP or preset, and notify designated staff; it must NOT automatically GO/hold/pause/mute audio, set venue lights/DMX, trigger PA/media/announcements, start emergency scene/preset, dispatch units or carry out other consequential incident-response operations. The possibility of false alarms and resulting public panic/harm is the rationale. This is an unconditional product policy for **operational incidents and alarms**, not an admin-configurable bypass or an exception for 'tested integration'. A permissioned, accountable **human must deliberately initiate** the approved action following assessment; log initiator, confirmation, linked incident, preset/version, result, and failures. Provide quick incident-linked actions but not default-on automatic acceptance.

**Differentiate ordinary show automation:** separately programmed and human-armed cue stacks, playback sequences, lighting console input, MIDI/OSC/MSC and timecode may continue to start permitted *non-emergency show cues* according to show programming; that is not authority for automatically activating an incident/emergency response. Incoming external signals claiming to be alarms are treated as alerts for human evaluation even if received over a show-control protocol. An external operator deliberately firing an authorized ordinary cue is still allowed, subject to arming and permissions.

**System-of-systems boundary:** independent certified fire alarms, evacuation/voice alarm, emergency lighting and physical overrides retain their own mandatory automatic functions. Eventiva's human-in-the-loop restriction is for Eventiva-initiated control actions and must not inhibit certified systems, lawful fire-panel interlocks, or physical emergency interventions. Do not call for an extra Eventiva confirmation where it could delay or prevent those independent measures. Any proposed direct control of safety-certified hardware requires separate safety engineering and approval.

**Acceptance criteria:** simulate a false fire/heat alarm and a mistakenly classified crowd incident: both notify MDT with a proposed response and initiate **zero** show/lighting/audio/PA/dispatch outputs without a deliberate authorized human action; no auto approval through agents, tenant rules or remote console input marked as emergency. Authorized manual response from MDT executes only the selected versioned preset and clearly reports partial success/failure. Ordinary human-armed playback and mapped external non-emergency cue input still work independently. Test no deferred/replayed emergency output after reconnect.

Implementation and dependencies remain unapproved.

## Two-way ingress and MDT control — owner clarification 15 November 2026

<issue id="e6838c83-005e-4ec5-bc2f-931de6cd0cb8" label="EVE-256" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-256/connect-mdt-incidents-and-external-controls-to-live-show-cues-and" /> requires **bidirectional bridge operation**: authorized local hardware/console OSC/MIDI/MSC/timecode/network input can request mapped show cues, not only receive outbound cues, and permitted F7 MDT actions can request mapped show operations/emergency-response presets through the one show-control action path. Add separately approved local input adapters, per-endpoint trust/source scope, opt-in mappings, input validation, replay/rate restrictions, show-mode/arming checks, and correlation with both show and incident logs. Raw MIDI/OSC/DMX is not generally authenticated: isolate sources/gateway and do not expose listeners publicly without a separately approved design. Distinguish request accepted, output sent and device-observed state; report partial failures. **Do not interpret** `show.stopAll` **as universal emergency blackout**—the configured venue emergency scene and certified independent systems control safe illumination/PA strategy. This is scope clarification, not approval of new dependencies, listeners or code.

## Goal

On show day, a cue called in Eventiva reaches the lighting console, playback system or media server within a few milliseconds over the local network, safely: nothing fires unless a person has armed the show, and anyone can stop everything.

## Context

* Parent: <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> sections 4 (`bridge.*`, `endpoint.*`, `show.arm`, `cue.fire`, `show.stopAll`), 5 (ShowBridge, ControlEndpoint, live never queued), 7 (human-only arming), 8 (`ShowBridge` transport), decisions D1 (decided 2026-11-08: option C, triggers here plus direct DMX in F1.14) and D6 (headless Effect process).
* Consoles and playback tools already accept OSC, MIDI notes and program changes, MIDI Show Control (MSC) and timecode (LTC audio, MTC over MIDI) (<issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> section 3). Eventiva sends triggers; the console stays the authority for looks.
* D1 = C: F1.14 (<issue id="39b7d4d1-cecf-4031-87c0-fa72276e8739" label="EVE-232" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-232/f114-build-direct-dmx-output-for-small-rigs-over-sacn-and-art-net" />) adds sACN and Art-Net level output on top of this bridge, so keep the transport service open for a `DmxOutput` layer.

## Scope

1. A new deployable `show-bridge` app (Nx `type:app`, Node, Effect platform) that runs on the show machine: pairs with an org by a one-time code shown in the app (`bridge.pair`, confirm), stores its key through <issue id="9d08c369-bac9-4eb7-b8a7-329b5ec9bff0" label="EVE-41" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-41/p12-build-app-config-settings-secrets-and-credentials" />, keeps a heartbeat, holds the show clock, and executes cue targets.
2. Transports behind one `ShowTransport` service with a layer each: OSC over UDP (no dependency needed, plain `dgram`), MIDI and MSC (needs a native MIDI library approved by Jonathan on this issue first; propose one with licence, platforms and maintenance), MTC over the same MIDI port, LTC generation as an audio output (needs an audio output library approved here; can ship after OSC and MIDI).
3. Table `control_endpoint` (event_id, bridge_id, protocol, target host and port or MIDI port, mapping from cue to message, for example OSC address template `/eos/cue/{list}/{number}/fire` or MSC `GO` with cue number). Mappings are data, editable by the department head.
4. Safety: `show.arm` is human only and per show run; `cue.fire` refuses unless the run is armed and the bridge is reachable now (typed error, never queued); `show.stopAll` sends each endpoint's configured stop or blackout-safe message and disarms; heartbeat loss over 2 seconds disarms on both sides; every fire has an idempotency key so retries on the LAN cannot double fire.
5. Actions: `bridge.pair`, `bridge.unpair`, `endpoint.create`, `endpoint.update`, `endpoint.test` (sends a harmless test message the department head chooses), `show.arm`, `show.disarm`, `cue.fire`, `show.stopAll`.
6. Telemetry: `cue_fired` with latency, `show_stop_all`; bridge spans exported when online, buffered with a bounded queue offline (<issue id="a03acb76-125b-4ead-815e-10ec986d8413" label="EVE-44" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor" />).
7. Screen: Show bridge settings (devices, endpoints, mappings, test buttons, last heartbeat) and the arm, fire and stop controls on the Show caller screen from F1.12.

## Acceptance criteria

* OSC: 100 fires to a test receiver on a LAN have p95 latency under 20 ms and no duplicates under injected packet retry.
* MIDI and MSC (once the library is approved): a virtual MIDI port receives the right MSC GO for cue 12.5 on each supported OS.
* `cue.fire` while disarmed, or with the bridge unreachable, fails with a typed error and nothing is sent.
* Agent calls to `show.arm` fail; a delegated agent can fire on an armed run; any person on the run can `show.stopAll`.
* Killing the app on the caller's device does not stop the bridge; pulling the bridge's network disarms within 2 seconds.
* Settings screen passes the unbound-control check and axe.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 house rules: transports are integration modules, vendor and native calls wrapped once in `Effect.try` or `Effect.tryPromise` with `// effect-boundary:`; every operation is an inventory action with one permission check, audit and change record; UI from Rambo-UI, WCAG 2.2 AA; behind PostHog flag `f1-show-control`; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; whitelabel ASCII copy; people docs (setup on the show machine, firewall ports, troubleshooting) and ai-docs in the same commit; ships to main with `node --run check` results here.

## Done signal

Merged with OSC latency, safety and pairing tests green, and a run against a real console or playback tool recorded here with exact versions.

## Blockers

F1.12, F1.5 (<issue id="cab9223d-ac24-4174-99b4-092df552d509" label="EVE-173" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-173/f15-build-department-cue-lists-with-numbering-segment-links-and" />), F1.10 (cue payloads for media servers), <issue id="9d08c369-bac9-4eb7-b8a7-329b5ec9bff0" label="EVE-41" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-41/p12-build-app-config-settings-secrets-and-credentials" />, <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />, <issue id="a03acb76-125b-4ead-815e-10ec986d8413" label="EVE-44" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-44/p15-build-telemetry-opentelemetry-spans-on-every-call-and-a-vendor" />.

issues.title: F1.14 Build direct DMX output for small rigs over sACN and Art-Net
issues.description:
## Goal

For small events with no lighting console, Eventiva itself sets simple lighting levels on cue, from the patch already in the plan, through the show bridge.

## Context

* Parent: <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> decision D1, decided 2026-11-08 by Jonathan: option C, so this slice is in scope.
* Uses the patch from F1.7 and the bridge from F1.13. sACN (ANSI E1.31) and Art-Net are UDP protocols carrying 512-channel DMX universes.

## Scope

1. `DmxOutput` transport layer in the show bridge for sACN (multicast and unicast, priority, source name) and Art-Net (ArtDmx unicast), written on plain `dgram` without a new dependency.
2. Looks: a `Look` record per event (fixture ids with intensity and, for colour-mixing fixtures, colour from the GDTF mode's channel map) and cues whose target is a look with a fade time. Simple intensity and colour only; no effects engine, no moving-light programming.
3. Output engine in the bridge: frame rate 30 to 44 Hz, crossfades between looks, highest-takes-precedence merging off; a blackout-safe `show.stopAll` that fades to a configured safe look.
4. Safety: output only while armed; on heartbeat loss hold the last look (configurable to fade to safe), never jump to full.
5. Actions: `look.create`, `look.update`, `look.delete`, `look.preview` (on screen only), plus `cue.fire` targets of type look.
6. Screen: Looks (fixture grid with intensity and colour, preview) with projection and bound controls.

## Acceptance criteria

* A capture of sACN and Art-Net packets matches the protocol layouts for a 3-universe show.
* A 2 second fade between two looks produces a monotonic ramp at the configured frame rate.
* Disarming or heartbeat loss behaves as configured and never outputs full.
* Screen passes the unbound-control check and axe.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 house rules (fade maths pure TypeScript); every operation is an inventory action with one permission check, audit and change record; UI from Rambo-UI, WCAG 2.2 AA; behind PostHog flag `f1-show-control-dmx` with default off; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; whitelabel ASCII copy; people docs and ai-docs in the same commit; ships to main with `node --run check` results here.

## Done signal

Merged with packet, fade and safety tests green and a test against a real sACN node recorded here.

## Blockers

F1.7 (<issue id="ccbe20c9-21c6-40f2-b50f-cd15ce876497" label="EVE-203" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-203/f17-build-lighting-gdtf-fixture-library-fixture-modes-and-dmx-patch" />), F1.13.

issues.title: F1.15 Build event templates and cloning: reuse phases, departments, plans and run-of-show skeletons with date shifting
issues.description:
## Goal

An organiser starts a new event from a past one or a saved template (a tour date, a yearly festival, a standard conference) and gets its phases, departments, plans, cue lists and run-of-show skeleton with every date shifted, in one step.

## Context

* Parent: <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" /> sections 4 (`event.clone`, `event.saveAsTemplate`), 5 (EventTemplate, EventSeries production package).
* For a tour, the EventSeries production package is a template every date in the series starts from.

## Scope

1. Table `event_template` (org-wide: name, snapshot of selected parts, day-0 relative offsets for all times).
2. Actions: `event.saveAsTemplate` (choose parts: phases, spaces, departments, documents, plans, cue lists, run of show, requirements), `event.clone` (from an event or a template, new day 0, new venue optional), `template.list`, `template.delete`.
3. Cloning rules: ids are new; references to other sets (F4 parties, F5 venue, F6 products) are kept; people (TeamMembers), itineraries, show runs, sign-offs and published versions are never copied; rigging sign-offs start void.
4. Large clones run as a durable job (<issue id="a626308a-598f-41ba-accd-4004cbbd9932" label="EVE-54" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow" /> pattern) so a closed app does not leave a half-copied event; the job is idempotent on retry.
5. Agent: "make next year's festival from this one, two weeks later, without the second stage" through the same actions.
6. Screen: a clone dialog on the Event overview and a Templates list, with projections and bound controls.

## Acceptance criteria

* Cloning a 3 phase, 2 space event with a run of show and 2 cue lists shifts every time by the chosen offset, including across a daylight-saving change.
* No TeamMember, itinerary, show run or sign-off is copied; sign-offs on the copy are void.
* Interrupting a clone and retrying produces exactly one complete event.
* Screen passes the unbound-control check and axe.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 house rules (date shifting is pure TypeScript); every operation is an inventory action with one permission check, audit and change record; UI from Rambo-UI, WCAG 2.2 AA; behind PostHog flag `f1-events-core`; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; whitelabel ASCII copy; people docs and ai-docs in the same commit; ships to main with `node --run check` results here.

## Done signal

Merged with shift, exclusion and retry tests green.

## Blockers

F1.1 (<issue id="43e4e4e4-42e9-4d64-8201-aa65787fe66c" label="EVE-166" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-166/f11-build-the-event-record-event-eventseries-phase-space-team-and" />), F1.3 (<issue id="cb0f80d4-48f4-4e2c-8957-26f36f9a838f" label="EVE-169" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-169/f13-build-the-run-of-show-segments-fixed-and-relative-timing" />), F1.5, F1.6, <issue id="a626308a-598f-41ba-accd-4004cbbd9932" label="EVE-54" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow" />.

issues.title: F14.14 Site templates and brand themes
issues.description:
## Goal

Organisations start from good event, venue and vendor templates, keep every site on brand through their brand kit, and save their own sites as reusable templates for the next event.

## Context

* Parent: <issue id="d6f1d3a2-12a8-474b-abae-aa29b394d45d" label="EVE-111" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-111/f14-website-builder-and-in-app-customisation" /> sections 4 (`templates.*`), 5 (Template) and 13 (no paid marketplace).
* Brand kits (colours, type, logo) come from <issue id="1d65d374-8d06-4d69-a9c6-f3b66d565b47" label="EVE-30" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-30/port-data-widgets-saved-dashboards-and-brand-kits" /> and feed Rambo-UI theming; site blocks read only theme tokens, never raw colours, so switching kit restyles a site and keeps contrast checks valid.
* F5 directory profiles use a locked template where only some blocks are editable by the vendor or venue.

## Scope

1. Template = a site snapshot without tenant data: pages, block trees with bindings expressed as slots ("the site's Event") rather than record ids, menus, SEO defaults, required brand tokens.
2. Platform templates at launch: single-day event, multi-day festival, conference with tracks, venue, vendor profile, organisation home. Each passes the F14.10 publish checks with sample data.
3. `templates.apply`: create a draft site from a template, binding its slots to chosen records (for example an Event) and the org's default brand kit.
4. `templates.saveFromSite`: org-scoped template from an existing site, stripping record ids into slots and removing form submissions and personal data.
5. Theme tokens: map brand kit to Rambo-UI tokens (colour roles, type scale, radius, spacing); a contrast check runs when a kit is applied and warns before publish.
6. Locked templates for F5 profiles: per-block `editableBy` (owner org, listed vendor) honoured by `pages.blocks.*`.
7. Template gallery screen with live previews.

## Acceptance criteria

* Applying the festival template to an Event yields a draft that passes publish checks with no edits.
* Switching brand kit restyles every block; a kit with failing contrast shows the warning and blocks publish until fixed.
* A saved org template applied to a second Event binds to it with no reference to the first Event's id (test).
* A vendor can edit only unlocked blocks on their F5 profile page (test on UI and MCP).

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; WCAG 2.2 AA; behind `f14-sites`; template content whitelabel and ASCII only; no new dependency without approval here; ships to main per the AGENTS.md delivery exception with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged with the six platform templates published to the gallery and the acceptance tests green.

issues.title: F3.10 Build the task rule builder: when X then Y, on a generic rule engine
issues.description:
Status: Approved (2026-11-08, Jonathan chose "Approve, add a rule builder" on the <issue id="4e19a499-139f-4016-88c4-264d3a0f7c33" label="EVE-62" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-62/f3-tasks-task-lists-assignments-dependencies-and-checklists-per-event" /> decision card). Planning only until Jonathan asks for implementation.

## Goal

An organiser or department lead sets up "when this happens to a task, do that" rules without code, and the rules run reliably, under clear permissions, with an audit trail.

## Context

* Parent spec: <issue id="4e19a499-139f-4016-88c4-264d3a0f7c33" label="EVE-62" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-62/f3-tasks-task-lists-assignments-dependencies-and-checklists-per-event" />, decision 7 (B: build a rule builder in F3).
* Market check: Asana rules and ClickUp automations both offer trigger, condition, action builders on tasks (<issue id="4e19a499-139f-4016-88c4-264d3a0f7c33" label="EVE-62" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-62/f3-tasks-task-lists-assignments-dependencies-and-checklists-per-event" /> section 3). Eventiva differs in that a rule can only call inventory actions, so a rule can never do something a person or agent could not.
* Architecture (house `extendable-module-architecture`): the engine is domain-agnostic and lives in its own package; F3 registers task triggers and actions into it. F14 (customisation) later adds triggers and actions from other sets to the same engine rather than building a second one.

## Scope

 1. A `rules` package: Rule, RuleRun and RuleRunStep tables (tenant-scoped); triggers are any event registered in the <issue id="ee08644c-eb3c-4a46-aea7-745864ad4263" label="EVE-45" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change" /> inventory; actions are any inventory action from <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" /> that the registering module marks rule-safe; conditions are a typed filter over the trigger payload (field equals, in, is empty, before or after a date, changed from or to).
 2. F3 registration: triggers `task.created`, `task.updated` (with field), `task.completed`, `task.assigned`, `task.unblocked`, `task.overdue` (from <issue id="d838fcc2-59de-47d6-a932-ab003b58cbab" label="EVE-89" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-89/f36-build-task-reminders-watchers-and-notifications" /> timers), `checklist.signedOff`; rule-safe actions `task.assign`, `task.setStatus`, `task.update`, `task.create` (subtask or follow-up), `checklist.addItem`, `reminder.set`, `task.watch`, plus "notify" through <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" />. `task.delete`, `checklist.signOff` and `guest.inviteToTask` are never rule-safe.
 3. Actions `rule.create`, `rule.update`, `rule.enable`, `rule.disable`, `rule.delete`, `rule.list`, `rule.get`, `rule.preview` (dry run against the last 20 matching events, showing what would change), `rule.runs` (history).
 4. Permissions: a rule runs as its owner, with the owner's permissions checked at run time (<issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />); if the owner loses access, the rule pauses and the owner and a tenant admin are told. Creating rules needs `tasks:rules` on the list or Event; tenant admins can see and pause all rules.
 5. Approvals: an action with confirm or always approval inside a rule pauses that run and asks the owner; it never auto-approves.
 6. Reliability: runs execute server-side as durable jobs on Effect Cluster (<issue id="a626308a-598f-41ba-accd-4004cbbd9932" label="EVE-54" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow" />), at least once with an idempotency key per trigger event and rule, so a retry never applies a step twice. Loop guard: a rule's own writes carry its run id and do not re-trigger the same rule; a chain stops at depth 5 and is flagged.
 7. Offline: rules do not run on devices. A device edit triggers rules when it syncs; the device shows rule results as normal synced changes.
 8. Screens (Rambo-UI, <issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" /> projections, every control bound to a `rule.*` action): rule list per Event or list, rule editor (trigger, conditions, actions as rows; keyboard usable), preview panel, run history with per-step outcome.
 9. Agent: the agent can create and edit rules through the same actions (confirm on `rule.enable`), explain why a rule fired from `rule.runs`, and suggest a rule when it sees the same manual edit repeated.
10. Telemetry: events `rule created`, `rule enabled`, `rule run` (outcome, step count, duration, no task text); flag `tasks-rules`, default off.

## Extension points kept for F14 (<issue id="8a7a26ad-455f-4ef7-a0e4-4dc75882ccc6" label="EVE-191" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-191/f145-automations-extend-the-f3-rules-engine-across-every-feature-set" />)

F14.5 extends this engine rather than building its own, so the `rules` package design must leave room for these without a schema rewrite. They are not built here:

* Trigger and action registration from any feature set (registry keyed by module, not hard-coded to tasks).
* Step kinds beyond action: wait, approval, branch, and a budgeted agent step. RuleRunStep stores a step kind and step state so new kinds slot in; the run is a durable workflow that can pause.
* `rule.runNow` and `rule.runs.cancel` actions.
* A registration check that refuses protected actions (for example F1 `show.arm`, `rigging.signOff`) as rule-safe; F3 implements the check with its own never-rule-safe list so F14 only adds entries.

## Acceptance criteria

* Rule "when a task in Lighting is completed, create a follow-up task assigned to the lighting lead due 1 day later" fires once per completion, including after a runner is killed mid-run.
* A rule whose owner is demoted to crew pauses on its next run and notifies the owner and an admin.
* A rule that assigns a task to its own trigger condition does not loop; a 6-deep chain stops and is flagged.
* `rule.preview` shows the changes the rule would have made on recent events and writes nothing.
* `task.delete` cannot be chosen as a rule action through UI, HTTP or MCP.
* An offline completion triggers the rule once on sync, not on the device.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 house rules; condition evaluation is pure TypeScript; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; WCAG 2.2 AA; whitelabel copy; ships to main per the AGENTS.md delivery exception with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged to main with the once-only, permission-pause, loop-guard and preview tests green, and the rule-safe action list posted here.

## Blockers

<issue id="d63643eb-423b-4502-b0a5-e4b99c887f54" label="EVE-64" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-64/f31-build-task-lists-and-tasks-as-synced-records-with-actions" /> (F3.1), <issue id="b092122b-6aea-4fec-b8c4-e1baf084c342" label="EVE-72" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-72/f33-build-subtasks-and-finish-to-start-dependencies-with-blocker" /> (F3.3, for `task.unblocked`), <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />, <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />, <issue id="ee08644c-eb3c-4a46-aea7-745864ad4263" label="EVE-45" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change" />, <issue id="a626308a-598f-41ba-accd-4004cbbd9932" label="EVE-54" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow" />; <issue id="d838fcc2-59de-47d6-a932-ab003b58cbab" label="EVE-89" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-89/f36-build-task-reminders-watchers-and-notifications" /> (F3.6) for the `task.overdue` trigger only.

issues.title: F5.13 Build seeded listings, claiming, claim disputes and removal requests
issues.description:
Status: Proposed (2026-11-08), part of <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> (F5 Directory and marketplace). Decision D5-1 (b) chosen by Jonathan on 2026-11-08: the directory also holds unclaimed listings seeded by Eventiva or organisers, which owners claim later.

## Goal

The directory has useful supply from day one, because Eventiva staff and organisers can add businesses that are not on Eventiva yet, and those businesses can claim, correct or remove their listing.

## Context

* <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> sections 4, 5, 9 and 11 (updated for seeded listings).
* An unclaimed listing has no accountable owner, so it carries only public business facts, is clearly labelled, and cannot take quotes, reviews or availability until claimed.
* Claiming transfers the same Listing id to the claimant tenant. F1 Event.venue_ref and F1 Space.venue_room_ref (<issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" />) stay valid across the transfer.
* Businesses only. Professionals are individuals, so they are never seeded (UK GDPR; they publish their own profile with consent through F5.3).

## Scope

1. Listing fields: ownership (claimed, unclaimed), seededBy (platform or organiser tenant id), seedSource (manual entry, public website given by the seeder), lastCheckedAt. Unclaimed listings live in a platform directory tenant scope.
2. Allowed fields on an unclaimed listing: name, kind (vendor or venue only), categories, address and point, website, public business phone and email, venue rooms with capacities from the venue's own published material. No media except a logo or photo the business published itself with a source link, no offerings or prices, no reviews, no availability.
3. Actions:
   * `directory.seed.create` and `.update`: platform:seed (Eventiva staff), or an organiser with enquiry:write. Organiser seeds go to moderation (F5.3) before they are public; the organiser can use them privately straight away.
   * `directory.claim.request`: a signed-in tenant asks to claim, with evidence. Automatic path: an email confirmation sent to an address on the listing's website domain (`directory.claim.verifyDomain`). Manual path: documents for a moderator.
   * `directory.claim.decide` (platform:moderate): approve transfers ownership, sets organisationRef to the claimant's F4 Organisation, and moves the listing to pending verification (F5.3 still applies before it shows as a claimed listing); reject with a statement of reasons.
   * `directory.claim.dispute`: another tenant contests a claim or a completed transfer once; a second moderator decides; the transfer and reversal are audited.
   * `directory.seed.removalRequest`: anyone (anonymous with the HumanCheck port) asks to remove or correct an unclaimed listing; removal for a business that asks is honoured within 30 days and its name goes on a do-not-seed list.
4. Enquiries to an unclaimed listing (F5.7): the organiser is told it is unclaimed; Eventiva sends one claim invitation email through <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" /> to the listing's public business email, carrying the brief summary without the organiser's contact details, with an unsubscribe that adds the address to a suppression list (PECR soft rules for business addresses). The enquiry recipient stays in `awaiting claim` until claimed, then becomes a normal recipient. At most 3 invitations per listing per 30 days.
5. Staleness: an unclaimed listing not refreshed or claimed for 12 months is unpublished automatically; the seeder is told.
6. Public label "Unclaimed listing: details from public sources, not checked by the business" and a "Is this your business?" claim entry point on listing detail (F5.5).
7. Ranking: an unclaimed listing ranks below a claimed one at equal relevance; this is listed on the ranking parameters page (F5.4).
8. No scraping and no bulk import from third-party directories (terms and database right). A licensed bulk dataset needs Jonathan's approval on this issue first.
9. Sub-flag `directory-seeded-listings`, default off.

## Acceptance criteria

* An unclaimed listing rejects offering, price, review and availability writes with typed errors.
* Domain-email claim: a confirmation from an address on the listing's domain approves the claim end to end in a test; a mismatched domain falls back to manual review.
* After transfer the Listing id is unchanged and an F1 Event referencing it still resolves (integration test with a fixture Event).
* A dispute reverses a transfer when decided against the first claimant, with audit rows for both moves.
* A removal request removes the listing and blocks re-seeding of the same name and domain (test).
* Invitation emails respect the per-listing cap and the suppression list (test).

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; no scraping; no new dependency or data vendor without Jonathan approving it on this issue; whitelabel ASCII copy; ships to main per the AGENTS.md delivery exception with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged with tests green, the seeding and removal policy in the people docs, and the public label text reviewed against the CMA guidance on misleading information.

## Blockers

F5.1 (listing model), F5.3 (moderation and verification), F5.7 (enquiries), <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" /> (email), F5.4 and F5.5 for the ranking rule and the public claim entry point.

issues.title: F5.14 Build quote payments with commission deducted at source
issues.description:
Status: Proposed (2026-11-08), part of <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> (F5 Directory and marketplace). Jonathan asked on 2026-11-08 to add commission, and chose D5-6 (b) on the decision card the same day: commission is deducted at source from organiser payments through F9 split payments.

## Goal

An organiser pays the vendor for an accepted quote inside Eventiva, the vendor receives the payment less Eventiva's agreed commission automatically, and Eventiva never holds the money itself.

## Context

* <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> sections 4, 5, 8, 11 and 15 (D5-6 b).
* Accepted quotes come from F5.8 (<issue id="f08bafe4-f32d-4906-9e87-5d69df56d6a0" label="EVE-124" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-124/f58-build-quotes-quote-comparison-and-the-acceptance-handoff-to-the" />). The commission base is each payment's amount excluding VAT.
* F9 decided connected accounts (<issue id="7d939472-20ba-4512-b231-c0f04c05574c" label="EVE-107" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-107/f9-online-and-in-person-sales-storefront-point-of-sale-orders-payments" /> D2): every tenant and vendor is its own merchant on the payment provider through the PaymentGateway port (F9.3, <issue id="382cab34-de6b-4524-8a47-241353c76b2b" label="EVE-174" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-174/f93-build-the-payment-gateway-port-and-online-card-payments" />). F9.12 (<issue id="05f45c5a-d89d-44e3-b726-e3a04db95a21" label="EVE-223" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-223/f912-build-vendor-sales-at-events-with-split-payments" />) builds split payments, SplitRules and connected-account onboarding; F9.8 (<issue id="cc848306-1827-4682-a18a-e5c255970dd3" label="EVE-215" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-215/f98-build-refunds-cancellations-exchanges-and-disputes" />) builds refunds and disputes. This issue reuses them and does not build a second payment path.
* Money model: the vendor is merchant of record; the organiser pays the vendor's connected account; Eventiva's commission is taken as the platform fee on the same charge. Funds sit with the regulated provider and the vendor, never in an Eventiva balance, so Eventiva does not hold client money (to be confirmed against the chosen provider's terms on <issue id="382cab34-de6b-4524-8a47-241353c76b2b" label="EVE-174" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-174/f93-build-the-payment-gateway-port-and-online-card-payments" />).
* Unclaimed listings (F5.13) cannot take payments; a vendor must be claimed, verified (F5.3), onboarded as a connected account, and have accepted commission terms.

## Scope

 1. CommissionPlan (platform scope, versioned): rate in basis points, optional minimum and cap per engagement, categories, effective from. Default plan plus optional per-tenant plans. The rate lives in this record, not in an environment variable; tests use 5 percent.
 2. CommissionTerms: `directory.commission.acceptTerms` (listing:publish, confirm) records plan version, who and when; plain-language terms, 15 days notice before a change applies (P2B).
 3. Payment schedule on the quote: the vendor sets it in the quote editor (F5.8): deposit percent or amount with due date, balance due date, or single payment. Shown to the organiser before acceptance.
 4. PaymentRequest per schedule line, created by the F5.8 handoff on acceptance: amount, due date, status (due, paid, overdue, refunded, cancelled). `directory.payment.pay` (quote:accept on the organiser side, always approval) opens F9 checkout against the vendor's connected account with a SplitRule of the platform commission. Card and bank transfer methods as F9.3 supports them.
 5. CommissionCharge per captured payment: payment id, base, rate, amount, plan version, status (collected, refunded, adjusted). Created from the gateway capture event, idempotent per payment.
 6. Refunds and cancellations: through F9.8; commission is refunded in proportion to the refunded amount unless the plan says commission on the deposit is non-refundable (default refundable). A dispute or chargeback on a payment reverses the commission share the same way.
 7. Off-platform settlement: if the organiser and vendor agree to settle outside Eventiva, the vendor records it with `directory.payment.markSettledOffPlatform` (reason, organiser confirmation on the thread); no commission is charged on it, the count shows in platform reporting only, and messages are never scanned for off-platform deals.
 8. Monthly commission statement and VAT invoice to each vendor for the commission collected (`directory.commission.statement`, listing:read), issued from the platform operator's own tenant with F11 sales invoices (<issue id="2ef1ed05-1c6a-4b1b-9b1c-04331398cac8" label="EVE-126" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-126/f114-build-sales-invoices-credit-notes-and-receivables" />) and VAT codes (<issue id="2dd28829-f5f7-4a45-bbf6-42592282e675" label="EVE-158" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-158/f117-build-vat-codes-vat-returns-and-mtd-submission" />), marked as already paid by deduction.
 9. Reminders: due and overdue payment notices to the organiser through <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" />; the agent can explain a payment or commission line and prepare a payment, but `directory.payment.pay` always waits for the organiser's approval.
10. Screens: organiser payments panel on the quote and the F1 Event (schedule, due, paid); vendor payments and commission screen (payouts, commission, statements). Organisers see what they pay, never the vendor's commission.
11. Platform finance role `platform:commission`: set plans, approve adjustments, write off.
12. Telemetry: directory_payment_requested, directory_payment_paid, directory_payment_refunded, directory_commission_collected, directory_payment_settled_off_platform (amount buckets only).
13. Sub-flag `directory-payments`, default off.

## Acceptance criteria

* In the fake gateway, a deposit and a balance payment on one accepted quote each pay the vendor's connected account less the plan commission, with one CommissionCharge per capture even when the capture event is delivered twice.
* A 50 percent refund of the balance returns 50 percent of that payment's commission; a chargeback reverses the full share.
* A vendor without a connected account, verification or accepted terms cannot be paid; the organiser sees a clear reason and the quote can still be accepted.
* An organiser principal cannot read commission records (negative test); an agent cannot complete `directory.payment.pay` without approval on screen and through MCP.
* Ranking does not use commission or payment data (property test over F5.4 ranking inputs).
* Sandbox evidence with the real adapter once <issue id="382cab34-de6b-4524-8a47-241353c76b2b" label="EVE-174" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-174/f93-build-the-payment-gateway-port-and-online-card-payments" /> has an approved provider.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; provider SDK only inside the F9 integration package; no Eventiva-held balances; no new dependency or vendor account without Jonathan approving it on <issue id="382cab34-de6b-4524-8a47-241353c76b2b" label="EVE-174" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-174/f93-build-the-payment-gateway-port-and-online-card-payments" /> or this issue; whitelabel ASCII copy; ships to main per the AGENTS.md delivery exception with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged with tests green, sandbox evidence pasted here, the commission and payment terms page in the people docs, and the F9 thread told the quote-payment contract.

## Blockers

F5.8 (<issue id="f08bafe4-f32d-4906-9e87-5d69df56d6a0" label="EVE-124" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-124/f58-build-quotes-quote-comparison-and-the-acceptance-handoff-to-the" />), F9.3 gateway (<issue id="382cab34-de6b-4524-8a47-241353c76b2b" label="EVE-174" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-174/f93-build-the-payment-gateway-port-and-online-card-payments" />), F9.12 splits and onboarding (<issue id="05f45c5a-d89d-44e3-b726-e3a04db95a21" label="EVE-223" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-223/f912-build-vendor-sales-at-events-with-split-payments" />), F9.8 refunds (<issue id="cc848306-1827-4682-a18a-e5c255970dd3" label="EVE-215" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-215/f98-build-refunds-cancellations-exchanges-and-disputes" />), F11.4 invoices (<issue id="2ef1ed05-1c6a-4b1b-9b1c-04331398cac8" label="EVE-126" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-126/f114-build-sales-invoices-credit-notes-and-receivables" />), F11 VAT codes (<issue id="2dd28829-f5f7-4a45-bbf6-42592282e675" label="EVE-158" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-158/f117-build-vat-codes-vat-returns-and-mtd-submission" />), F5.3 verification.

issues.title: F10.12 Venue and building plans: arenas, halls, custom structures and festival builds
issues.description:
## Goal

Site maps work just as well for an arena, a conference centre, a theatre, a custom-built structure or a festival build as for an outdoor field. Organisers draw or import multi-level buildings with walls, rooms, doors, stairs, seating bowls and services, with or without a street map underneath.

## Context

* Parent <issue id="f8432c08-24bb-4690-a3e1-16ed79977eee" label="EVE-108" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-108/f10-interactive-site-maps" />. Jonathan, 2026-11-08: "The site maps need to fully work for things like arenas and custom buildings or festivals or such. Its not just a street map."
* Engine is MapLibre (D-F10-1). Every Site already has a site-local frame in metres (<issue id="9b8adbfb-05a9-4f10-9c60-baa5bfcfd4fa" label="EVE-146" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-146/f101-sites-levels-base-layers-and-calibration" />), so a building needs no geography. At venue scale (under 2 km) a frame anchored to any point has negligible distortion, so MapLibre can render pure plans with the basemap switched off. <issue id="75206124-f123-452e-baa0-2c8ec3d42e59" label="EVE-120" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-120/f100-spike-map-engine-with-offline-tiles-and-yjs-bound-editing-on-expo" /> must prove this plan-only mode (see its scope).
* F1 (<issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" />) owns Space and DesignElement; a room or zone here is geometry that an F1 Space links to by feature id. F8 owns seats (<issue id="3682ce53-f6e7-41d9-a911-2fb44d73f7c6" label="EVE-211" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-211/f811-build-the-seat-map-editor-and-reserved-seating-in-f8" />) and may use these plans as a read-only backdrop.

## Scope

1. Site kinds (field on Site): `outdoor` (geo-referenced, basemap on by default), `venue` (building or campus, levels, basemap optional), `plan` (no geography at all: blank canvas in metres, for custom structures, festival builds on an unsurveyed field, or a design before the site is chosen). A `plan` site can be anchored to a real location later without moving any feature.
2. Building elements as feature kinds with metric attributes: wall (thickness, height), room or area (name, use, area, occupancy limit), door or opening (clear width, fire exit flag, direction), column, stair, ramp, lift and escalator (as vertical connectors linking two or more levels), fixed seating section and arena bowl (rows and tiers as geometry only), stage, rigging point and grid (position and reference to an F1 DesignElement; no load calculation), service point (power, water, data, gas), loading dock and vehicle access.
3. Drawing tools in the editor (extends <issue id="c2c22f6e-0703-449c-a01d-0a6552d1d9fc" label="EVE-178" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-178/f103-map-editor-screen-with-screen-awareness" />): wall tool with snapping and auto-joined corners, room from enclosed walls, door placed into a wall, orthogonal and angle snapping, dimensions and offset input by keyboard, copy a level to a new level.
4. Levels: level switcher with ghosted level below, vertical connectors drawn across levels, mezzanines and partial levels, level heights.
5. Nested plans: any footprint feature (a marquee, a building, a container stage) can open its own interior plan as a child map with its own levels, so a festival site holds detailed tent interiors and an arena holds its back-of-house.
6. Venue templates in the starter library: arena (bowl, floor, concourse, back of house), theatre (stage, fly tower footprint, stalls, circle), exhibition and conference hall (grid of stands), marquee interiors, festival arena enclosure.
7. Imports, as reference or as editable features: DXF layers mapped to walls, doors and rooms by a layer mapping step; IMDF (the open indoor mapping JSON format) imported to levels, units, openings and amenities; PDF floor plans as calibrated reference (<issue id="9b8adbfb-05a9-4f10-9c60-baa5bfcfd4fa" label="EVE-146" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-146/f101-sites-levels-base-layers-and-calibration" />). No new dependency without approval here.
8. Checks across levels (extends <issue id="0a770823-74c2-43b8-849a-45631c15d9e5" label="EVE-183" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-183/f105-measurements-zones-routes-and-rule-checks" />): exit width per room from its doors, travel routes through doors and vertical connectors to exits, occupancy per room against its limit, step-free route availability between levels.
9. Public and crew maps (<issue id="c67f094b-8c19-4427-8672-51c0648b44fd" label="EVE-202" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-202/f108-offline-map-packs-and-the-crew-map" />, <issue id="cadefb17-f505-4ddc-9238-ad3d83926bf3" label="EVE-207" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-207/f1010-public-attendee-map-and-website-embed" />) show levels and indoor routes: "find the nearest accessible toilet on this level".

## Acceptance criteria

* A `plan` site with no basemap renders, edits and measures correctly on web and Android, and can be anchored to a real location later with all features kept.
* A three-level arena fixture (bowl, concourse, back of house) is drawn with walls, rooms, doors, stairs and lifts; the agent answers "how many exits does level 2 have and what is their total width" from the actions.
* An IMDF sample venue and a DXF floor plan import to editable levels.
* A marquee on a festival site opens its interior plan, and its interior features appear in the site quantities.
* Cross-level checks flag a room whose exit width is below the rule set, and a level with no step-free route.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3; geometry pure TypeScript in shared contracts; WCAG 2.2 AA for every new tool, including keyboard drawing; no new dependency without approval here; ships to main with check results; flag `f10-site-maps`.

## Done signal

Merged with the arena fixture, imports and checks green, and recordings on web and Android attached here.

## Blockers

<issue id="9b8adbfb-05a9-4f10-9c60-baa5bfcfd4fa" label="EVE-146" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-146/f101-sites-levels-base-layers-and-calibration" /> (frame and levels), <issue id="82fab111-6d01-4616-85c7-1e4ff88ca469" label="EVE-152" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-152/f102-site-maps-and-layers-as-yjs-documents-with-a-feature-record" /> (layer documents), <issue id="c2c22f6e-0703-449c-a01d-0a6552d1d9fc" label="EVE-178" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-178/f103-map-editor-screen-with-screen-awareness" /> (editor). It feeds <issue id="0a770823-74c2-43b8-849a-45631c15d9e5" label="EVE-183" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-183/f105-measurements-zones-routes-and-rule-checks" /> (cross-level checks) and <issue id="cadefb17-f505-4ddc-9238-ad3d83926bf3" label="EVE-207" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-207/f1010-public-attendee-map-and-website-embed" /> (indoor public maps).

issues.title: F13.10 Build performance reviews, goals and feedback
issues.description:
## Goal

Managers and workers run regular reviews, set and track goals, and give feedback after each event, so performance history sits with the worker record and informs future crewing, for employees and for freelancers who work repeatedly.

## Context

* Parent: <issue id="253839bc-c987-416b-92ea-206c9e9e8d2e" label="EVE-80" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-80/f13-human-resources-worker-records-onboarding-qualifications-and-leave" />, decision 7 approved by Jonathan on 2026-11-08 as option (b): reviews are part of F13.
* Builds on Worker and reporting lines (<issue id="7cc5c061-dd2d-4963-8e03-f0175a4f12b9" label="EVE-98" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-98/f131-build-worker-records-engagements-and-organisation-structure" />) and sensitive-data masking (<issue id="636f7592-553b-41f2-adb0-9a336d0188e3" label="EVE-116" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-116/f132-build-the-sensitive-profile-with-field-masking-reveal-audit-and" />). Review text is a collaborative document attached to the review record (<issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" />); cycles are durable scheduled runs (<issue id="a626308a-598f-41ba-accd-4004cbbd9932" label="EVE-54" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow" />); reminders through <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" />. Post-event feedback links to an F1 Event and the F1 TeamMember who worked it.

## Scope

1. Tables ReviewTemplate (versioned: sections, rating scales, questions), ReviewCycle (name, audience filter, period, deadlines), Review (worker, reviewer, status draft, self-review, manager review, calibrated, shared, acknowledged), Goal (owner, description, measure, due, progress, status, optional link to F3 tasks), Feedback (giver, subject worker, optional F1 Event, ratings, comment, visibility: private to HR and manager, or shared with the worker).
2. Actions: `hr.reviewTemplates.create` / `.update`; `hr.reviewCycles.create` / `.launch` (confirm; creates one Review per worker in the audience); `hr.reviews.submitSelf`, `.submitManager`, `.calibrate` (HR, confirm), `.share` (confirm), `.acknowledge` (worker only, human-only); `hr.goals.create`, `.update`, `.updateProgress`, `.close`; `hr.feedback.give`, `hr.feedback.list`; `hr.eventFeedback.request` (asks the crew chief of an F1 Event for short feedback on each TeamMember after the Event ends).
3. Permissions: worker sees own reviews once shared and own goals; manager sees direct reports; HR sees all; peers can give feedback but never read it; supplying agencies see nothing. Grants hr:reviews:*, hr:goals:*, hr:feedback:\*.
4. Review content is personal data: masked in projections for anyone without access, excluded from telemetry and agent memory (<issue id="636f7592-553b-41f2-adb0-9a336d0188e3" label="EVE-116" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-116/f132-build-the-sensitive-profile-with-field-masking-reveal-audit-and" /> rules), included in the subject export and covered by a retention default (6 years after the engagement ends, configurable).
5. Screens `hr.reviews` (cycle board), `hr.review` (collaborative editor with sections), `me.reviews`, `me.goals`, with projections and every control bound to its action.
6. Agent: drafts a review summary from goals, feedback and post-event ratings for the manager to edit; suggests goals; chases overdue reviews. It never submits a manager review or acknowledges a review for anyone (human-only), and never writes ratings itself. Behind flag `hr-agent-review-drafting`, default off.
7. Repeat-freelancer view: average post-event ratings and the last three feedback comments visible to crew coordinators only if the tenant enables it (setting, default off), so F2 can prefer well-rated crew without exposing review text.
8. Telemetry: `hr_review_cycle_launched`, `hr_review_submitted`, `hr_review_shared`, `hr_goal_closed`, `hr_feedback_given` (no content).

## Acceptance criteria

* Launching a cycle for 20 workers creates 20 reviews; self and manager reviews submit; HR calibrates and shares; the worker acknowledges; every step is audited.
* A peer who gave feedback cannot read it back, and a crew coordinator cannot read any review text (negative tests on UI, HTTP, MCP and ACP).
* After an F1 Event ends, the crew chief receives one feedback request per TeamMember; submitted ratings appear on each worker's record.
* The agent drafts a summary that the manager edits, and is refused with `HumanOnlyAction` when asked to submit or acknowledge.
* No review text appears in spans, events or agent memory in a full test run.

## Constraints

Effect-TS v3 house rules; no zod; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; behind `hr-module` and its own flag `hr-reviews`, default off; ship to main per the AGENTS.md delivery exception with `node --run check` results pasted here.

## Done signal

Merged to main with a recorded review cycle (actions, approvals, audit rows) linked here.

## Blockers

<issue id="7cc5c061-dd2d-4963-8e03-f0175a4f12b9" label="EVE-98" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-98/f131-build-worker-records-engagements-and-organisation-structure" /> (F13.1), <issue id="636f7592-553b-41f2-adb0-9a336d0188e3" label="EVE-116" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-116/f132-build-the-sensitive-profile-with-field-masking-reveal-audit-and" /> (F13.2), <issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" />, <issue id="a626308a-598f-41ba-accd-4004cbbd9932" label="EVE-54" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow" />, <issue id="9aae6a50-4a43-4327-ae6a-51d18bc69b35" label="EVE-24" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-24/port-notifications-messaging-channels-and-transactional-email" />; F1 Event and TeamMember (<issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" />) for post-event feedback.

issues.title: S4 follow-up: run the PowerSync and Yjs device test on iOS
issues.description:
## Goal

Confirm the chosen sync engine (PowerSync with Yjs, decided on <issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" />) works on a real iPhone or the iOS simulator, as it already does on web, Expo web and Android.

## Context

* Decision and evidence: <issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" />. Android passed 6 of 6 on 2026-11-09; web and Expo web passed 7 of 7.
* iOS was never built or run, because it needs a Mac with Xcode.
* Spike app and runbook: project files `eve-s4-sync/expo/` and `eve-s4-sync/RUNBOOK-device-test.md`. Local backend: `eve-s4-sync/local-stack/` (docker compose: Postgres 16, PowerSync service 1.27.2, the Node spike backend).
* The app is an Expo SDK 58 development build (not Expo Go) using `@powersync/react-native` with op-sqlite and Yjs. lib0 needs a webcrypto provider on React Native; the spike shims it in `metro.config.js`.

## Work

1. On a Mac with Xcode, run `npx expo prebuild --platform ios` and build the spike app for a device or simulator.
2. Start `local-stack` on the same machine or network and point the app at it. iOS blocks plain HTTP by default, so allow it for the dev host only (App Transport Security exception), as `usesCleartextTraffic` does on Android.
3. Run the six runbook checks with the iOS app as bob and Expo web in a browser as alice: live sync, offline edit queue, concurrent edits, queue survives app restart, convergence, revocation.
4. While on the Mac, also open the Expo web build in Safari and run the same checks, since Safari/WebKit storage rules are the main web risk and have not been tested.

## Acceptance

A comment here with the device or simulator model, iOS version, Xcode version, the result of each check, and any build changes needed. If a check fails, say which and why, and whether it changes the <issue id="60101c56-d4e4-4e4f-b7c8-b4c40f44ada0" label="EVE-17" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and" /> decision.

## Out of scope

Neon logical replication (separate, still untested), production client code, App Store distribution.

## Done signal

The comment above, with all six checks passing on iOS, or a failure written up with a proposed fix.

## Blocker

Needs Jonathan at a Mac with Xcode. Does not block <issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" /> starting, but <issue id="a1348819-43cc-4005-8e8d-a896a761af03" label="EVE-51" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and" /> cannot claim iOS support until this passes.

issues.title: Archive the manual pre-Amp packages and create a clean package tree
issues.description:
## Final reset decision from Jonathan - 2026-11-10

Do not preserve any manually created Eventiva package, test, coverage, declaration-doc, Nx or workspace tooling as active infrastructure merely because current CI references it. The whole manual workspace is being reset. Archive the historical originals under Examples/eventiva-before-amp as inspectable reference, then remove their active workspace/CI/config references. This includes Kafka and the manual test-repo and cluster-tooling/dts-docs infrastructure identified in the inventory. Do not point active checks into Examples and do not recreate replacement tooling in <issue id="6b614c3b-413d-4d91-939b-d1792fefe210" label="EVE-242" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-242/archive-the-manual-pre-amp-packages-and-create-a-clean-package-tree" />.

The replacement sequence is explicit: <issue id="6b614c3b-413d-4d91-939b-d1792fefe210" label="EVE-242" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-242/archive-the-manual-pre-amp-packages-and-create-a-clean-package-tree" /> leaves a minimal clean repository after the archive; a following issue fully enrols Eventiva in Smartcloud and applies current house-generated guidance, governance, workflows and repository configuration; a final following issue scaffolds a fresh Nx/PNPM/Expo/React Native/Effect workspace and fresh testing/tooling from current specifications and house preferences. Old tests may inform requirements but do not constrain the new architecture by default. Preserve Git history and do not delete the historical archive.

## Goal

Give Amp workers a clean production package tree while preserving Jonathan's functional manual implementation as clearly labelled reference material.

## Context

Jonathan clarified on 2026-11-10 that the current implementations under packages/cluster-compose, packages/cluster-tooling, packages/core, packages/databases (including pg), packages/extensions and packages/platforms were written manually before the Amp-led rebuild. They are useful, functional evidence, but must not be treated as the production baseline. Existing Examples/packages-old is a different snapshot and must not be overwritten or silently merged.

Archive the manual implementation under Examples/eventiva-before-amp. Use git-aware moves so history remains reviewable. Start from a fresh clean checkout of current main, not the stopped <issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" /> worker's uncommitted tree.

## Work

1. Inventory every active packages/\* project and all root/workspace references before moving anything.
2. Move the confirmed manual implementation directories named above to Examples/eventiva-before-amp/, preserving their relative layout and documentation.
3. Investigate packages/integrations and packages/test-repo separately. Do not assume they are disposable: retain them unless repository evidence clearly establishes they are part of the same manual implementation, or stop and ask Jonathan.
4. Leave a clean production packages/ location ready for the new architecture, with only minimal tracking/readme material if necessary. Do not scaffold the replacement architecture in this issue.
5. Update pnpm/Nx/TypeScript/lint/test/docs/config references so archived examples are not discovered as active workspace projects, built, published or used by new workers.
6. Add a prominent README in the archive: functional historical reference only; inspect for behaviour and lessons; do not copy as the implementation baseline. Point new workers to <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> and current AGENTS.md.
7. Do not delete either legacy snapshot, tests or history. Do not weaken gates merely to accommodate archived code.

## Validation

* A fresh workspace/project discovery shows no archived package as active.
* Root setup and all checks that remain applicable to the clean skeleton are run and reported honestly; distinguish pre-existing gate problems.
* rg checks show no production configuration importing the archived paths.
* git status and diff demonstrate moves rather than destructive deletion where possible.

## Out of scope

Rebuilding core packages, copying legacy implementation into new packages, changing architectural decisions, dependency additions, or resolving <issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" /> itself.

## Escalation

Stop before moving an ambiguous package, overwriting Examples/packages-old, discarding test infrastructure, or bypassing a house rule. Record the exact ambiguity for Jonathan.

## Done signal

The archive and clean production package tree are ready for review, with validation evidence on this issue. Do not claim <issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" /> is unblocked until this cleanup is accepted.
