issues.title: Define provider-neutral connected-account invoicing and settlement orchestration
issues.description:
Status: Approved direction (Jonathan, 2026-11-12). Planning only: no implementation, provider agreement, account provisioning, or SDK dependency is authorised by this issue.

## Goal

Eventiva creates supplier-owned invoices, presents buyer payment methods, deducts Eventiva commission, mirrors settlements, and manages contractual fulfilment through one provider-neutral action model. Stripe Connect is the first adapter; Airwallex, GoCardless, and later providers must be replaceable without rewriting domain, UI, agent, audit, or accounting logic.

Full specification: [Provider-neutral marketplace payments](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/provider-neutral-marketplace-payments-8bc6fe8e-e18a-4286-8c97-219ad8e1c0ca>)

## Binding decisions

* Supplier remains seller/merchant of record through a provider-managed connected account.
* Eventiva is non-custodial: it never stores payment credentials, holds customer money, issues e-money, or presents itself as escrow.
* Stripe Connect direct-charge invoices are the first implementation. Eventiva creates them in the supplier connected-account context and takes an application fee.
* Destination/separate charges are not the default because formal disputes debit Eventiva's platform balance first.
* Eventiva owns canonical invoice, payment instruction, commission, fulfilment, refund, dispute, reconciliation, and audit records. Provider identifiers are mappings, never domain identity.
* Provider SDKs and objects stay inside integration packages behind neutral Effect services with Effect Schema contracts and typed capability errors. Domain code never branches on provider names.
* Capability discovery is per provider, merchant, country, currency, charge model, payment method, limits, refund, dispute, and payout capability. Portability does not require a lowest-common-denominator feature set.
* UI, API, MCP, ACP, webhooks, and agents use the same authorised actions. Issuing invoices, moving money, approving refunds, changing payouts, and submitting final dispute evidence require the same human approval and step-up policy across all surfaces.
* Signed webhooks are replay-protected, idempotent, retried, dead-lettered, and reconciled by provider read-back.
* No payment executes offline. Offline preparation produces drafts requiring fresh authorization and provider capability checks after reconnection.

## Required provider-neutral capabilities

1. Merchant onboarding, verification state, capabilities, disconnect/revocation.
2. Provider-scoped customer mapping from canonical Eventiva parties.
3. Invoice draft, revision, approval, issue, cancel, read-back, and externally-paid marking.
4. Payment-method discovery and provider-hosted or embedded payment sessions.
5. Commission/application fees with versioned calculation and proportional refund adjustment.
6. Refunds, disputes, evidence requirements/deadlines, settlement, payouts, and reconciliation.
7. Typed unsupported-capability outcomes rather than silent fallback.

Provider-neutral records include MerchantConnection, PaymentCustomerMapping, Invoice/InvoiceRevision, PaymentInstruction/PaymentAttempt, CommissionCharge, FulfilmentRecord, Settlement/Payout, Refund/Dispute, ProviderEventReceipt, and ReconciliationEntry.

## Core workflow

1. Supplier or authorised agent creates a canonical draft from a quote, order, event, contract, milestone, or manual entry.
2. Supplier policy controls human approval before issue.
3. Eventiva checks live merchant capabilities and creates/finalises the provider invoice under that supplier.
4. Buyer sees eligible methods for the supplier, country, currency, amount, and invoice; credentials remain with the provider.
5. Provider webhooks update local state; reconciliation resolves missed, duplicate, or reordered events.
6. Accounting receives one idempotent event for invoice, commission, fee, refund, settlement, and payout changes.

Stripe's first adapter should support eligible connected-account combinations of Invoicing, direct charges, application fees, cards, bank transfers, Pay by Bank, Bacs Direct Debit, local methods, refunds, payout state, and formal disputes. Availability is capability-driven. Bacs is asynchronous, has provider limits, and permits final indemnity claims without a fixed dispute period, so high-value invoices should prefer bank transfer or Pay by Bank where suitable.

## Fulfilment, settlement, and supplier maturity

Describe this as provider-held delayed settlement, never Eventiva escrow:

* Supplier marks an obligation or milestone fulfilled and attaches evidence.
* Buyer confirmation starts the supplier maturity delay; no buyer response permits eligibility 14 days after the contracted completion/event date when no dispute is open, with reminders first.
* A contractual dispute pauses release only where provider capabilities and agreements permit.
* Event occurrence supports but does not prove fulfilment; milestone contracts assess each accepted milestone separately.
* Every supplier starts at New. Maturity combines settled volume, completed contracts, distinct verified clients, time, fulfilment, refunds, chargebacks, disputes, verification, and compliance. Turnover alone never grants trust.

Initial calibration, kept versioned/configurable rather than hard-coded:

| Level | Qualification target | Payout policy |
| -- | -- | -- |
| New | Mandatory at onboarding; enhanced verification/provider limits | 14 days after fulfilment eligibility and slower provider payout cadence where supported |
| Established | Six months history; £50k–£100k settled; 12+ completed contracts; 2–3 distinct verified clients per qualifying month; acceptable loss/dispute rates | About seven days after fulfilment eligibility |
| Proven | Six qualifying months; £500k–£1m settled; 50+ completed contracts; around 10 distinct verified clients per qualifying month; sustained low loss/dispute rates | 72 hours after confirmation or provider's safest standard schedule |

Qualification requires target activity in at least five of six consecutive months. Maintenance uses a rolling six-month window: one missed month is grace, two gives warning/review, and three triggers proportionate demotion review. Fraud, sanctions, lapsed verification, severe disputes, or provider restrictions can pause payouts immediately. Ordinary demotion provides reasons, notice where safe, and appeal. A long-lived reliable low-turnover supplier needs an alternative evidence path.

Post-Proven Bronze/Silver/Gold or named volume badges may recognise sustained provider-verified Eventiva transaction history, but never alter payout risk, ranking, permissions, verification, or dispute treatment and never imply quality endorsement. Exact turnover is public only with supplier consent.

Eventiva contractual mediation remains separate from card, bank, Direct Debit, fraud, or provider disputes. Eventiva does not fund dispute protection at launch.

## Portability and migration

The Stripe adapter and a fake adapter must pass one conformance suite. Airwallex is a future candidate for connected multi-currency wallets, FX, global accounts, and payouts; GoCardless is a candidate for bank debit/open-banking collection where its model fits.

Switching provider routes new drafts/payments after capability validation. Historical provider mappings remain available for refunds, disputes, and reconciliation. Issued invoices and captured payments are never silently transplanted.

## Acceptance criteria

* Fake and Stripe sandbox adapters pass the same contract tests.
* One supplier-authorised invoice is drafted, approved, issued, paid, refunded, and reconciled through UI and agent surfaces using the same actions.
* At least card and one bank method work without credentials touching Eventiva.
* Sandbox evidence proves supplier merchant identity, Eventiva application fee, and liability boundaries.
* Duplicate, invalid, reordered, and missing webhooks converge to one correct result.
* Provider outage produces explicit degraded mode and never pretends money moved.
* Refunds adjust commission and accounting exactly once.
* 72-hour cooling-off, 14-day no-response eligibility, milestone release, and dispute pause are tested with a fake clock; unsupported provider holds fail safely.
* Cross-tenant access, buyer access to supplier commission/payouts, agent payment without approval, and secret/PII telemetry leakage all fail negative tests.
* Adapter replacement changes composition only; domain handlers, UI actions, invoice records, and accounting contracts remain unchanged.

## Existing ownership

Reuse rather than duplicate:

* <issue id="382cab34-de6b-4524-8a47-241353c76b2b" label="EVE-174" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-174/f93-build-the-payment-gateway-port-and-online-card-payments" /> owns the neutral payment gateway and initial online adapter.
* <issue id="cc848306-1827-4682-a18a-e5c255970dd3" label="EVE-215" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-215/f98-build-refunds-cancellations-exchanges-and-disputes" /> owns refunds and provider/payment disputes.
* <issue id="5a243280-5cb5-4b48-affd-917d0c670b89" label="EVE-222" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-222/f911-build-receipts-reconciliation-sales-reporting-and-accounting" /> owns reconciliation and accounting events.
* <issue id="7dba7530-e7b6-4259-be26-9924f9ebddcb" label="EVE-237" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-237/f514-build-quote-payments-with-commission-deducted-at-source" /> owns quote payments and marketplace commission.
* <issue id="2ef1ed05-1c6a-4b1b-9b1c-04331398cac8" label="EVE-126" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-126/f114-build-sales-invoices-credit-notes-and-receivables" /> owns canonical sales invoices and receivables.

## Out of scope

Eventiva acting as bank, payment institution, e-money issuer, escrow provider, or supplier merchant of record; reusable Eventiva-held balances; Eventiva-funded chargeback protection; final pricing before cost-to-serve evidence; provider signup or implementation in this planning issue.

issues.title: Research supplier product-catalogue coverage and bulk inventory onboarding
issues.description:
## Goal

Define a low-friction, trustworthy supplier inventory onboarding and product-catalogue enrichment strategy so a new supplier can search for a manufacturer/model by name, find the correct technical reference quickly, and bulk-load their existing stock without rebuilding every product record manually.

**Status: deferred product research / specification discovery only.** Capture the challenge and return to it after foundational module and platform design. Do not start scraping, importing, implementation or external supplier outreach from this ticket.

## Context

Eventiva's F6 product catalogue and supplier inventory feed technical equivalence (<issue id="f08bafe4-f32d-4906-9e87-5d69df56d6a0" label="EVE-124" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-124/f58-build-quotes-quote-comparison-and-the-acceptance-handoff-to-the" />), supplier recommendations (<issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" />), and supplier quote selection (<issue id="03bd23d1-9da5-4272-8f2e-0b0bf4f7f846" label="EVE-119" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-119/f57-build-cross-tenant-enquiries-rfps-and-private-message-threads" />). The shared reference product/model specification must be distinct from tenant-private supplier stock, quantities, pricing, reservations and ownership. Accurate product identity and evidence will matter before useful automatic equipment matching can be trusted. Prior plans for supplier-selectable catalogue records and controlled uploads are in <issue id="eaa9fbf7-7a3c-4c1c-9470-a76edd5316ff" label="EVE-81" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-81/f61-build-the-equipment-catalogue-products-tracking-modes-and-kits" /> and its linked decisions D6-7/D6-8/D6-9.

The key adoption hurdle: when a supplier types a brand, product name or model, they should normally find the correct existing product and its relevant manufacturer specifications immediately, rather than spending hours manually recreating equipment descriptions and dimensions. The user suggested significant catalogue research, data acquisition/web scraping (possibly Firecrawl or similar), interviews/surveys of supplier inventory tools, CSV/export-based import, and efficient team-based manual/bulk entry. Supplier-account setup, KYC and payment onboarding (e.g. Stripe connected-account requirements) are separate, later work - do not expand this ticket into payments onboarding.

## Research and design questions to resolve when resumed

1. **Product reference coverage and search.** Identify priority live-event equipment categories and manufacturers/models, canonical identifiers, version/variant/SKU distinctions, synonyms, search-as-you-type relevance, typos and duplicate/mislabelled records. Define realistic coverage and search-confidence targets, not an unsupported guarantee that all products exist.
2. **Trusted data acquisition.** Investigate manufacturer catalogues, datasheets, published APIs, licensed feeds, distributors and appropriate crawling/extraction approaches (Firecrawl is a candidate, not a chosen dependency). Assess source permission/terms, robots directives, copyright/database rights, freshness, update frequency, provenance and cost. Prefer authoritative manufacturer information where feasible; do not treat arbitrary scraped sales copy as verified technical evidence.
3. **Normalisation and validation.** Category-specific typed specifications, units, dimensions, interfaces, intended uses, accessories, model revisions, conflicting sources, evidence versioning, confidence/verification, duplicate detection, controlled supplier corrections and reconciliation. Avoid silently merging different models.
4. **Supplier ecosystem discovery.** Survey or interview representative rental/production suppliers to learn which inventory/asset/hire systems they use, what export formats and fields are available, whether APIs/connectors exist, and common data-quality issues. Do not assume any one vendor or format dominates before research.
5. **Bulk import experience.** Define CSV (and other justified exports) upload, template/sample files, column mapping, unit transforms, preview/validation, model matching, duplicates, missing values, supplier SKU mapping, kit/asset/serial versus bulk-stock distinctions, staged confirmation, partial errors, undo/idempotent re-import and import audit. Permit manual, collaborative team-assisted entry and streamlined bulk edits, not only file upload.
6. **Onboarding usability.** Compare quick find-and-add, guided bulk import, supplier self-service and multiple team-member workflows. Separate shared product references from supplier-owned quantities and calendar/availability. Track import completeness and confidence without blocking quotations when specifications remain incomplete.
7. **Agent-native parity, privacy and architecture.** Ensure all catalogue search/import/review actions are available to authorised users and agents through the common Effect-based action layer. Preserve F6 private inventory and <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> D5-16 detailed/dates-only/hidden publication controls and explicit recommendation matching opt-out. No default shared-model training of supplier-private records.

## Validation / deliverables for this future planning ticket

* A cited source/licensing and acquisition feasibility matrix, with sample verified manufacturer records across a small representative equipment set; explain coverage gaps and conflict handling.
* A supplier discovery findings summary identifying actual commonly used inventory tools, viable export formats and prioritised import patterns.
* A documented candidate data model and provenance/verification workflow showing reference product vs supplier stock identity, quantity, kit, reservation and quote mapping.
* Reviewed user journeys for search-add, team/bulk manual entry and CSV import, including invalid/duplicate rows, re-import and rollback scenarios.
* An actionable phased implementation specification with explicit acceptance metrics to be agreed from evidence (e.g. representative search hit quality, matching precision and import success), dependencies, risks and cost estimates. This planning ticket is complete when these decisions are documented and reviewed, **not** when a scraper or importer has been built.

## Out of scope

Do not execute research, scraping, supplier survey, ingestion, imports, code changes, model training, user onboarding/KYC, Stripe setup, or deployment at this stage. No assumption that every manufacturer permits scraping or that Firecrawl is definitely required. No premature importer/vendor selection.

## Escalation / decisions on resumption

Return for decisions on initial categories and manufacturer coverage, licensed/allowed data sources, target inventory software integrations, privacy and verification ownership, budget constraints, and what import quality is acceptable. Stop if proposed crawling conflicts with legal terms, if source identity cannot be verified, or if matching risks conflating supplier-private stock with public model reference data.

Related: <issue id="eaa9fbf7-7a3c-4c1c-9470-a76edd5316ff" label="EVE-81" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-81/f61-build-the-equipment-catalogue-products-tracking-modes-and-kits" /> (catalogue owner), <issue id="928dc098-5cc9-4586-88bb-50abbe03071a" label="EVE-63" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-63/f6-warehousing-and-inventory-equipment-stock-availability-purchasing" /> (inventory), <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" /> (directory), <issue id="03bd23d1-9da5-4272-8f2e-0b0bf4f7f846" label="EVE-119" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-119/f57-build-cross-tenant-enquiries-rfps-and-private-message-threads" /> (enquiries), <issue id="f08bafe4-f32d-4906-9e87-5d69df56d6a0" label="EVE-124" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-124/f58-build-quotes-quote-comparison-and-the-acceptance-handoff-to-the" /> (comparisons), <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> (core agent-native foundations). Product research backlog, not delegated to a coding agent.

issues.title: Revisit and remove Eventiva's temporary house AI-gate override
issues.description:
## Goal

Remove Eventiva's temporary exception from the house AI-credit ruleset gates, and restore Copilot code review and the Code Quality merge gate, once the owner has approved appropriate budgets.

## Context

* <issue id="583894b0-6b9f-4759-8b2d-145a78d15933" label="EVE-243" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-243/fully-enrol-eventiva-in-smartcloud-house-synchronization" /> put Eventiva on `Resnovas/.github/smartcloud/house-base.yml` instead of `house.yml`. The base preset has every house rule except `settings.ruleset.copilotReview` and `settings.ruleset.codeQuality`, both of which spend GitHub AI credits.
* This was needed because the Resnovas Actions and all-AI-credit budgets are held at USD 0 with hard stop after the 2026-11 billing lock. The September charge came from Code Quality AI credits.
* The override lives after the `house:local` line of Eventiva's `.github/smartcloud.yml`: `sync.values.HOUSE_PRESET: house-base.yml` and `settings.ruleset.copilotReview: false`. The managed `extends` line points at `house-base.yml`. Process: `Resnovas/.github` docs/preset.md#base.

## Work

1. The owner approves non-zero monthly AI-credit (and, if needed, Code Quality licence) budgets in GitHub Billing, with hard stop and alerts. Record the amounts, scope and evidence here, without payment details.
2. The owner decides to restore paid Copilot review and Code Quality on Eventiva.
3. In Eventiva, remove `sync.values.HOUSE_PRESET` and `settings.ruleset.copilotReview: false`, and point the managed `extends` line back at `Resnovas/.github/smartcloud/house.yml@main`. Update docs/smartcloud-enrollment.md.
4. Validate with the Smartcloud CLI (`validate`, `plan settings`): the effective config must match `house.yml` with `codeQuality: errors` and `copilotReview: true`. Push under the direct-main exception and read back the `house: default branch` ruleset.

## Acceptance

* Approved budgets are recorded here.
* Eventiva's effective config is identical to every other house repository's, and the live ruleset contains the `code_quality` and `copilot_code_review` rules.
* AI-credit spend is reviewed one billing cycle after restoration.

## Out of scope

Raising any budget without the owner's explicit approval.

## Done signal

Eventiva extends `house.yml` with no local AI-gate override, and the ruleset read-back shows both gates.

## Current repository source status - 2026-11-17

The canonical current repository replacement/index for the unavailable historical `Eventiva-marketplace-infrastructure-v1.md` is [docs/architecture/eventiva-platform-and-marketplace.md](<https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/main/docs/architecture/eventiva-platform-and-marketplace.md>). Jonathan directed this bounded source reconciliation on 2026-11-17 through [the Puck coordination thread](<https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a1e940-37a3-7691-a5c0-e935b711c99a>); the exact owner-instruction time is unavailable. This is a replacement designation, not recovery or reconstruction of the original, a new architecture approval, or completed implementation.

Historical architecture-index/missing-source and archive comments are preserved unchanged as historical evidence. Their claims that the absent document must arrive before current source reconciliation, or that the whole architecture is still unapproved, are explicitly superseded for current source status by this designation and the later binding owner decisions. Their historical checks and narrower unresolved policy statements are not erased. The missing-file source blocker is resolved by the replacement, not by pretending to have read the original.

Owner decisions on Linear remain authoritative: <issue id="b8132640-ebe4-4424-bcf3-161376ebd72b" label="EVE-250" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-250/decide-controlled-cross-tenant-marketplace-gateway-architecture" /> comment [91db949b](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-250#comment-91db949b-6e9c-4cc8-8a80-879f2d815be3>), 2026-11-16T18:51:51.499Z, confirms bounded controlled-marketplace architecture; <issue id="4f5ecaa3-aedf-446d-8993-0c07c98d4bb4" label="EVE-251" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251/decide-marketplace-service-attestation-and-cryptographic-trust" /> comment [15483735](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251#comment-15483735-fbab-487d-a03e-3c15f27e2682>), 2026-11-16T19:03:34.533Z, confirms provider-neutral implementation under the binding <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> security decisions. Concrete crypto/provider/verifier/custody/canonicalization/timing choices, legal/residency/retention policies, freshness/recovery/reconciliation/moderation parameters, existing dependency/security gates and full acceptance remain open where not independently approved. No production activation, provisioning, spending, dependency adoption or status completion is authorized here.

Status: ARCHITECTURE CONFIRMED, implementation and acceptance pending. The owner's 2026-11-16 comment 91db949b-6e9c-4cc8-8a80-879f2d815be3 is authoritative: controlled marketplace service, tenant-owned canonical operational records, participant-scoped exchanged snapshots/workflow state, centrally governed revocable participant grants and durable idempotent saga/outbox orchestration across independent databases. Bounded implementation is authorized within existing dependency/security gates. No direct cross-tenant database access or cross-database ACID claim. <issue id="4f5ecaa3-aedf-446d-8993-0c07c98d4bb4" label="EVE-251" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251/decide-marketplace-service-attestation-and-cryptographic-trust" /> cryptographic trust/attestation/provider/algorithm/custody choices remain separate; no provisioning, spending or unspecified dependencies are approved. Original comments are preserved as historical evidence.

## Goal

Define how Eventiva's directory and marketplace connect independently isolated tenant databases without broad database access, false global ACID guarantees, or duplication of already settled F5, purchasing, sales and payment decisions.

## Settled requirements this decision must preserve

* Each tenant keeps its private operational database, including internal inventory, staff, private pricing, finance and PII.
* <issue id="b22fbb0d-100b-47a3-8c32-eeacadc4c9fe" label="EVE-66" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-66/f5-directory-and-marketplace-vendor-venue-and-professional-listings" />/<issue id="2d6f6f8d-4f15-4279-80cd-42db7339e8a0" label="EVE-75" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-75/f51-build-the-listing-model-category-taxonomy-and-listing-actions" />: published listings expose only an allowlisted public projection; draft/private fields remain tenant-owned.
* <issue id="03bd23d1-9da5-4272-8f2e-0b0bf4f7f846" label="EVE-119" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-119/f57-build-cross-tenant-enquiries-rfps-and-private-message-threads" />: each enquiry recipient has a private two-party thread; recipients cannot see each other.
* <issue id="f08bafe4-f32d-4906-9e87-5d69df56d6a0" label="EVE-124" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-124/f58-build-quotes-quote-comparison-and-the-acceptance-handoff-to-the" /> D5-7: preserve requirement-level and product-level comparison, approved functional alternatives, package allocations without invented unit prices, revision redlines, and mixed-supplier awards with a separate supplier contract, commitment and payment schedule for each winner.
* <issue id="7dba7530-e7b6-4259-be26-9924f9ebddcb" label="EVE-237" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-237/f514-build-quote-payments-with-commission-deducted-at-source" />/<issue id="0bb5afb4-c634-4b0a-a364-648e1ea650ef" label="EVE-246" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-246/define-provider-neutral-connected-account-invoicing-and-settlement" />: the supplier is merchant/seller of record through its provider-connected account; Eventiva is non-custodial; commission is taken by the regulated provider; canonical invoice/payment/reconciliation records remain provider-neutral; no payment executes offline.
* <issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />: people and agents use the same scoped permissions, approval and audit path.

## Selected architecture and policy details to validate

1. **Publication gateway.** A supplier action emits a versioned, allowlisted public listing projection to a shared directory/search service through an outbox. The projection records source tenant, listing/version, publication consent, provenance and expiry. Unpublish, suspension, consent withdrawal and erasure produce higher-priority tombstones and invalidate caches. The index never reads a supplier database directly.
2. **Marketplace interaction service.** Enquiries, participant grants, quote snapshots, comparison mappings, award plans and workflow correlations live in a controlled marketplace service containing only information both parties are authorised to exchange. Access requires a participant grant scoped to the exact thread/quote/contract and tenant role. A grant never exposes either tenant database.
3. **Tenant-owned canonical records.** Buyer requirements, internal budgets and purchasing records stay in the buyer database. Supplier inventory, availability, private prices, sales records and invoices stay in the supplier database. The marketplace stores immutable exchanged snapshots and identifiers, not writable mirrors of either private system.
4. **Durable orchestration.** Cross-tenant workflows use an idempotent saga/process manager plus per-database transactional outboxes/inboxes. Each step has a stable command id, expected version, retry policy, compensation or manual-recovery state and immutable evidence. Eventiva does not claim one ACID transaction across tenant databases, marketplace storage and payment providers.
5. **Freshness and consent.** Availability, stock, quote validity and private pricing are independently asserted by the owning tenant with as-of time, expiry and confidence/status. Comparison distinguishes verified, stale and unknown. Private prices enter the exchange only through supplier consent or a sent quote.
6. **Payments and ledgers.** The provider-connected supplier account owns the invoice/payment. Signed callbacks are idempotently reconciled into supplier and buyer ledgers plus the marketplace correlation record. Eventiva holds no customer funds and stores no payment credentials.
7. **Mixed awards.** One award plan may select comparable lines from several suppliers, but acceptance creates one immutable contract/quote snapshot, commitment, payment schedule and invoice-reconciliation stream per supplier. Partial selection from an indivisible package requires a supplier-confirmed re-quote. Invoice comparison stays line/requirement aware and never invents component pricing.
8. **Privacy and residency.** Define controller/processor roles, legal basis, participant visibility, retention, export/erasure, moderation access and regional placement separately for public projections, private exchange records and tenant-owned records.

## Alternatives

1. **Shared marketplace database as canonical for all F5 records.** Simpler querying and workflows, but weakens tenant ownership and increases concentration, residency and access risk.
2. **Peer-to-peer tenant service calls only.** Keeps ownership strongest, but makes search, offline delivery, audit, retries and multi-supplier comparison fragile.
3. **Replicate full supplier records into the platform.** Easiest analytics, rejected as the default because it over-collects private inventory, pricing, finance and PII.

## Open decisions for Jonathan

1. The marketplace holds only participant-scoped exchanged snapshots and workflow state; operational canonical records remain tenant-owned. Specify permitted fields and whether participant-visible messages fit that exchange boundary before implementing messages.
2. Participant grants are centrally governed and revocable. Specify and test revocation/retention propagation to offline devices and caches without treating stale cached grants as fresh authorization.
3. How fresh must stock/availability be before quote send, award, contract acceptance and payment? Which steps require a synchronous supplier recheck?
4. What compensation/manual-recovery rules apply when one tenant commits and another tenant or provider step fails?
5. Which data classes may be regionally replicated, and which must remain in the owning tenant's residency boundary?
6. Does invoice reconciliation compare provider invoice lines, supplier accounting lines, or an immutable Eventiva contract schedule when they differ?
7. Which platform staff roles may access private exchange records for moderation, disputes and support, with what audit/approval?

## Required validation for delivery

* Negative authorization matrix across organiser, each supplier, platform moderator, support and agents.
* Publish/unpublish/tombstone tests prove private fields never reach the index and revoked content leaves caches.
* Saga fault injection at every boundary proves no duplicate contract, invoice, commission, stock hold or payment and exposes recoverable partial states honestly.
* Mixed award test with three suppliers preserves separate contracts and invoices while retaining requirement-level comparison/redlines.
* Stale availability, expired quote, revoked participant and delayed/replayed provider callback tests.
* GDPR retention/export/erasure and residency review with named owners.

## Out of scope

Production database provisioning, <issue id="4f5ecaa3-aedf-446d-8993-0c07c98d4bb4" label="EVE-251" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251/decide-marketplace-service-attestation-and-cryptographic-trust" /> cryptographic/provider/algorithm/custody selection, unapproved SDKs/dependencies, payment setup, billing/settings changes and changes to settled F5 product behaviour remain out of scope. Bounded code/tests within the approved architecture are permitted; issue creation or agent reconciliation grants no additional authority.

Jonathan approves this decision only:

- The shared marketplace service owns participant grants, the private two-party enquiry/message workflow, immutable exchanged quote and contract snapshots, comparison and mixed-award mappings, and saga state/correlations.

## APPROVED — standard marketplace decryption profile (2026-11-14)

Jonathan approves this architecture direction:

- Private exchanged enquiries, quotes and contracts in the standard marketplace profile may be decrypted **only inside an authorized and attested workload** after the four independent EVE-13 gates agree: identity/delegation; exact resource/purpose authorization; workload integrity/attestation; and HSM/key-broker authorization.
- Shared-service signatures, mutually authenticated transport and permission to decrypt are separate controls. A valid signature or mTLS identity does not itself authorize plaintext access.
- Vault/zero-knowledge records require a separate explicitly designed client/user/device-side workflow and must never silently become server-decryptable.
- Tenant↔marketplace exchange is a high fraud/abuse boundary requiring encrypted authenticated transport, request/payload integrity and origin authentication, replay/expiry/idempotency controls, rotation/revocation and auditable processing.

Architecture approval only: no dependency, algorithm, infrastructure provider, paid service, implementation or key provisioning is approved.

Authoritative EVE-13 sources: [9e6e287a](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-9e6e287a-4a28-4695-801a-23a0889f6a56), [ebbcbe62](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-ebbcbe62-4eab-4919-9b33-03288c232e73), [08f09405](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-08f09405-dbfb-4d5f-ac19-920cf95a98df), [c3a06adc](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-c3a06adc-8c33-4a6c-b43c-815bb8479410), [1da54684](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-1da54684-89c0-4ce7-895c-aeec61af9c8a), [6770565a](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-6770565a-053c-47e6-8980-adab5ed9a109).

## APPROVED — private marketplace payload encryption boundary (2026-11-14)

- Every **private cross-tenant marketplace exchange** requires application-layer envelope encryption in addition to authenticated TLS/mTLS and encryption at rest. This includes private enquiries/messages, supplier quotes and pricing, contracts, award decisions/mappings, invoice/payment-related records, and private attachments/metadata as appropriate.
- Decryption remains governed by the sealed core security profile and independent identity/delegation, exact resource/purpose authorization, workload-attestation and HSM/key-broker gates.
- Allowlisted public listing projections may use authenticated HTTPS/TLS plus encryption at rest without a separate private-payload envelope for genuinely public fields. Publication still requires integrity/provenance, signed source and version, consent, revocation/tombstones and cache invalidation.
- Confidential fields must never be classified as public. Private cross-tenant records are not universally decryptable. Vault/zero-knowledge records retain their separate client/user/device-side rules.
- Preserve root-trust/service-key separation, signed requests, fraud controls, anti-replay/expiry/idempotency, auditable processing and A1 business-record integrity.

Architecture approval only. No algorithm, dependency, infrastructure provider, paid service, implementation or key provisioning is approved.

Related: EVE-250, EVE-66, EVE-119, EVE-124 and EVE-246.

Canonical security record: [EVE-251](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251/decide-marketplace-service-attestation-and-cryptographic-trust).

## APPROVED — marketplace security classification defaults (2026-11-14)

- Private enquiries and messages default to **Sensitive**.
- Quotes, contracts, supplier awards, invoices and payment evidence default to **Restricted/regulated**.
- Attachments inherit the strongest applicable parent classification or their own stronger field/resource classification.
- Vault/client-side zero-knowledge remains a separate explicit opt-in workflow and must not silently become server-decryptable.
- Restricted server-side decryption requires achieved **A4 confidential-workload assurance** plus every independent core gate. If A4 is unavailable, processing fails closed or uses only degraded behavior explicitly permitted by the sealed core profile.
- Classification applies consistently to exchanged snapshots, logs, queues, sync/offline copies, files, backups and temporary processing artefacts. Individual fields may be strengthened when their content warrants it.

Architecture approval only. No implementation, dependency, algorithm, infrastructure provider, paid service or key provisioning is approved.

References: EVE-13, EVE-250, EVE-66, EVE-119, EVE-124, EVE-237 and EVE-246.

## APPROVED — cross-tenant marketplace key governance (2026-11-14)

- Dedicated marketplace-service KEKs operate under the existing deployment M-of-N custodian/quorum governance.
- Private records use separate unique/versioned per-record DEKs with envelope encryption.
- Participant access is scoped and purpose/resource/action/recipient-bound, with independent identity, authorization, attestation, key-broker and audit gates.
- There is no universal marketplace decrypt key. One participant cannot unilaterally delete or crypto-shred another participant's legally required contractual evidence.
- Identity/signing and encryption authorities remain separate; keys are non-exportable; rotation, revocation, recovery and self-hosted root ownership follow the established EVE-13 policies.
- Participant grants authorize only exchanged marketplace records. They never expose another tenant's internal inventory, purchasing, sales, staff, finance, PII or other private operational records.

Architecture approval only. Exact providers, infrastructure, algorithms, dependencies and implementation remain unapproved.

Retention interaction remains a proposal: grant revocation should stop new exchange and ordinary ongoing access, but preserved contractual evidence may remain available only under an independent contractual/legal basis, purpose-limited access and audit. Lawful erasure should remove or anonymize separable personal data where permitted; legal hold and mandatory retention suspend deletion or crypto-shredding. Final key destruction should occur only after every applicable participant, statutory, contractual, dispute and hold obligation expires.

References: EVE-13, EVE-250, EVE-66, EVE-119, EVE-124, EVE-237 and EVE-246.

Detailed security record: [EVE-251](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251/decide-marketplace-service-attestation-and-cryptographic-trust).

comments.body:
## APPROVED — revocation, retention and lawful erasure (2026-11-14)

- Revocation immediately stops new exchange and ordinary participant access under revoked grants.
- Legitimate contractual, payment and audit evidence remains purpose-limited, access-controlled and audited for as long as legally required.
- Separable personal information is erased or anonymized when lawful. Valid legal holds suspend applicable deletion.
- Cryptographic shredding occurs only after all relevant retention periods, legal holds and independently held participant obligations have expired. Neither participant may unilaterally destroy the other's legally retained contractual evidence.
- Retention is classified by record type, jurisdiction, purpose and applicable law; there is no universal marketplace retention duration.
- Revocation propagates to short-lived grants and key handles, service-side cached permissions, synced/offline devices with bounded expiry, search projections and authorization of future operations.
- The policy does not promise impossible retroactive erasure of plaintext already lawfully downloaded, and does not weaken immutable legitimate evidence. Subsequent use remains governed by law, contract, purpose limitation and audit.
- EVE-13 sealed security profiles, no universal decrypt key, deployment M-of-N custody and separately governed legal hold remain controlling.

Architecture approval only. Jurisdiction-specific lawful bases, schedules and regional rules remain unresolved proposals. No implementation, dependency, algorithm, infrastructure provider, paid service or key provisioning is approved.

References: EVE-13, EVE-116, EVE-250, EVE-66, EVE-119, EVE-124, EVE-237 and EVE-246.

Detailed security record: [EVE-251](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251/decide-marketplace-service-attestation-and-cryptographic-trust).

issues.description:
## Current repository source status - 2026-11-17

The canonical current repository replacement/index for the unavailable historical `Eventiva-marketplace-infrastructure-v1.md` is [docs/architecture/eventiva-platform-and-marketplace.md](<https://github.com/Resnovas/Eventiva/blob/main/docs/architecture/eventiva-platform-and-marketplace.md>). Jonathan directed this bounded source reconciliation on 2026-11-17 through [the Puck coordination thread](<https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a1e940-37a3-7691-a5c0-e935b711c99a>); the exact owner-instruction time is unavailable. This is a replacement designation, not recovery or reconstruction of the original, a new architecture approval, or completed implementation.

Historical architecture-index/missing-source and archive comments are preserved unchanged as historical evidence. Their claims that the absent document must arrive before current source reconciliation, or that the whole architecture is still unapproved, are explicitly superseded for current source status by this designation and the later binding owner decisions. Their historical checks and narrower unresolved policy statements are not erased. The missing-file source blocker is resolved by the replacement, not by pretending to have read the original.

Owner decisions on Linear remain authoritative: <issue id="b8132640-ebe4-4424-bcf3-161376ebd72b" label="EVE-250" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-250/decide-controlled-cross-tenant-marketplace-gateway-architecture" /> comment [91db949b](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-250#comment-91db949b-6e9c-4cc8-8a80-879f2d815be3>), 2026-11-16T18:51:51.499Z, confirms bounded controlled-marketplace architecture; <issue id="4f5ecaa3-aedf-446d-8993-0c07c98d4bb4" label="EVE-251" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251/decide-marketplace-service-attestation-and-cryptographic-trust" /> comment [15483735](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251#comment-15483735-fbab-487d-a03e-3c15f27e2682>), 2026-11-16T19:03:34.533Z, confirms provider-neutral implementation under the binding <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> security decisions. Concrete crypto/provider/verifier/custody/canonicalization/timing choices, legal/residency/retention policies, freshness/recovery/reconciliation/moderation parameters, existing dependency/security gates and full acceptance remain open where not independently approved. No production activation, provisioning, spending, dependency adoption or status completion is authorized here.

## BINDING RECONCILIATION — <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> architecture confirmed; concrete composition remains gated (2026-11-16)

<issue id="4f5ecaa3-aedf-446d-8993-0c07c98d4bb4" label="EVE-251" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-251/decide-marketplace-service-attestation-and-cryptographic-trust" /> **implements the binding security architecture already approved by the owner in** <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" />; it does not reopen or redesign it. The following are confirmed: deployment-owned offline/HSM-backed root trust with M-of-N custody; no universal self-hosted decrypt key; separate signing and encryption authorities; tenant/resource KEKs and unique versioned per-record DEKs with envelope encryption; non-exportable keys and short-lived scoped handles; four independent release gates (identity/delegation, exact resource/purpose authorization, workload attestation, HSM/key-broker authorization); A1–A5 assurance; sealed Baseline/Sensitive/Restricted/Vault profiles; zero-trust authenticated transport plus application-layer encryption; fail-closed protected release; region-scoped marketplace cells; and participant grants limited to exchanged records. Modules and tenants may strengthen these controls but cannot weaken or redefine them.

Implementation may proceed now with provider-neutral trust, attestation and key-broker contracts; typed signed-request/evidence envelopes; profile and gate conformance fixtures; replay, revocation, staleness, audience/resource/purpose mismatch and unavailable-broker negative tests; algorithm-agnostic rotation/version metadata; and secret-free audit evidence references.

This confirmation does **not** approve unspecified algorithms, key sizes/formats, cryptographic libraries, attestation products/evidence formats, KMS/HSM vendors, exact custody deployment, provider infrastructure, provisioning, paid services, regional infrastructure, or production activation. Those require exact technical/dependency/security review before concrete composition. Remaining owner policy inputs are limited to regional/legal processing rules, record-class retention/legal-hold schedules, mandatory independent-review and non-overridable degraded-assurance cases, and any product-wide custodian quorum policy. Concrete vendor and implementation selections are not new architecture decisions.

Later stale proposal wording in this issue is subordinate to this reconciliation and the cited binding <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> owner comments.

# PROPOSAL — not approved for implementation

## Purpose and source status

Define the trust, attestation and encrypted-transport architecture for the high-risk tenant↔shared-marketplace and shared-service↔provider boundaries introduced by <issue id="b8132640-ebe4-4424-bcf3-161376ebd72b" label="EVE-250" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-250/decide-controlled-cross-tenant-marketplace-gateway-architecture" />.

**Owner-stated requirement:** Eventiva has a top-level keypair and subordinate shared-service keypairs used for signing/decryption, with robust encryption between tenant and shared-service instances. The root private key must not perform routine payload decryption.

**Authoritative current source — correction:** the exact owner-approved hierarchy and decryption/attestation policy is recorded in <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> comments. These override the archived historical notes:

* [9e6e287a — Encryption and key-authority decision](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-9e6e287a-4a28-4695-801a-23a0889f6a56>): offline/HSM-backed deployment root trust signs intermediates/recovery policy and is not a routine decryption key; Cloud M-of-N custody; self-hosted roots; tenant KEKs, resource-class keys and versioned DEKs; distinct signing identities; envelope encryption; scoped short-lived key handles; rotation/revocation/crypto-shredding; no universal Eventiva self-hosted decrypt path.
* [ebbcbe62 — Decryption guard and runtime attestation](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-ebbcbe62-4eab-4919-9b33-03288c232e73>): non-exportable keys and four independent gates—identity/delegation, resource/purpose, workload attestation, and HSM/key broker—producing short-lived signed evidence and failing closed.
* [08f09405 — Sealed core security profiles](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-08f09405-dbfb-4d5f-ac19-920cf95a98df>): only versioned core security contracts define cryptographic guarantees; modules cannot override them.
* [c3a06adc — Security profiles](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-c3a06adc-8c33-4a6c-b43c-815bb8479410>): Baseline, Sensitive, Restricted/regulated and Vault/zero-knowledge share a modern cryptographic floor but differ in key granularity and decrypting authority.
* [1da54684 — Zero trust](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-1da54684-89c0-4ce7-895c-aeec61af9c8a>): mTLS/service identity and the same canonical authorization policy apply across every route and surface.
* [6770565a — Assurance levels](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-6770565a-053c-47e6-8980-adab5ed9a109>): A1–A5; A4 confidential workload is the default minimum for Restricted server-side decryption.

The archived `Examples/eventiva-before-amp/.cursor/plans/completed/notes.md` §§2.1.2–2.1.4 is secondary historical context only.

## Threat model

Protect against tenant or service impersonation; stolen service credentials; malicious or compromised workloads; cross-tenant confused-deputy access; replay, reordering and downgrade; payload or price/contract alteration; recipient substitution; stale/revoked grants; webhook forgery; duplicate financial or inventory effects; compromised keys; insider misuse; log tampering; region/residency leakage; and offline clients presenting queued work as confirmed.

## Proposed trust and message flow

1. Use the Eventiva top-level key only as a trust/governance root: certify or authorize subordinate identities and publish versioned trust metadata/revocations. Never use its private key for ordinary request signing or payload decryption.
2. Give each tenant gateway and shared service distinct, independently revocable identities. Separate identity/attestation, signing and encryption key purposes; do not assume one subordinate keypair serves all three.
3. Mutually authenticate endpoints over TLS, potentially mTLS where deployable. Before accepting a request, resolve both service identity and request-scoped participant/recipient grant; transport identity alone grants no marketplace data access.
4. Canonicalize and sign security-relevant request metadata and payload digests, including protocol version, sender, intended recipient/service, tenant and participant scope, action, correlation/idempotency key, timestamp/expiry and nonce. Reject unknown versions, stale windows, replayed nonces and recipient/scope mismatch.
5. For fields requiring protection beyond transport termination, use application-layer envelope encryption to the intended recipient/service. Routine payload decryption uses service/workload encryption keys or short-lived data keys, never the Eventiva root private key.
6. Bind accepted messages to A1: authorization and approvals are revalidated as required; successful authoritative mutations atomically persist domain change, idempotency evidence, state/history, outbox event and receipt/audit. Cross-tenant work remains a recoverable saga/outbox workflow, not false global ACID.
7. Provider callbacks require provider-supported signature verification, replay controls and idempotent reconciliation to supplier and buyer ledgers. Preserve Eventiva's non-custodial connected-account payment decision.
8. Keep tamper-evident, access-controlled security/audit records for issuance, trust changes, grant decisions, signatures, decryption/key-use events, saga transitions and webhook verification, without logging plaintext secrets or sensitive payloads.

## Key lifecycle proposal

* Keep root, subordinate identity/signing keys, encryption keys and data keys in separately authorized custody boundaries.
* Version keys and trust documents; support overlap during rotation, explicit expiry, emergency revocation, deny-by-default unknown key IDs and rapid propagation to every region/runtime.
* Define compromise playbooks: freeze affected identity/grants, revoke and rotate, terminate sessions/ephemeral material, quarantine ambiguous messages, replay/reconcile outboxes safely and notify affected tenants.
* Cryptographic erasure, escrow/recovery and tenant-held-key consequences require explicit policy. No algorithm, HSM/KMS vendor or dependency is selected here.

## Offline and regional constraints

Offline clients may prepare and sign/queue work but cannot treat authoritative marketplace, stock, ticket, dispatch or payment effects as confirmed. Reconnect must re-authenticate, reauthorize, check revocation/freshness and run through idempotent saga processing. Trust/revocation material needs bounded-staleness regional distribution; payload placement and key custody must respect tenant residency. Safety-sensitive degraded operation remains governed by separately approved procedures.

## Open decisions for owner

The remaining decisions are consolidated in the Eventiva architecture decision batches document. Unresolved marketplace items include jurisdiction-to-region placement, cross-region lawful-basis policy, exact infrastructure/provider choices, attestation evidence/verifier separation, canonicalization, algorithms, rotation timing and anti-fraud thresholds. None is approved by this issue description.

## Acceptance before implementation

Original design reconciled or explicitly superseded; threat model reviewed; hierarchy/key-purpose diagram approved; handshake and canonical request format approved; custody/rotation/revocation/compromise runbooks approved; offline/region behavior approved; provider-webhook and saga integration tests specified; dependencies, algorithms and any paid services separately approved.

## Protected extension release constraints (2026-11-15)

Spec [https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c>), <issue id="afb95d96-359d-4c0f-a462-a7ce41e2c988" label="EVE-262" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-262/implement-governed-observation-only-execution-and-lifecycle-hooks-with" /> hooks and <issue id="b025ea11-9298-48b2-9bd4-d44decabcab4" label="EVE-261" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-261/integrate-the-modular-platform-and-prove-every-owner-required" /> acceptance. Later approved owner comments govern over stale proposal wording. Reuse sealed baseline/sensitive/restricted/vault and achieved A1-A5 assurance; do not add independent hook trust classes. Installation/registration/signature/catalogue or tenant-admin trust grants no decrypt rights. Preserve four independent authorization/attestation/broker/client-release gates and non-universal root/KEK/DEK hierarchy. Initial hooks deny decrypting/emergency events; executable third-party observers denied on Restricted/Vault/protected operations; financial additive hook dispatch denied. Any allowed metadata-only release checks exact tenant/resource/purpose/profile and current revocation; even identifiers/timing may leak. Prove no protected plaintext in event/outbox/dead-letter/error/log/span/projection. Missing attestation/broker/client release capability fails closed. No exact crypto/provider/algorithm/key-custody choice approved here. AI-authored planning addition.

comments.body:
## APPROVED — standard marketplace decryption profile (2026-11-14)

Jonathan approves this architecture direction:

- Private exchanged enquiries, quotes and contracts in the standard marketplace profile may be decrypted **only inside an authorized and attested workload** after the four independent EVE-13 gates agree: identity/delegation; exact resource/purpose authorization; workload integrity/attestation; and HSM/key-broker authorization.
- Shared-service signatures, mutually authenticated transport and permission to decrypt are separate controls. A valid signature or mTLS identity does not itself authorize plaintext access.
- Vault/zero-knowledge records require a separate explicitly designed client/user/device-side workflow and must never silently become server-decryptable.
- Tenant↔marketplace exchange is a high fraud/abuse boundary requiring encrypted authenticated transport, request/payload integrity and origin authentication, replay/expiry/idempotency controls, rotation/revocation and auditable processing.

Architecture approval only: no dependency, algorithm, infrastructure provider, paid service, implementation or key provisioning is approved.

Authoritative EVE-13 sources: [9e6e287a](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-9e6e287a-4a28-4695-801a-23a0889f6a56), [ebbcbe62](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-ebbcbe62-4eab-4919-9b33-03288c232e73), [08f09405](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-08f09405-dbfb-4d5f-ac19-920cf95a98df), [c3a06adc](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-c3a06adc-8c33-4a6c-b43c-815bb8479410), [1da54684](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-1da54684-89c0-4ce7-895c-aeec61af9c8a), [6770565a](https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and#comment-6770565a-053c-47e6-8980-adab5ed9a109).

Still open: application-layer envelope encryption for every marketplace payload versus only profile-classified fields/records; exact service class, custodianship and infrastructure.

comments.body:
## APPROVED — private marketplace payload encryption boundary (2026-11-14)

- Every **private cross-tenant marketplace exchange** requires application-layer envelope encryption in addition to authenticated TLS/mTLS and encryption at rest. This includes private enquiries/messages, supplier quotes and pricing, contracts, award decisions/mappings, invoice/payment-related records, and private attachments/metadata as appropriate.
- Decryption remains governed by the sealed core security profile and independent identity/delegation, exact resource/purpose authorization, workload-attestation and HSM/key-broker gates.
- Allowlisted public listing projections may use authenticated HTTPS/TLS plus encryption at rest without a separate private-payload envelope for genuinely public fields. Publication still requires integrity/provenance, signed source and version, consent, revocation/tombstones and cache invalidation.
- Confidential fields must never be classified as public. Private cross-tenant records are not universally decryptable. Vault/zero-knowledge records retain their separate client/user/device-side rules.
- Preserve root-trust/service-key separation, signed requests, fraud controls, anti-replay/expiry/idempotency, auditable processing and A1 business-record integrity.

Architecture approval only. No algorithm, dependency, infrastructure provider, paid service, implementation or key provisioning is approved.

Related: EVE-250, EVE-66, EVE-119, EVE-124 and EVE-246.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
## APPROVED — marketplace security classification defaults (2026-11-14)

- Private enquiries and messages default to **Sensitive**.
- Quotes, contracts, supplier awards, invoices and payment evidence default to **Restricted/regulated**.
- Attachments inherit the strongest applicable parent classification or their own stronger field/resource classification.
- Vault/client-side zero-knowledge remains a separate explicit opt-in workflow and must not silently become server-decryptable.
- Restricted server-side decryption requires achieved **A4 confidential-workload assurance** plus every independent core gate. If A4 is unavailable, processing fails closed or uses only degraded behavior explicitly permitted by the sealed core profile.
- Classification applies consistently to exchanged snapshots, logs, queues, sync/offline copies, files, backups and temporary processing artefacts. Individual fields may be strengthened when their content warrants it.

Architecture approval only. No implementation, dependency, algorithm, infrastructure provider, paid service or key provisioning is approved.

References: EVE-13, EVE-250, EVE-66, EVE-119, EVE-124, EVE-237 and EVE-246.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
## APPROVED — cross-tenant marketplace key governance (2026-11-14)

- Dedicated marketplace-service KEKs operate under the existing deployment M-of-N custodian/quorum governance.
- Private records use separate unique/versioned per-record DEKs with envelope encryption.
- Participant access is scoped and purpose/resource/action/recipient-bound, with independent identity, authorization, attestation, key-broker and audit gates.
- There is no universal marketplace decrypt key. One participant cannot unilaterally delete or crypto-shred another participant's legally required contractual evidence.
- Identity/signing and encryption authorities remain separate; keys are non-exportable; rotation, revocation, recovery and self-hosted root ownership follow the established EVE-13 policies.
- Participant grants authorize only exchanged marketplace records. They never expose another tenant's internal inventory, purchasing, sales, staff, finance, PII or other private operational records.

Architecture approval only. Exact providers, infrastructure, algorithms, dependencies and implementation remain unapproved.

Retention interaction remains a proposal: grant revocation should stop new exchange and ordinary ongoing access, but preserved contractual evidence may remain available only under an independent contractual/legal basis, purpose-limited access and audit. Lawful erasure should remove or anonymize separable personal data where permitted; legal hold and mandatory retention suspend deletion or crypto-shredding. Final key destruction should occur only after every applicable participant, statutory, contractual, dispute and hold obligation expires.

References: EVE-13, EVE-250, EVE-66, EVE-119, EVE-124, EVE-237 and EVE-246.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
## APPROVED — revocation, retention and lawful erasure (2026-11-14)

- Revocation immediately stops new exchange and ordinary participant access under revoked grants.
- Legitimate contractual, payment and audit evidence remains purpose-limited, access-controlled and audited for as long as legally required.
- Separable personal information is erased or anonymized when lawful. Valid legal holds suspend applicable deletion.
- Cryptographic shredding occurs only after all relevant retention periods, legal holds and independently held participant obligations have expired. Neither participant may unilaterally destroy the other's legally retained contractual evidence.
- Retention is classified by record type, jurisdiction, purpose and applicable law; there is no universal marketplace retention duration.
- Revocation propagates to short-lived grants and key handles, service-side cached permissions, synced/offline devices with bounded expiry, search projections and authorization of future operations.
- The policy does not promise impossible retroactive erasure of plaintext already lawfully downloaded, and does not weaken immutable legitimate evidence. Subsequent use remains governed by law, contract, purpose limitation and audit.
- EVE-13 sealed security profiles, no universal decrypt key, deployment M-of-N custody and separately governed legal hold remain controlling.

Architecture approval only. Jurisdiction-specific lawful bases, schedules and regional rules remain unresolved proposals. No implementation, dependency, algorithm, infrastructure provider, paid service or key provisioning is approved.

References: EVE-13, EVE-116, EVE-250, EVE-66, EVE-119, EVE-124, EVE-237 and EVE-246.
comments.author: jonathan@resnovas.com

comments.body:
## APPROVED — regional marketplace topology (2026-11-15)

- Eventiva keeps one logical operational database per tenant.
- Private tenant↔marketplace exchanges are handled by region-scoped marketplace cells.
- Region-bound data includes private ciphertext, marketplace-service KEKs and versioned DEKs, A4 confidential-workload decryption for Restricted records, and security/audit evidence.
- Global replication is limited to explicitly published public listing projections and minimum non-sensitive routing/trust metadata.
