issues.title: Implement Effect Cluster sharding and multi-runner recovery in the fresh Eventiva backend
issues.description:
## Binding deployment/runtime decision — 2026-11-15 (Jonathan approved)

**Effect Cluster sharding is part of the Eventiva core execution architecture NOW**, not an optional feature added only for agent runs or advanced deployments. Preserve **one cluster-capable authorized execution path** across all editions: domain and action contracts remain transport-/driver-neutral, and server-side cluster routing, runner orchestration and storage are composed in backend infrastructure/adapters. There must not be an independent local-only business-execution engine that behaves differently from distributed mode.

**Deployment defaults**

* **Community / single-host default:** run **one Effect Cluster runner** locally (with any required co-located services) in a supported single-host profile, with no requirement for Eventiva Cloud, SaaS identity or a multi-machine cluster. It must run the same action, authorization, transaction, persistence and dispatch semantics as multi-runner mode; a single runner is a deployment size, not a separate implementation.
* **Cloud / Production default:** **multiple independent runner processes/instances**, distributing work/shard ownership and recovering from runner loss. Define a production-ready minimum topology and expose actual achieved runner count, shard ownership, health, degraded state and capacity. Do not silently claim distributed redundancy when only one runner is healthy.
* **Scalability:** Community/self-hosted may explicitly opt into multi-runner; a single physical host may run one or several runner processes. Cloud may scale runner count based on actual capacity/load controls. Work remains stable across runner placement; no process-local state dependency.
* **Runtime config and topology:** typed, validated deployment-profile config selects topology, runner count, shard count, timeouts/leases/health, endpoints and storage. Separate logical compute sharding from the already-approved one operational database per tenant. Support a fully local deployment via supported storage adapters, without requiring the managed Neon project; verify backend/cluster storage compatibility before claiming SQLite-only cluster support.
* **Safety/reliability:** persist business-critical actions by default with stable idempotency and A1 atomic audit/outbox/transition evidence. At-least-once delivery is not exactly-once execution; retain genuine business deduplication. Enforce same delegated permissions and approval gates on every runner and after a shard moves. Protect local and distributed paths equally.
* **Validation:** same conformance suite for single-runner Community and 2+ independent runners; real distribution, deliberate runner drain/SIGKILL, retry/deduplication, ordering, live configuration, restart/recovery, tenant isolation, and no double-applied business mutation. Include CI integration tests plus documented local launch commands; no fake in-memory-only unit tests substituted for cluster evidence. Test availability/reliability before declaring cloud readiness.

**Priority and execution:** Elevate <issue id="55c2d64a-d779-41d9-b74e-dcc7d062b86b" label="EVE-252" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-252/implement-effect-cluster-sharding-and-multi-runner-recovery-in-the" /> to critical core-foundation implementation. <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" /> has now landed and is Done. Begin <issue id="55c2d64a-d779-41d9-b74e-dcc7d062b86b" label="EVE-252" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-252/implement-effect-cluster-sharding-and-multi-runner-recovery-in-the" /> compatibility/harness/contract work immediately on GPT/Codex in an isolated worktree, avoiding <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> SQL implementation files; finish SQL-backed integration once <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" />'s required storage adapters are verified. Preserve the user's approved dependency/version, direct-to-main, signed commits, security approvals and spending guardrails. Ask explicit approval for any genuinely NEW dependency or paid infrastructure, not for ordinary coordination or task dispatch.

This decision supersedes any reading that Effect Cluster is optional, cloud-exclusive, agent-only, or that the archived pre-rebuild sharding prototype is already the active runtime.

## Finding — fresh production core is not yet Effect Cluster-backed

Verified on `Resnovas/Eventiva` `main` (2026-11-15): `apps/server/package.json` includes `@effect/cluster@0.60.5` and `@effect/workflow@0.19.1`, but `apps/server/src/main.ts` constructs only a **local, in-process** `ActionHostLive`, registers `platform.status`, attempts one invocation with fail-closed audit and exits. No current production source file implements or starts SQL-backed Effect Cluster runners, shard ownership/routing, runner registration, load distribution or failover. `@eventiva/runtime` correctly remains provider-neutral and must NOT import Cluster directly. Historical two-runner spike <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" /> used archived pre-rebuild `@effect/cluster@0.56.4` and does not prove the rebuilt workspace is distributed.

### Goal

Make the **current** Effect v3 backend execute eligible Eventiva actions and durable work across multiple independent **Effect Cluster** runner processes with DB-supported shard ownership, observability, graceful drain, crash recovery, idempotent persistence and tenant isolation. Preserve one action/authorization/audit path for UI/API/agents; shard by canonical entity/work identity, **not** by splitting tenant databases or bypassing the authorized ActionHost.

### Scope

1. Reconcile the actual `@effect/cluster@0.60.5` API and `@effect/workflow@0.19.1` with Effect v3 and <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" />'s measured legacy behavior. Do **not** copy archived old code by default or assume older `NodeClusterSocket.layer({storage: 'sql'})` signatures still apply. If new dependency/version is needed, request explicit approval first.
2. Define portable action-to-durable-entity/work message envelopes and stable correlation/primary/idempotency keys. Keep contracts/schema/runtime shared packages driver-free; Effect Cluster, Node runner transport, Postgres adapters and infrastructure belong in backend integration/composition roots.
3. Build an actual **2-runner** launch/test harness against isolated PostgreSQL 17 (CI/local); validate compatibility with production target Neon PostgreSQL 17 in London, including direct/pooled connection suitability, advisory locks and tenant database routing. Existing Neon dev project is synthetic-only; no CDC/logical replication needed or permitted for this feature.
4. Confirm shards are assigned only to processes hosting required entity types (avoid the legacy empty 'shard-manager' bug from <issue id="dc2c113f-3da9-45f8-9106-5ba2c94efb6c" label="EVE-37" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-37/remove-the-shard-manager-process-that-owns-shards-with-no-entities" />), and define configurable shards-per-group, heartbeat/lease/expiry, drain and runner-health visibility per <issue id="2f9fdfdc-7e1d-4c27-9557-77465a22e3a9" label="EVE-38" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-38/cut-runner-loss-failover-from-36s-and-expose-the-cluster-settings-in" />.
5. Mutating and sensitive operations preserve authorized Effect action invocation, A1 atomic domain+idempotency+history+outbox+audit transaction semantics, and persisted-by-default, per-entity-ordered handling with deduplication under at-least-once delivery (<issue id="1b79a257-9ea0-40b5-a8f7-23e1c09221be" label="EVE-39" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-39/make-every-entity-action-idempotent-and-persisted-by-default" />). Never claim exactly-once execution from transport.
6. Long-running agent, schedule and production jobs use Workflow activities and recoverable checkpoints rather than blocking entity mailboxes (related <issue id="ae557bfe-e194-4268-93e7-e68ee250a84a" label="EVE-34" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-34/agent-runs-restart-from-scratch-when-their-shard-moves" />/35/36/54), with later feature-specific implementation staged appropriately.
7. Include operational documentation, graphs and test instrumentation; do not confuse compute sharding with database-per-tenant architecture.

### Acceptance

* Two separate Node runner processes demonstrably each own shards and process their relevant entities under load.
* Graceful runner drain and SIGKILL/failure/recovery tests show ownership reallocation, continuity of persisted work, no *double-applied business mutations*, per-entity order, clear measured failover and no false delivery guarantees.
* A deliberate duplicate/replay with identical idempotency key returns one persisted result; volatile behavior is explicitly documented and never used for financial, dispatch or safety-critical effects.
* An empty/non-entity runner cannot silently capture shards it cannot serve.
* Tenant A operations never route into tenant B data; all action, permission and audit policies still enforce with runner relocation.
* Automated checks pass, CI evidence and exact commands are recorded, and code is committed directly to `main` with signed conventional commit after <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />/<issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> integration gates.

### Dependencies and coordination

Implementation requires the current <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" /> authorized action host and <issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" /> SQL-storage adapter/conformance to land. In the meantime a GPT/Codex **read-only compatibility/design orb** may investigate <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" /> legacy results, current package APIs and tests without editing files owned by <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />/<issue id="e4fa521d-c5d2-4f24-ab86-ed41def53953" label="EVE-42" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state" />. <issue id="dc2c113f-3da9-45f8-9106-5ba2c94efb6c" label="EVE-37" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-37/remove-the-shard-manager-process-that-owns-shards-with-no-entities" />/38/39 remain useful finding references but require re-scoping for the clean rebuild. No new dependencies, paid services, Neon resource changes or other infrastructure provisioning are approved by this planning issue.

**Source evidence**: <issue id="5c7aeec2-d49c-4028-9eca-1bc641d3618c" label="EVE-13" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-13/establish-modular-core-foundations-for-database-adapters-expo-and" /> 'Server-side sharding and load distribution', <issue id="37a1be99-529e-478c-a187-48c120672aeb" label="EVE-18" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-18/s5-verify-sharding-across-two-independent-runners-with-drain-and" /> S5 tested legacy two-runner setup, <issue id="dc2c113f-3da9-45f8-9106-5ba2c94efb6c" label="EVE-37" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-37/remove-the-shard-manager-process-that-owns-shards-with-no-entities" />/38/39, <issue id="a626308a-598f-41ba-accd-4004cbbd9932" label="EVE-54" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-54/p18c-build-durable-agent-runs-on-effect-cluster-and-workflow" />; live `apps/server/src/main.ts`, `apps/server/package.json`, `packages/runtime/src/host.ts` on `main`.

## Kernel generation/workflow handoff acceptance (2026-11-15)

Spec [https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c>); <issue id="ceb453e5-ab8e-4566-bf54-47d742b0f425" label="EVE-257" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-257/implement-the-composable-module-kernel-and-safe-lifecycleprovider" /> local lease API is NOT distributed fencing. issues.title: Build shared guided SOP procedures and governed step execution
issues.description:
## BINDING owner decision — 15 November 2026: human-in-the-loop for ALL operational emergency actions

**Never automatically actuate a show-control or operational response from an incident, alarm, emergency sensor, issue classification, agent interpretation, integration alert or rules-engine event.** An alarm/event may be ingested, classified, displayed, logged, correlated, escalated to people, propose a configured SOP or preset, and notify designated staff; it must NOT automatically GO/hold/pause/mute audio, set venue lights/DMX, trigger PA/media/announcements, start emergency scene/preset, dispatch units or carry out other consequential incident-response operations. The possibility of false alarms and resulting public panic/harm is the rationale. This is an unconditional product policy for **operational incidents and alarms**, not an admin-configurable bypass or an exception for 'tested integration'. A permissioned, accountable **human must deliberately initiate** the approved action following assessment; log initiator, confirmation, linked incident, preset/version, result, and failures. Provide quick incident-linked actions but not default-on automatic acceptance.

**Differentiate ordinary show automation:** separately programmed and human-armed cue stacks, playback sequences, lighting console input, MIDI/OSC/MSC and timecode may continue to start permitted *non-emergency show cues* according to show programming; that is not authority for automatically activating an incident/emergency response. Incoming external signals claiming to be alarms are treated as alerts for human evaluation even if received over a show-control protocol. An external operator deliberately firing an authorized ordinary cue is still allowed, subject to arming and permissions.

**System-of-systems boundary:** independent certified fire alarms, evacuation/voice alarm, emergency lighting and physical overrides retain their own mandatory automatic functions. Eventiva's human-in-the-loop restriction is for Eventiva-initiated control actions and must not inhibit certified systems, lawful fire-panel interlocks, or physical emergency interventions. Do not call for an extra Eventiva confirmation where it could delay or prevent those independent measures. Any proposed direct control of safety-certified hardware requires separate safety engineering and approval.

**Acceptance criteria:** simulate a false fire/heat alarm and a mistakenly classified crowd incident: both notify MDT with a proposed response and initiate **zero** show/lighting/audio/PA/dispatch outputs without a deliberate authorized human action; no auto approval through agents, tenant rules or remote console input marked as emergency. Authorized manual response from MDT executes only the selected versioned preset and clearly reports partial success/failure. Ordinary human-armed playback and mapped external non-emergency cue input still work independently. Test no deferred/replayed emergency output after reconnect.

Implementation and dependencies remain unapproved.

## Decision status and purpose

**Approved product behavior — 2026-11-15.** Owner approved the design choice that guided Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are **advisory by default**, with a tenant administrator able to require particular procedures/steps, supporting evidence, and authorized sign-off. This issue defines a **shared guided-procedure capability**, not a parallel MDT-only workflow engine. This is specification approval only; implementation, new dependency versions, integrations and production changes require normal authorization.

The live operational system receives actual pre-existing **issues, requests, incidents, tasks and alerts**. Guided procedures attach to and advance those records; **there is no simulated 999/101 call-intake product** in the live F7 control-room scope. Lightweight scenario simulation remains an optional <issue id="9268485b-c9f1-49ed-93b7-a3c90b9bc7c6" label="EVE-245" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-245/build-the-integrated-training-competency-and-certification-platform" /> **training submodule** using strictly isolated synthetic state.

## Goals

A controller, event technician, dispatcher, crew leader, support agent or learner can follow an appropriate, versioned procedure against an existing Eventiva record. Examples: assessing and escalating an incident, handling a production/audio fault, checking an equipment or vehicle defect, triaging an IT service issue, and preparing an operational closeout.

One canonical Effect Schema action/Effect Workflow model serves web, mobile/MDT, API, agent and protocol adapters. Screen-awareness projections show the current procedure, required actions, approvals and outstanding steps. Procedure publication uses Eventiva's controlled content/change governance, not AI-authored live instructions.

## Scope and policy

1. **Definitions:** tenant- and module-owned `ProcedureDefinition` with immutable published version, author, competent approver for regulated/controlled steps, purpose, applicability (record type, severity, service/department, event, capability and terminology profile), locale, prerequisites, response deadlines/expiry, content provenance, and policy override rules. Draft/edit/review/publish/supersede/retire with audit and historical version fidelity.
2. **Execution:** `ProcedureRun` linked to the **original** issue/task/incident (not an automatic duplicate CAD), assigned operator(s), owner/team, record state and current procedure version; tracked step attempts, device/server timestamps, input, decisions, evidence, escalations, skip/override reasons and durable receipts. Support pause/resume, reassignment/handover, restart/recovery and immutable history/corrections.
3. **Steps:** informational guidance, question/input, conditional branch, document or data lookup, validated Eventiva action, evidence/attachment, check, escalation, named approval/sign-off and closeout condition. Steps may be optional or marked required; *default new procedure/step is advisory*. Tenant policy can make chosen procedures or steps mandatory by context, including evidence and approver/competency. Mark critical safeguards as non-skippable at the applicable controlled policy floor; ordinary advisory skips are logged with reason when requested. **No tenant override weakens platform-enforced authorization or an applicable regulated/safety rule.**
4. **Actions and rules:** bind executable steps to pre-existing canonical Eventiva actions (<issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />/<issue id="7f612e80-3332-4acf-a74c-d35db06fe4e8" label="EVE-43" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and" />) with fresh permissions, current state/version, idempotency, human approvals and append-only audit; use <issue id="55c2d64a-d779-41d9-b74e-dcc7d062b86b" label="EVE-252" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-252/implement-effect-cluster-sharding-and-multi-runner-recovery-in-the" /> Effect Cluster/Workflow for durable execution and F3/F14's single rule engine for triggers/notifications. Rules may suggest/start procedures when authorized; they cannot bypass step approval or silently self-sign protected actions. No second special-purpose automation system.
5. **Live control integration:** on actual incoming F7/F1/F3 incidents/requests, offer matching guidance; maintain incident priority/assessment and reason trail, owner/control-group handover, comms template and acknowledgments, dispatcher/crew progress, required closeout forms and policy-driven closure gates. Avoid hardcoded police/fire/ambulance standards; configured roleplay and operational profiles are mapped to stable semantics (<issue id="338aae77-d10e-4f8a-9189-fe3655bd3572" label="EVE-28" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-28/port-localization-for-people-and-for-the-agent" />).
6. **Offline & safety:** allow viewing cached approved procedures, collecting routine answers and queueing allowed evidence/notes offline. Authoritative actions—dispatch, allocation, safety-critical state, live control, irreversible approvals—stay online and revalidate; show stale procedure/version warnings and resolve conflicts on reconnect. A deployment without a separate safety case is for coordination, not certified emergency-service operation.
7. **Agent-native:** identical discoverability and action semantics for human and delegated agents; permission-filtered suggested SOPs, explanations, version/evidence gaps and next steps. Agents may recommend and draft but not invent safety procedures, falsely claim verification, approve their own actions or issue practical competency.
8. **Training reuse:** <issue id="9268485b-c9f1-49ed-93b7-a3c90b9bc7c6" label="EVE-245" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-245/build-the-integrated-training-competency-and-certification-platform" /> optional lightweight branching scenarios reuse published SOP content/terminology and view patterns, but run with **synthetic, separately scoped records and test-only action projections** that can NEVER send real dispatch/messages, write live operations, alter external services or issue credentials. Record learning outcomes and exact content/profile version; instructor sign-off remains separate.

## Candidate action inventory (validate naming with canonical inventory)

* `procedure.definition.createDraft/updateDraft/publish/supersede/retire/get/list`
* `procedure.run.start/assign/pause/resume/get/list`
* `procedure.step.respond/skip/submitEvidence`
* `procedure.run.escalate/complete`
* `procedure.approval.request/decide` (reuse <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" /> approval mechanism, not a second permission flow)
* `procedure.run.history`

All have typed schemas/permission metadata and side-effect/approval classification. No generic form submission may directly invoke a privileged backend outside ActionHost.

## Minimum acceptance tests

* An existing technical issue launches a branched advisory SOP; an optional step can be skipped with recorded reason, while the linked issue remains the source of truth.
* Tenant admin publishes a controlled procedure that requires specified evidence and an independent authorized sign-off; closure without them fails on **UI, API and agent** paths.
* Offline responses to a routine checklist reconcile in order with visible conflict and version changes; no dispatch, sign-off or restricted action executes offline.
* Mid-run operator handover preserves in-progress answers, ownership, timestamps and immutable audit; runner restart replays safely without duplicated applied steps.
* A revoked user/agent lacks permissions on resume; attempts to self-approve, to bypass a mandatory step or to fabricate confirmation fail closed.
* A training scenario runs on synthetic fixtures; test proves no writes/messages/dispatch reach live Eventiva operational services.
* Procedure/terminology revisions do not rewrite historical evidence or accidentally replace the original issue/CAD.

## Explicit dependencies and boundaries

Coordinate <issue id="37310611-807d-43de-a5fb-ff53dc3a494e" label="EVE-71" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-71/f7-fleet-and-live-operations-vehicles-maintenance-units-dispatch-and" /> **(F7 live control)**, <issue id="acc43644-11f0-4a63-b850-f1099ce4626c" label="EVE-147" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-147/f77-build-the-incident-control-log-and-dispatch-for-live-events" /> **(CAD/dispatch)**, <issue id="e0be080f-0e5b-427b-9545-8b7430befe4e" label="EVE-148" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-148/f78-build-crew-mdt-mode-in-the-one-app" /> **(crew MDT)**, <issue id="9268485b-c9f1-49ed-93b7-a3c90b9bc7c6" label="EVE-245" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-245/build-the-integrated-training-competency-and-certification-platform" /> **(optional learning simulation)**, <issue id="cbcfb707-a7d4-4089-8e84-d9e2a2bd4d94" label="EVE-235" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-235/f310-build-the-task-rule-builder-when-x-then-y-on-a-generic-rule" /> **(rules)**, <issue id="8a7a26ad-455f-4ef7-a0e4-4dc75882ccc6" label="EVE-191" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-191/f145-automations-extend-the-f3-rules-engine-across-every-feature-set" /> **(cross-module automation)**, <issue id="dc89a6af-338c-417b-a352-80cbfb05ec1e" label="EVE-40" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-40/p11-build-the-action-contract-and-inventory-in-effect-schema" />/43/45/50/52/54, and the Eventiva training/competency authorization model.

**Not in scope:** mock 999/101 phone services, voice/radio provider integration, a standalone roleplay simulator, second SOP-only rules engine, medical advice generator or unsafe automated emergency response. Historical SWRPC training documents are workflow design examples, not licensed canonical clinical/emergency guidance; original Drive files and their sharing remain unchanged.

issues.description:
## BINDING owner decision — 15 November 2026: human-in-the-loop for ALL operational emergency actions

**Never automatically actuate a show-control or operational response from an incident, alarm, emergency sensor, issue classification, agent interpretation, integration alert or rules-engine event.** An alarm/event may be ingested, classified, displayed, logged, correlated, escalated to people, propose a configured SOP or preset, and notify designated staff; it must NOT automatically GO/hold/pause/mute audio, set venue lights/DMX, trigger PA/media/announcements, start emergency scene/preset, dispatch units or carry out other consequential incident-response operations. The possibility of false alarms and resulting public panic/harm is the rationale. This is an unconditional product policy for **operational incidents and alarms**, not an admin-configurable bypass or an exception for 'tested integration'. A permissioned, accountable **human must deliberately initiate** the approved action following assessment; log initiator, confirmation, linked incident, preset/version, result, and failures. Provide quick incident-linked actions but not default-on automatic acceptance.

**Differentiate ordinary show automation:** separately programmed and human-armed cue stacks, playback sequences, lighting console input, MIDI/OSC/MSC and timecode may continue to start permitted *non-emergency show cues* according to show programming; that is not authority for automatically activating an incident/emergency response. Incoming external signals claiming to be alarms are treated as alerts for human evaluation even if received over a show-control protocol. An external operator deliberately firing an authorized ordinary cue is still allowed, subject to arming and permissions.

**System-of-systems boundary:** independent certified fire alarms, evacuation/voice alarm, emergency lighting and physical overrides retain their own mandatory automatic functions. Eventiva's human-in-the-loop restriction is for Eventiva-initiated control actions and must not inhibit certified systems, lawful fire-panel interlocks, or physical emergency interventions. Do not call for an extra Eventiva confirmation where it could delay or prevent those independent measures. Any proposed direct control of safety-certified hardware requires separate safety engineering and approval.

**Acceptance criteria:** simulate a false fire/heat alarm and a mistakenly classified crowd incident: both notify MDT with a proposed response and initiate **zero** show/lighting/audio/PA/dispatch outputs without a deliberate authorized human action; no auto approval through agents, tenant rules or remote console input marked as emergency. Authorized manual response from MDT executes only the selected versioned preset and clearly reports partial success/failure. Ordinary human-armed playback and mapped external non-emergency cue input still work independently. Test no deferred/replayed emergency output after reconnect.

Implementation and dependencies remain unapproved.

## Owner clarification — bidirectional MDT/show control, 15 November 2026

The approved requirement is **not just to notify show operators of incidents**: a permitted F7 MDT/controller must be able to invoke **preconfigured show cues and venue emergency-response presets** from an active incident (e.g. bring on approved work lights, pause entertainment audio, coordinate external consoles), with the F1 show engine as the only playback/output executor. Inbound authorized console/media-server OSC/MIDI/MSC/timecode/network events must be able to target permitted F1 cues, and mapped external events may drive approved F7 alerts/issues/SOPs. <issue id="e6838c83-005e-4ec5-bc2f-931de6cd0cb8" label="EVE-256" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-256/connect-mdt-incidents-and-external-controls-to-live-show-cues-and" /> owns the cross-module command/event mappings and tests. Incidents must not automatically fire safety-affecting outputs just because of a classification; human-invoked approved preset is the default. Independently certified venue safety systems remain independent. Product scope confirmed; implementation separately gated.

## BINDING owner scope decision — 2026-11-15: complete QLab-class capability, separate local playback module

The owner explicitly selected **native playback AND external control** (resolves the former A/B question in favour of A), with the complete QLab-inspired capability families as product requirements: audio, mic/live audio, video/stills, camera/live video, text, lighting, fades, network, MIDI, MIDI file, timecode and programmable/script cues, plus cue lists, groups/nested sequences, timelines, cue carts and operator transport/control cues (GO, stop/pause, wait, load/reset, goto/target, arm/disarm, etc). The benchmark includes high-quality routing, effects, synchronization, rehearsal preview, cue grouping/timing and repeatable show programming; **feature parity is a design/acceptance target, not a claim of present implementation nor a licence to copy proprietary QLab code/UI**. Exact engine libraries/codecs and support by OS still require proof and dependency approval.

**Separate modules, one production:** native audio/video/media playback and deterministic real-time device output belong in a **dedicated local show-engine/playback module**, NOT inside the F7 MDT/CAD dispatch module. F7 owns incoming operational issues/requests, incidents, unit dispatch, status, comms and escalations. F1 owns event phases, production plans, cue authoring/calling, rehearsal, production logs and publication. A common versioned action/event/readiness model coordinates both, using the same Eventiva identities, tenant isolation, approvals, audit, screen awareness and agent-native interface. Live cue output never depends on the cloud or a non-deterministic LLM and must not share the MDT dispatch queue as its execution path.

**Repeatability is first-class and must be easy for operators:** reusable show templates, reusable hierarchical cue sets/palettes/carts, versioned cue libraries, device/output/venue patch profiles, scene/sequence templates, per-show instances with safe overrides, dry-run/preflight, rehearsal/test and immutable published/armed show snapshots. Tour/repeat-date templates carry cue/media assets and a dependency/asset manifest, relative timings and venue mappings; live runs pin exact versions, with explicit review/rehearsal/republish when source templates change. Workspaces should not silently mutate a published show when a shared reusable cue set is edited. Preserve F1.15 template/cloning semantics without copying live runs, approvals or rigging sign-offs.

**Bidirectional event handling:** outbound integrations remain planned (OSC, MIDI/MSC, timecode, Art-Net/sACN and adapters for external QLab/media servers/consoles). Native show engine also needs **incoming external control and time signals** (e.g., OSC, MIDI/MSC, MTC/LTC and supported network triggers) that can drive eligible cue actions through authenticated/authorized routes with replay/rate/input validation. Independently, incoming real issues, requests, live incidents and operations/status events must be visible to show operators and linked to cue hold/escalation SOPs, without automatically firing safety-critical outputs. The owner's words "handling the incoming" should be clarified in context; do not assume which incoming signals or platform events should trigger automated GO.

**Scripting:** programmable cue behavior is in scope, but an unsandboxed script must never gain system shell, credentials, privileged control or side-effect access beyond allowed Eventiva actions/driver ports. Script language/runtime, portability, deterministic behavior, execution budgets, review/signing and trust policy require a separately approved design and dependency set.

**Safety:** separate plan/edit, rehearsal/test, live/go and postshow modes; protect external outputs in simulation; preserve explicit human arming, permission boundaries, operator ownership/fencing, emergency stop, qualified rigging sign-off and certified external safety systems. Agents can build, test, explain and propose cues but may only act within delegated live permissions/approvals and no auto-generated emergency logic. Retain functioning Community single-host local playback in offline/degraded situations.

**Implementation status and authorization:** this records a **confirmed product scope decision only**. It does not approve any dependency/driver/codec, image, new executable, OS-specific device support, paid service, network listener exposure or code delivery yet. Further design should produce a capability by cue type/protocol and a staged test/rollout matrix. An <issue id="1e42a35f-12ae-4abf-869a-c8b2669ee85d" label="EVE-254" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-254/define-qlab-class-cue-playback-and-end-to-end-production-control" /> independent playback/engine child can be planned while reusing <issue id="96b947e4-5f8f-4905-9e99-fa55a95a0482" label="EVE-231" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-231/f113-build-the-show-bridge-a-local-process-that-fires-cues-to-consoles" />'s transport bridge and F1.15 repeatable event templates.

The prior A/B "native playback or orchestration only?" paragraph remains as historical discussion and is **superseded by this binding decision**.

## Owner goal (2026-11-15)

Eventiva should serve **the entire live production lifecycle**, from advance, rigging and pre-show construction through installation, commissioning, rehearsal, every show cue/task/incident/emergency, and derig/load-out and reporting, within **one shared event and control system**. QLab ([https://qlab.app/](<https://qlab.app/>)) is a primary **functional and operator-workflow benchmark**, not source code/UI/assets to copy. This is a product-direction/specification and gap-review issue, **not implementation authorization**.

## Confirmed existing specifications

* F1 <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" />/166 event, phase, space, department records: advance, build, load-in, technical, rehearsal, show, changeover, derig, load-out
* <issue id="f3615509-1ebf-4495-9f61-e5a0544e56f4" label="EVE-201" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-201/f16-build-production-plans-a-collaborative-canvas-per-space-and" /> production canvas/MVR; <issue id="ccbe20c9-21c6-40f2-b50f-cd15ce876497" label="EVE-203" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-203/f17-build-lighting-gdtf-fixture-library-fixture-modes-and-dmx-patch" /> patch/GDTF; <issue id="a920d4e5-3f25-4596-b429-27847cd09fb1" label="EVE-206" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-206/f18-build-rigging-points-loads-indicative-load-summary-and-competent" /> rigging loads and independent competent-person sign-off
* <issue id="cb0f80d4-48f4-4e2c-8957-26f36f9a838f" label="EVE-169" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-169/f13-build-the-run-of-show-segments-fixed-and-relative-timing" /> rundown timings; <issue id="cab9223d-ac24-4174-99b4-092df552d509" label="EVE-173" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-173/f15-build-department-cue-lists-with-numbering-segment-links-and" /> department cue lists; <issue id="e51720db-b1e4-46f2-8709-871d46a6cabd" label="EVE-230" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-230/f112-build-live-show-calling-and-show-sequences-run-the-run-of-show" /> show-calling, clocks, standby, sequences and audit log
* <issue id="96b947e4-5f8f-4905-9e99-fa55a95a0482" label="EVE-231" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-231/f113-build-the-show-bridge-a-local-process-that-fires-cues-to-consoles" /> local show bridge, OSC/MIDI/MSC/timecode outputs; <issue id="39b7d4d1-cecf-4031-87c0-fa72276e8739" label="EVE-232" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-232/f114-build-direct-dmx-output-for-small-rigs-over-sacn-and-art-net" /> simple direct sACN/Art-Net DMX
* F3 tasks, F6 equipment/stock, F7 incidents/dispatch/messages; <issue id="5beffe53-7de1-44a4-9d23-3166327dc2b1" label="EVE-253" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-253/build-shared-guided-sop-procedures-and-governed-step-execution" /> governed SOP, <issue id="9268485b-c9f1-49ed-93b7-a3c90b9bc7c6" label="EVE-245" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-245/build-the-integrated-training-competency-and-certification-platform" /> isolated training scenarios

These are mostly **planned**, not implemented. The current plan is heavily **trigger/orchestration-oriented**, not QLab's complete native audio/video/media engine.

## QLab capabilities to compare explicitly

Source: official [https://qlab.app/docs/v5/](<https://qlab.app/docs/v5/>) (QLab 5 manual, 2026). Cue lists and playhead/GO, non-linear cue carts, nested groups (timeline/playlist), pre/post waits and durations, auto-follow and auto-continue, manual/clock/timecode triggers, start/stop/pause/load/reset/devamp/target/goto/wait/memo/arm/disarm, fades, preview/audition versus live execution, editing/show modes and separate view/edit/control roles, monitors/overrides/collaboration. Cue types: Audio, Mic, Video, Camera, Text, Light, Network, MIDI, MIDI File, Timecode and scripting. Local audio output patching, multichannel routing/fades and media file management; video output stages/geometry/effects/NDI; MIDI/MSC/OSC/LTC/MTC; independent live cue sequences. Document supported/unsupported Eventiva functionality in a testable matrix; don't claim all QLab features already exist.

## Proposed design — for review, NOT yet locked

One canonical Event/Phase/Space/RunOfShow graph links F3 tasks, F6 equipment, F1 rigging sign-off, <issue id="5beffe53-7de1-44a4-9d23-3166327dc2b1" label="EVE-253" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-253/build-shared-guided-sop-procedures-and-governed-step-execution" /> guided procedures and F7 incidents with versioned cue sequences. Cue models with stable ids/number, typed targets, list/cart/group/timeline, trigger, delay, repeat, duration, output routing, preflight/readiness, state and audit. Rehearsal/preview/test is isolated from live outputs. Published live cue package is immutable, changes are versioned and qualified. Operator modes: plan/program, rehearse, show-control/GO and postshow audit; functional UI/API/agents share actions and screen projections.

Critical architecture: run physical media and device outputs in a **deterministic local show executor**, capable of running through WAN/cloud loss. Effect Cluster/Workflow coordinates authorization, shared state and durable history, but does not sit in per-frame playback or low-latency signal generation. Local ownership/fencing and safety-tested handoff must prevent competing GO or duplicated device effects. Distinguish hold/pause/panic/stop/failsafe and certified emergency equipment. Human-only arming, protected sign-off, manual takeover and fail-closed authorization; agents may draft/preview/analyze and perform only explicitly delegated authorized actions. Versioned procedures cannot invent emergency/safety steps. Preserve self-hosted Community and independent physical backup controls.

End-to-end acceptance scenarios: a staged build from drawing and task dependency to signed-off rigging; a rehearsal cue stack with manual/auto-follow, groups/cart and controlled outputs; a mixed audio/video/lighting cue whose physical outcomes and timestamp accuracy are validated; missed cue/failed output, media missing, WAN disconnection, clock jump, process crash, competing controllers; an incident prompts documented safe operational response and handover without fabricating safety controls; derig returns equipment, raises defects and generates postshow reports. Test on real playback/hardware before claiming QLab-class reliability.

## One major scope decision remaining

**A — Native QLab-style playback:** Eventiva ultimately plays/renders audio/video and other media itself through its local executor while supporting external consoles and QLab interoperability.
**B — Orchestration-first only:** Eventiva contains cue programming/GO and all lifecycle control but delegates actual media playback to QLab, consoles and media servers.

Determine this before locking implementation layers, media dependencies or execution roadmap. Do not silently restrict the owner's 'replicate QLab' ambition to sending OSC triggers. Every new dependency/version, native runtime, host platform and output hardware test requires the usual explicit gate. Existing F1.13 D1=C (protocol triggers + direct DMX for small rigs) remains approved and is not automatically rescinded by this proposed expansion.

issues.title: Build separate local show playback and cue execution engine
issues.description:
## BINDING owner decision — 15 November 2026: human-in-the-loop for ALL operational emergency actions

**Never automatically actuate a show-control or operational response from an incident, alarm, emergency sensor, issue classification, agent interpretation, integration alert or rules-engine event.** An alarm/event may be ingested, classified, displayed, logged, correlated, escalated to people, propose a configured SOP or preset, and notify designated staff; it must NOT automatically GO/hold/pause/mute audio, set venue lights/DMX, trigger PA/media/announcements, start emergency scene/preset, dispatch units or carry out other consequential incident-response operations. The possibility of false alarms and resulting public panic/harm is the rationale. This is an unconditional product policy for **operational incidents and alarms**, not an admin-configurable bypass or an exception for 'tested integration'. A permissioned, accountable **human must deliberately initiate** the approved action following assessment; log initiator, confirmation, linked incident, preset/version, result, and failures. Provide quick incident-linked actions but not default-on automatic acceptance.

**Differentiate ordinary show automation:** separately programmed and human-armed cue stacks, playback sequences, lighting console input, MIDI/OSC/MSC and timecode may continue to start permitted *non-emergency show cues* according to show programming; that is not authority for automatically activating an incident/emergency response. Incoming external signals claiming to be alarms are treated as alerts for human evaluation even if received over a show-control protocol. An external operator deliberately firing an authorized ordinary cue is still allowed, subject to arming and permissions.

**System-of-systems boundary:** independent certified fire alarms, evacuation/voice alarm, emergency lighting and physical overrides retain their own mandatory automatic functions. Eventiva's human-in-the-loop restriction is for Eventiva-initiated control actions and must not inhibit certified systems, lawful fire-panel interlocks, or physical emergency interventions. Do not call for an extra Eventiva confirmation where it could delay or prevent those independent measures. Any proposed direct control of safety-certified hardware requires separate safety engineering and approval.

**Acceptance criteria:** simulate a false fire/heat alarm and a mistakenly classified crowd incident: both notify MDT with a proposed response and initiate **zero** show/lighting/audio/PA/dispatch outputs without a deliberate authorized human action; no auto approval through agents, tenant rules or remote console input marked as emergency. Authorized manual response from MDT executes only the selected versioned preset and clearly reports partial success/failure. Ordinary human-armed playback and mapped external non-emergency cue input still work independently. Test no deferred/replayed emergency output after reconnect.

Implementation and dependencies remain unapproved.

## MDT and external command boundary — clarified 15 November 2026

See <issue id="e6838c83-005e-4ec5-bc2f-931de6cd0cb8" label="EVE-256" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-256/connect-mdt-incidents-and-external-controls-to-live-show-cues-and" />: a controller can request approved show actions and emergency response presets through the F7 MDT, but they execute only via the authorized F1 cue/command interface and local show engine. Incoming desk/console control must launch mapped native audio/video/lighting cues through the same arming/version/permission model. Support response per-endpoint status and partial failures, offline-local operations, and no stale/replayed emergency commands. The statement that an incoming *incident notification* does not itself fire emergency outputs remains correct; an **authorized deliberate MDT emergency-action command** may invoke a rehearsed preset. No automatic modification of published/armed show snapshots.

## Goal and decision status

**Owner-approved product scope, implementation NOT YET AUTHORIZED.** Deliver an independently deployable **local show playback / cue execution engine** for Eventiva, inspired by the full QLab 5 cue functionality in [EVE-254](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-254/define-qlab-class-cue-playback-and-end-to-end-production-control>), **not as a submodule of the F7 MDT/CAD**. Must work for a single-host Community deployment as well as paired production show machines, with essential live execution independent of WAN/remote AI.

## Functional cue types and control

* Audio playback (local files, trims, loop, fades, volume, multichannel outputs/patch/routing), live Mic input, video/still media, camera inputs, rendered text, lighting, fades/effects, network/OSC, MIDI/MIDI file/MSC, LTC/MTC timecode and programmable/script cues; treat advanced routing/codecs/effects as phased capabilities with exact per-platform requirements and tests.
* Lists with playhead & GO, nested/parallel and sequential group cues, timeline and cue carts for out-of-order execution, auto-follow and auto-continue, waits/delays/repeats, targeted start/stop/pause/load/reset, fade/devamp, goto/target, explicit cue arm/disarm, duration/timecode scheduling, logging and output-device status.
* Author cues, review/edit with live preview versus rehearsal/test versus operator show mode; no test action may unexpectedly actuate live output. Validated script semantics, secure sandbox/allowed actions and resource budgets (separate exact runtime/dependency approval; never run arbitrary scripts as system user).
* Incoming local hardware/control triggers (OSC, MIDI/MSC, LTC/MTC and selected network input) as well as outbound ports; map through signed/authorized show-run commands with input validation, rate/replay handling, per-cue trigger permission, clock-source attribution and output fencing. Distinguish external transport triggers from incoming **operational issue/incident** notifications owned by F7.
* Versioned asset/preload/manifest catalog, missing-file/codec test, media preflight, supported OS drivers/codecs/displays and output patch. Keep console/media-server/QLab interoperability through <issue id="96b947e4-5f8f-4905-9e99-fa55a95a0482" label="EVE-231" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-231/f113-build-the-show-bridge-a-local-process-that-fires-cues-to-consoles" />'s transport services, not a competing command implementation.

## Easy reuse / repeated shows

* A **ShowTemplate** and reusable, versioned **CueSet** can include cue-list, cart, grouped sequences and dependent assets; support one-click create/recreate of show runs for repeated dates, productions, tours or venues with day-zero-relative timings, scene/cue overrides, media links and venue-specific output/patch profiles.
* Instantiate a **published pinned snapshot** for each running show, preserving exact cue-set versions/media hashes, operator-authorized changes, test evidence and a frozen output manifest. Source template edits cannot silently modify a live or published run. Explain/present diffs and allow a deliberate reviewed update/rehearsal workflow.
* Shared Event/Phase/Space/RunOfShow from F1, F6 equipment/patch, F3 build tasks, F7 incident/MDT work and <issue id="5beffe53-7de1-44a4-9d23-3166327dc2b1" label="EVE-253" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-253/build-shared-guided-sop-procedures-and-governed-step-execution" /> SOP integration by IDs. Avoid creating a duplicate Event, RunOfShow, task, incident or workflow engine.

## Runtime / safety architecture

* Local deterministic clock and cue scheduler with independent output drivers; Effect Cluster/Workflow/ActionHost handles durable publication, roles, audit and coordination, **never per-frame media processing** or arbitrary offline live commands. A local operator remains authoritative on-site if WAN fails, with bounded signed authorization and exact version/readiness checks; design offline live authorization separately rather than bypassing security.
* Fencing/leadership prevents multiple devices simultaneously issuing GO or repeated non-idempotent MIDI/network effects during failover; distinguish accepted command, transport delivered and external device-observed success. Expose stale/unknown physical state explicitly.
* Human-controlled arming, manual takeover, configurable emergency safe/stop behaviors with redundant independent physical safety equipment; no software substitutes for certified evacuation/fire/emergency functions. Actions require current permissions and controlled approvals; do not let agents approve themselves or call arbitrary scripts.
* Export reliable logs and after-action records; controlled closure/derig workflow links F1/F3/F6/F7 actual outcomes into one Eventiva production lifecycle.

## Acceptance cases to define before implementation

* Load/publish/reuse a cue set with multiple nested groups, cue carts, fades and several cue types for three dates/venues; show instances remain unchanged when the template is edited until explicitly updated.
* Receive real OSC/MIDI/timecode triggers and emit the corresponding paired outputs locally at measured latency/jitter; show what happens for replayed, out-of-order or unauthorized triggers.
* Run simultaneous audio/video output and a lighting cue while WAN is offline; preloading/asset validation and a local clock still operate. Driver/codec/platform-specific performance measured on actual supported hardware, not estimated.
* Demonstrate rehearsal and preview have no unintended live outputs, disarmed invocation fails, and local manual STOP still works when the server/agent is unreachable. Tests for crash, clock jump, endpoint missing, operator handover and split-brain.
* An incoming F7 operational incident is visible and links to the active show and relevant approved SOP without automatically firing emergency outputs.
* Agent-native inventory and UI-to-agent screen parity; no arbitrary script, unsafe provider privilege escalation or forbidden action route.

## Implementation and approval boundaries

First output is a **source-backed gap matrix and staged runtime/dependency/host-OS proof** against QLab, including separate optional advanced features and supported platform choices. Proposed dependencies for audio/video/OSC/MIDI/timecode/rendering/scripting and any native build scripts must be batched for **explicit owner approval before adding them**. Nothing here authorizes provisioning, code change, production media/control outputs or paid services.

Related: <issue id="1e42a35f-12ae-4abf-869a-c8b2669ee85d" label="EVE-254" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-254/define-qlab-class-cue-playback-and-end-to-end-production-control" />, <issue id="fbcff205-decd-464a-b8ab-a1278e71fbe4" label="EVE-73" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show" />, <issue id="cab9223d-ac24-4174-99b4-092df552d509" label="EVE-173" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-173/f15-build-department-cue-lists-with-numbering-segment-links-and" />, <issue id="e51720db-b1e4-46f2-8709-871d46a6cabd" label="EVE-230" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-230/f112-build-live-show-calling-and-show-sequences-run-the-run-of-show" />, <issue id="96b947e4-5f8f-4905-9e99-fa55a95a0482" label="EVE-231" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-231/f113-build-the-show-bridge-a-local-process-that-fires-cues-to-consoles" />, <issue id="39b7d4d1-cecf-4031-87c0-fa72276e8739" label="EVE-232" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-232/f114-build-direct-dmx-output-for-small-rigs-over-sacn-and-art-net" />, <issue id="265f83d9-0b6e-4b1b-a222-77d386289316" label="EVE-233" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-233/f115-build-event-templates-and-cloning-reuse-phases-departments-plans" />, <issue id="37310611-807d-43de-a5fb-ff53dc3a494e" label="EVE-71" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-71/f7-fleet-and-live-operations-vehicles-maintenance-units-dispatch-and" />, <issue id="5beffe53-7de1-44a4-9d23-3166327dc2b1" label="EVE-253" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-253/build-shared-guided-sop-procedures-and-governed-step-execution" />, <issue id="91297309-acc4-4bb9-ad68-33fbc2720e5a" label="EVE-50" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-50/p111-build-screen-awareness-app-state-navigation-and-the-screen" />, <issue id="55c2d64a-d779-41d9-b74e-dcc7d062b86b" label="EVE-252" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-252/implement-effect-cluster-sharding-and-multi-runner-recovery-in-the" />. QLab trademarks and proprietary interface, code and content are not to be copied.

issues.title: Connect MDT incidents and external controls to live show cues and emergency response presets
issues.description:
## BINDING owner decision — 15 November 2026: human-in-the-loop for ALL operational emergency actions

**Never automatically actuate a show-control or operational response from an incident, alarm, emergency sensor, issue classification, agent interpretation, integration alert or rules-engine event.** An alarm/event may be ingested, classified, displayed, logged, correlated, escalated to people, propose a configured SOP or preset, and notify designated staff; it must NOT automatically GO/hold/pause/mute audio, set venue lights/DMX, trigger PA/media/announcements, start emergency scene/preset, dispatch units or carry out other consequential incident-response operations. The possibility of false alarms and resulting public panic/harm is the rationale. This is an unconditional product policy for **operational incidents and alarms**, not an admin-configurable bypass or an exception for 'tested integration'. A permissioned, accountable **human must deliberately initiate** the approved action following assessment; log initiator, confirmation, linked incident, preset/version, result, and failures. Provide quick incident-linked actions but not default-on automatic acceptance.

**Differentiate ordinary show automation:** separately programmed and human-armed cue stacks, playback sequences, lighting console input, MIDI/OSC/MSC and timecode may continue to start permitted *non-emergency show cues* according to show programming; that is not authority for automatically activating an incident/emergency response. Incoming external signals claiming to be alarms are treated as alerts for human evaluation even if received over a show-control protocol. An external operator deliberately firing an authorized ordinary cue is still allowed, subject to arming and permissions.

**System-of-systems boundary:** independent certified fire alarms, evacuation/voice alarm, emergency lighting and physical overrides retain their own mandatory automatic functions. Eventiva's human-in-the-loop restriction is for Eventiva-initiated control actions and must not inhibit certified systems, lawful fire-panel interlocks, or physical emergency interventions. Do not call for an extra Eventiva confirmation where it could delay or prevent those independent measures. Any proposed direct control of safety-certified hardware requires separate safety engineering and approval.

**Acceptance criteria:** simulate a false fire/heat alarm and a mistakenly classified crowd incident: both notify MDT with a proposed response and initiate **zero** show/lighting/audio/PA/dispatch outputs without a deliberate authorized human action; no auto approval through agents, tenant rules or remote console input marked as emergency. Authorized manual response from MDT executes only the selected versioned preset and clearly reports partial success/failure. Ordinary human-armed playback and mapped external non-emergency cue input still work independently. Test no deferred/replayed emergency output after reconnect.

Implementation and dependencies remain unapproved.

## Product decision — 15 November 2026

Eventiva must support **bidirectional operational control between the F7 control room/MDT and the separate F1 show-control/local playback system**. This is a confirmed product requirement, **not implementation, driver, dependency, listener, or deployment approval**. It is not a separate duplicate dispatch or cue engine.

### User scenarios / required UX

1. **Nightclub emergency from MDT:** an incoming live incident (e.g. crowd crush/injury on dance floor, fire, or another urgent venue issue) is received as a normal F7 issue/incident. An authorized controller can, from the incident or MDT screen, invoke a preconfigured **venue emergency-response cue/action preset**, coordinating (where safe/approved) house/work lights, music pause/stop/attenuation, PA or other audio routing, selected screens and external lighting/audio consoles. Show the incident, procedure, requested actions, individual outputs' acknowledgement/observed-state and failures in one control room; preserve fast access during stress. Response must be predefined and rehearsed, not generated ad hoc by AI.
2. **Normal cross-control:** a permitted MDT/controller action can hold/resume or GO a specific cue/group/cart, subject to live show permissions and current arming/snapshot; cue events can create/log/advance an approved F7 operational action/incident/SOP when mapped.
3. **External-to-Eventiva show control:** an incoming OSC, MIDI/MSC, timecode or supported network command from a lighting console, media server, desk or authorized control system can start an eligible Eventiva audio/video cue or cue set. Example: operator fires a cue on the lighting desk, and the mapped incoming control starts the matching sound in Eventiva.
4. **External-to-MDT operational control:** explicitly mapped incoming events from authorized external equipment/integrations can create an issue, append incident update, raise an alert, request a dispatcher action or start an SOP, and potentially make other permissioned actions when specified. No arbitrary incident closure, dispatch or privilege mutation by unmapped protocol traffic.
5. **Remote operators:** authorized crew/control staff can reach allowed MDT/show actions from their appropriate interface, including an on-site local control path when the WAN is unavailable, with honest online/reachability status. A device without a safe reachable local bridge may not promise remote control.

### Architecture boundaries

* F7 owns issues, incident triage/priority, tasks, units, assignments, control-room view, logs, handover and SOP association. F1 owns cue definitions, show modes, cue execution intent, programmed response presets and show logs. <issue id="43f1ddca-7626-469e-a568-96ae44f272eb" label="EVE-255" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-255/build-separate-local-show-playback-and-cue-execution-engine" /> owns deterministic local audio/video/lighting cue playback; <issue id="96b947e4-5f8f-4905-9e99-fa55a95a0482" label="EVE-231" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-231/f113-build-the-show-bridge-a-local-process-that-fires-cues-to-consoles" /> owns local bidirectional hardware/console transports; no direct F7 execution of per-frame playback and no duplicate command queues.
* A typed, auditable **control-event/mapping layer** maps incoming source events or authorized F7 commands to allowlisted inventory actions. Context: tenant, event, show run, venue, channel, source identity, actor, source sequence/timestamp, mapping version, target, intent and correlation with incident/cue. Separate a 'detected/received event' from an 'authorized command', an 'accepted command', a 'transport delivered' and a 'verified observed hardware state'.
* Show runners pin a tested response/cue snapshot and venue-specific mappings and endpoint targets. Emergency response presets are named, versioned, reversible where appropriate, and bound to the approved venue profile. No implicit global one-size-fits-all blackout/house-light action.
* Inputs are opt-in with explicit per-endpoint trust zone, credential or paired-device identity where possible, binding/mapping, per-action permissions, mode/arming rules, allowlists, freshness/replay/deduplication/rate-limit safeguards and output fencing. OSC/MIDI/DMX are not inherently authenticated; don't claim packet-level identity from those transports without a separately protected gateway. Do not expose raw OSC/MIDI/DMX listeners to public WAN by default.
* Non-safety show-control triggers may run automatically when enabled and armed according to policy. **Operational emergencies do not automatically drive safety-affecting outputs by default**; a permitted human operator selects an approved response. No exception for alarm/sensor/incident-generated automated show outputs is permitted under this product requirement; any future proposal to change that policy requires a new explicit owner decision and a separate safety review. Agents cannot self-approve emergency actions.
* Keep documented distinction between 'pause/stop entertainment audio', 'route a certified/public-address announcement', 'house/work lighting', 'certified emergency lighting/fire alarm systems' and 'physical emergency stop'. Eventiva is not the certified life-safety system; independent physical/manual controls remain. Failure/partial execution must be visible with immediate fallback instructions and responsible controller, never a false success message.
* Live execution avoids WAN/LLM dependence, does not enqueue stale GO/emergency commands for later replay, and must have tested loss-of-network, duplicate, delayed input, split-brain, device-offline, unexpected timecode, override, emergency macro conflict and recovery cases.
* Shared Agent-Native actions and screen-awareness should expose available permitted commands and outcome status to UI/MDT, APIs and authorized agents while enforcing the same permissions/approvals.

### Acceptance tests to specify and run on actual hardware

* Controller opens a nightclub incident in MDT, chooses an approved response preset; locally (with remote cloud disconnected) a test rig reports light/audio changes, shows partial/failed endpoints accurately, links the actions to incident and show logs and offers manual recovery.
* An incoming authorized lighting-console OSC/MIDI trigger launches the correct Eventiva sound cue with a unique correlation id; an unauthorized, replayed, disarmed or unmapped trigger does nothing.
* A configured external alert creates one F7 incident/action with full source and timestamp; it cannot silently dispatch units or start an emergency response without separate explicit permission/approval.
* Safety-certified systems still operate independently and are never bypassed. An unauthorized user/agent and a remote device with no live bridge cannot execute emergency presets.
* Updating a reusable show template never silently changes the armed emergency-response snapshot.

### Planning / dependencies

issues.title: Implement the composable module kernel and safe lifecycle/provider contracts
issues.description:
## Goal

Add the smallest domain-neutral kernel over existing ActionHost: registry, exact manifests, declared dependency environments, named providers, lifecycle and safe generation updates.

## Context and contract

Owner modular-platform request 2026-11-15; canonical specification: [https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c](<https://ampcode.com/artifacts/eventiva-modular-platform-b115f8c7-0edb-4b1b-9219-abf845e2f85c>). Existing <issue id="c31b6b08-1532-4a7a-945f-24a70bbab765" label="EVE-23" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-23/split-core-into-portable-contracts-and-backend-runtime-with-a-shared" />/40/244 remain Done. Kernel implementation lane owns only the paths below.

Public contracts in module-manifest.ts: ModuleId, ModuleVersion (exact numeric x.y.z pins only; no range grammar), ModuleDependency, CapabilityDeclaration, CapabilityRequirement, MigrationDeclaration, KernelManifest, ProviderBinding, PlatformComposition, LifecycleOperation, ModuleState, ReadyReceipt, UpdateResult. module-policy.ts owns KernelError (Data.TaggedError, closed safe reasons) and KernelAuthority admit/authorize using existing Caller.

Manifest {id,version,trust,isolation,dependencies,provides,requires,migrations,restartRequired}; capabilities {name,capability,version}; composition {modules:\[{id,version}\],bindings:\[{consumer,requirement,provider,instance}\]}. Provider key is {module,instance}; explicit consumer requirement selects one declared provider instance and exact capability version. Reject duplicates, ambiguity, missing/undeclared dependencies, cycles, incompatible contracts and unachieved trust/isolation/assurance. resolve is metadata only, KernelEnvironment supplies only declared services. No arbitrary executable isolation based on a manifest assertion.

## Implementation ownership

packages/contracts/src/module-manifest.ts; packages/contracts/src/module-policy.ts; packages/runtime/src/kernel-runtime.ts; tests/contracts/src/module-manifest.spec.ts; tests/runtime/src/kernel-runtime.spec.ts; optional tests/runtime/kernel-vitest.config.mts. Runtime exports KernelModule, KernelEnvironment, ModuleDefinition, Kernel, KernelLive. ModuleDefinition.validate is typed Effect config validation without feature mutation; compatibleWith is exact predecessor pin for explicit hot compatibility. Shared exports/host/schema adapters remain coordinator-owned.

## Acceptance and evidence

1. Cover all register/validate/install/activate/ready/deactivate/unregister/retire/update/recover operations against the specification transition table, including invalid/repeated calls, reverse-order Scope cleanup, dependent removal refusal, failure and recovery. States are registered/validated/installed/active/ready/inactive/failed/retired; unregister removes registration but never history/data. No implicit activation during recover.
2. Compose two platforms with unchanged feature source. Test same implementation twice with independent named Config/Scope and two provider modules sharing a local instance name; explicit bindings select deterministically. Negative fixtures cover every resolution rejection; no registration-order fallback or global service locator.
3. workflow returns scoped {module,version,generation}. Any active-runtime mutation conservatively fails busy while relevant leases exist; scope close drains rather than cancels work. Test old pinned workflow survives refused update, safe release permits replacement, no duplicate side effect/finalizer, initial failure cleans candidate and update failure retains old serving generation. Process-local leases are NOT distributed fencing; <issue id="55c2d64a-d779-41d9-b74e-dcc7d062b86b" label="EVE-252" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-252/implement-effect-cluster-sharding-and-multi-runner-recovery-in-the" />/54 integration remains required.
4. Hot replacement requires explicit compatibleWith, same major, preserved existing dependency/provided/required/security contracts and candidate readiness. Breaking/staged/offline migration or restartRequired returns UpdateResult restart-required with reason incompatible/migration/declared without mutation. MigrationDeclaration is exactly {id,kind:additive|staged,online:boolean}; execution/checksums/schema history belong resource/storage plan, not kernel SQL.
5. ReadyReceipt {runtimeId,generation,emitted}; monotonically increasing successful topology generations invalidate prior ready, repeated ready emits false. Process-local proof must not claim durable platform.ready outbox delivery (<issue id="ee08644c-eb3c-4a46-aea7-745864ad4263" label="EVE-45" href="https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-45/p16-build-the-change-flow-domain-events-and-a-durable-resource-change" />). Required dependency/layer failure cannot yield ready.
6. KernelError public reasons distinguish manifest/config/identity/state/dependency/provider/trust/isolation/assurance/lease/readiness/activation/recovery failures without secret values or arbitrary Cause serialization; expanded union reviewed at integration. Existing ActionHost/Storage errors keep their ownership.
7. Focused Effect tests, typecheck and portable-boundary checks recorded, then coordinator adds @eventiva/contracts/module-manifest, @eventiva/contracts/module-policy, @eventiva/runtime/kernel-runtime (existing source/types/default convention, no root barrel) only when all lanes checkpoint.

## Done signal

Focused evidence linked here; reviewed isolated changes handed to coordinator; complete-platform readiness not claimed until durable hooks, migration, audit and multi-runner integration gates pass.

## Constraints and delivery

Implement in the fresh main foundation, never the Examples archive. Effect v3 typed errors/Schema/Config/Context/Layer/Scope, existing authorized action path, explicit subpath exports and acyclic Nx boundaries. No unapproved dependencies, crypto choices, providers, production provisioning or settings changes. Secrets never enter payloads, errors, logs or issue evidence. Shared manifests/host/generated files are coordinator-owned until checkpoint. Feature rollout uses existing flag service with safe defaults, not environment switches. Record exact commands, decisive output and limitations here; satisfy people and agent docs, full verify and graph requirements before authorized integration. This brief was authored by Amp with AI assistance; it is not an implementation-completion claim.

## Owner continuity addendum — 2026-11-15 (binding implementation requirements)

This is part of the coordinated Eventiva modular-extension platform gate, not a completion claim. Original context: `Examples/preamp` historical extension/HookRegistry/onLoad/Effect.logInfo/structured annotations/Eventiva ASCII word-art; inspect exact archived source before implementing or copying artwork. Preserve original banner bytes/layout where compatible, do not fabricate an equivalent. User-approved directions: strict central typed database API for features; centrally approved declaration migrations; hybrid safe hot changes with controlled restarts; observational and additive hook events only (never mutation, veto, override, synchronous critical-path blockers); additional approval/security boundaries for accounting, payment, emergency and vault-protected operations. No module registration grants decryption rights. Existing security taxonomy Baseline/Sensitive/Restricted-Regulated/Vault-Zero-Knowledge and assurance A1-A5 take precedence; no competing independently granted hook trust taxonomy. Protected notifications only via explicitly authorized, minimized, audited boundary service, not arbitrary plugin callbacks inside protected execution.

Cross-cutting acceptance: install sample extension with manifest + lifecycle registration, receive platform.ready, print *exact archived Eventiva word art* through central structured console logging, emit OTel correlated spans/logs, observe execution and step events, provide an allowed declarative UI extension, and uninstall cleanly, all with NO modifications to host/core or original feature module.
